text: Identify the lines labelled X and Y in Fig. 1.1.
context: BPT manufactures bicycles in country A. It uses batch production. The Operations Director is preparing a break-even chart for one of BPT's bicycles. The chart shows two lines — X starts from a positive y-intercept (total cost line) and Y starts from the origin (total revenue line). BPT imports 60% of its raw materials and exports its bicycles to 8 countries. Total fixed costs are $50,000. Break-even output is 125 units.
ms: 1 mark per correct answer (max 2). X: Total cost(s). Y: Total revenue. Only award the first response given for each answer.

text: Define 'import tariff'.
context: BPT manufactures bicycles in country A. BPT imports 60% of its raw materials. The Managing Director wants to know how the introduction of import tariffs might affect BPT.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): A tax placed on imported goods when they arrive into a country. Partial definition (1 mark): Type of tax. Tax on imported goods.

text: Outline two ways BPT could lower its break-even level of output.
context: BPT manufactures bicycles in country A using batch production. Total fixed costs are $50,000. Break-even output is 125 units. BPT imports 60% of its raw materials and exports to 8 countries.
ms: 1 mark per way + 1 mark application (max 2 ways = 4 marks). Ways: Increase price of its bicycles; Lower fixed cost or examples e.g. reduce rent below $50,000; Lower variable/raw material costs so may consider importing more than 60%. Application words: bicycles or related words, 60%/import raw materials, $50,000 total fixed costs, 125 break-even output, 8 countries, batch production.

text: Explain two ways a depreciation in country A's exchange rate might affect BPT.
context: BPT manufactures bicycles in country A. BPT imports 60% of its raw materials and exports its bicycles to 8 countries. Total fixed costs are $50,000. Break-even output is 125 units.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 ways = 6 marks). Ways: Increased cost of imports which would increase break-even output/increase in price of bicycles; Exports appear cheaper which may increase demand/sales in the 8 countries; May have to find alternative/cheaper suppliers as imports its raw materials which could take time/lead to production delays. Application words: bicycles, 60% of raw materials are imported, 125 break-even output, $50,000 fixed costs, 8 countries.

text: Do you think batch production is the best method of production for a business to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Batch production: Flexibility so can change what to make/quickly adapt to meet customer demands; Production may not be greatly affected if machinery breaks down; Variety/range of products made which could widen customer base/help spread risk; Can motivate workers leading to less absenteeism/lower labour turnover; Time lost switching/resetting machines between batches could lead to lost output/lower efficiency; Need to move/store semi-finished goods leading to increased storage costs; One fault could affect entire batch leading to waste. Flow production: High output; Likely to benefit from economies of scale/discounts for bulk purchasing reducing average costs; Capital intensive methods/fewer employees needed lowering wage cost; If one machine breaks down the whole production line will stop; High set up costs; Inflexible if demand changes. Job production: Unique/meet exact customer needs which can help brand loyalty; Can charge higher price which may increase profit margin; Skilled labour needed which increases labour costs; No economies of scale leading to higher average cost; Production can take a long time; Costs are higher as labour intensive; Mistakes can be expensive to correct. Justification must compare two methods and explain why one is better than another with reasoning - e.g. batch production is the best method because flexibility to adapt to changes in customer demand is likely to be more important than high output levels from flow production.

text: Define 'inflation'.
context: Ramon is an entrepreneur who plans to start up a home tutoring service to provide students with extra help to learn maths. He is concerned about how an increase in the rate of inflation might affect his business.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): An increase in the general price level of goods and services over time. Partial definition (1 mark): An increase in the price of goods/services.

text: Identify two characteristics of a successful entrepreneur.
context: Ramon is an entrepreneur who plans to start up a home tutoring service.
ms: 1 mark per characteristic (max 2). Only award first two responses. Characteristics: Risk-taker; Creative; Hard-working; Innovative; Effective communicator; Optimistic; (Self) confident; Independent; (Self) motivated/focused/determined/committed; Resourceful/adaptable; Leadership; Resilience/determination/patience; Initiative.

text: Outline two ways a business plan might help Ramon.
context: Ramon is an entrepreneur starting a home tutoring service to help students learn maths. He has prepared a business plan. He is considering buying a franchise and is concerned about inflation. He is considering crowdfunding as a source of finance.
ms: 1 mark per way + 1 mark application (max 2 ways = 4 marks). Ways: Get a bank loan/finance/attract investors if decides not to use crowdfunding; Set targets/objectives/future planning for his tutoring business; Understand/reduce possible risks/threats for him as an entrepreneur; Acts as a checklist/way to track progress/compare against goals of his start-up; Helps decision-making; Helps organise resources/labour requirements/marketing strategy. Application words: entrepreneur, start-up/new business, home tutoring/help to learn maths, franchise, increase in inflation, crowdfunding.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to Ramon of buying a franchise.
context: Ramon is an entrepreneur starting a home tutoring service. He is considering buying a franchise. He has a business plan and is concerned about increasing inflation. He is considering crowdfunding.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantages: Easier/quicker to build a customer base which can help gain sales/revenue for his tutoring service; Training/advice offered by franchisor which saves costs important for a start-up; Franchisor pays for advertising which will reduce his cash outflows calculated in his business plan; Banks may be more willing to lend finance to a franchisee so may not need to use crowdfunding; Sell under established/successful brand name so easier to attract customers/can help reduce risk of failure. Disadvantages: Cost to buy franchise which he may not be able to afford at a time when inflation is increasing; Do not have total control/less independence which may be why he became an entrepreneur; Unable to make decisions that suit local area; Must pay royalties/franchise fee/percentage of revenue/profit which could reduce profit margin/increase costs. Application words: entrepreneur, start-up/new business, home tutoring service/learn maths, inflation, crowdfunding, business plan.

text: Do you think crowdfunding is the best source of finance for a start-up business to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Crowdfunding: No initial fee is payable so does not increase cash outflows; Allows for the public reaction to be tested/help advertise which could lead to more customers; Proposal may be rejected using time which could have been used for other purposes; May allow competitors the opportunity to learn more about your business before launch which could lead to fewer sales; No guarantee can raise full amount/not raise enough funds so may have to find another source. Other sources: Own savings as there is no need to repay but may not have sufficient funds; Bank loan so more likely to raise full amount needed quickly but will need to pay interest. Justification must compare crowdfunding with another source and explain why one is better than another - e.g. crowdfunding is best because a new business is risky so the bank may not lend to them anyway and even if it did, it may not be able to afford the repayments.

text: Define 'private sector'.
context: LRL makes skincare products including face cream. It is a private sector business in country X. One of LRL's objectives is to contribute to sustainable development. The total value of sales of skincare products in country X for 2023 was $120 million. LRL has a 30% market share.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): The part of the economy that is controlled by individuals/companies for profit. When business activities are owned by individuals/group of individuals. Partial definition (1 mark): Run by individuals. Do not award: Examples. Features of a sole trader, partnership or limited company.

text: Calculate the value of LRL's market share in 2023.
context: LRL is a private sector business making skincare products. The total value of sales of skincare products in country X for 2023 was $120 million. LRL's market share is 30%.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): $36 million / $36,000,000. Method (1 mark): 120 × 30% = 36. If correct answer given with no working shown, award 2 marks. Award only 1 mark if $36m is written as part of the answer but is not given as the final answer. Need 'million' for 2 marks.

text: Outline two ways LRL could contribute to sustainable development.
context: LRL makes skincare products including face cream. It is a private sector business in country X. LRL has a 30% market share. The total market value is $120 million, so LRL's revenue is $36 million. LRL has objectives including contributing to sustainable development and maintaining customer loyalty.
ms: 1 mark per way + 1 mark application (max 2 ways = 4 marks). Ways: Reduce amount/number of resources used when making skincare products; Develop environmentally friendly products which could help the marketing mix; Use environmentally friendly methods of production at this private sector business; Use environmentally friendly materials/buy materials from sustainable sources which may help improve customer loyalty; Use environmentally friendly packaging/reduce packaging; Reduce waste; Reuse products/materials; Recycle products/materials; Replant trees. Application words: skincare or examples such as face cream, private sector business, marketing mix, customer loyalty, 30% market share, $120 million total value of market sales, $36 million revenue.

text: Explain two advantages to LRL of maintaining customer loyalty.
context: LRL makes skincare products including face cream. It is a private sector business with 30% market share. Total market value is $120 million so LRL revenue is $36 million. LRL has an appropriate marketing mix and contributes to sustainable development.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 advantages = 6 marks). Advantages: Easier to match products to existing customer needs reducing wastage as know which are the popular types of skincare products; Improve/good reputation/brand image so less promotion needed/lower cost by this private sector business; Increase sales/customers which could increase revenue/market share above $36m; Encourages existing customers to try new products; May be able to increase prices which would increase profit margin. Application words: skincare/face cream, marketing mix, sustainable development, 30% market share, private sector business, $120 million total value, $36 million revenue. Increase market share is analysis only.

text: Explain two elements of the marketing mix. Which do you think is the most important element for a business? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Candidates must discuss two elements of the marketing mix to access evaluation marks.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Must discuss two elements to access evaluation marks. Promotion: Raises awareness/informs potential customers leading to more sales; Attracts/persuades potential customers increasing revenue; Creates/builds brand image increasing customer loyalty; Way to communicate with customers. Product: Without a product there is nothing to sell/if dislike the product customers will not buy it; A poor quality product will not last long in the market; Good quality product can encourage customer loyalty; Good quality can improve brand image. Place: Close/near target market/customers to ensure sales; A suitable location might have high rent leading to increased costs/higher prices. Price: A low price could create image of low quality damaging its reputation; If price is too low may not cover costs; If the price is too high the business may be less competitive lowering market share. Justification must compare two elements and explain why one is MORE important than another with reasoning.

text: Define 'commission'.
context: RHN is a clothing retailer. It has 50 shops and 290 employees. Commission is used as one method of financial reward. The business often uses internal recruitment when there is a job vacancy. Last year RHN made a profit of $1.5 million.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Payment to employees relating to the number/value of sales made. Partial definition (1 mark): Money based on sales/what sold.

text: Identify two external users of accounts.
context: RHN is a clothing retailer. The Managing Director, as an internal user of accounts, has been analysing RHN's statement of financial position.
ms: 1 mark per user (max 2). Only award first two responses. External users: Banks/lenders; Suppliers; Government; Potential investor; Local community/pressure groups.

text: Identify four ways the information in a statement of financial position can be used.
context: RHN is a clothing retailer. The Managing Director has been analysing RHN's statement of financial position.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 4). Only award first four responses. Ways: Calculate working capital; Calculate current ratio; Calculate acid test ratio; Shows how the business finances its activities/shareholders can see how any expansion has been funded; Shows the assets the business owns/what the business owns; Show value of liabilities/what the business owes; Support loan application/raise finance/show investors; Show value of the business/what the business is worth; Compare performance over time; Compare performance against competitors.

text: Explain two possible reasons why providing training for its employees is important to RHN.
context: RHN is a clothing retailer with 50 shops and 290 employees. All employees are provided with training. Commission is used as a financial reward. The business often uses internal recruitment. Last year RHN made a profit of $1.5 million.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 reasons = 6 marks). Reasons: More skilled/flexible employees so can cover absences of others in its 50 shops; Fewer mistakes/better quality service from its 290 employees which could improve its reputation; Increases motivation which can help reduce labour turnover which is helpful as uses internal recruitment; Fewer customer complaints about its clothing increasing customer loyalty; Less supervision needed so managers have time to focus on other activities; Improves efficiency/productivity; Fewer accidents/ensure safe working conditions; Able to train others reducing training costs; Provide new ideas/improves innovation; Helps attract potential employees; Helps introduce a new process. Application words: clothing, shops/retailer, 290 employees, commission, internal recruitment, $1.5m profit, 50 locations. Analysis only: Better reputation; Increase sales; Employee loyalty/lower labour turnover; Customer loyalty.

text: Do you think the advantages for a business of using internal recruitment are greater than the disadvantages? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Advantages: Employees know the business so can start work more quickly/less training needed; Low cost/cheaper which reduces cash outflows/as do not have to spend funds on job advertisements; Less time-consuming/quicker which means time can be used for other purposes; Can motivate employees so reducing labour turnover/encourages employee loyalty/improve efficiency; Company knows the employee which reduces risk/likelihood of employing someone who is not appropriate for the job. Disadvantages: Suitable candidates may not be available/employees may not have experience/skills needed which could lead to mistakes/wrong actions taken; Reduces pool/fewer potential candidates; Would create another vacancy for the business to fill; Could create resentment/jealousy among those not selected which could demotivate these employees; Lack of new ideas so business may become less competitive. Justification must compare advantages and disadvantages and explain why advantages are GREATER or LESSER than disadvantages with reasoning.

text: Identify two features of a private sector business.
context: Avtar owns a car repair business which operates in the private sector. It is a small business with 2 full-time employees.
ms: 1 mark per feature (max 2). Only award first two responses. Features: Owned by individuals/not owned by government; Profit motive/objective; Financed by banks/individuals. Other appropriate responses credited.

text: Identify two reasons why a business might remain small.
context: Avtar owns a car repair business, a small business with 2 full-time employees.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two responses. Reasons: Owner's objectives; Limited access to finance/capital; Market size; Market domination/a few large businesses control the market; Lack of knowledge/skills/experience; Wants to maintain close relationship with customers; To remain flexible/respond quickly to changes in consumer tastes; Type/nature of industry/market/product/service.

text: Outline one reason why Avtar might need each of the following types of finance: Short-term finance AND Long-term finance.
context: Avtar owns a car repair business in the private sector with 2 full-time employees. Avtar's business needs finance for many reasons.
ms: 1 mark reason + 1 mark application per type (max 2 marks each = 4 marks). Short-term finance: Pay day-to-day expenses/provide working capital for this private sector business; Pay wages/salary of his 2 employees; Purchase inventory; Prevent cash-flow problem/improve cash position. Long-term finance: Purchase non-current assets or examples for the repair business; Fund expansion/growth in case he decides not to keep the business small; Fund takeover of another business; Develop new products/services. Application words: (car) repair/garage, 2 workers, full-time employees, private sector business, economic recession, small business, added value.

text: Explain two ways an economic recession might affect Avtar's business.
context: Avtar owns a car repair business (private sector, 2 full-time employees). Avtar wants to know how an economic recession might affect his business.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 ways = 6 marks). Ways: Less/lower demand/sales for car repairs reducing revenue/need to make redundancies; Less/lower competition (as other businesses fail) which could increase potential customer base; Widen pool of potential employees if he wants more than 2 employees which may lower recruitment costs; Reduce number of employees so lower break-even/cash outflows/lower costs so does not need finance; May lower prices which reduces added value, increase demand; Material costs may be lower which may increase profit margin/lower variable costs; May delay any expansion plans as not able to afford it so business must remain small; Hard to survive/may close down/objective may switch to survival so may lose investment/difficult to attract investment; May have cash flow problems so need overdraft/loan/cannot repay loans/day-to-day costs; Customers may delay payment/more bad debts; More difficult to raise finance/banks may not lend. Application words: (car) repair/garage, 2 workers, full-time employees, private sector business, small business, added value, short-term/long-term finance. Some points such as lower costs can be knowledge or analysis but only award once. Points about repaying loans/interest/borrowing from bank are analysis only.

text: Explain two ways a business can increase added value. Which is likely to be the best way for a business to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Ways to increase price: (Improve) quality of product/service so customers may be prepared to pay higher prices; (Build a) brand image/marketing/packaging so customers think the product is worth more; (Improve) product features/change/create a unique design making the product more desirable than similar products so willing to pay more; Convenience — customers may pay more for a product they can have straightaway. Ways to lower (input/raw material) costs: Buy cheaper raw materials/find cheaper suppliers reduces material/input costs, widening the gap between cost and price; Reduce the number of materials used. Justification must compare two ways and explain why one is better — e.g. improving quality is better because cheaper materials could damage the reputation leading to fewer sales, while improving quality could even help attract new customers. Analysis can be awarded for explaining the reason why price/cost may be higher/lower, or how the way increases added value. Some analysis can be used for more than one point but only award once.

text: Define 'licensing'.
context: SNT manufactures a range of soft drinks using batch production. SNT's directors are planning to expand into new markets in other countries by forming a joint venture, and are considering licensing as another way to overcome potential problems of entering new markets.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Business gives permission for another company (in the new market being entered) to produce the branded/patented products (under licence). OR A business in one country permits a firm (in a foreign country) to produce its branded products (under licence). OR When a business gives the right to others to produce/sell its products (in another country). Partial (1 mark): Allow someone else to make/sell your products. For 2 marks need the idea of permission/rights given by one business to another AND idea of what (produce/sell/operate for its products). Do not need to refer to other countries/new markets to gain two marks.

text: Identify two factors which might affect how much inventory a business should hold.
context: SNT manufactures soft drinks using batch production. There are many factors which affect how much inventory the business should hold.
ms: 1 mark per factor (max 2). Only award first two responses. Factors: Demand for product/amount of sales; Perishability/nature/type of product/durability; (Storage) space available; Cost of storage/warehouse; Delivery charges; Seasons/celebrations/festivals; Amount of money available (to buy inventory)/cost of inventory/finance; Lead time/reliability of supplier; Method of production/rate/quantity of output; Stock control system/JIT; Forecast/expected shortages.

text: Outline two benefits to SNT of using batch production.
context: SNT is an ethical business manufacturing soft drinks using batch production. In 2023 SNT produced 300 000 bottles of soft drinks each week. SNT plans to expand into new markets in other countries.
ms: 1 mark per benefit + 1 mark application (max 2 benefits = 4 marks). Benefits: Flexible, helping the business adapt to new markets in other countries; Production may not be greatly affected if machinery breaks down so can continue to make some soft drinks; Range/variety of products when making 300 000 bottles per week; Can motivate workers. Application words: soft drinks, 300 000 (bottles per week), new markets (in other countries)/planning to expand, (how much) inventory is important, ethical (business). Comparative statements such as 'more/less' can only be accepted when referring to an alternative method e.g. quicker than job production.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to SNT of forming a joint venture when entering new markets in other countries.
context: SNT is an ethical business manufacturing soft drinks (300 000 bottles/week) using batch production. SNT's directors are planning to expand by forming a joint venture, and are also considering licensing.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantages: Increase capital/share costs/share resources when making its soft drinks which can help reduce borrowing; Access to shared knowledge/expertise increasing productivity/efficiency above 300 000 bottles/week; Less need for market research, lowers marketing costs; Avoid/reduce competition, increasing market share; Share/lower financial risk which reduces possible losses; May be a legal requirement (in some countries). Disadvantages: Possible (management) conflict/disagreements/different ways of working as other business may be less concerned about being ethical, which can slow down decision-making; Mistakes will reflect on all parties which can damage its reputation, reducing its ability to offer licensing; Must share profit which may reduce motivation of each party; Takes time/effort to find the right partner which may delay expansion. Application words: soft drinks, 300 000 bottles/week, ethical business, licensing, batch production. Some points can be knowledge or analysis but do not award the same point twice e.g. share risk.

text: Do you think the advantages to a business of being ethical are greater than the disadvantages? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Advantages: Good image/reputation so can charge higher prices; Good relations with customers which can develop customer loyalty; Increase demand/sales/customers/enter new market, increasing revenue; Help motivate workers leading to lower absenteeism/lower labour turnover/increased productivity; Help recruit/attract employees; Investors more likely to invest, which may make it easier to expand/grow the business; Can help create better supplier relations. Disadvantages: Limited/fewer materials available leading to less output; Higher costs could lead to higher prices; May take time to source suitable/ethical supplies which could delay production; May have to pay more to suppliers/for materials leading to higher variable costs/cost of goods sold/lower gross profit margin. To access evaluation, must discuss a valid advantage and a valid disadvantage. Some points could be knowledge or analysis but do not award the same point twice e.g. customer loyalty, increase prices. Accept problems of not being ethical e.g. damaged reputation.

text: Define 'non-current assets'.
context: HRO manufactures children's toys. It is a private limited company. The Finance Director is preparing HRO's statement of financial position: Non-current assets $480,000, Current assets $250,000, Current liabilities $200,000, Non-current liabilities $300,000.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Resources owned by a business which will be used for a period longer than one year. OR Items owned by a business for more than one year. Partial (1 mark): Items owned/bought/possessed by the business, OR items in the business for more than one year. For both marks must have idea of 'owned by a business' and held 'more than 1 year'.

text: Calculate HRO's current ratio. Show your working.
context: HRO's statement of financial position: Non-current assets $480,000, Current assets $250,000, Current liabilities $200,000, Non-current liabilities $300,000.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): 1.25:1 or 1.25. Method: Current assets ÷ current liabilities = 250/200 (1 mark for correct method). If correct answer given with no working shown, award 2 marks. Award only 1 mark if 1.25 written as part of the answer but not given as final answer.

text: State whether each of the following would be classified as a current asset or as a current liability: Trade receivables; Trade payables; Overdraft; Inventory.
context: HRO is a private limited company preparing its statement of financial position.
ms: 1 mark per correct answer (max 4). Trade receivables: Current asset. Trade payables: Current liability. Overdraft: Current liability. Inventory: Current asset. Only award the first response given for each answer.

text: Explain one way the objective of HRO's shareholders to increase profit might conflict with the objectives of each of the following stakeholder groups: Customers AND Suppliers.
context: HRO manufactures children's toys, a private limited company. The main objective of HRO's shareholders is to increase profit. This might conflict with other stakeholder groups, including its 30 suppliers. Market research can help with marketing decisions. Current liabilities are $200,000.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per stakeholder (max 6 marks). Customers: Value for money/lower prices but HRO might want to increase prices of its toys; HRO might want to increase prices of its toys whereas customers want value for money/lower prices/refuse to buy/go to competitor; Customers want good/better quality of products which may increase (material) costs of this private limited company; Wider range of products but this could increase HRO's costs; Reliable products/services. Suppliers: Might want to increase prices whereas HRO might want to lower prices, so HRO has more funds for market research; HRO wants to pay lower prices which lowers revenue/profit for suppliers; Increased/regular number of orders but HRO might want to place fewer orders to reduce its $200,000 current liabilities; To be treated fairly. Application words: (children's) toys, private limited company, market research, 30 (suppliers), $200,000 (current liabilities). Knowledge can be awarded for identifying an objective of either the business (other than profit) or stakeholder. Analysis mark for explaining how this might conflict with the other party.

text: Do you think the advantages to a business of using primary market research are greater than the disadvantages? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Advantages: Up to date/new (data) which can help make better/informed decisions/able to satisfy customer demand, increasing sales; Business specific/relevant data can be gathered so should help the business find out only what it needs to know; Only available to own business/not available to competition. Disadvantages: Expensive as need to recruit experts to assist, which increases cash outflows/costs; Time to collect which could mean opportunities are missed. To access evaluation, must discuss a valid advantage and a valid disadvantage. Analysis can explain the effect of the advantage/disadvantage, or the reason why it arises.

text: Identify one advantage and one disadvantage to employees of being members of a trade union.
context: TLA is a large hotel with 200 rooms and 3000 employees. Many of these employees are members of a trade union.
ms: 1 mark per advantage/disadvantage (max 2). Only award first response given for each. Advantages: Strength in numbers/more power when negotiating with employers/collective bargaining; Offer (legal) advice to employees; Protect job security/protect against possible redundancy/unfair dismissal; Improve health and safety/better working environment/protect against unfair work practices; Help obtain a pay rise/extra holiday entitlement/change in hours; Improved benefits for members who are not working (sick, retired, redundant); Protect employee rights/ensure workers are not exploited. Disadvantages: Must pay (membership fee)/expensive; Decisions of majority is binding on all members, even if they do not agree.

text: Identify one benefit and one limitation of a business using induction training.
context: TLA is a large hotel with 200 rooms and 3000 employees. All of TLA's new employees receive induction training.
ms: 1 mark per benefit/limitation (max 2). Only award first response given for each. Benefits: Familiarise with work/settle quickly into the job; Helps be made aware of workplace/important health and safety issues before starting the job; Helps understand job role/who main personnel are; May be a legal requirement for health and safety (at start of job); Workers less likely to make mistakes. Limitations: Increases costs/expensive; (Wages paid but) no output; Time-consuming; Delay when employee starts working. Do not award answers about on-the-job/off-the-job training.

text: Outline one reason why each of the following stages of recruitment might be important for TLA: Job description AND Job advertisement.
context: TLA is a large hotel with 200 rooms and 3000 employees. The Human Resources Director has been asked to recruit 2 new managers.
ms: 1 mark reason + 1 mark application per stage (max 2 marks each = 4 marks). Job description: Provides a clear idea of what the job involves/sets out roles and responsibilities of the position for the 3000 employees; Provides basis for drawing up a contract for the new managers; Helps decide basis for pay; Helps create person specification; Helps create appropriate job advert/decide where to advertise; Helps resolve disputes. Job advertisement: Makes (potential) applicants aware of/know about the job at the hotel; Helps attract a range of applicants as planning to expand. Application words: large business, hotel, 200 rooms, 3000 (employees), (2/new) managers, induction training, trade union, planning to expand/grow.

text: Explain two possible diseconomies of scale as TLA grows.
context: TLA is a large hotel with 200 rooms and 3000 employees, many of whom are trade union members. The Managing Director is planning to expand but is worried about possible diseconomies of scale.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 diseconomies = 6 marks). Diseconomies: Low morale/motivation/lack of loyalty/commitment from its 3000 employees leading to higher labour turnover/more workers leaving; Poor communication as more levels for messages to pass through/more mistakes in the hotel; Weak/lack of co-ordination leading to the wrong decisions by the 2 managers; Lack of control which may lead to some employees working less efficiently at this large business. Application words: large business, hotel, 200 rooms, 3000 (employees), 2/new managers, induction training, trade union. Increase in average/unit cost is analysis only. Analysis can explain the effect of the diseconomy or the reasons why it arises.

text: Do you think the advantages of managers using a democratic leadership style are greater than the disadvantages for a business? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. The Human Resources Director knows it is important that all managers use the most appropriate leadership style.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Advantages: Gain (more) ideas/suggestions which may increase sales; Can increase motivation/more committed leading to less absenteeism/(lower) labour turnover/improve efficiency/output; Better decisions could be made as can use employees' experience and skills; Positive work environment. Disadvantages: Employees may not have the necessary experience/want to be involved in decisions, leading to mistakes; Takes time to consult employees which can slow down decision-making. To access evaluation, must discuss a valid advantage and a valid disadvantage. Some points can be knowledge or analysis but only award once e.g. help keep worker loyalty. Points about motivation could be an advantage or disadvantage but only award once. Do not award: reference to delegation.

text: Identify two benefits to a business of using flow production.
context: RSL manufactures paint using flow production. Last year it produced 10 million litres of paint. RSL has 6 managers and 80 employees working in its factory.
ms: 1 mark per benefit (max 2). Only award first two responses. Benefits: High output/large number of products made; (Purchasing) economies of scale/discounts for bulk buying/low average-unit costs; Lower labour cost/less workers needed; Increased efficiency/productivity/goods produced quickly; No need to move goods from one part of the factory to another; Consistent/standardised quality. Do not award vague comments such as saves time, cheaper, quicker, faster on their own.

text: Identify two reasons why people work.
context: RSL manufactures paint using flow production with 6 managers and 80 employees.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two responses. Reasons: (Earn) money/wage/salary/improve standard of living; Job satisfaction/feel as if you have done a good job; Safety/security e.g. job security; Social or examples such as feel part of a group/company; Esteem/recognition/status/feel important/valued; Opportunity to reach potential/challenge self to do new things; Help people/provide a service to community/others. Do not award vague answers such as relieve boredom, something to do, like what they do.

text: Outline one advantage of RSL using each of the following methods of internal communication: Email AND Telephone calls.
context: RSL manufactures paint using flow production, producing 10 million litres last year. RSL has 6 managers and 80 employees, and uses email and telephone calls as its methods of internal communication.
ms: 1 mark advantage + 1 mark application per method (max 2 marks each = 4 marks). Email: A lot of information/detail/documents can be shared with the 80 employees; Can send information/message to multiple people at the same time about the paint; Keep a copy (to refer to); Can communicate with people in a different location; Low cost/cheap; Can check if the message has been read. Telephone calls: Quick if there is a problem using flow production; Opportunity for (instant) questions/discussion/decisions with one of the 6 managers; Feedback (straightaway). Application words: paint, 10 million litres, flow production, relocate (to another country), 80/86 employees, 6 managers, factory, manufacturer, different leadership styles. Award only once in the answer: low cost/cheap; fast/quick.

text: Explain two leadership styles RSL's managers might use.
context: RSL manufactures paint using flow production with 6 managers and 80 employees. The managers use different leadership styles.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 styles = 6 marks). Styles: Autocratic — when the manager instructs/tells workers what to do when using flow production; Democratic — when one of its 6 managers asks employees for their ideas/opinions before making a decision; Laissez-faire — when the managers leave it up to employees to make decisions/decide what to do when making paint. Application words: paint, 10 million litres, flow production, relocate (to another country), 80/86 employees, 6 managers, email, telephone calls, factory, manufacturer.

text: Explain two factors a manufacturing business should consider when relocating its operations to another country. Which factor is likely to be the most important? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. The Operations Manager wants to understand why some manufacturing businesses are relocating their operations to other countries.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Factors: Access to raw materials — without materials it can delay/stop production so not able to meet orders; Labour issues e.g. cost/access to suitable/skilled/enough employees — lower wage rates could help lower labour costs, increasing profit margin; Land issues e.g. availability/cost of suitable land — could increase/lower fixed costs; Trade restrictions such as tariffs/quotas — quotas could limit the amount of goods allowed into a country; Availability of government grants/rates of taxation — could reduce the amount of finance needed; Legal controls — could stop/determine where the business can operate; Infrastructure e.g. access to utilities, communications — without suitable power it would be difficult to operate efficiently; Available market/demand for the product/level of competition — may reduce transport costs; Language/cultural problems. Some analysis could be used for different points but only award once. Accept costs once if no specific reason given.

text: Define 'entrepreneur'.
context: Mitchell is an entrepreneur. He wants to start up a business selling books.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): A person who organises, operates and takes the risk for a new business venture. OR An individual who takes the (financial) risk of starting a new business. OR A person who combines factors of production to start a business. OR An individual who takes the risk by combining factors of production. Partial (1 mark): A person who starts/sets up a business. Do not award: answers such as managing a business or answers which identify the skills of an entrepreneur on their own.

text: Define 'business plan'.
context: Mitchell is an entrepreneur wanting to start up a business selling books. As part of his business plan Mitchell has carried out market research.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): A document containing the business aims/objectives and important details about the operations, finance and owners of a business. OR A detailed written document outlining the purpose and aim of a business which is often used to persuade lenders or investors to finance a business proposal. OR States aims and/or objectives and shows how business plans to achieve them. Partial (1 mark): A document stating the aims of the business, OR a document containing details about the operations, finance and owners of a business.

text: Outline one advantage and one disadvantage to Mitchell of using microfinance as a source of finance.
context: Mitchell is an entrepreneur starting a business selling books, having carried out market research as part of his business plan. Mitchell will use microfinance as a source of finance.
ms: 1 mark advantage/disadvantage + 1 mark application (max 2 marks each = 4 marks). Advantages: Do not need a good credit record/history for this retailer; Less paperwork/no business plan required for this new entrepreneur; No need to provide security/collateral which can help as it is a start-up business. Disadvantages: Only for a small amount so cannot buy many books; Usually high interest rates (as low/poor credit rating). Application words: business plan (can be knowledge or application but not both), new/start-up business, books, ecommerce, entrepreneur, retailer.

text: Explain how the market research data in Chart 1 and Chart 2 could help Mitchell when making decisions.
context: Mitchell's market research: Chart 1 (type of people reading books) — Adults 20%, Older people 27%, Students 18%, Children 35%. Chart 2 (book sales by type, million) — Electronic books, Audiobooks (10m), Paperbacks (50m), Hardbacks (15m).
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per chart (max 6 marks). Chart 1: Decide the target market as children read the most, which could help increase sales/revenue; Decide where to advertise to attract most customers. Chart 2: Decide which type to sell as only 15 million hardbacks are sold, which could help reduce the amount of unsold inventory; Decide how many of each type of book he will sell, therefore must have more of these in stock. Application words: books (allow once), Chart 1 figures (27% older people, 35% children, 20% adults, 18% students), Chart 2 figures (audio/10 million, paperback/50 million, hardback/15 million, other 20 million). Do not award answers which simply state what the chart shows as this is repetition.

text: Do you think the opportunities of ecommerce for a new business are greater than the threats? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Mitchell wants to know whether the opportunities of using ecommerce for a new business are greater than the threats.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Opportunities: More potential customers/sales/widen market, which can increase market share; No/fewer shops needed so less rent/lower fixed costs, increasing profit margin; Fewer employees needed, lower labour/wage costs; Easy to update. Threats: Increased competition so may have to spend more on advertising/set lower prices; Potential customers do not trust online business/risk of fraud/hacking, therefore less likely to purchase; Not everyone has access to the internet, reducing potential customer base; Lack of personal service/no face-to-face contact, difficult to maintain customer loyalty; Increased costs of postage/distribution, leading to higher prices; Cost to set up/maintain website which business might not be able to afford. Lower costs may be knowledge or analysis but allow only once.

text: Define 'capital employed'.
context: JTA is a public limited company selling holidays in a mass market, with 44 shops and 200 employees. Financial extract: Revenue $900m, Profit $100m, Capital employed $800m.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): (Shareholders/owners) equity plus non-current liabilities and is the total long-term capital invested in the business. OR Value of all long-term finance invested in a business. OR Represents how much money has been invested in the business to pay for all assets. Partial (1 mark): Finance/money invested in a business. Accept correct calculations for 2 marks: Non-current assets + working capital; Long term liabilities plus equity; Total assets − current liabilities.

text: Calculate JTA's return on capital employed (ROCE). Show your working.
context: JTA's financial extract for 2023: Revenue $900m, Profit $100m, Capital employed $800m.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): 12.5%. Method: Profit ÷ capital employed × 100 = 100 ÷ 800 × 100 (1 mark). If correct answer given with no working shown, award 2 marks. Only award 1 mark if 12.5% is written as part of the answer but not given as the final answer.

text: Outline two benefits to JTA of selling in a mass market.
context: JTA is a public limited company selling holidays in a mass market, with 44 shops and 200 employees. Revenue $900m, Profit $100m.
ms: 1 mark per benefit + 1 mark application (max 2 benefits = 4 marks). Benefits: High number of customers/sales from its 44 shops; Spread risk when selling holidays; Economies of scale/examples of economies of scale which could help increase its profit of $100m; Opportunities for growth for this public limited company. Application words: holidays, $900m (revenue), $100m (profit), 44 shops, public limited company, 200 employees, (Finance Director is considering) increase to profit.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of JTA being a public limited company.
context: JTA is a public limited company selling holidays in a mass market (44 shops, 200 employees). Revenue $900m, Profit $100m, Capital employed $800m. The Finance Director is considering ways to increase profit.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantages: Able to raise more/large amount of finance to fund growth in this mass market; No restrictions on buying/selling shares/can sell shares to general public, so can raise more/large amounts of finance; Limited liability (for shareholders) as personal assets do not have to be sold if business cannot pay debts; Incorporated/separate legal identity; Continuity so the business will not have to close down on the death of any owner. Disadvantages: Risk of takeover of the holiday business which could change the direction/objectives of the business; Many legal formalities to follow which increases costs; Have to publish accounts which takes time away from other activities; Business information can be seen by competitors, allowing them to copy ideas/find ways to compete; Shareholders expect dividends which can decrease retained profit/increase cash outflows. Application words: holidays, mass market, $900m (revenue), $100m (profit), $800m (capital employed), 44 shops, 200 employees, increase to profit. Some points can be knowledge or analysis but only award once.

text: Do you think increasing prices is the best way for a business to increase its profit? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. The Finance Director is considering ways a business can increase its profit.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Increasing prices: Increases revenue (if sell the same amount of products); Higher prices may suggest better quality, so customers will be willing to pay the higher prices; Fewer customers because customers may switch to competitors, reducing market share; Increase profit margin. Alternatives: Buy cheaper raw materials which may lower quality leading to fewer sales; Improve packaging/quality of product increasing the number of sales; Target new markets/develop new products which could increase advertising costs; Lower rent/expenses or other examples lowering fixed costs. Some analysis can be used for different points but only award once. Allow lower costs only once as either knowledge or analysis. Allow lower/higher sales as analysis only once.

text: Define 'external costs'.
context: FSW is a multinational company with operations in 6 countries. It manufactures steel for use in the construction industry.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Costs paid for by (the rest of) society, other than the business, as a result of business activity. OR Costs paid for by (the rest of) society as a result of business actions. OR Costs/disadvantages that fall on third parties not directly involved in the production process. OR Negative effect on a third party/society due to business actions. Partial (1 mark): Costs that society/third party must pay, OR costs incurred by people who do not take part in the production process. Do not award examples.

text: Identify one objective each of the following stakeholder groups might have: Employees AND Customers.
context: FSW is a multinational company manufacturing steel, with many stakeholder groups interested in its activities.
ms: 1 mark per objective (max 2, one per stakeholder group). Only award first response given for each. Employees: Increased pay/wages/fair wages/regular pay; Better/safe working conditions; Access to training; Job security; Have contract of employment; Work provides motivation/opportunities for promotion/improved status/job satisfaction. Customers: Safe/reliable products; Value for money/reasonable prices; Well-designed/good quality products; Reliable/good service.

text: Identify four ways a pressure group might try to influence business decisions.
context: FSW is a multinational company manufacturing steel. The Managing Director is aware that pressure groups try to influence business decisions.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 4). Only award first four responses. Ways: (Organise) customer boycotts; Raise awareness or examples such as cause negative publicity/publish information/write to newspaper; Lobby/send letters to government; Demonstrations/protests; Arrange petitions; Legal action.

text: Explain one possible benefit and one possible drawback to a country of having FSW (a multinational company) operating there.
context: FSW is a multinational company with operations in 6 countries, manufacturing steel for the construction industry. Quality assurance is used to ensure quality production. The Managing Director knows FSW's business creates external costs.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per benefit AND drawback (max 6 marks). Benefits: Creates jobs/provides income for those making the steel, improving living standards; Orders for local suppliers from its 6 factories, increasing local incomes/GDP; Technical knowhow increased, which could help improve production methods/efficiency/output such as new ways to maintain quality; Companies pay taxes, increasing government income/government able to provide more services; Improve international reputation of country, attracting other businesses; Increased investment/infrastructure development in a country; Introduces new products to the country. Drawbacks: Competition for local businesses leading to lower demand/prices for construction businesses; Uses limited resources which may upset pressure groups as there is less available for other local businesses; Profits are often repatriated, limiting the country's growth; Jobs created may be unskilled; Creates pollution when producing steel. Application words: steel or related words e.g. iron, construction industry, manufacturer, quality assurance/quality production, (6) countries, 500/3000 workers, stakeholder groups, external costs, pressure groups.

text: Do you think quality assurance is the best way for a business to achieve quality production? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Quality assurance is used by FSW to ensure quality production.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Quality assurance: Errors are spotted earlier in the process, so less money/time spent on rework; Increased motivation of employees leading to higher output; Need to train all workers which increases training costs; Time taken to train all workers who may ask for higher wages; Slows down production/time consuming, so productivity will fall; Not all workers might be interested/able to spot problems. Quality control (as alternative): Does not stop production while checking, so some output is made; Not all workers need to be trained, which can help reduce fixed costs; Need to recruit quality inspectors, increasing labour cost; Does not find out how/where fault occurred; Products will need to be scrapped/reworked; Does not encourage all workers to be responsible for quality; Not possible to check all products, damaging reputation. Some points can be presented as an advantage or disadvantage of different methods but do not award the same point twice.

text: Identify one non-current asset and one non-current liability.
context: WFT is a primary sector business which harvests timber (wood) from trees, with 30 employees. Statement of financial position extract at 30 April 2024: Non-current assets $600,000, Current assets $120,000, Current liabilities $150,000, Non-current liabilities $320,000.
ms: 1 mark per correct answer (max 1 each). Non-current assets: Land/buildings; Equipment; Machinery; Vehicles; Fixtures and/or fittings. Non-current liabilities: Bank loans. Only award first response for each type.

text: Calculate WFT's current ratio in 2024. Show your working.
context: WFT's statement of financial position: Current assets $120,000, Current liabilities $150,000.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): 0.8:1 or 0.8. Method: Current assets ÷ current liabilities = 120000/150000 (1 mark). If correct answer given with no working shown, award 2 marks. Award only 1 mark if 0.8 is written as part of the answer but not given as final answer.

text: Outline two ways legal controls over business activity affecting the environment might affect WFT.
context: WFT is a primary sector business harvesting timber from trees, with 30 employees, using a lot of technology to process timber. There are many legal controls over business activity affecting the environment.
ms: 1 mark per way + 1 mark application (max 2 ways = 4 marks). Ways: May have to change where/how to dispose of waste from harvesting trees; Might have to pay fines/buy pollution permits for this primary sector business; Might limit use of energy which may matter as the business uses a lot of technology; May have to move/change location/restrict what can do in a certain area, affecting its 30 employees; May have to limit/reduce amount/output; May have to change equipment/how operate; May have to retrain/provide more training for employees; Increase costs; May have to replant/reforest/return land to its former state. Application words: primary sector, (harvests) wood/trees/timber, 30 employees, (uses a lot of) technology, increase added value, $320,000 (non-current liabilities).

text: Explain two factors WFT should consider when deciding on a source of finance.
context: WFT harvests timber with 30 employees, using a lot of technology. WFT often needs finance. Statement of financial position: Non-current assets $600,000, Current assets $120,000, Current liabilities $150,000, Non-current liabilities $320,000.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 factors = 6 marks). Factors: Amount — as uses a lot of technology it may need a large amount which may not be available from internal sources; Level of existing loans/debts/borrowing — as has non-current liabilities of $320,000 so bank may not be willing to lend; Size/legal form of business — if this primary sector business is a limited company it would be able to issue shares; Interest/cost of finance — high interest would increase cash outflows; Purpose/why it is needed; Length of time required for; Credit history. Application words: primary sector, (harvests) wood/trees/timber, 30 employees, (uses a lot of) technology, increase added value, $600,000 (non-current assets), $120,000 (current assets), $150,000 (current liabilities), $320,000 (non-current liabilities).

text: Explain two ways a business might increase added value. Which do you think is the best way? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. WFT is always considering ways to increase added value.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Ways: Use cheaper materials/supplier will help lower (input) costs; Increase price as this would widen the gap between (input) cost and price; Improve the packaging so customers perceive the product to be worth more, prepared to pay extra; Excellent customer service so customers may be prepared to pay a higher price; Branding/improve brand image/marketing; Additional product features; Convenience. Justification must compare two ways and explain why one is better — e.g. setting a higher price is better because customers may still be willing to pay more to maintain good quality, whereas using cheaper materials is more likely to lower quality and lower sales. Some points of analysis could apply to more than one way but only award once.

text: Define 'profit'.
context: Alana opened a restaurant in the city centre 5 years ago, providing plant-based meals. In 2023 the business made a profit of $80,000.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Difference between revenue and total costs. OR The financial gain of a business once all the costs have been paid using revenue. Partial (1 mark): Revenue minus costs. For 2 marks must have the idea of revenue and total/all costs.

text: Identify two reasons why consumer spending patterns might change.
context: Alana's restaurant uses primary market research to help identify changes in consumer spending patterns.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two responses. Reasons: Technology; Consumer tastes/fashions/trends; Income; Age (profile of population); Price of own product; Price of competitor's products; Advertising/promotional activities.

text: Outline two methods of primary market research Alana might use.
context: Alana opened a plant-based restaurant in the city centre 5 years ago with 16 employees. She uses primary market research to identify changes in consumer spending patterns.
ms: 1 mark per method + 1 mark application (max 2 methods = 4 marks). Methods: Focus groups from her customers over the past 5 years; Observations by her 16 employees; Interviews by asking people in the city centre; Surveys about the restaurant; Questionnaires about her plant-based meals. Application words: restaurant such as menus/cooking, plant/vegetable-based meals or related words such as food/cooking, city centre, 16 employees, market segment/segmentation, 5 years ago, consumer spending patterns, $80,000 (profit).

text: Explain two possible effects of an increase in interest rates on Alana's business.
context: Alana's plant-based restaurant (city centre, 5 years old, 16 employees, $80,000 profit in 2023) — she wants to know how an increase in interest rates might affect her business.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 effects = 6 marks). Effects: Cost of borrowing increases for the restaurant, so less likely to invest/expand/increase prices; Less demand/customers/sales, so lower revenue, because of changes in consumer spending patterns; May be more difficult to obtain loans/borrow, so may have to rely on other sources of finance such as her $80,000 profit; May delay/reduce level of investment/expansion. Application words: restaurant such as menus/cooking, plant/vegetable-based meals, city centre, 16 employees, market segment/segmentation, 5 years ago, consumer spending patterns, $80,000 (profit). Some points could be knowledge or analysis but do not award the same point twice.

text: Do you think income is the best way for a business to segment a market? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Market research can be used to help segment a market.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Income: Can target advertising at particular groups, more cost-effective use of budget/reducing expenses; Can target groups with different products, leading to more sales/market share; Can price the product differently for each income group, increasing sales/revenue; Product could be associated as cheap/expensive, reducing potential market. Alternative methods (region/gender/age/use of product/lifestyle) can also be discussed. Justification must compare income against another method — e.g. income is likely better as gender could lead to missing out on half the potential market, whereas income allows pricing based on ability to pay, leading to a wider potential market overall.

text: Define 'public limited company'.
context: CQT is a public limited company manufacturing paint using flow production, employing 50 workers.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Businesses owned by shareholders, but it can sell shares to the public (and their shares are tradeable on the stock exchange). OR A company that sells its shares to the general public (through a stock exchange). Partial (1 mark): A business that can sell shares. For 2 marks need the idea that shares are sold AND to whom sold to/by.

text: Identify two reasons for globalisation.
context: CQT's Operations Director knows there are many reasons for globalisation.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two responses. Reasons: Increasing number of free trade agreements/reduction in trade barriers; Improved/cheaper travel links; Improved communication networks/technology; Emerging markets are expanding quickly; Change in government economic policy/allowing businesses from other countries to set up operations in own country.

text: Outline two economies of scale CQT might benefit from.
context: CQT is a public limited company manufacturing paint using flow production (50 workers), buying all raw materials from local suppliers. This method allows CQT to benefit from economies of scale.
ms: 1 mark per economy + 1 mark application (max 2 = 4 marks). Economies: Purchasing economies when buying from local suppliers; Technical, especially as using flow production; Managerial, to help the business take advantage of globalisation; Marketing, to help increase sales of paint; Financial, which may help fund any relocation to other countries. Application words: paint, flow production, 50 (employees/workers), local suppliers, globalisation, relocate its operations.

text: Explain two limitations for CQT of using flow production.
context: CQT is a public limited company manufacturing paint using flow production (50 workers), benefiting from economies of scale. The Operations Director has been asked about factors when relocating the factory.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 limitations = 6 marks). Limitations: Inflexible/production line is difficult to change, so difficult to meet customer demand/needs for paint; Demotivating for its unskilled 50 employees, so may lower efficiency/output; High level of raw materials/inventory is held, increasing storage space/cost for this public limited company; If one machine breaks down the whole production line stops, which could lower output so may not benefit from globalisation; High initial/set up cost which the business may not be able to afford. Application words: paint, economies of scale, 50 (employees/workers), local suppliers, globalisation, relocate its factory, public limited company. Some points can be knowledge or analysis but only award once.

text: Explain two factors a business should consider when deciding whether to relocate its factory to another country. Which factor is likely to be the most important? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Factors: Access to/able to find (suitable) employees, increasing recruitment/training costs/may need to pay higher wages; Access to/cost of suitable land/rent, may need a big space/to lower fixed costs; Access/cost of raw materials/distance from suppliers/need to find new suppliers, as if far away may increase transport costs; Different legal controls/standards, so may have to change how/where to operate; Communication/language problems, may lead to mistakes; Trade barriers e.g. quotas/tariffs; Access to government grants/incentives. Justification must compare two factors — e.g. legal controls most important because a business can hire translators to overcome communication problems, whereas a business has limited/no control over the laws of the country.

text: Identify two advantages to a business of having part-time employees.
context: MTO is a bank providing loans and financial services to 1 million customers, with 70 branches and 2800 employees. Many of its employees work part-time.
ms: 1 mark per advantage (max 2). Only award first two responses. Advantages: Cheaper than full-time/reduce labour costs/no need to pay when not working; More flexible hours of work; Can ask/more likely to work at busier times; Can/more likely to extend working hours; Provides a wider range of skills/experience; Helps attract well-qualified employees who need flexible hours; Helps retain experienced workers.

text: Define 'organisational structure'.
context: MTO is a bank with a tall organisational structure and its managers have a narrow span of control.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Refers to the levels of management and division of responsibilities within an organisation. OR The formal, internal framework of a business that shows how it is managed and organised. Partial (1 mark): Shows levels of management in a business, OR shows responsibilities of employees. One mark for idea of positions/levels/hierarchy in the organisation; one mark for understanding it refers to how it is managed/organised/responsibilities.

text: Identify four reasons why effective internal communication is important for a business.
context: MTO is a bank with 70 branches and 2800 employees. Effective internal communication is important.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 4). Only award first four responses. Reasons: Fewer mistakes/less waste/prevent mistakes; Enable faster/better decision-making; Improve motivation; Improve coordination; Improve efficiency/productivity; Increase output; Better collaboration between workers/manager/better teamwork. Question requires candidates to identify the benefit of communicating properly, not why communicate.

text: Using Table 4.1, explain two reasons why MTO should select applicant A as its new manager.
context: MTO is a bank (1 million customers, 70 branches, 2800 employees, tall structure, narrow span of control). One objective is growth. Applicant A: University degree in Business, good at decision-making, 18 months at another business including 3 months as a manager.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 reasons = 6 marks). Reasons: Knows what the job involves/experience as has been a manager for 3 months, so less likely to make mistakes/may need less training; Has (relevant) qualifications as has a degree in Business, so should be able to do the job; Good at decision-making which can help the bank, may help improve efficiency; May bring in new ideas, so may be able to help the business achieve its objective of growth. Application words: bank/financial services e.g. provide loans, 1 million customers, 2800 employees, 70 branches, 3 months experience (as a manager), 18 months (at another business), (University) degree in Business, good decision-making skills, growth (as objective), narrow span of control, tall organisational structure.

text: Explain two reasons why a business might want to grow. Which reason is likely to be the most important? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. One of MTO's objectives is growth.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Reasons: Increase market share, so able to set/control prices, which may reduce competition; Benefit from economies of scale, leading to lower unit/average costs, which can increase profit margin; Increase sales, which could lead to additional revenue; Spread risk, so if no sales in one market, can still gain revenue from other markets; Increase profit, which can act as a source of finance/reinvest back into business; Increased status/reputation, could attract customers; Protect against risk of takeover; Survival. Justification must compare two reasons — e.g. economies of scale are likely to be the most important because lower unit costs will also increase the profit margin, whereas the ability to increase sales may depend on the level of competition.

text: Identify two reasons why a government might support business start-ups.
context: Nicky wants to be a successful entrepreneur, planning to start up a travel business specialising in walking holidays, operating in a niche market. She has been told government support is available for business start-ups.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two responses. Reasons: Create jobs/reduce unemployment; Increase/contribute to output/GDP; Gain more taxes/revenue (for the country); Bring ideas for/provide goods/services/innovation; Increase competition/increase choice/motivate other businesses to start up; To benefit society.

text: Identify two ways a business can build customer relationships.
context: Nicky knows building customer relationships will be important for her travel business.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 2). Only award first two responses. Ways: Offer good quality services/products; Provide special offers or discounts to regular customers/loyalty schemes; Market research/find out what customers want/ask for feedback; Communicate with customers e.g. send newsletters; Respond to complaints/offer refunds; Provide extra services such as credit/delivery/after sales service; Build brand image.

text: Outline one benefit and one limitation to Nicky's business of operating in a niche market.
context: Nicky is starting a travel business specialising in walking holidays, operating in a niche market, preparing a business plan.
ms: 1 mark benefit/limitation + 1 mark application (max 2 each = 4 marks). Benefits: Less/low competition for her start-up business; Needs of customers can be focused on/help target customers for her holidays; Builds up specialist skills/knowledge which can help build customer relationships; Can often charge a higher price, influencing decision-making. Limitations: Lack of economies of scale which can affect business plan; Limited sales/revenue/customers/target market is small for this entrepreneur; Does not spread risks/relying on one product. Application words: entrepreneur, start-up/new business, building customer relationships, (walking) holidays/tickets, travel business/tourism, business plan, decision-making, government support.

text: Explain one way each of the following sections in the business plan might be helpful to Nicky: Business objectives AND Data about the market.
context: Nicky is preparing a business plan to help with her decision-making for her new walking holidays travel business.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per section (max 6 marks). Business objectives: Can act as a goal/target/sense of direction for the travel business which she can use to measure/monitor progress/provide motivation; Improved decision-making/planning so fewer errors/chance of failure/increase efficiency/save cost/save time/increase sales of the new business; Act as a measure of success so able to check progress to know whether she is a successful entrepreneur. Data about the market: Show size of market/can spot trends/gaps so know level of demand in this niche market; Show whether/where there is sufficient demand which will affect sales/revenue/location for her walking holidays; Information about her target market so decide how to promote the business which can help build customer relationships; Information about competitors/level of competition so help decide on a suitable method of pricing; Help set prices/make marketing decisions increasing sales. Application words: entrepreneur, start-up/new business, (walking) holidays/tickets, travel business/tourism, niche market, government support, building customer relationships.

text: Explain two characteristics of a successful entrepreneur. Which characteristic is likely to be the most important? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Characteristics: Creative — have (new/unique) ideas/make a business stand out from competitors, therefore help gain sales; Risk-taker — as investment may be lost; Perseverance/determination/resilience/self-motivated — will need to be prepared to keep going when faced with problems; Effective communicator — as may need to convince suppliers/banks/customers to provide goods/lend/buy products; Good decision-maker/manager — as changes in market may require action; Hard-working — must be ready to do everything themselves; Independent — able to work without any help; Optimistic — so always think they will succeed; Self-confident — so convince people/banks to invest; Innovative — able to put ideas into practice in new/different ways; (Multi-)skilled — may not need to recruit employees for specific roles. Justification must compare two characteristics — e.g. risk-taker is likely to be most important because if they do not take risks, they may miss out on the opportunity to make sales, and therefore may never know whether the new idea could be successful.

text: Define 'tertiary sector'.
context: GTB is a business which operates in the tertiary sector, owning 5 cafés selling food and drinks.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Provides services to consumers/other sectors of industry. OR Firms that supply a service to consumers/other businesses. Partial (1 mark): Business that provides services, OR service sector business. First mark for understanding it provides services; second mark for reference to whom services are provided.

text: Calculate GTB's Return on Capital Employed (ROCE). Show your working.
context: GTB's financial statements 2023: Revenue $600,000, Profit $150,000, Capital employed $750,000, Profit margin 25%.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): 20%. Method: Profit ÷ capital employed × 100 = 150,000/750,000 × 100 (1 mark). If correct answer given with no working shown, award 2 marks. Answer must be shown as a percentage (%) to gain both marks. Award only 1 mark if 20% is written as part of the answer but not given as final answer.

text: Outline two ways GTB could improve its profit margin.
context: GTB operates 5 cafés in the tertiary sector, uses social media for promotion. Revenue $600,000, Profit $150,000, Capital employed $750,000, Profit margin 25%. The Finance Manager is considering ways to improve GTB's profit margin.
ms: 1 mark per way + 1 mark application (max 2 ways = 4 marks). Ways: Increase price of the food; Lower/control fixed costs (or examples such as lower rent) of its cafés; Lower/control variable costs (or examples) which could help increase the profit margin of 25%. Application words: café, selling food/drinks or examples such as coffee, 5 (cafés), 25% (profit margin), $600,000 (revenue), $150,000 (profit), $750,000 (capital employed), social media for promotion.

text: Explain two advantages to GTB of using social media as its method of promotion.
context: GTB operates 5 cafés in the tertiary sector, using social media as its method of promotion. Revenue $600,000, Profit $150,000, Capital employed $750,000, Profit margin 25%.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 advantages = 6 marks). Advantages: Can target specific groups of customers which could help encourage brand loyalty at each of the 5 locations; Low-cost so fewer cash outflows/lower expenses which could help improve the profit margin of 25%; Cover wide area/seen by many people, increasing sales/revenue/attract customers for the café; Quick to update so can spend time on other tasks such as analysing the financial statements; Can reach groups that are difficult to reach any other way.
