Application words: café, selling food/drinks or examples such as coffee, 5 (cafés), 25% (profit margin), improve profit margin, $600,000 (revenue), $150,000 (profit), $750,000 (capital employed), tertiary sector. Advantages must be to the business not the customer.

text: Do you think banks are the main external users of the accounts of a business? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Moeen knows there are other users that are interested in the accounts of a business.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Banks: Whether to give a bank loan, to see if a business can repay; Whether a business can repay loans/overdraft as this will influence the terms/interest rate/period of the loan; To help decide the interest rate to set, to reflect the level of risk; To decide the amount to lend; Check interest payments can/are being made. Other users: Government — want to check the profit/to know the correct amount of tax has been paid/will be paid. Suppliers/Trade payables — assess/shows liquidity position to know whether the business is likely to be able to repay them; see level of debt. Justification must compare banks against another user — e.g. banks are likely the main external user because they often lend large sums of money, whereas suppliers may be less interested in the accounts if orders are small.

text: Define 'laissez-faire leadership style'.
context: RBG is an oil company with operations in 6 countries, 2000 employees including 60 managers. Some managers use a laissez-faire leadership style.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Makes the broad objectives of the business known to employees, but then they are left to make their own decisions and organise their own work. OR A style of leadership that supports employees in achieving targets at the same time as allowing them the freedom to decide how to meet the targets. Partial (1 mark): Managers do not tell workers what to do/how to organise work. For both marks need the idea that it links to decision making — and it is the employees/workers who make them.

text: Identify two roles of a manager.
context: RBG is an oil company with 2000 employees including 60 managers.
ms: 1 mark per role (max 2). Only award first two responses. Roles: Planning; Controlling; Organising; Leading/commanding/directing/give instructions/tasks; Coordinating; Motivating/inspiring others; Decision-making/solve problems; Communicating/give feedback; Delegating. Accept any tasks that managers are likely to do. Do not award: managing activities on own e.g. managing finance.

text: Outline one external cost and one external benefit RBG's business activities might create.
context: RBG is an oil company with operations in 6 countries, 2000 employees, 60 managers. The Managing Director knows RBG's business activities can create external costs and external benefits.
ms: 1 mark cost/benefit + 1 mark application (max 2 each = 4 marks). External costs: Loss of space/land from its operations in 6 countries; Pollution/waste or examples such as gas emissions, which is why it must respond to pressure groups; Congestion/traffic; Deplete/exploit natural/non-renewable resources; Use of energy. External benefits: Employment opportunities/lower unemployment as may recruit more than 2000 employees; Taxes will be paid to governments from extracting oil; Improved infrastructure/better transport systems. Application words: oil, 6 countries, pressure groups, 2000 employees, 60 managers, IT based methods.

text: Explain two methods of IT based communication RBG might use with its employees.
context: RBG is an oil company with operations in 6 countries, 2000 employees, 60 managers. All of RBG's internal communication uses information technology (IT) based methods.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 methods = 6 marks). Methods: Email — written record for all 2000 employees; Text messages/SMS/DM — saves time/quick for the 60 managers; Website/social media or examples e.g. Facebook/X/Twitter — seen by many people at once in the 6 countries; Video conferencing or examples e.g. Zoom/Teams/online meeting — can see body language; Phone/mobile (call) at the oil company — able to get feedback/allows for two-way communication. Application words: oil, 6 countries, 2000 employees, 60 managers, laissez-faire. Can award as analysis for different methods but only once: low cost; quick; send to many people at once; send large amounts of information/attachments; written record; instant feedback; do not have to travel.

text: Explain two ways a pressure group might try to influence business decisions. Which way do you think is likely to be the most effective? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. The Managing Director says: 'Pressure groups often try to influence business decisions.'
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Ways: (Customer) boycotts/encourage customers not to buy, leading to fewer sales and possibly less revenue; Raise/increase awareness or examples such as cause negative publicity/publish information/write to newspaper/publicity stunts, which could damage the business's reputation; Lobbying (politicians)/send letters to government, which could lead to changes in the law/could take time; Demonstrations/protests, which could lead to fewer people willing to invest in the business; Arrange petitions; Take legal action but may increase costs. Justification must compare two ways — e.g. a boycott is the most effective way because fewer sales could mean less revenue which directly affects the business, whereas lobbying may not achieve anything other than raising awareness.

text: Define 'import quota'.
context: DLT manufactures cups and plates in country X, exports 30% of its products to country Y where it benefits from lower rates of taxation and no import quotas.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Physical limit on the number/amount of goods that can be imported/allowed into a country. OR Restriction on the quantity of a product that can be imported. Partial (1 mark): Limit on number/quantity of goods, OR limit on imports. Do not award answers which confuse the term with a tariff.

text: Identify two benefits to a business of lower rates of taxation.
context: DLT exports 30% of its products to country Y where it benefits from lower rates of taxation.
ms: 1 mark per benefit (max 2). Only award first two responses. Benefits: May encourage investment/growth; Increase sales/revenue/income; Lower costs/less cash outflow/lower expenses/cheaper raw materials/cheaper imports; More (retained) profit; Higher profit margin.

text: Identify four legal controls over employment.
context: DLT's factory uses flow production and has 75 employees. The Human Resources Director is aware that there are many legal controls over employment.
ms: 1 mark per legal control (max 4). Only award first four responses. Controls: Unfair dismissal; Discrimination/equal opportunities; (Health and) safety/working conditions/working environment; Minimum wage; Contract of employment or examples such as sickness policy/holiday entitlement/notice period/rate of pay/salary/pension entitlement; Redundancy; Working hours/provide breaks; Legal working age/child labour. Allow examples of discrimination only once. Do not award ethical points such as fair pay.

text: Explain one reason why DLT needs to consider each of the following factors when deciding where to relocate in country X: Suppliers AND Suitability of land.
context: DLT manufactures cups and plates using flow production in country X, 75 employees. DLT exports 30% of its products, and the Managing Director is considering relocating its factory to meet increased demand for exports.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per factor (max 6 marks). Suppliers: Distance — if closer to the factory may reduce transport costs/may be able to get resources quicker; May need to change supplier/can they still use current supplier, leading to delays so cannot meet increase in demand; Quality/range of materials could damage its reputation of its cups/plates; Cost, which could lower its profit margin. Suitability of land: May need a large area/space otherwise this could limit production/so able to expand for its exports; Access to power/water/electricity as using flow production, need continuous supply to operate 24 hours a day; Cost of land/rent as may increase fixed costs; Links to transport/accessible to ensure deliveries can be made on time; Environmental impact; Government influence or examples such as taxes. Application words: cups/plates, flow production, (30%) exported, factory, 75 employees, increased demand (for its products).

text: Do you think the advantages for a manufacturing business of using flow production are greater than the disadvantages? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. DLT's factory uses flow production.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Advantages: Benefit from economies of scale, lowering unit/average costs; Capital intensive so can lower the labour/wage costs; Output can be produced 24 hours a day/continuous; Workers can specialise/little training may be needed. Disadvantages: Inflexible/difficult to change/cannot customise products, so may not meet customer needs; Demotivate employees, raises absenteeism/labour turnover; If one machine breaks down the whole production line will stop, delaying output; Requires high level of raw materials/inventory, increasing storage space/cost. Justification must compare an advantage and a disadvantage — e.g. advantages are greater as lower unit costs could result in lower prices which can increase demand; if the product has high sales this could reduce the need for flexibility.

text: Define 'diseconomies of scale'.
context: FBM is a boat building business with 100 skilled employees. Variable costs per unit $5000, Fixed costs per year $600,000, Number of boats made each year 300. The Operations Director is concerned the business is starting to experience diseconomies of scale.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Factors that lead to an increase in average costs as a business grows beyond a certain size. OR Factors that cause average costs to increase as the scale of operations increases. OR The disadvantages of a business growing (too large) that result in an increase in costs per unit. Partial (1 mark): When costs increase because business grows, OR increase in average unit cost. For two marks candidates must have the idea that 'business grows' AND it 'increases average/unit costs'. Do not award examples.

text: Identify two ways a business can use cost data to help make decisions.
context: The Finance Director has been asked to analyse FBM's cost and output data.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 2). Only award first two responses. Ways: Setting prices; Decide whether to stop/continue production/change production; Decide on the best location; Decide if finance is required/set budgets; Decide which costs need to be reduced/whether to change suppliers; Setting objectives. Allow 'carry out break-even analysis'.

text: Identify four fixed costs a business might have.
context: FBM is a boat building business with 100 skilled employees.
ms: 1 mark per fixed cost (max 4). Only award first four responses. Fixed costs: Rent/rates/storage costs; Insurance; Advertising; Salaries; Interest (on loans)/finance payments; Cleaning/maintenance. Do not award: wages/direct labour costs or power. Allow heating/lighting/electricity/water/utilities once.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to FBM of holding a high level of inventory.
context: FBM is a boat building business with 100 skilled employees. Variable costs per unit $5000, Fixed costs per year $600,000, Number of boats made each year 300. The Operations Director is concerned that FBM holds a high level of inventory.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantages: Maintain production so able to meet orders on time of boats; Benefit from (purchasing) economies of scale leading to lower average/unit cost; Able to respond quickly to unexpected order, increasing customer loyalty. Disadvantages: Space needed to store products, increasing (storage) costs so costs increase above $600,000; Cash/money tied up in inventory, leading to cash flow/liquidity problems; Risk of damage/waste; Opportunity cost; Insurance. Application words: boat (building) or related words, 100 employees, skilled (workers), diseconomies of scale, $5000 (variable cost), $600,000 (fixed costs), 300 (boats), total cost $2,100,000.

text: Do you think customers have a more important role in the success of a business than its employees? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Customers: Buy the products, and if the business ignores their needs it will lose revenue/won't survive; Can share opinions to help improve products, which can help increase market share; Provide recommendations/word of mouth advertising. Employees: Make the products, otherwise there is nothing to sell; Employees can affect quality, which could damage/improve its reputation; Employees provide customer service, which is important for brand image; Without sufficient employees the business may not be able to meet demand; Workers can be replaced by machines. Justification usually follows from relevant analysis — e.g. customers are more important as without revenue the business cannot cover its costs and survive in the long term, whereas a business can use automation reducing the importance of employees.

text: Define 'span of control'.
context: ADN is a food retailer with 5 shops and 300 full-time employees, a tall hierarchical structure. Managers have a narrow span of control.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): (Number of) subordinates working directly under a manager. OR (Number of) subordinates reporting to each supervisor/manager. OR (Number of) subordinates someone has within their authority/under their control. Partial (1 mark): (Number of) staff that a manager is responsible for, OR subordinates who work under a manager.

text: Define 'autocratic leadership style'.
context: ADN's managers all use an autocratic leadership style.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Leader/manager makes all the decisions. OR Where the manager expects to be in charge of the business and to have their orders followed. Partial (1 mark): Employees are simply told what to do, OR employees have no say in decisions. For two marks candidates need to show awareness that decision making is by a leader or manager, not a director or person in the company.

text: Outline two benefits to ADN of having full-time employees.
context: ADN is a food retailer with 5 shops and 300 full-time employees, tall hierarchical structure, narrow span of control, autocratic leadership style. ADN's directors are planning to expand.
ms: 1 mark per benefit + 1 mark application (max 2 benefits = 4 marks). Benefits: Consistent service at the 5 shops; Workers likely to be loyal/less likely to leave the food retailer; Easy to communicate with/update the 300 employees; Need to recruit/train fewer employees. Application words: food or related words, 5 (locations), shops/retailer, 300 employees, tall hierarchical organisational structure, narrow span of control, autocratic leadership style, planning to expand/internal growth/external growth.

text: Explain one benefit and one limitation to ADN of using off-the-job training.
context: ADN is a food retailer with 5 shops and 300 full-time employees. All ADN's employees receive off-the-job training.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per benefit AND limitation (max 6 marks). Benefits: Learn the latest/new methods for use in the 5 shops so business can remain competitive; Broad range of skills can be taught to the full-time employees so they can become more efficient; Can learn from experts/specialists which may be helpful as trying to expand; Can focus 100% on training therefore make fewer mistakes; Mistakes when learning don't affect the business, which can protect the reputation of the food retailer; Workers do not learn bad habits so mistakes are avoided; It does not disrupt work of other employees; Increased motivation of employees. Limitations: High cost/expensive as have 300 employees, which increases expenses; Loss of working time, leading to less work done/fewer sales; Not necessarily tailored to individual business; Additional qualifications mean it is easier for the employee to leave/find another job, increasing time/cost of recruitment. Application words: food or related words, 5 (locations), shops/retailer, 300 employees, full-time, narrow span of control, autocratic leadership style, planning to expand/internal growth/external growth.

text: Do you think it is better for a business to use internal growth or external growth when planning to expand? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. ADN's directors are planning to expand and cannot decide whether it is better to use internal growth or external growth.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Internal growth: Easier to control/manage growth, which can help avoid diseconomies of scale; Lower investment may be needed, so less need to borrow (as much); Slow method, so business may become uncompetitive/may miss business opportunities; Less risk. External growth: Quick method, so able to take advantage of new market opportunities which can increase revenue; Removing a competitor increases market share/power, may be able to set/influence prices; Large amounts of finance may be required, which increases finance costs. Advantages of one method can be presented as disadvantages of the other but do not award the same point twice. Justification usually follows from relevant analysis — e.g. external growth is better as by taking over a competitor market share can be increased, increasing market power.

text: Define 'mass market'.
context: IDT manufactures clothes for the mass market, a multinational company with factories in 4 countries.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Where there are a large number of sales of a product. OR A large market containing lots of customers buying similar products. Partial (1 mark): Lots of sales/customers, OR lots of buyers, OR market for goods that are produced in large quantities. For two marks candidates must have the idea of a 'large number of sales' AND it is for 'one product'.

text: Calculate IDT's working capital in 2023.
context: IDT's statement of financial position: 2023 — Current assets $420m, Current liabilities $280m, Non-current liabilities $400m.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): $140 million. Method: Current assets − current liabilities = 420 − 280 (1 mark). If correct answer given with no working shown, award 2 marks. Award only 1 mark if $140 million written as part of the answer but not given as final answer. Award max 1 where candidate calculates working capital for 2022 using the correct method i.e. $130 million. For 2 marks the answer must have the right units i.e. million/m in answer.

text: Outline one reason why IDT might need the following types of finance: Short-term finance AND Long-term finance.
context: IDT manufactures clothes for the mass market, a multinational company with factories in 4 countries. IDT has short-term and long-term financial needs.
ms: 1 mark reason + 1 mark application per type (max 2 marks each = 4 marks). Short-term finance: To pay day-to-day costs/working capital when making clothes; Improve cash flow position/liquidity of the multinational company; Meet any unexpected emergencies/opportunities. Long-term finance: Fund expansion/growth such as the new factory; Purchase non-current assets in one of the 4 countries; Develop new products. Application words: multinational company, clothes or related words such as shirts/trousers, manufacturer, mass market, factory, 4 countries, $140 million (working capital), $280 million (current liabilities), $400 million (non-current liabilities).

text: Explain two ways an increase in non-current liabilities might affect IDT.
context: IDT manufactures clothes for the mass market, a multinational company with factories in 4 countries. Non-current liabilities: $300m (2022), $400m (2023). Current liabilities $280m, Current assets $420m.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 ways = 6 marks). Ways: Must pay interest on the $400m, which increases expenses/cash outflows; Difficult to raise additional finance/more collateral required, as lenders may worry whether the business will be able to repay despite being a multinational company; More difficult to repay loans/more debt to pay back, increases financial risk for this clothing retailer. Application words: multinational company, clothes or related words such as shirts/trousers, manufacturer, mass market, factory, 4 different countries, working capital/$140 million, $400 million (non-current liabilities), $280 million (current liabilities), $420 million (current assets).

text: Explain two advantages to a business of being a multinational company. Which advantage do you think is likely to be the most important? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Advantages: Increase sales/new customers/access new markets, increasing revenue; Improve brand image/reputation to help increase/maintain customer loyalty; Spreading risk as not reliant on one market for all its sales, fall in sales in one country can be offset by increase in another; Economies of scale, leading to lower average/unit costs; Easier access to/cheaper raw materials, reducing transport costs; Lower cost of labour (in some countries), improving profit margin; Avoid import quotas/tariffs; Lower/favourable tax rates/government grants/subsidies. Justification must compare two advantages — e.g. access to raw materials is more important because lower costs may lead to lower prices helping the business be more competitive and improve their market share.

text: Define 'social enterprise'.
context: CFG is a social enterprise. It buys cocoa beans from local farmers and then uses the beans to make chocolate. Being ethical is important to the business.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): An organisation that has social objectives as well as an aim to make a profit to reinvest back into the business. OR A business with social objectives that reinvests most of its profits back into the business/into benefiting society at large. OR A business that seeks to raise income, which it invests in a specific social or environmental issue. OR A business set up to help society/a community rather than make a profit. Partial (1 mark): A business that aims to help/benefit society.

text: Identify two ways legal controls over marketing might affect a business.
context: The Marketing Manager knows there are many legal controls over marketing that might affect a business.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 2). Only award first two responses. Ways: No misleading promotion/advertising; No price fixing/charging very high prices where there is little or no competition; No selling faulty/dangerous goods/certain ingredients; Ensure products are fit for purpose; Price reductions must be genuine; Increased costs to meet the legal controls/pay fines; Spend longer time ensuring they meet the legal controls; May need to alter packaging; Restrictions on advertising certain products to some age groups/places.

text: Outline one advantage and one disadvantage to CFG of using skimming as its pricing method.
context: CFG is a social enterprise buying cocoa beans from local farmers to make chocolate. CFG has developed a new chocolate bar. The Marketing Manager plans to use skimming as its pricing method.
ms: 1 mark advantage/disadvantage + 1 mark application (max 2 each = 4 marks). Advantages: Helps establish a high-quality image/customers may think it is a good quality, which may also help as want to be ethical; Can quickly recover research/development costs, which is important as developed a new product; Higher revenue per item for its chocolate; May have a lower break-even output. Disadvantages: High price might discourage (potential) customers for this social enterprise; High prices/profitability could encourage competitors to enter market, so may not be able to support local farmers. Application words: social enterprise, cocoa beans, local farmers, chocolate (bar), retailers, ethical, (developed) a new product, legal controls over marketing.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to CFG of using retailers as its distribution channel for the new product.
context: CFG is a social enterprise, uses retailers as its distribution channel for its new chocolate bar. Being ethical is important, buying cocoa beans from local farmers.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantages: Producers can sell in large quantities to retailers, increasing revenue from its new product; Reduced costs (compared to selling direct to consumers), increasing profit margin in this social enterprise; Retailer shares the cost of holding inventory, lowering expenses; Retailers will promote the product, reducing the cost of promotion/increasing sales; Access wider range of customers. Disadvantages: No direct contact with consumer about its chocolate bar, so may not adapt to changing needs; Final price (paid by consumer) is often high, so may be uncompetitive; Retailer takes some of profit away from the producer; Producer loses some control of marketing mix; Retailers usually sell competitors' products as well. Application words: social enterprise, cocoa beans, (make) bars of chocolate, ethical, (local) farmers, legal controls over marketing.

text: Do you think being ethical will always lead to lower profit for a business? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Being ethical is important to CFG, a social enterprise.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: Limited/fewer sources of materials leading to less output; Higher cost of materials leading to higher variable costs/cost of goods, which lowers gross profit margin; Workers may have to be paid more/fair pay, increasing labour costs; May take time to source ethical supplies, which could delay production; Good image/reputation, so can charge higher prices/lead to customer loyalty; Higher demand/increase sales/enter new market/more customers, which could increase revenue; Help recruit/motivate/retain workers, leading to lower absenteeism/increased productivity; Investors more likely to invest; Can help create better supplier relations (by paying a fair price); Less opposition from pressure groups. Justification: being ethical will not always mean lower profit because a better reputation is likely to attract more customers, and the extra revenue gained could cover the costs, increasing profit overall. Do not credit answers which relate to the costs of being unethical.

text: Define 'added value'.
context: TCH is a small bakery producing pastries and cakes, operating in the secondary sector. The added value of TCH's products has increased since it opened 3 years ago.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): The difference between the selling price of a product and the cost of bought-in materials and components. Partial (1 mark): Improvement to the product/that makes it worth more. For two marks needs reference to the difference between both cost and selling price/what the product is sold for.

text: Define 'secondary sector'.
context: TCH is a small bakery producing pastries and cakes, operating in the secondary sector.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Manufactures goods using raw materials (provided by the primary sector). OR Uses manufacturing to transform the raw materials generated in the primary sector into a product. OR Firms that process/manufacture goods from natural resources. Partial (1 mark): Make a product. For two marks need idea of manufacture/produce AND from what/where the products are made from (primary sector/raw materials). Do not award examples.

text: Outline two reasons why TCH's business objectives might have changed.
context: TCH is a small bakery, opened 3 years ago, secondary sector, 6 employees. TCH's business objectives have changed since it started up; one new objective is to expand.
ms: 1 mark per reason + 1 mark application (max 2 reasons = 4 marks). Reasons: Previous objectives have been achieved/previous objectives were unrealistic at the bakery; Change of owners/managers over the last 3 years; Changes in the government objectives/legal controls affecting secondary sector businesses; Change in customer preferences/demand/follow new trends, so may need more/less than 6 employees; Change in competition, which may be why want the business to expand. Application words: bakery, pastries/cakes, small (business), 3 years, secondary sector, 6 employees, expand/expansion.

text: Explain two non-financial methods of motivation TCH could use.
context: TCH is a small bakery producing pastries and cakes, 3 years old, secondary sector, 6 employees. TCH uses non-financial methods to motivate its employees.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 methods = 6 marks). Methods: Job rotation — increases the variety of the work/reduces boredom of workers at the bakery; Job enrichment — for the 6 employees, as they are being given more responsibility/can use their full range of abilities; Training — so employees have a higher level of skills when making pastries/cakes; Delegation — allows employees to make decisions/workers feel empowered, so TCH's manager(s) can focus on expansion; Praise — no cost/free for this small business; Teamworking — can increase sense of belonging/loyalty, so less need to use external recruitment; Opportunities for promotion — given a role higher up in the hierarchy; Recognition/Employee of the month. Application words: bakery, pastries/cakes, small (business), 3 years, secondary sector, 6 employees, expand/expansion, external recruitment, business objectives. Analysis can focus on explaining what the method is or how it can increase motivation.

text: Explain two methods of external recruitment a business could use. Which is likely to be the best method to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Many businesses use external recruitment when they expand.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Methods: Specialist magazines — can target potential employees interested in this industry/type of work; Online recruitment sites/social media/website — can reach large numbers of people/include detailed information, but not everyone has access to the internet; Recruitment agencies — saves administration time, but agencies charge a fee for their services; (Government-run) job centres — no cost to the business, but only reach those actively looking for a job; Local newspapers — which people could ignore; National newspapers — but must pay to advertise, which increases costs. Justification must compare two methods — e.g. an online recruitment site is the best method because having access to a wider pool of people can make it easier to find the right person for the role, which may reduce the need to readvertise in future. Do not award methods of selection e.g. interviews.

text: Identify two characteristics of a recession.
context: PLY manufactures hats in its factory in country X. The economy of country X is in a recession.
ms: 1 mark per characteristic (max 2). Only award first two responses. Characteristics: Rising unemployment; GDP falls/negative; Low levels of consumer spending/falling consumer confidence/fewer sales; Falling prices; Low/falling inflation; Low(er) business profit; Low(er) tax revenue for government; Low(er) levels of business output; Businesses fail/close; Low(er) levels of business investment; Low(er) business confidence; Low(er) interest rates.

text: Define 'pressure group'.
context: PLY's Managing Director is aware of the role of pressure groups.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Pressure groups are groups of people who act together to try to force businesses or governments to adopt certain policies. OR People who have a common interest who take action to change/influence business/government decisions. Partial (1 mark): People who try to influence business activities, OR group formed by people with a common interest, OR people who take action against a business. For two marks needs idea of a group with a common/same interest AND idea of influence on business/government decisions. Do not award examples e.g. boycott/protest.

text: Outline two ways PLY could be affected by legal controls over business activity affecting the environment.
context: PLY manufactures hats in its factory in country X, sells online to the mass market. The economy is in a recession. The Managing Director is considering ways for PLY to become more environmentally friendly, aware of new legal controls over business activity.
ms: 1 mark per way + 1 mark application (max 2 ways = 4 marks). Ways: May have to use renewable sources of energy/change their energy sources in its factory; May have to change materials used/find new supplier, which could be difficult to do in a recession; May have to relocate to produce hats; May have to reduce waste/find alternative ways to dispose of waste, leading to fewer issues with pressure groups; May have to change what they make/redesign products to ones that are environmentally friendly; May have to pay tax/obtain licence to pollute/pay fines, which could affect its cash-flow forecast; May have to lower/limit output; May have to change production method/buy new machinery (that pollutes less); May have to change the packaging; Require more training/retraining. Application words: hats, pressure groups, factory, recession, environmentally friendly, mass market. Do not award advantages/disadvantages of being environmentally friendly or examples of environmental damage.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of PLY using email to communicate with its customers.
context: PLY manufactures hats, sells online to the mass market in a recession economy. PLY uses email to communicate with its customers.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantages: Can be sent to many people at once/in different countries, which can save time/allow the business to focus on other activities such as becoming environmentally friendly; Low cost, which lowers expenses during the recession; Can be saved for future reference/refer to message, which can help avoid disagreements/deal with complaints; Can be read at a time that suits the customer; Can add attachments/images to the message. Disadvantages: May be language barriers/complex language used, so customer may not understand message about the hats; Not all customers may have an email address/no access to technology/server issues/may go into junk folder, so customer is not able to read/check it; Can be sent to wrong person/people, which may reduce sales/revenue; Too many emails received, so may be difficult to pick out the relevant information; Cannot see body language; No immediate feedback. Application words: hats, mass market, recession, environmentally friendly, market research, sell online.

text: Explain two reasons why a business uses market research. Which reason is likely to be the most important? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. PLY uses market research when making decisions.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Reasons: Identify customer needs/wants/demand/target market, to ensure sales/revenue/so know where to sell/can produce products that meet customer needs/what amount to produce; Find out about competition/competitors' products, to help gain competitive advantage/decide prices/improve products; Help predict changes in trends, so can spot possible gaps in the market; Help predict current/future size of market, to help make decisions/help inform the marketing mix; Help decide what/amount to produce/buy right amount of materials, to keep variable costs low/reduce wastage; To decide price/what price to set, so able to cover costs; Help decide where to locate/operate from/know where to sell; Help decide how to promote/promotion strategy for its products. Justification must compare two reasons — e.g. identifying customer needs is more important as if a business develops a product that customers don't want, it is unlikely to generate any revenue, whatever the price set.

text: Identify one cash inflow and one cash outflow for a business.
context: FR's Financial Director is constructing a cash-flow forecast for the new hotel's first year of trading.
ms: 1 mark cash inflow + 1 mark cash outflow (max 1 each). Cash inflows: Cash sales; Money/payment from trade receivables; Sale of non-current assets/sell unwanted machinery/land; Cash received from loan/grants; Cash/funds from investors/shareholders. Cash outflows: Money/payments to trade payables/purchase goods or materials/pay suppliers; Pay wages/salaries; Pay expenses or examples such as rent; Purchase non-current assets/purchase machinery/land; Repay loans/debts; Pay dividends; Cash purchases. Only award the first response given for each.

text: Identify two factors which might affect the source of finance a business chooses to use.
context: FR's Financial Director is considering which source of finance to use to fund the expansion of the new hotel.
ms: 1 mark per factor (max 2). Only award first two responses. Factors: Size/legal form of business; Amount required; Length of time required for/whether short-term or long-term; Level of existing loans/debts/borrowing; Purpose/reason for finance; Interest/cost of finance; How quickly/urgently need money; Credit history; Security/collateral. Do not award examples of sources of finance.

text: Identify four ways a market can be segmented.
context: FR is a multinational company with hotels in 18 countries, planning to expand into a new market. FR's Marketing Director is considering how the market can be segmented.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 4). Only award first four responses. Ways: Age; Socio-economic grouping; Gender; Income; Ethnic background; Family size; Lifestyle/interests; Personality; Attitudes; By use of product; Location/region.

text: Explain two advantages to FR of being a multinational company.
context: FR is a multinational company with hotels in 18 countries, wants to expand into a new market and is planning to build another hotel.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 advantages = 6 marks). Advantages: Access to cheaper labour, which could increase profit margin/lower total costs for the hotel; Access to bigger/new markets, which can increase sales/revenue/increase market share in the 18 countries; Spreads risk when expanding, as sales falling in one country may be offset by rising sales in another country; Access to government grants, which could increase cash inflows and improve its cash-flow forecast; Better image/reputation, which could allow them to set higher prices/attract more customers; Take advantage of lower tax rates. Application words: hotel or related words e.g. rooms/chefs, 18 countries, expand, cash-flow forecast, new markets. Do not award access/cheaper raw materials/lower production costs as this is a tertiary sector business.

text: Explain two ways a cash-flow forecast could be used by a business. Which is likely to be the most important way? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. FR's Financial Director is constructing a cash-flow forecast for the new hotel's first year of trading.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Uses: Support loan applications/attract investors, to show if the business has sufficient cash to repay a loan; To know how much cash is available for paying bills/wages, so they can arrange an overdraft if necessary; To identify if there will be a cash-flow problem/identify shortfalls, so they can cut back on spending/take corrective action; To show if the business is likely to run short of cash, avoid having a lack of liquidity; To manage the cash flows in and out of the business, so will be aware of how much cash is available when operating; To help plan/make decisions, so waste fewer resources. Justification must compare two uses — e.g. identifying possible cash flow problems is most important as if there isn't enough cash to cover day-to-day expenses then the business may not be able to operate, whereas it may still be able to operate if it did not get a loan.

text: Define 'break-even output'.
context: Suliman owns a small business selling t-shirts on its website, operating as a sole trader. Break-even output 500 t-shirts, Current sales 550 t-shirts, Selling price per t-shirt $3.99, Variable cost per t-shirt $1.99.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): The quantity that must be produced/sold for total revenue to equal total cost. OR Where total revenue equals total cost. Partial (1 mark): The business is making neither a profit or a loss, OR where revenue equals cost.

text: Calculate the margin of safety. Show your working.
context: Suliman's data: Break-even output 500 t-shirts, Current sales 550 t-shirts.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): 50 units. Method: Current sales − break-even output = 550 − 500 (1 mark). If correct answer given and no workings shown, award 2 marks. Award a maximum of one mark if 50 units is calculated but it is not written as the final answer.

text: Outline two methods of sales promotion Suliman could use for the new shop.
context: Suliman owns a small business selling t-shirts on its website, operating as a sole trader. He wants to open his first shop. Break-even output 500 t-shirts, Current sales 550, Selling price $3.99, Variable cost $1.99.
ms: 1 mark per method + 1 mark application (max 2 methods = 4 marks). Methods: Point of sale displays by the sole trader; Price reductions/discounts/coupons below $3.99; Buy one get one free (BOGOF) for the t-shirts; Gifts/gift cards, which may help increase sales above 550; Loyalty reward schemes/cards; Competitions; Free samples. Application words: t-shirts, sole trader, small (business), $3.99 (selling price), 550 (units/current level of sales), margin of safety/50, $2194.50 (revenue).

text: Explain two factors Suliman should consider when deciding on a suitable location for the new shop.
context: Suliman owns a small business selling t-shirts on its website, operating as a sole trader, wants to open his first shop and needs to decide on a suitable location. Break-even output 500 t-shirts, Current sales 550, Selling price $3.99, Variable cost $1.99.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 factors = 6 marks). Factors: Number of customers/demand/sales, which could increase potential revenue from t-shirts; Competition, as many competitors may mean high footfall/less competition could mean higher market share for this sole trader; Rent/taxes/cost of site, which the business could not afford/could increase costs for this small business; Availability of labour, as if there is a low supply of labour then wage demands may be higher/if no suitable employees could be unable to operate; Space/size, as may need a large space to display products; Parking available, otherwise may miss out on customers/sales; Distance/access to supplier, to reduce transport costs; Access government support/grants, which could lower costs; Legal controls; Infrastructure/access to electricity/water; Security/safety/level of crime. Application words: t-shirts, sole trader, small (business), $3.99 (selling price), $1.99 (variable cost), 550/500 units, margin of safety/50, $2194.50 (revenue).

text: Do you think operating as a sole trader is the best type of organisation for a small business? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Suliman operates his small business as a sole trader.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: Own boss/complete control, so may lead to quicker decision-making; Keep all profits, increase motivation of owner; Do not have to publish financial information, so competitors cannot access this information; Has freedom to choose own holidays/work hours; Unlimited liability, so the owner's personal possessions are at risk (if the business cannot pay its debts); Limited sources of finance, so may be difficult to expand; No-one to cover if owner is ill, so business may lose sales. Alternative forms of ownership: Partnership — can share workload; Private limited company — to benefit from limited liability. Justification: a sole trader is best for a small business because quicker decision-making could allow them to respond more quickly to opportunities, which could help increase sales and may reduce the chances of the business not being able to pay its debts. Advantages of one type can be disadvantages of another, but do not award twice as mirror arguments are not accepted. Do not award public limited company or limited company as alternatives.

text: Identify two benefits to a business of specialisation.
context: DBR is a mining business, a large public limited company operating in the primary sector, with 8 diamond mines and 3000 employees. Specialisation is important.
ms: 1 mark per benefit (max 2). Only award first two responses. Benefits: Increases output; Quicker production/increases productivity/higher efficiency; Lower unit cost/economies of scale; Workers become expert/more skilled/employees focus on what they are good at; Improves accuracy/better quality/fewer mistakes/reduces waste; Helps improve competitiveness.

text: Identify two ways a business can grow.
context: DBR has grown quickly over the past 5 years, a large public limited company in the primary sector.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 2). Only award first two responses. Ways: Takeover; Merger; Develop new products; Enter new markets; Increasing sales (of existing products)/open more locations; Franchising.

text: Outline one possible advantage and one possible disadvantage of DBR being a public limited company.
context: DBR is a large public limited company operating in the primary sector, 8 diamond mines, 3000 employees. In 2022 DBR's profit was $600 million.
ms: 1 mark advantage/disadvantage + 1 mark application (max 2 each = 4 marks). Advantages: Can raise large amounts of finance so can continue to grow; Can sell shares to general public/no restrictions on buying, transferring/selling shares of this mining business; May be able to borrow at low rates of interest; High status/seen as more creditworthy to suppliers; Limited liability (for shareholders); Incorporated business/separate legal identity; Continuity. Disadvantages: Many regulations/has to publish its accounts so everyone knows its profit was $600 million; High cost/lengthy process to sell shares; Risk of takeover/original owners may lose control (if too many shares are issued). Application words: mining business/mine, diamonds, 8 (mines), grown quickly/continue to grow, $600 million (profit), large (business).

text: Explain two diseconomies of scale DBR might experience.
context: DBR is a large public limited company in the primary sector, 8 diamond mines, 3000 employees, $600 million profit in 2022. The Managing Director is worried about possible diseconomies of scale.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 diseconomies = 6 marks). Diseconomies: Low motivation/lack of commitment for its 3000 employees leading to higher labour turnover/more workers leaving; Poor communication between the mines leading to mistakes being made/inefficiency; Weak/lack of co-ordination leading to the wrong decisions reducing the profit of $600 million; Lack of control leading to higher average costs. Application words: mining business/mine, diamonds, 8 (mines), 3000 (employees), grown quickly/continue to grow, $600 million, specialisation, public limited company, large (business).

text: Explain two ways the size of a primary sector business can be measured. Which do you think is the best way? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. DBR operates in the primary sector.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Ways: Number of employees — simple/easy to calculate, but may use a lot of machinery/capital intensive, may have many part-time employees so business may look larger than it is/difficult to compare; Value of sales — easy/quick to access data, but some businesses may sell seasonal products, if sell high value items may not reflect size; Value of output — can be easy to compare across similar businesses, but if sell high value items may not reflect size; Value of capital employed — may have a lot of expensive machinery/capital which makes business look bigger than it is. Justification must compare two ways — e.g. value of output is likely a better way because many primary sector businesses may use a lot of machinery which means fewer employees, so any comparison of employees is likely to be misleading.

text: Define 'current liabilities'.
context: NPZ is a pizza restaurant with 35 part-time employees. Extract from NPZ's financial statements 2022: Revenue $600,000, Gross profit $240,000, Profit for the year $60,000, Current liabilities $75,000, Capital employed $300,000.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Short-term debts owed by a business, repaid in less than one year. OR Debts of a business which it expects to pay before the date of the next statement of financial position. Partial (1 mark): Money owed by a business.

text: Calculate NPZ's return on capital employed (ROCE). Show your working.
context: NPZ's financial statements 2022: Profit for the year $60,000, Capital employed $300,000.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): 20%. Method: Profit ÷ capital employed × 100 = 60,000/300,000 × 100 (1 mark). If correct answer given with no working shown, award 2 marks. Award max 1 mark if 20% written as part of the answer but not given as final answer. Answer must be shown as a percentage (%) to gain both marks.

text: Outline two possible benefits to NPZ of having well-motivated employees.
context: NPZ is a pizza restaurant with 35 part-time employees. The owner, Trent, thinks having well-motivated employees is important.
ms: 1 mark per benefit + 1 mark application (max 2 benefits = 4 marks). Benefits: Increased productivity/efficiency of the 35 employees; Increase output of pizzas; Reduced absenteeism among the part-time employees; Lower labour turnover so business can focus on ways to increase profit; Willing to accept changes/new methods of working in the restaurant; Improves quality. Application words: restaurant or related words, pizza or related words such as food, 35 employees, part-time, ways to increase profit, $600,000 (revenue), $240,000 (gross profit), $60,000 (profit), $300,000 (capital employed), 20% (ROCE).

text: Explain two methods NPZ could use to improve employee motivation.
context: NPZ is a pizza restaurant with 35 part-time employees. Trent is interested in different methods to improve motivation.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 methods = 6 marks). Methods: Increased wages/salary/rate of pay as the revenue is $600,000, so workers are better able to meet their basic needs; Praise to meet esteem needs of the 35 employees; Offer training so employees feel more valued/important to the restaurant; Employee of the month/recognition so workers feel their hard work is acknowledged; Job enrichment as gives employees tasks which require more skills/responsibilities; Introduce job rotation so employees are not bored doing the same thing/work is more varied; Bonus so workers have an incentive to work harder to get bonus; Profit-sharing so employees have an interest in the success of the business; Offer fringe benefits (or examples — discounts on products); Team working would provide support/sense of belonging; Opportunity for promotion which could lead to higher pay. Application words: restaurant or related words, pizza or related words such as food, 35 employees, part-time, ways to increase profit, $600,000 (revenue), $240,000 (gross profit), $60,000 (profit), $300,000 (capital employed), 20% (ROCE).

text: Do you think reducing variable costs is the best way for a business to improve profit? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Trent is considering ways to increase NPZ's profit.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Reducing variable costs: No need to increase prices, as this could result in fewer sales; Would reduce break-even output; Increase (gross) profit margin; Cheaper materials may lower quality, damaging reputation. Other ways: Increasing prices — may increase revenue, may improve brand image, but lead to lower customers/could make them less competitive; Increase number of sales/quantities sold — may increase costs of advertising, competitors may respond with own promotion; Lowering fixed costs (or examples such as lower rent) — reduces break-even output, but unlikely to be able to change fixed costs quickly. Justification must compare two ways — e.g. increasing the quantity sold is a better method because the reputation of the business is protected so existing customers should remain loyal, and the additional revenue should hopefully cover the extra cost.

text: Define 'brand image'.
context: BKS is a manufacturer which makes a range of food products. Having a good brand image is important.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Identity/logo/unique name of a product that distinguishes it from other brands. OR The general impression/perception/reputation of a product held by consumers. Partial (1 mark): Identity given to a product, OR something that distinguishes a product from its competitors, OR how the product is seen/perceived by others/public.

text: Identify one benefit and one limitation for a business of developing new products.
context: BKS is always developing new products, having a good brand image.
ms: 1 mark per benefit/limitation (max 1 each). Benefits: Increase sales/revenue/customers; Spread risk/diversification; Enter new markets; Help expand into existing markets/increase market share; Improve competitive advantage/USP; Improve brand image/better reputation; Maintain customer loyalty. Limitations: Cost of market research; Cost of research and development (R&D); Cost of producing/testing trial products; Cost of new machinery; May need to recruit/cost of additional employees/specialists; Cost of launching/promoting/advertising new product in market.

text: Outline two possible reasons why BKS might respond to environmental pressures.
context: BKS is a manufacturer of food products, most sold directly to large retailers, always developing new products, good brand image important.
ms: 1 mark per reason + 1 mark application (max 2 reasons = 4 marks). Reasons: Avoid pressure group action/boycotts which may damage brand image; Protect reputation/brand image of its food; Respond to changing customer demands by developing new products; Attract/maintain sales to (large) retailers; Differentiate from competitors. Application words: brand image, food, developing new products, (sell to) retailers, product life cycle.

text: Explain how BKS's marketing decisions about promotion might be affected if a product is in the following stages of the product life cycle: Introduction stage AND Maturity stage.
context: BKS's Marketing Manager knows the stage of the product life cycle will influence marketing decisions about promotion, food products.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per stage (max 6 marks). Introduction stage: High level of promotion (spending) to attract/inform customers about the new foods; (Advertise) to persuade/attract/inform customers about its new products to gain sales. Maturity stage: Low/less promotion (spending) as product is well-known/want to spend budget on other things such as responding to environmental pressures; May be used to remind customers so keep buying its products/remain loyal/have constant sales. Application words: brand image, food, (developing) new products, (sell to large) retailers, environmental pressures. Do not award examples of advertising/promotion.

text: Do you think selling direct to retailers is the best channel of distribution for a manufacturer to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Most of BKS's products are sold directly to large retailers.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Retailers: Can sell in large quantities/wide distribution/access to more customers leading to higher potential revenue; Retailers can help promote/advertise products which raises awareness/increase sales; Can hold less inventory lowering storage costs; No direct contact with customers so may lack up-to-date information/difficult to build customer relationships; Retailers take some of the profit, lowers profit margin. Wholesalers: bulk buy, save storage space, but price may be higher as wholesaler adds mark-up leading to fewer sales. Sell direct to customers: can sell at lower price leading to more sales, higher profit/no need to pay middleman, but may need extra employees to manage orders which increases costs. Agent: has local market knowledge. Do not award benefits to customers. Justification must compare two channels — e.g. selling to retailers is better as the high sales will increase total revenue, which will offset the lower profit margin.

text: Define 'import quota'.
context: FXN manufactures mobile phones, a multinational company, plans to build a new factory in country Y due to the government's decision to introduce import quotas.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Physical limit on the number/amount of goods that can be imported/allowed into a country. OR Restriction on the quantity of a product that can be imported. Partial (1 mark): Limit on number of goods, OR limit on imports. Do not award answers which confuse the term with a tariff.

text: Identify two advantages to a country of having lower levels of unemployment.
context: The Managing Director said the new factory will create 1200 jobs and help lower the level of unemployment in country Y.
ms: 1 mark per advantage (max 2). Only award first two responses. Advantages: Increase in incomes/higher standard of living; Lower payments for benefits/less government spending; Increased tax receipts; Economic growth/higher GDP/increased demand/sales.

text: Identify four possible drawbacks for a country of having a multinational company located there.
context: FXN manufactures mobile phones, a multinational company, planning to build a new factory in country Y creating 1200 jobs.
ms: 1 mark per drawback (max 4). Only award first four responses. Drawbacks: (Increased) competition; May offer low wages/poor working conditions/may only create unskilled jobs/exploitation of labour; Use up scarce resources; Environmental issues/damage/pollution; Repatriation/send profits back to home country; Often try to avoid/reduce amount of tax paid; Power to influence government decisions/local economy.

text: Explain two factors FXN should consider when deciding on a suitable location for the new factory.
context: FXN manufactures mobile phones, a multinational company, planning to build a new factory in country Y creating 1200 jobs. Will start the recruitment process once a location is decided.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 factors = 6 marks). Factors: Rent, increasing fixed costs when making phones; Available/amount of space, as likely to need a large area; Availability/access to employees, as 1200 jobs to make sure quality/efficiency is maintained; Availability of/distance to raw materials/suppliers, to avoid import quotas which could increase transport costs; Access to water/power/utilities, so production does not stop; Government influence/legal controls/access to grants, which would reduce costs for this multinational company; Environmental impact, which could damage brand image; Transport/communication links. Application words: multinational company, 1200 jobs, (mobile) phones, lower level of unemployment, recruitment process, import quotas. Do not award factory as application as stated in question.

text: Do you think a recruitment website, which advertises jobs, is the best method for a business to use when recruiting a large number of employees? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. FXN will start the recruitment process once a decision has been made about a suitable location.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Recruitment website: as many/most people use the internet to look for jobs, so able to attract a wider pool of candidates; some people do not have access to the internet; advert could easily be missed (as many different websites). Newspapers: seen by many people/wide exposure, but most people do not read newspapers, only shown for limited time, must pay to advertise which increases expenses. Recruitment agency: have expert knowledge/only send suitable people, saving time on interviewing, but charge a high fee which increases expenses. Justification must compare two methods — e.g. a recruitment agency is better when recruiting a large number of employees because it can use its knowledge to only send suitable candidates, so the business does not waste time interviewing a large number of unsuitable people.

text: Define 'working capital'.
context: Paolo wants to start up a business making cakes, plans to sell all his products to a wholesaler. Average price per cake $6, Average cost per cake $4, Forecast average number of cake sales per day 50.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Finance needed by a business to pay day-to-day costs. OR The capital needed to finance the day-to-day running costs/expenses. OR Current assets less/minus current liabilities. Partial (1 mark): Funds to buy inventory/materials/pay wages, OR finance to pay short-term debts. 1st mark for idea of finance/funds/money/capital to pay costs; 2nd mark for reference to day-to-day/daily costs.

text: Calculate the average revenue per day. Show your working.
context: Paolo's data: Average price per cake $6, Forecast average number of cake sales per day 50.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): $300. Method: Price × number of units sold = $6 × 50 (1 mark). Award only 1 mark if $300 is written as part of the answer but not shown as final answer. $ sign not required.

text: Outline two reasons why packaging will be important for Paolo's business.
context: Paolo wants to start up a business making cakes, sells to a wholesaler. Average price $6, average cost $4, 50 sales/day. Considering crowdfunding, needs working capital.
ms: 1 mark per reason + 1 mark application (max 2 reasons = 4 marks). Reasons: Protect the product/keep product safe/helps ensure quality, especially as selling cakes; Promote brand image/differentiate it from other products for this new business; Add value/higher price than $6; Help advertise/attract customers/increase sales; Ease of storage/display at the wholesaler; Ease of transport for the 50 products; Provide information/meet legal requirements; Make the product easy/convenient to open. Application words: cakes or related words such as ingredients, 50 (units per day), start-up/new business, $6 (price), wholesaler, $300 (revenue, OFR can apply), $4 (cost per cake).

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to Paolo's business of using crowdfunding as a source of finance.
context: Paolo is starting up a business making cakes, considering crowdfunding as a source of finance, needs working capital, sells to a wholesaler.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantages: No/low interest so does not increase cash outflows for his start-up; Allows for the public reaction to be tested for the cakes, which could lead to more customers; No need to repay/permanent, so does not add to its liabilities/debt; No collateral needed. Disadvantages: No guarantee can raise full amount/may not raise enough/sufficient funds/must repay everyone if cannot raise full amount, so must find another source; Competitors may learn more about your business before launch such as ideas for packaging, leading to less revenue; Not a reliable/stable source of finance; A lot of paperwork. Application words: cake or related words such as ingredients, start-up/new business, packaging, $300 (revenue, OFR can apply), $6 (price), 50 (units per day), $4 (unit cost), working capital, wholesaler.

text: Do you think selling to a wholesaler is the best channel of distribution for a start-up business to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Paolo plans to sell all of his products to a wholesaler.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Wholesaler: Likely to buy in large quantities, increasing sales; Can hold less inventory, less storage space/costs; Only deliver to one location, lowering transport costs; No direct contact/feedback with customer, so difficult to build customer relationship/loyalty; Price may be higher, leading to fewer sales; Lose (some) control over marketing/advertising; Wholesaler takes part of the profit, which lowers profit margin. Other channels: Sell direct (ecommerce/online) — more control over marketing/build rapport. Retailers — reach wider range of customers. Agents — local knowledge, higher sales. Points must be from viewpoint of the start-up business. Justification must compare two channels — e.g. a wholesaler is the best channel because being able to lower costs is important especially as a start-up business will have limited capital.

text: Identify two ways business activity could have an impact on the environment.
context: TBX manufactures high-quality steel used to build railways. The Managing Director knows business activity could have an impact on the environment.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 2). Only award first two responses. Ways: Pollution (or examples e.g. noise, air)/global warming/emission of greenhouse gases; Energy use/use fossil fuels; Congestion/transport of goods; Land use/use up natural resources/deforestation; Waste (disposal)/use single use/non-renewable/non-recyclable materials.

text: Identify two ways a business could contribute to sustainable development.
context: TBX is considering ways the business can contribute to sustainable development.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 2). Only award first two responses. Ways: Reduce amount/number of resources used; Reduce number of products made/level of output; Reduce waste; Reuse products/materials; Recycle products/materials; Use renewable energy; Develop environmentally friendly products; Use environmentally friendly production methods/sustainable materials; Use environmentally friendly/sustainable packaging; Replant trees; Use electric vehicles.

text: Outline two possible economies of scale TBX might benefit from.
context: TBX manufactures high-quality steel for railways. The method of production used allows TBX to benefit from economies of scale. Holds a high level of inventory including iron ore.
ms: 1 mark per economy + 1 mark application (max 2 = 4 marks). Economies: Purchasing (economy) for the iron ore; Technical (economy) to manufacture steel; Managerial (economy) helping contribute to sustainable development; Financial (economy) so can have a high level of inventory; Marketing (economy). Application words: steel, railways, iron (ore), high level of inventory, sustainable development/impact on environment, high-quality.

text: Explain two possible problems for TBX of holding a high level of inventory.
context: TBX manufactures high-quality steel for railways, holds a high level of inventory including iron ore, benefits from economies of scale.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 problems = 6 marks). Problems: Rent/storage space/large space needed for the steel, which can increase fixed costs/expenses; Ties up working capital such as iron ore, which could lead to liquidity/cash flow problems/difficult to pay suppliers; Insurance costs, which increase cash outflows so less funds to contribute to sustainable development; Opportunity cost/funds could be used for other purposes; Risk of damage/theft/wastage/product could rust, leading to higher costs. Application words: steel, railways, iron (ore), high-quality, sustainable development/impact on environment.

text: Do you think quality control is the best method for a manufacturing business to use to achieve quality production? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Quality control (QC): Tries to eliminate/lower chance of faults before products reach customer, to help maintain reputation; Does not stop production while checking, so some output is available; Need to recruit inspectors, which increases labour costs; Spots errors at end/does not show where error happened in process, which could increase wastage. Quality assurance (QA): Errors stopped before happen/spotted earlier in process/products checked throughout, so less funds/time spent on rework; Increase employee motivation leading to higher output; Need to train all employees, which increases costs; Not all workers interested/able to spot problems. Justification must compare QC and QA — e.g. quality assurance is the best way because fewer mistakes is likely to mean fewer resources are wasted, and the funds saved should hopefully cover the additional cost of training.

text: Define 'public sector'.
context: Country X has a mixed economy with both private and public sector organisations.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Government/state owned businesses. Partial (1 mark): Run/operated/controlled by government.

text: Define 'gross domestic product' (GDP).
context: Economic sectors in country X as a percentage of GDP: Primary 60% (2000) → 20% (2020); Secondary 15% → 30%; Tertiary 25% → 50%.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): The total value of output of goods and services in a country in one year. OR The monetary value of all goods and services produced by an economy during a specific period (of time). Partial (1 mark): Value of goods produced by a country. First mark for idea of value of goods and services in the country; second mark for the time period (one year/period of time).

text: Identify four types of business organisation in the private sector.
context: Country X has a mixed economy with both private and public sector organisations.
ms: 1 mark per type (max 4). Only award first four responses. Types: Sole trader; Partnership; Private limited company; Public limited company; Joint venture; Franchise; Social enterprise. Only award unincorporated company if no specific examples given. Only award limited company if no specific examples given.

text: Using the data from Table 3.1, explain two possible reasons for the changing importance of the primary sector in country X.
context: Table 3.1 — Economic sectors in country X as % of GDP: 2000: Primary 60%, Secondary 15%, Tertiary 25%. 2020: Primary 20%, Secondary 30%, Tertiary 50%. In the last 20 years the primary sector has become less important to country X's economy. The government is planning to encourage multinational companies to set up factories.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 reasons = 6 marks). Reasons: Fewer/depletion of natural resources leading to a decrease in primary sector of 40% so workers must find jobs in other sectors/may need to import resources; Increased use of machinery/technology in primary sector reduces the need for employees which is why primary sector is only 20% in 2020; Industrialisation/setting up of factories which creates jobs in the secondary sector which has increased by 15%; Better/increased education so workers seek higher paid jobs which is why tertiary sector has increased to 50%; Fewer grants/less government support for primary sector OR more grants for secondary/tertiary sector businesses; Import (more)/cheaper raw materials. Application must refer to the data in Table 3.1 (60%, 20%, 40% decrease, 15%, 30%, 15% increase, 25%, 50%, 25% increase). Do not award deindustrialisation.

text: Do you think the benefits to a country of having a multinational company located there are always greater than the drawbacks? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. The government is planning to encourage multinational companies to set up factories in country X.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Benefits: Increase number/availability of jobs, reduces unemployment; Increase taxes, which can be used to improve public services; Increase reputation of country, could encourage other businesses to set up/invest; Increasing orders for local suppliers, increasing income for local businesses/GDP; Wider choice/quality of goods; Improve infrastructure/new investment/new technology; Knowledge-sharing/new ideas. Drawbacks: Increased competition, reducing sales for local businesses which can force them out of business/reducing revenue; Use up scarce resources; Repatriation of profits/send profits back to home country, so country does not receive expected amount of tax revenue; Often only unskilled jobs created/may offer low wages/poor working conditions/exploitation of labour; Often try to avoid/reduce amount of tax paid (in host country); Power to influence government decisions/local economy. Justification: multinational companies create employment opportunities which reduces unemployment; however they can try to avoid taxes so less funds to provide public services; countries do benefit even if the full amount of tax isn't paid, as the amount paid can still be used to develop the country.

text: Identify two advantages to a business of maintaining customer loyalty.
context: TFN is a travel business which sells holidays, 37 shops and 1000 employees. Last year TFN's profit increased to $46 million. Good customer service has helped maintain customer loyalty.
ms: 1 mark per advantage (max 2). Only award first two responses. Advantages: Maintain/increase sales/repeat customers/customers return/not go to competitors; Improve reputation/brand image; Current customers recommend/tell others about the products/less marketing needed/lower cost of marketing; Remain competitive; Easier to introduce new products; Easier to gain feedback/learn about trends; May be able to increase prices/become price inelastic.

text: Identify two hygiene factors from Herzberg's two-factor theory.
context: TFN's managers use ideas from Herzberg's two-factor theory to help motivate employees.
ms: 1 mark per hygiene factor (max 2). Only award first two responses. Two from: Working conditions/safe environment; Salary/wages/pay; (Job) security; Relationships with other workers; Relationships with supervisor.

text: Outline two reasons why profit might be important to TFN.
context: TFN is a travel business (37 shops, 1000 employees), last year profit increased to $46 million.
ms: 1 mark per reason + 1 mark application (max 2 reasons = 4 marks). Reasons: Source of finance/reinvest in the business/finance the purchase of non-current assets/pay back debts for its 37 shops; Measure of success of business as shown by profit of $46 million/increase in profit; Reward for risk-taking of this travel business; Provides a return to shareholders/helps attract investors/pay dividends; Support loan applications. Application words: travel business, sells holidays, (37) shops/stores, 1000 employees, $46 million/increase in profit.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to TFN of its managers having a wide span of control.
context: TFN is a travel business (37 shops, 1000 employees, $46 million profit). Each manager has a wide span of control. All employees are provided with off-the-job training.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantage: Fewer supervisors/managers needed, helping reduce labour costs/expenses so may help increase its profit of $46 million; Faster communication, leading to quicker/better decision-making in its 37 shops; Encourages delegation, which can increase motivation of its 1000 employees. Disadvantage: Less control, so less work done/lower productivity at the travel business; Workers might not have skills to cope with extra responsibility, leading to mistakes; Effective communication may be difficult/communication problems, as large number of subordinates/employees to inform/ask; Managers might not have the necessary skills (to manage so many people). Application words: travel business, sells holidays, (37) shops/stores, 1000 employees, $46 million (profit)/increase in profit, (good) customer service, maintain customer loyalty, Herzberg's two-factor theory, training.

text: Do you think off-the-job training is the best method of training for a service sector business to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. All TFN employees are provided with off-the-job training.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application.
