Off-the-job: Allows for mistakes to be made when learning, lower risk of damaging reputation; Up to date/new skills can be gained; Skills might not be available in the business, so benefit from new techniques/ideas; Use specialists/expert trainers, is expensive/increases costs; Travel costs, increasing cash outflows. On-the-job training: Employees can carry on working, so some work is done; Control what is taught/employees learn exact way business wants things done, so workers only learn skills needed; Cheaper (than off-the-job), reducing (training) costs; Reinforce errors/bad habits of trainer, reducing sales/damaging reputation; Trainer is less productive when training others. Induction training: only suitable for new employees, help learn culture. Justification must compare two methods — e.g. off-the-job training is better especially for a service sector business because fewer mistakes can help protect the business reputation, leading to extra customers helping cover the additional costs of the training.

text: Define 'unincorporated business'.
context: Desmond wants to be a successful entrepreneur, leaving his office job to start up a gardening business cutting grass and planting flowers. It will be an unincorporated business.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): A business that does not have a separate legal identity. Partial (1 mark): Owner is/are responsible for business debts/unlimited liability. Max 1 for features of an unincorporated business e.g. business ends if an owner leaves.

text: Identify two objectives a new business might have.
context: Desmond has identified his business objectives for the first year for his gardening business.
ms: 1 mark per objective (max 2). Only award first two responses. Objectives: Survival; Break-even; Make a profit; Become known in the market/create good reputation; Generate sales/gain customers; Encourage customer loyalty; Offer good customer service; Create added value; Social responsibility/ethical; Growth/expansion/increase market share.

text: Identify four characteristics of a successful entrepreneur.
context: Desmond wants to be a successful entrepreneur, starting a gardening business with $750 start-up capital.
ms: 1 mark per characteristic (max 4). Only award first four responses. Characteristics: Risk-taker; Problem solver; Decisive; Creative; Innovative; Hard-working; Perseverance/determined/focused/(self-)motivated; Resourceful/adaptable; Optimistic; Self-confident/esteem; Independent; Effective communicator; Organised; Multi-skilled; Results driven/ambitious; Leadership; Team player; Good at networking/prepared to learn from others.

text: Explain two reasons (other than lack of finance) why Desmond's new business might be at greater risk of failure than an established business.
context: Desmond is leaving his office job to start an unincorporated gardening business, aware a new business is at greater risk of failure than an established business.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 reasons = 6 marks). Reasons: Inadequate/no market research about gardening, so may not offer what customers want; Providing wrong/poor quality service; Lack of experience/poor decision-making/skills, as only worked in an office, so more likely to make mistakes; Difficult to compete with competitors/lack of customers/insufficient sales for this unincorporated business, leading to less revenue; Poor planning/no business plan, despite setting objectives, so does not have time/opportunity to resolve problems; No reputation/brand image/poor marketing, therefore potential customers do not trust him. Application words: gardening or examples such as cutting grass/planting flowers, service, entrepreneur, $750, office job, unincorporated business, business objectives.

text: Do you think owner's savings are the most suitable source of finance for a start-up business? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Desmond has calculated he will need $750 for his start-up capital.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Owner's savings: No need to repay/no debt, helping to reduce/keep cash outflows low/less risk; No interest payable, therefore not increasing cost; May not have enough/any savings, delaying/stopping their plans; Immediately available. Alternatives: Crowdfunding — no initial fees payable, allows the public's reaction to be tested, but platform might reject the proposal, publicising could allow competitors to copy the idea. Bank loan — could provide all the finance at once but must be repaid, interest payable increases expenses, quick to arrange. Borrow from friends and family — may give longer time/better terms to repay. Government grant — no need to repay/no interest, but may be conditions attached. Do not award 'issue shares' or 'profit' as not appropriate for a start-up business. Justification: e.g. a bank loan may be best because plans are not delayed through lack of finance — by the time the owner has saved enough, they might have missed out on the business opportunity.

text: Identify two limitations of break-even analysis.
context: LCT manufactures cooking pots with 16 employees, uses social media as its method of advertising. Carole is analysing LCT's break-even chart.
ms: 1 mark per limitation (max 2). Only award first two responses. Limitations: Assumes that all costs can be represented by straight lines; It is not easy to separate costs into fixed and variable; Assumes that all output is sold/does not allow for inventory (stock) holding costs; Assumes only one type of product sold; Assumes selling price remains unchanged for all products sold; Concentrates on break-even point/ignores other aspects of operations; It is a prediction/forecast/does not include unexpected costs.

text: Calculate LCT's profit if it sells 800 units. Show your working.
context: LCT's break-even chart: fixed costs $2000, price $10/unit, variable costs $5/unit, break-even output 400 units. At 800 units, total revenue is $8000 and total cost is $6000.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): $2000. Method: Profit = total revenue − total cost = 8000 − 6000 (1 mark). Award only 1 mark if 2000 is written as part of the answer but not given as final answer. $ sign not required.

text: Outline two possible benefits to LCT of having a good brand image.
context: LCT manufactures cooking pots with 16 employees, uses social media as its method of advertising, Carole knows brand image is important, considering ways to lower break-even output.
ms: 1 mark per benefit + 1 mark application (max 2 benefits = 4 marks). Benefits: Encourage/maintain (customer) loyalty for this small business; Can help increase sales/customers/market share of cooking pots; Aids recognition/awareness/advertising on social media; May be able to charge high price (than for unbranded products) which can help lower its break-even output; Helps differentiate product from competitors so may be able to sell more than 800 units; Helps launch new products in the market; May attract investors; Helps with employee recruitment. Application words: (cooking) pots, manufactures/production, 16 (employees), small business, social media (for advertising), (lower) break-even output, 400 units (break-even output), $10 (price per unit), 800 units, total revenue $10,000, total costs $7000.

text: Explain two ways LCT might lower its break-even level of output.
context: LCT manufactures cooking pots with 16 employees, fixed costs $2000, price $10, variable costs $5, break-even output 400 units. Carole is considering possible ways to lower LCT's break-even level of output.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 ways = 6 marks). Ways: Increase price higher than $10, which would increase revenue; Lower rent or other example below $2000, lowering fixed costs/expenses OR lower fixed costs lead to lower total costs (TC); Buy cheaper raw materials or other example for its cooking pots reducing variable cost OR lower variable costs lead to lower total costs (TC). Application words: (cooking) pots, manufactures/production, 16 (employees), small business, good brand image, $2000 (fixed costs), $10 (price), $5 (variable costs per pot), 400 (break-even output), social media, $10,000, $7,000. Only allow one example of fixed costs and one example of variable costs.

text: Do you think social media is the best method of advertising for a small business to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. LCT uses social media as its method of advertising, a small business.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Social media: Cover wide area/seen by many people leading to an increase in sales/more revenue; Low-cost method of advertising so fewer cash outflows; Easy/quick to update so can spend time on other tasks; Can target specific groups, could encourage brand loyalty; Way to build relationship/communicate with customers/gain direct feedback; Risk of hacking/fraud/virus; Bad reviews can be seen by everyone, could lead to a bad reputation; No internet access/not everyone uses social media/easy to lose message; Takes time to continually post/monitor messages. Other methods: Newspapers, leaflets, posters/billboards, website, pop-up adverts, television, radio. Justification must compare two methods — e.g. social media is the best way for a small business because it is unlikely to have a large marketing budget, so the low cost allows funds available for other purposes.

text: Identify two external users of accounts.
context: ACP manufactures computers, being ethical is important, employs 3000 workers, imports 65% of its raw materials. Directors plan to analyse financial performance using profitability ratios.
ms: 1 mark per external user (max 2). Only award first two responses. Users: Banks/lenders; Suppliers; Government; Competitors; Other businesses e.g. insurance companies; Pressure groups; Investors/shareholders; Customers. Do not award examples of internal users of accounts e.g. employees. Accept creditors alone as an alternative to lenders/bank/suppliers if no specific example given.

text: Identify two profitability ratios.
context: ACP's directors plan to analyse ACP's financial performance using profitability ratios.
ms: 1 mark per ratio (max 2). Only award first two responses. Two from: Gross profit margin/ratio/percentage; Profit margin/ratio/percentage; Return on capital employed/ROCE. Allow correct formula e.g. Gross profit:sales revenue.

text: Outline two possible reasons why ACP imports its raw materials.
context: ACP manufactures computers, being ethical is important, employs 3000 workers in its factory, imports 65% of its raw materials.
ms: 1 mark per reason + 1 mark application (max 2 reasons = 4 marks). Reasons: Lower prices/cost of materials which could help the business manage its cash flow; Access to a wider range of materials to make its computers; Limited resources available from own country, especially as trying to act in an ethical way; Better quality (than available in own country), which may be why the business already imports 65%; Purchasing from ethical supplier. Application words: 65%, cash flow, production/manufacture, (manufacture) computers, (act in an) ethical way, 3000 (workers), factory, profit is important.

text: Explain one benefit and one limitation to ACP of being ethical.
context: ACP manufactures computers, being ethical is important, 3000 employees, imports 65% of its raw materials. The Finance Director thinks profit is more important than managing cash flow.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per benefit AND limitation (max 6 marks). Benefits: Good image/good reputation/customer loyalty, so customers more willing to pay high prices for its computers; High/higher demand/sales, which can help increase revenue; Can help recruit/motivate/retain workers, reducing recruitment costs as the business has 3000 employees; Better supplier relations (as pay a fair price), which can help ensure the necessary supply to maintain production; Investors more likely to invest; Less opposition from pressure groups. Limitations: Limited/fewer sources of materials, which may lead to less output as already imports 65% of raw materials; May have to pay more to suppliers, leading to higher variable costs/cost of goods sold; Workers may have to be paid more at the factory, increasing labour costs; Higher costs could lead to higher prices. Application words: 65%/import, cash flow, raw materials, computers, 3000 employees, factory, production/manufacture, profit is important/profitability ratios.

text: Do you think making a profit is more important for a business than managing its cash flow? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. The Finance Director thinks making a profit is more important for a business than managing its cash flow.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Profit: It is a source of finance, may increase opportunity for growth; Reward for risk-taking/allows dividend for owners, without it owners will have less incentive to invest; Reward for enterprise; Indicator/measure of success; Important for long-term survival. Cash flow: Need cash to pay day-to-day costs/ensures liquidity/help avoid cash flow problems/pay debt, otherwise might have insufficient funds/working capital to continue production; Sales may be on credit, therefore money received later; Reduced need for overdraft, which would add to interest costs. Justification must compare profit and cash flow — e.g. managing cash flow is likely to be more important because a business can continue in the short term without making a profit, but without sufficient cash flow a business may be unable to operate and earn revenue.

text: Define 'delegation'.
context: MRN is a food retailer with 490 shops and 70,000 employees, plans to close 80 shops. The HR Director wants to encourage delegation.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Giving a subordinate the authority to perform particular tasks. OR When a manager gives authority to another employee to complete a task, although the manager retains the ultimate responsibility for the completion of the task. OR Passing responsibility to perform tasks to employees (lower down the organisation). Partial (1 mark): Manager gives task to employee, OR subordinate given task to do, OR giving authority to a subordinate/employee. Do not award answers which identify reasons for using delegation e.g. motivates, creates time for managers.

text: Identify two legal controls over employment.
context: MRN is a food retailer, will continue to follow legal controls over employment.
ms: 1 mark per control (max 2). Only award first two responses. Controls: (Unfair) dismissal; Discrimination/equal opportunities; Health and safety; Legal minimum wage; Legal minimum age/child labour; Contract of employment/conditions of employment; Redundancy.

text: Outline two functions of MRN's shop managers.
context: MRN is a food retailer with 490 shops and 70,000 employees, plans to close 80 shops. 20% of management jobs will be removed.
ms: 1 mark per function + 1 mark application (max 2 functions = 4 marks). Functions: Planning, so have the necessary resources for this food retailer; Organising, to ensure everyone is working effectively in each of the 490 stores; Commanding, to help guide the 70,000 employees; Co-ordinating, so better placed to respond to increased competition; Controlling. Application words: food, 490/410 shops, 80, 70,000 employees, (increased) competition, 20% (management) jobs, delegation, legal controls over employment. Do not award motivate/communicate as knowledge.

text: Explain two factors MRN should consider when deciding which shops to close.
context: MRN is a food retailer with 490 shops and 70,000 employees, has announced plans to close 80 of its shops. 20% of management jobs will be removed.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 factors = 6 marks). Factors: Level of demand/where its customers are/number of sales of food, as some might have lower revenue; Level of competition/number/type of shops in area, which could reduce sales/demand; Rent/rates for each of the 80 locations, as this could make some sites too expensive to run; Distance from suppliers, increased transport costs; Space, as in some locations there may not be enough room to display everything; Shops which are too close together; Economic state of area/area in decline; Local wage rates/labour availability, leading to higher costs; Number of workers employed, to reduce redundancy payments; Profitability of each shop. Application words: food, 490/410 shops, 70,000 employees, 80, increased competition, 20% management jobs, delegation, legal controls over employment.

text: Explain two ways a retail business could respond to increased competition. Which would be the best way to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. MRN's directors know it is important that businesses respond to increased competition.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Ways: Introduce new products, therefore gaining a USP, but may have limited shelf space; Lower prices/change pricing method, can sell more products/increased market share, increasing revenue; Improve quality of service/products, but this might increase (training) costs, may lower profit margin; Maintain/build good customer relationships, which could encourage customer loyalty; Increase promotion/advertising; Renovating shop; Relocate; Merger/takeover. Justification must compare two ways — e.g. introducing new products is a better way because price might not be important to the customer, so lowering the price will simply reduce profit margin.

text: Define 'mass market'.
context: TDG is a bicycle retailer with 3 employees, needs to maintain customer loyalty as the business sells in a mass market.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Where there is a very large number of sales of a product. OR Selling the same product to the whole market. OR A large market containing lots of customers buying similar products. Partial (1 mark): Lots of customers/lots of sales/lots of buyers. Do not award: alternative words for mass e.g. big/large market; lots of sellers, competitors, or products as this describes a market.

text: Calculate X and Y.
context: TDG's cash-flow forecast ($000): July: Cash inflow X, Cash outflow 50, Net cash flow 10, Opening 20, Closing 30. August: Cash inflow 50, Cash outflow 50, Net cash flow 0, Opening 30, Closing 30. September: Cash inflow 40, Cash outflow Y, Net cash flow (40), Opening 30, Closing (10).
ms: 1 mark per correct calculation. X: $60,000 or 60. Y: $80,000 or 80 or (80). $ sign not required.

text: Outline two reasons why managing cash flow might be important for TDG.
context: TDG is a bicycle retailer with 3 employees, sells in a mass market, needs to maintain customer loyalty. Simon manages a cash-flow problem in September.
ms: 1 mark per reason + 1 mark application (max 2 reasons = 4 marks). Reasons: To be able to pay wages to its 3 employees; Pay suppliers/trade payables for the bikes; Pay expenses/heating/rent/advertising to avoid cash flow problem in September; Repay (short-term) debts of the retailer; Predict/plan/prevent cash flow problems such as the $80,000 shortfall; Ensure business survival/continue; Cash available for emergency. Application words: bicycles/bikes, retailer, ($10,000) closing balance/cashflow problem in September, customer loyalty, mass market, 3 employees, $80,000 (cash outflow in September, OFR), $40,000 (cash inflow in September). Do not award invest/expand, references to profit, or 'know how to improve' as too vague.

text: Explain two ways TDG could overcome its short-term cash-flow problem in September.
context: TDG is a bicycle retailer with 3 employees, sells in a mass market. September closing balance is -$10,000.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 ways = 6 marks). Ways: Delay payments to suppliers for its bicycles, keeping cash in the business for longer; Ask/offer discounts so customers pay quicker/insist on cash sales, so business receives cash sooner but may not help maintain customer loyalty; Overdraft, allows the business to have a negative cash balance to cover the −$10,000; Bank loan, to increase cash inflow above $40,000; Delay/not purchase/buy cheaper equipment, which prevents cash outflows; Sell (non-current) assets, generates cash inflows. Application words: bicycles/bikes, retailer, −$10,000 (closing balance), customer loyalty, mass market, 3 employees, $80,000 (cash outflow, OFR), $40,000. Analysis must show impact on cash flow. Do not award long-term solutions such as introduce more capital/sell shares/retained profit, decrease price/advertise, or references to raw materials/production.

text: Explain two methods a retailer could use to maintain customer loyalty. Which would be the best method to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. TDG needs to maintain customer loyalty as it sells in a mass market.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Methods: Offer loyalty cards/points for every purchase/discount for regular customers, so incentive/reward to return; Train staff/offer good service/friendly conversations, which would make them feel welcome; Communicate with customers or examples such as newsletters/social media, so they remember your business; Ask for feedback/carry out market research, so know what is being sold matches customer needs; Introduce new/sell high-quality products; Resolve complaints quickly; Offer extra services e.g. delivery/credit facilities. Justification must compare two methods — e.g. good service is better because this may not include any costs which a loyalty card would, which could help increase profit margin as well as customer loyalty.

text: Define 'quality control'.
context: KCL manufactures paper used in the production of newspapers and books, holds a high level of inventory, buys raw materials including wood from local suppliers. Quality control is important.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Checking of goods at the end of the production process (whether it is the production of the product or a service). OR Checking the standard of goods through inspection. Partial (1 mark): Checking the work, OR making sure goods are up to standard. 'At end of production' is +1 only.

text: Identify two ways a pressure group might try to influence business decisions.
context: Pressure groups are trying to influence KCL's decisions to ensure the business does not create more external costs than external benefits.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 2). Only award first two responses. Ways: Create negative publicity/publish information about business/write to newspaper; Organise customer boycotts; Organise demonstrations/protests/rally opposition; Lobby/petition/send letters to government; Demand interview with company; Take legal action.

text: State four benefits to a business of increasing efficiency.
context: KCL's Operations Director is considering ways to increase efficiency in the factory.
ms: 1 mark per benefit (max 4). Only award first two — actually first four responses given. Benefits: Reduce average/unit costs; Fewer mistakes/errors; Less waste; Fewer materials needed; Increase output; Quicker/faster production; Reduced inputs needed for the same level of output. Do not award lower labour turnover/less absenteeism or more revenue/sales/profit.

text: Explain one external cost and one external benefit that may be created by KCL's business.
context: KCL manufactures paper for newspapers and books, holds a high level of inventory, buys raw materials including wood from local suppliers, quality control is important.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per cost AND benefit (max 6 marks). External cost: Pollution/smoke/fumes created from making paper, could damage health of people in the community; Congestion caused by deliveries to the factory, so longer to move about/slow down deliveries to other businesses; Use up natural resources to obtain the wood, meaning fewer resources available for other uses/future generations; Destruction/spoil landscape, reducing tourism. External benefit: Provide jobs as it uses local suppliers, so low(er) rates of unemployment; Help economic growth, which can result in additional taxes; Improved infrastructure/better road links, improving access for local community/businesses; New production techniques may be introduced. Application words: paper/newspapers/books, wood (or other raw materials), factory, increase efficiency, (raw materials from) local suppliers, pressure groups, high level of inventory. Do not award costs/benefits to business or uses of paper.

text: Explain two factors a manufacturing business should consider when deciding how much inventory to hold. Which factor is likely to be the most important? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. KCL holds a high level of inventory.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Factors: Whether product is perishable or not/shelf life, to reduce the amount of wastage; Level of demand/sales, as if high demand needs to hold high inventory; Seasons/celebrations/festivals/predictability of demand; Storage space available, could increase storage costs; Cost of holding inventory, as high levels could increase cash outflows; Method of production/level of output, as flow production may require high levels of inventory; Amount of finance available (to buy inventory), as this could cause cash flow problems/cannot afford to hold large amount; Delivery/lead time/where products come from/reliability of supplier, so production can continue/meet orders on time. Justification: e.g. delivery time is more important because if production stops, any costs saved on storage may be lost as the business still has to pay its workers, and the lack of available products could lead to fewer sales.

text: Define 'span of control'.
context: PCY provides insurance services for businesses such as farms and factories. Being ethical is important, 4 offices, 500 employees. The span of control could change.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Number of subordinates reporting to each supervisor/manager. OR Number of subordinates/employees working (directly) under a manager. Partial (1 mark): Whom you are responsible for, OR who reports to one manager.

text: Identify two leadership styles.
context: PCY's managers use different leadership styles.
ms: 1 mark per style (max 2). Only award first two responses. Styles: Autocratic; Democratic; Laissez-faire. Do not award descriptions of styles.

text: Outline two benefits to PCY of encouraging its managers to use delegation.
context: PCY provides insurance services, 4 offices, 500 employees, being ethical is important. The Managing Director wants to reduce communication barriers and encourage delegation.
ms: 1 mark per benefit + 1 mark application (max 2 benefits = 4 marks). Benefits: Reduce managers' workload/managers have time to focus on other (important) tasks such as how the business is organised/managed; Quality of managers' work improves/managers likely to make fewer mistakes in the 4 offices; Increase employee motivation of its 500 employees; Builds trust/better working relationship between managers and employees, which could influence its leadership style; Way to develop employee skills/increase employee flexibility/employees may have better knowledge of issue at the insurance business. Application words: (4) offices, 500 (employees), insurance (services), business customers/farms/factories, leadership style, being ethical, communication barriers, span of control, planning to change how business is managed/organised. Do not award benefits to employees e.g. feel trusted.

text: Explain two possible reasons why being ethical is important to PCY.
context: PCY provides insurance services for farms and factories, being ethical is important, 4 offices, 500 employees.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 reasons = 6 marks). Reasons: Increased/retain sales/demand/customers from farms/factories, leading to higher revenue; Build/better reputation/brand image, leading to better customer loyalty/sales/competitive advantage for its insurance; Help attract/motivate/retain employees, improving efficiency/better quality of service/less labour turnover from its 500 employees; Investors may be more likely/willing to invest, increasing the amount of capital/funds. Application words: 4 offices, 500 employees, insurance (services), business customers/farms/factories, leadership style, communication barriers, span of control, delegation. Do not award compliance with laws/less risk of legal action, examples of being unethical, or ways to be ethical.

text: Do you think lack of feedback is the main barrier to effective communication in a business? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. The Managing Director wants to reduce communication barriers within PCY.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Lack of feedback: Do not know whether message has been understood, which could lead to errors/wrong actions taken; Do not know whether recipient has received, which can lead to delays. Other barriers: Technical problems e.g. no signal/equipment breakdown, so message cannot be sent/received; Too much information sent in message, which can lead to mistakes/slow down decision-making; Jargon used/language, so receiver cannot understand; Noise/distractions, so not able to hear the message; (Wrong) communication method used, so people are unable to access/read message; Message has to pass through too many levels/employees, so message gets distorted/lost; Send wrong message/send to the wrong person, so the actual message is never sent/received. Justification: e.g. lack of feedback is the most important barrier because they are more likely to know whether a technical problem has happened, whereas with a lack of feedback they may not know until an error is made, damaging the business's reputation.

text: Identify two ways a government might support business start-ups.
context: Meena wants to leave her job as a teacher to become a successful entrepreneur, producing handmade jewellery, knows there is government support for business start-ups.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 2). Only award first two responses. Ways: Offer financial support or examples such as grants/(low-cost) loans; Provide training; Provide information/advice/support/mentors; Provide low-cost/rent-free property/location; Offer lower tax rates/tax breaks/tax relief; Encourage universities to make research facilities available; Organise business fairs.

text: Identify two ways a market can be segmented.
context: Meena plans to use market research to help identify a market segment for her jewellery.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 2). Only award first two responses. Ways: Age; Gender; Socio-economic group/social status/class; Location/region/geographic; Interests/lifestyle; Family characteristics; Education; Occupation; Use of product; Ethnic group. Can award demographic if age/gender/socio-economic group/social status/ethnic group not awarded; psychographic if lifestyle/personality/attitudes not awarded.

text: Outline two characteristics Meena will need to become a successful entrepreneur.
context: Meena wants to leave her teaching job to become an entrepreneur producing handmade jewellery. Her brother has offered to be her business partner but she is deciding between sole trader and partnership.
ms: 1 mark per characteristic + 1 mark application (max 2 characteristics = 4 marks). Characteristics: Risk-taking, as leaving her job; Self-motivated/determination/resilience/perseverance for her start-up; Hard-working, especially if she decides to be a sole trader; Creative, as products will be handmade; Effective communicator, as may need to discuss matters with partner; Self-confident; Optimistic/positive; Independent; Innovator. Application words: handmade, jewellery, leaving her job/teacher, start-up/new business, brother, sole trader, partner, government support, market research, market segment.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to Meena of operating as a sole trader rather than being in a partnership.
context: Meena is considering whether to become a sole trader or take on her brother as a business partner for her handmade jewellery business.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantages: Keep all the profit from the new business, so she has an incentive to work harder/decide how to invest it; Can make all/quick decisions, even if it's her brother, so may be more responsive to changes in demand; Complete control/own boss, less chance for disagreement/no need to consult anyone; Has freedom to choose own holidays/work hours, to gain a better work/life balance. Disadvantages: No one to share workload/responsibility/control with, so less time to specialise on certain activities such as making jewellery; Access to less finance/partner may provide extra finance, so need to borrow more/may need more government support; Fewer ideas/less knowledge/experience, so less able to compete; No one to share any risks/potential loss/costs with. Application words: handmade, jewellery, leaving her job/teacher, entrepreneur, government support, market research, market segment, brother, business start-up/new business. Do not award features of unincorporated businesses such as unlimited liability, no continuity.

text: Do you think accessing government sources, such as statistics, is the best method of market research for a start-up business to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Meena plans to use market research to help identify a market segment.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Government sources: Free/cheap to collect, which can help keep fixed cost low; Readily available, so can make decisions more quickly; Provides data on a range of topics/shows trends across whole country/market, so can make more informed decisions; May be out-of-date, so information may not be relevant to what the business needs to know now; Data may not be relevant/specific to the business, leading to wrong decisions. Other methods: Reports from market research agencies — but will have to pay; Questionnaires/surveys — large amounts of information collected; Focus groups — highly detailed responses; Interviews — time consuming; Online survey; Observation. Justification: e.g. government statistics are better because a new business may not be able to afford the cost of having a questionnaire designed properly, and government statistics are likely to be accurate enough to still prove helpful.

text: Identify two reasons why a business might offer training to its employees.
context: FBW manufactures watches using job production, 5 full-time production employees, offered regular training. Last year FBW sold 600 watches.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two responses. Reasons: To introduce a new process/new equipment; Improve efficiency/productivity; Increase output; Reduce mistakes/fewer errors/better quality goods or services; Improve employee skills; Increase knowledge; Improve motivation; Help reduce labour turnover; Decrease the chance of accidents; Familiarise new employees with business/other employees.

text: Calculate the following values using Fig. 1.1: Break-even output AND Break-even revenue.
context: FBW's break-even chart shows fixed costs, total costs, and total revenue lines for watches, up to 800 units.
ms: 1 mark per correct answer. Break-even output: 500 (watches). Break-even revenue: $60,000 or 60,000.

text: Outline two possible effects on FBW's break-even chart if the prices of its products are increased.
context: FBW manufactures watches using job production, 5 employees, sold 600 watches last year, break-even output 500, margin of safety 100. Managing Director plans to use break-even analysis to decide whether to increase price.
ms: 1 mark per effect + 1 mark application (max 2 effects = 4 marks). Effects: Reduce/lower break-even output below 500 units; Increase the margin of safety above 100; Increase contribution per unit when using job production; Increase revenue from sale of its watches; Reduce break-even revenue; Increase profit margin; Increase (potential) profit/reduce (potential) loss. Application words: watches, 5 (employees), training (every year), job production, 600 units (sold), 500 (break-even output), 100 (margin of safety), $4000 (profit at 600 units), $60,000 (break-even revenue).

text: Explain two benefits to FBW of having full-time employees.
context: FBW manufactures watches using job production, 5 full-time employees, regular training, sold 600 watches last year, break-even output 500.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 benefits = 6 marks). Benefits: Workers likely to be more loyal/committed, so lower labour turnover/lower cost of recruitment for its 5 employees; Easy to communicate/update when making its watches, so could be more efficient; Consistent standard of work, leading to better reputation which is helpful as using job production; Fewer workers needed, so less training required; Less employees to manage, so managers can focus on other issues; Employees become more familiar with the business; Always available/can find when needed. Application words: watches, 5 (employees), (regular) training, job production, 600 units sold, 500 (break-even output).

text: Do you think job production is the best method of production for a small business to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. FBW manufactures watches using job production.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Job production: Meet exact customer requirements, which increases customer loyalty/sales; Unique/high-quality products, can charge higher price; Products made to order/can take a long time to make, so low output; No economies of scale, leading to higher average cost; Skilled labour is needed, increases labour/training costs; Requires a lot of employees/labour intensive. Batch production: Some economies of scale; Able to produce more, so unit costs lower; Can produce range/variety of products; Demotivated employees, increasing labour turnover; Machines must be reset between batches; Added cost of moving/storing semi-finished goods; Warehouse space is needed/increases storage costs. Do not award comparisons between batch and flow. Justification: e.g. job production is not the best method for a small business, especially as the number of sales may not cover the additional cost of the skilled labour, so the business is unable to make a profit.

text: Identify two ways a business plan can help a business to reduce risk.
context: Gloria is a sole trader providing house-cleaning services, has been told producing a business plan can help reduce risk.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 2). Only award first two responses. Ways: Help secure funding/attract investors; Can show whether/when extra finance needed/help budgeting; Help set goals/objectives/provide sense of direction; Help monitor/check/track progress; Test feasibility of idea/identify demand; Help set (suitable) prices; Understand level/type of competition; Help identify skills/employees needed; Help allocate resources (appropriately).

text: Identify two possible reasons why a business might want to expand.
context: Gloria wants to expand her house-cleaning business by offering a repair service.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two responses. Reasons: Increase sales/revenue; Increase profit; Widen customer base/target new markets; Increase market share; Increase reputation/more prestige/status; Increase output; Spread risk/diversify; Gain economies of scale.

text: Outline one advantage and one disadvantage to Gloria of using telephone calls as a method of communication with her employees.
context: Gloria is a sole trader with 4 employees providing house-cleaning services, uses telephone calls to communicate with employees.
ms: 1 mark advantage/disadvantage + 1 mark application (max 2 each = 4 marks). Advantages: Instant/quick to contact her 4 employees; Opportunity to get immediate feedback about cleaning jobs; Can talk to employees who are anywhere/elsewhere; Can leave a message/voice note. Disadvantages: Technical problems e.g. no internet/signal, so will not help reduce her workload; No hard copy/nothing to refer to; Receiver may not answer the phone/might be busy; Not face to face/no body language; May only be able to speak to one person at a time; Cannot show data/chart over a phone; Cost. Application words: (house) cleaning, 4 employees, sole trader, can help share her workload.

text: Explain two factors Gloria should consider when deciding whether to take on a business partner.
context: Gloria is a sole trader (4 employees) wanting to reduce her workload, considering taking on a business partner. Plans to expand into a repair service.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 factors = 6 marks). Factors: Have to share responsibilities/management/control of the cleaning business, which could lead to conflict; Offer skills (or examples of), which could lead to business opportunities such as the repair service; May offer experience/expertise/knowledge, increasing efficiency to help reduce the workload; Access to finance/capital, so can grow faster/upgrade equipment, making it easier to expand; Different objectives/ways of working, which could lead to slower decision-making/conflict; Whether want to share decision-making/take longer to make decisions, but may lead to better decisions; Someone to share risk/losses/costs; Whether wants/have to share any profit compared to staying as a sole trader. Application words: (house) cleaning, expand/repair service, 4 employees, effective communication is important, reduce her workload, sole trader, market research.

text: Explain two methods of primary market research a business could use to find out the demand for a new product or service. Which would be the best method to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Gloria plans to carry out some market research.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. (Postal) questionnaire/survey: Customer opinions/preferences/suggestions can be gathered; Large amounts of information can be collected; Detailed information can be gathered; Questions may be poorly worded; People may not tell the truth; Customers may not return questionnaires. Online survey: Data quickly presented/analysed using IT tools; Fast response time; Cheaper than interviews/postal questionnaire; No representative needed. Interview: Allows for detailed information; can explain questions; interviewer bias possible; expensive; time consuming. Focus group: highly detailed responses; chance to ask follow-up questions; group members can influence others; expensive; time consuming. Observation: seeing what people do can be more accurate than what they say; more expensive. Test marketing: cost of mistake limited to small output; takes longer for final product to reach market. Justification must compare two methods — e.g. a focus group might be better because the ability to ask follow-up questions is important especially when offering a new product, so the extra detail could allow more informed decisions.

text: Define 'import tariff'.
context: VVA manufactures school backpacks (bags) in country X, uses retailers as its channel of distribution, imports 45% of its raw materials.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): A tax placed on imported goods when they arrive into a country. OR A specific form of tax imposed on imported goods. Partial (1 mark): Type of tax, OR tax on imported goods. First mark for understanding it is a tax.

text: Identify two reasons why some markets can become more competitive.
context: The Managing Director knows there are many factors that can affect demand including how competitive the market is.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two responses. Reasons: Globalisation/free trade; Internet/ecommerce/social media/developments in technology; Improvements in transport/infrastructure; New legal controls/provide grants/removal of tariffs/quotas; Increase in competitors. Do not award factors affecting demand/spending patterns e.g. changes in population, advertising, or actions of competitors.

text: State the four stages of the business cycle.
context: The Managing Director knows there are many factors that can affect demand including the stage of the business cycle.
ms: 1 mark per stage (max 4). Stages: Recession; (Economic) growth; Boom; Slump/depression. The order does not matter.

text: Explain one possible effect of the following changes on VVA when importing raw materials: Introduction of import quotas in country X AND Appreciation of country X's exchange rate.
context: VVA manufactures school backpacks, imports 45% of raw materials. The Managing Director is worried that import tariffs, import quotas, and an appreciation in the exchange rate will affect VVA.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per change (max 6 marks). Import quotas: Limit/reduce the amount of imports as import 45% of these, which could reduce output/may have to find more (local) suppliers; May mean have to find local/alternative suppliers, leading to increase time/cost; Fewer imports possible, leading to fewer (potential) sales; Lower production. Appreciation of exchange rate: Imports become cheaper, reducing VVA's costs of its school bags; Imports become cheaper, so may be able to lower prices; Lower import price, so could increase its profit margin; Imports become cheaper, so can import more; Can import more (materials), so can increase output. Application words: school backpacks/bags, 45% (raw materials)/55% locally, retailers, increased level of competition. Do not award tariff as application.

text: Do you think retailers are the best channel of distribution for a manufacturing business to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. VVA uses retailers as its channel of distribution.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Retailers: Wide distribution/access to customers/sell in different places, increase sales/revenue; Retailers will carry out/pay for advertising/promotional activities, raise awareness/increase sales; Can sell in large quantities/higher sales; Manufacturer can hold less inventory, lower storage costs; Price may be higher, leading to fewer sales; No direct contact with customers, so difficult to build/maintain customer relationship; Loss of (some) control of marketing mix; Retailer takes some of the profit, which reduces profit margin. Other options: sell direct/online — all profit goes to manufacturer, can sell at a lower price, but increased delivery costs and may need extra workers. Wholesalers — buy in bulk, saves storage space, but loss of control over marketing mix and takes part of the profit. Agents — have local market knowledge. Points must focus on viewpoint of manufacturing business. Justification: e.g. retailers offer a wide distribution which can help increase potential sales, whereas selling direct means keeping all the profit — selling to retailers is better as the high sales will increase total revenue, offsetting the lower profit margin.

text: Define 'retained profit'.
context: CPF is a clothing retailer, a private limited company with 4 shops and 30 employees. The amount of retained profit is low.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Profit (left, or) reinvested back into the business, (after all payments have been made). OR Profit (remaining after all expenses, tax and dividends have been paid), which is ploughed back into the business. Partial (1 mark): Profit/money to reinvest, OR profit left after dividends/shareholders paid.

text: Define 'current assets'.
context: CPF's Finance Director is concerned about the amount of current assets because working capital is important.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Items owned by/belong to business and used within one year. OR Resources that the business owns and expects to convert into cash before the date of the next statement of financial position. Partial (1 mark): Items in the business for less than one year/12 months/within a financial year, OR assets owned.

text: Outline two possible reasons why working capital is important for CPF.
context: CPF is a clothing retailer, a private limited company, 4 shops, 30 employees. Retained profit is low. Directors are planning to expand by opening a new shop.
ms: 1 mark per reason + 1 mark application (max 2 reasons = 4 marks). Reasons: To pay day-to-day expenses/(short term) debts or examples such as pay wages for its 30 employees; To pay for unexpected expenses/emergencies, especially as the business is looking to expand; To ensure the business has a good credit reputation for the 4 shops; Ensures the business can take advantage of special offers/discounts on bulk purchases of its clothes; To cope with seasonal demand. Application words: (4) shops/retailer/stores, 30 (employees), clothes, private limited company, plans to expand, retained profit is low.

text: Explain one way each of the following stakeholder groups might be affected by CPF's plans to expand its business: Employees AND Suppliers.
context: CPF is a clothing retailer, a private limited company, 4 shops, 30 employees, planning to expand by opening a new shop, which will affect many stakeholder groups.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per stakeholder (max 6 marks). Employees: Opportunities for promotion for the 30 employees, so may be able to benefit from higher wages; Work extra hours at the new shop, so gain extra payments/which may lead to mistakes; Greater variety/different tasks/work to do, making the work more interesting/less boring; More job security, increasing motivation; Employees may have to move location, so long time to get to work/travel costs increase. Suppliers: Additional orders/sales/produce more of clothing, leading to additional revenue; Security/certainty of regular orders, so able to plan effectively; May struggle to meet extra demand; May have to distribute goods to a new area, increasing transport costs. Application words: (4/new) shops/retailer/stores, 30 (employees), clothes, private limited company, low retained profit.

text: Do you think it is better for a private limited company to use debt (e.g. a loan) or equity (issuing more shares) as a source of long-term finance? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. CPF needs a suitable source of long-term finance for its expansion.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Debt: May be difficult to raise additional finance if banks/suppliers concerned about ability to repay existing loans; No change of ownership, so lenders have no say in decisions; Can receive all the money at once; Must pay interest, which increases costs/cash flow problems; Need to repay; Need security, which can lose if unable to repay. Equity/issue shares: No interest/finance costs to pay, so no extra cash outflows; Permanent source of capital/no need to repay; Can only sell to friends and family/small number of shareholders, which can limit the amount of capital raised; Dividends expected/paid to shareholders, so less retained profit; Give up some ownership. Justification: e.g. equity is better because if the business has financial difficulties, debt is still expected to be repaid, which increases the risk of business failure.

text: Define 'specialisation'.
context: WLT manufactures carpets, exports 40% of its products, uses specialisation, 60 employees, quality assurance is important.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): When people/businesses/countries concentrate on what they are best at. OR Focusing an individual or group on one particular skill or process that they are suited to or for which they possess the correct skills. OR Way in which work is divided so each worker concentrates on a specific task (1) so they become expert at it (1). Partial (1 mark): Workers do only one job.

text: Identify two methods of production.
context: WLT's directors are considering the best way to increase efficiency, its method of production allows WLT to use specialisation.
ms: 1 mark per method (max 2). Only award first two responses. Two from: Job (production); Batch (production); Flow/mass (production). Do not award lean production or cell production.

text: Outline two advantages to WLT of using quality assurance.
context: WLT manufactures carpets, exports 40%, uses specialisation, 60 employees, quality assurance is important.
ms: 1 mark per advantage + 1 mark application (max 2 advantages = 4 marks). Advantages: Reduces faults/errors at all stages of production/fewer mistakes when making carpets; Less waste/less rework (of faulty products), which could help improve efficiency; Encourages teamwork which may motivate workers among its 60 employees; Fewer customer complaints/fewer customer returns/replacements; Better brand image/improve/maintain reputation; Reduce inspection costs/do not need to hire inspectors; Allows business to know at what stage mistakes happen. Application words: carpets, 40%/exported, globalisation, specialisation, 60 (employees), efficiency, manufactures/production. Do not award improve customer satisfaction, better quality, increase sales, lower cost on its own, or encourages teamwork/motivation on its own.

text: Explain one opportunity and one threat of globalisation for WLT.
context: WLT manufactures carpets, exports 40% of its products, globalisation has created opportunities and threats, uses specialisation, 60 employees.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per opportunity AND threat (max 6 marks). Opportunities: Increase potential sales/access to more markets, as it exports 40% of its products, increasing revenue; Cheaper raw materials from other countries to manufacture, which can improve the profit margin; Labour may be cheaper, reducing (labour) costs; Economies of scale or relevant examples; Global brands are more recognised/desirable. Threats: Increased competition, leading to a reduction in market share; Employees may leave if WLT cannot pay as much as international competitors, so may lose some of its 60 employees, increasing recruitment costs; Over dependent on supplies from other countries. Application words: carpets, 40%/exported, specialisation, 60 (employees), efficiency, manufactures/production. Accept sales as either knowledge or analysis but not both.

text: Do you think improving labour skills is the best way for a manufacturing business to increase efficiency? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. WLT's directors are considering the best way to increase efficiency.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Improving labour skills: Able to work faster, which will increase output per worker; Fewer mistakes are made, leading to less rework/wastage; Training takes employees time, which will lower output in the short-term; Increase training costs, which will increase unit costs; Workers are more versatile/flexible. Other ways: Automation/machinery allows operation with fewer employees; Lean production/Just-in-time/Kaizen, therefore lower cost per unit; Improved motivation or methods of motivating e.g. piece rate. Do not award increased productivity, profitability, lower cost, or more output as analysis on its own. Justification: e.g. improving labour skills is best because automation could lead to redundancies which may demotivate remaining employees, potentially leading to less output overall.

text: Identify two reasons why a business might have cash-flow problems.
context: LMA is a family-owned restaurant, started 20 years ago, remained small, a partnership. The Finance Manager is analysing LMA's cash-flow forecast.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two responses. Reasons: Too much inventory; Growing too quickly/overtrading; Allow customers/trade receivables too long to pay; Paying suppliers/trade payables too quickly; Seasonal/low demand; Poor (financial) planning.

text: Calculate X and Y.
context: LMA's cash-flow forecast ($000): July: Cash inflow 420, Cash outflow 410, Net cash flow X, Opening 60, Closing 70. August: Cash inflow 300, Cash outflow 320, Net cash flow (20), Opening 70, Closing 50. September: Cash inflow 330, Cash outflow 360, Net cash flow (30), Opening 50, Closing Y.
ms: 1 mark per correct calculation (max 2). X = $10,000 or 10. Y = $20,000 or 20. $ sign not required.

text: Identify four examples of a cash inflow.
context: LMA is a family-owned restaurant, a partnership, considering whether to become a private limited company.
ms: 1 mark per example (max 4). Only award first four responses. Examples: (Cash) sales/revenue; Payments from trade receivables/money from credit sales; Grants; Bank loan; Sponsorship; Sale of non-current assets; Funds from investors/share issue/capital introduced by owner; Dividends from shares in other companies; Interest received from savings/bonds/investments. Do not award trade receivables alone.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to LMA of becoming a private limited company.
context: LMA is a family-owned restaurant, started 20 years ago, remained small, a partnership. The partners are considering whether LMA should become a private limited company.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantages: Limited liability, so personal assets are not at risk/only liable for the amount invested; Separate legal identity, so the owners are not held responsible for the actions of the business, which is not true for a partnership; Able to raise finance by selling shares to fund expansion if the business decides it does not want to remain small; Continuity; Can choose who buys shares. Disadvantages: More legal formalities, which takes time away from other activities in the restaurant; Separation of ownership and control, so the owners may not be involved/agree with business decisions taken as the directors may not listen to the family; Expensive/time consuming to change to this form of business organisation; Accounts must be made available; Dividends may be paid, reducing retained profit. Application words: restaurant, partnership, remain small, 20 years ago, family(-owned).

text: Explain two reasons why a business might remain small. Which reason is likely to be most important? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. LMA is a family-owned restaurant that has remained small.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Reasons: Access to capital/lack of finance, which makes it difficult to fund expansion/working capital; Small market, so there is not sufficient demand; Lack of skills/knowledge to expand/larger business more difficult to manage, so more likely to make mistakes if expand; Lack of workers; Type of industry/service industries (offer a personal service)/specialised products where close contact may be needed; Personal objectives/owner's objectives or example such as better communication with customers, keeping control, which might help retain/increase customer loyalty; Market dominated/controlled by a few large competitors, so will struggle to attract more customers. Justification: e.g. the size of the market is more important because without customers there is no revenue, which is likely to reduce the need for finance anyway.

text: Define 'job description'.
context: DZD is a large parcel delivery business, many part-time employees, planning to expand, recruiting 60 new employees. The HR Director is preparing a job description.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Outlines the responsibilities and duties to be carried out by someone employed to do a specific job. OR A list of the key points about a job, job title, key duties, responsibilities, and accountabilities. OR A description of the tasks, role, and responsibilities of a particular position. OR What the job entails/explains the job with a list of suitable content. Partial (1 mark): What they must do in a job/list of content.

text: Identify two levels from Maslow's hierarchy of needs.
context: DZD's HR Director is considering using Maslow's hierarchy of needs to increase motivation.
ms: 1 mark per level (max 2). Only award first two responses. Two from: Physiological/physical; Safety/security; Social/(love and) belonging; Esteem; Self-actualisation. Do not award examples such as job security, or vague answers like 'psychological' or 'basic needs'.

text: Outline two factors DZD should consider when deciding which applicants to recruit.
context: DZD is a large parcel delivery business, planning to expand, recruiting 60 new employees and 20 new vehicles. Many employees work part-time.
ms: 1 mark per factor + 1 mark application (max 2 factors = 4 marks). Factors: Experience of delivering parcels; Qualifications or relevant examples such as a driving licence to drive the (20) vehicles; Skills or examples such as good at communication as will work in a large business; Whether they match the requirements of business/job or examples such as physical ability/know the area, willing to work part-time; Whether they match the culture of the business; Performance during interview/testing; Age; References. Application words: delivery business or examples such as parcels, 60 employees, large business, (20) vehicles, part-time, planning to expand, Maslow, human resource director.

text: Explain two sources of finance DZD might use for the new vehicles.
context: DZD is a large parcel delivery business, planning to expand, has to decide on a suitable source of finance for 20 new vehicles, will also recruit 60 new employees.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 sources = 6 marks). Sources: Bank loan, as able to purchase immediately so there is no delay to the planned expansion; Retained profit, as it's a large business, no need to repay; Leasing of the 20 vehicles, as do not need to make a large initial payment; Hire purchase; Grant; Selling of assets; Owner's capital/share issue; Debenture; Crowdfunding. Application words: delivery business or examples such as parcels, planning to expand/expansion, large business, 20 (vehicles). Do not award 'vehicles' as application as stated in question. Do not award short-term options such as overdraft.

text: Do you think a service business should only employ part-time workers? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Many of DZD's employees work part-time.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Part-time: When not working no need to pay wages, helping to reduce labour costs; Need to recruit/train more employees, taking more time/money; Could allow the business to recruit wider range of skills; More flexible hours/less likely to take time off for appointments; Easier to extend worker hours at busy times; Some employees may not be willing/want part-time jobs, so may miss out on possible candidates if not offered full-time option. Full-time: Able to offer consistency of service, so could improve reputation/increase customers; Workers may be committed to business, which could increase productivity; Easier to communicate/update; Less workers needed. Focus should be on benefit/cost to the business not the worker. Justification: e.g. a service sector business should not have only part-time employees as service quality is vital for customer loyalty and therefore sales.

text: Identify two factors that might affect the accuracy of market research.
context: NLR manufactures branded skincare products including hand cream. The Marketing Director is analysing market research data.
ms: 1 mark per factor (max 2). Only award first two responses. Factors: Sample size; Sample chosen/who is asked; Interviewer experience/interviewer bias; Wording of the questions; Who carried out research; Age of information/when data gathered/information might be out of date; People's actions do not always match what they say; Anonymity; Bots or use of AI.

text: Identify two benefits to a business of using market segmentation.
context: NLR makes use of market segmentation for its skincare products.
ms: 1 mark per benefit (max 2). Only award first two responses. Benefits: Able to tailor goods to specific needs of segment/know what to produce; Identify gaps in the market; Help decide best place to sell; Research is simpler; Help focus spending/make best use of resources; Help target promotion/advertising; Help set prices; Help increase sales/revenue.

text: Outline two ways NLR might respond to environmental pressures.
context: NLR manufactures branded skincare products including hand cream. Market research shows 85% of consumers expect businesses to respond to environmental pressures.
ms: 1 mark per way + 1 mark application (max 2 ways = 4 marks). Ways: Reduce amount of materials used/wastage when making its skincare products; Use recycled materials for the packaging; Develop environmentally friendly products based on its market research; Buy energy efficient/environmentally friendly machinery/use renewable energy; Offer different sizes/only make to order/reduce number of products available; Alter/reduce transport use; Promote/support environmentally friendly causes; Ask customers to reuse containers (when buying from shops) as 85% of consumers want this. Application words: skincare or examples such as hand cream, packaging, 85% of consumers/customers, product life cycle, market research, branded. Do not award environmental pressures as application on its own.

text: Explain how NLR's pricing decisions might be affected at two different stages of the product life cycle.
context: NLR manufactures branded skincare products including hand cream, packaging is important. The Marketing Director knows the stage of the product life cycle can influence pricing decisions.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per stage (max 6 marks). Points: During introductory stage, the business may set a low price to attract customers to their hand cream; At growth stage, prices may be lowered due to increased competition; At maturity stage, price is likely to be similar to competitors to retain market share for the branded products; During decline stage, discounts might be offered to maintain sales/sell remaining inventory; Skimming pricing can be used at introductory stage to recover development costs of new packaging; Penetration pricing in some market segments; Cost plus pricing; Competitive pricing; Promotional pricing. Application words: skincare or examples such as hand cream, 85%, market research, packaging, environmental pressures, branded (product), market segmentation.

text: Do you think promoting the brand image is the most important role of packaging? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Packaging of NLR's products is important.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: This can help the product attract customers/stand out against competitor's products, which can help increase/maintain sales, leading to higher revenue; Protect the product, so the product does not get damaged/can be kept fresh, which can help reduce wastage; Ease of storage/transport, which could lead to lower storage/transport costs; Provide information about the product; Legal requirements, as a business might have to identify the ingredients to avoid legal action; Easy to open the container and use the product. Justification: e.g. protecting the product is the most important role because damaged goods will not sell — brand image is not the most important role although customers need to be aware of the product in order to buy it.

text: Define 'inflation'.
context: HCB manufactures cars in country X, 200 employees, changed its method of production due to new technology. The interest rate in country X has increased due to rising inflation.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): An increase in the general price level of goods and services over time. Partial (1 mark): An increase in the price of goods/services. For both marks must have reference to increase in prices [1] and the time element [+1].

text: Identify two ways technology could change production methods.
context: HCB manufactures cars, has changed its method of production due to new technology.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 2). Only award first two responses. Ways: Wide variety/new products can be designed/made; High/faster output; Fewer mistakes/better quality/more accurate/less waste; Fewer employees/replace labour; Automation/become capital intensive; Mechanisation/use (more) machinery; Computer-aided design (CAD)/3D design; Computer-aided manufacturing (CAM)/3D printing/robotics; Computer-integrated manufacturing (CIM).

text: Outline two ways HCB could become more ethical.
context: HCB manufactures cars in country X, 200 employees, the Managing Director is considering ways to become more ethical.
ms: 1 mark per way + 1 mark application (max 2 ways = 4 marks). Ways: Pay fair wages to its 200 employees; Ensure fair working conditions for employees in its factory; Pay suppliers on time when buying materials for its cars; Pay fair price to suppliers; Charge customers fair prices/not fix prices with competitors; Source environmentally friendly materials/less pollution/not dump waste/use renewable energy (allow only once). Application words: cars, factory, 200 employees, new technology/changed production method.

text: Explain two ways HCB could be affected by an increase in the interest rate in country X.
context: HCB manufactures cars in country X, 200 employees. The interest rate in country X has increased due to rising inflation.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 ways = 6 marks). Ways: Increase costs of finance/borrowing, so less cash/funds to spend on other areas of the business such as becoming more ethical; Decreased demand/fewer sales, which could lower revenue from its cars; More difficult to get/more expensive to take out a loan for the factory, which could delay investment; Delay investment into new technology, so may become less competitive. Application words: cars, factory, 200 employees, new technology/change production method, (more) ethical.

text: Do you think manufacturing businesses will always benefit from the introduction of import tariffs? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. HCB is aware other businesses in country X have started to import cars.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: Higher costs of importing raw materials, which could lead to higher prices/lower profit margin/need to find new suppliers locally; May increase price of imported finished goods, which may lead to fewer sales/less revenue/increase demand for locally made products; Other countries may retaliate/introduce import tariffs, making it more difficult to export. Justification: e.g. whether businesses benefit is likely to depend on the proportion of raw materials which are imported, especially if there are no alternative local suppliers, it is more likely to be negatively affected.

text: Identify two possible causes of business failure.
context: WFH produces hats and sells to a mass market, holds a high level of inventory. The Managing Director thinks the business might fail.
ms: 1 mark per cause (max 2). Only award first two responses. Causes: Poor planning/lack of objectives; Cash flow problems/lack of working capital; Poor management skills/lack experience/lack of knowledge; Overexpansion/business expands too quickly; Lack of demand/sales/(too much) competition; Poor marketing; Economic influences/changes in business environment.

text: Calculate WFH's acid test ratio for 2022. Show your working.
context: WFH's financial statements ($000): 2022 — Current assets 50, Inventory 30, Trade receivables 10, Cash 10, Current liabilities 40, Loss (10).
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): 0.5:1. Method: (Current assets − inventory) ÷ current liabilities = (50,000 − 30,000)/40,000 (1 mark). Where 0.5 is shown with no working, can award two marks.

text: Identify four reasons why businesses hold inventory.
context: WFH produces hats, sells to a mass market, holds a high level of inventory.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 4). Only award first four responses. Reasons: To maintain production; To protect against delays from suppliers; To benefit from economies of scale; To benefit from special offers/supplier discounts; To reduce transport costs; To meet unexpected changes in demand/sudden order; To meet seasonal changes in demand; To meet orders/meet (high) demand.

text: Explain why the following two stakeholder groups might be interested in WFH's financial statements: Employees AND Suppliers.
context: WFH produces hats, sells to a mass market, holds a high level of inventory. Financial statements show falling profit turning to a loss in 2022. Other stakeholder groups might be interested in WFH's financial statements.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per stakeholder (max 6 marks). Employees: To know if they have job security/whether made redundant as profit is falling, so may decide to look for jobs elsewhere; To know if they will receive wage payments on time as there is less cash in the business, so may not be able to cover basic needs/better standard of living; To know whether to ask for a pay rise when making hats, they might look at the level of profit. Suppliers: To see current level of debt, to help decide whether to give/extend trade credit for materials needed for the hats; To see level of cash/liquidity, to know whether they will receive payments on time; To know whether will receive payment on time, as if not may stop supplying especially as WFH might fail; Assess level of sales, as high/low may lead to additional/fewer orders. Application words: hats, 15,000/10,000/cash has decreased, ($10,000)/loss, 50,000/60,000 (current assets), high levels of inventory, 30,000/20,000/10,000 increase (inventory), 0.5 (acid test ratio, OFR applies), mass market, business might fail.

text: Do you think it is always better for a business to sell to a mass market? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. WFH produces hats and sells them to a mass market.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Mass marketing: (Potential for) high sales/customers, increases revenue; Benefit from economies of scale, so lower average/unit costs; Spreads risk, so falling sales in one area may be offset by sales elsewhere; High levels of competition, may mean have to lower prices. Niche marketing: May be possible to charge higher prices, which can increase profit margin; Able to closely meet customer needs, could lead to high customer loyalty; Opportunity to earn higher profits might attract new competitors, so prices may have to be reduced. Justification: e.g. it is better for a business to operate in a mass market because lower average costs may allow lower prices which is likely to attract more customers, meaning a higher overall amount of revenue than possible in a niche market.

text: Identify two responsibilities of supervisors.
context: AH is an insurance business operating in a competitive market, 1000 employees including 50 supervisors who use an autocratic leadership style.
ms: 1 mark per responsibility (max 2). Only award first two responses. Responsibilities: Provide feedback/report to managers (on progress/issues); Give out tasks/orders (to employees); Make sure employees carry out tasks; Check/monitor quality of work/product; Check workers are being efficient.

text: Identify two methods of written communication.
context: The Managing Director is considering how to communicate with AH's employees about a planned takeover.
ms: 1 mark per method (max 2). Only award first two responses. Methods: Letter; Notice/notice board; Text; Memo; Email; Newsletter; Website; Social media/Facebook/WhatsApp; Billboards/posters; Leaflets/flyer; (Local/national) newspapers; (Specialist/general) magazines.

text: Outline two benefits to AH of taking over a competitor.
context: AH is an insurance business, competitive market, 5% market share, 1000 employees, 50 supervisors, planning to take over a competitor.
ms: 1 mark per benefit + 1 mark application (max 2 benefits = 4 marks). Benefits: Increase in market share from 5%; Benefit from economies of scale in the competitive market; Power to set/influence market prices for insurance; Gain brand name of competitor; Gain skills/resources (from other business); Protection from risk of takeover. Application words: insurance, 5% (market share), 1000 employees, 50 supervisors, competitive market.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to AH of its supervisors using an autocratic leadership style.
context: AH is an insurance business, competitive market, 5% market share, 1000 employees, 50 supervisors using autocratic leadership style, planning to take over a competitor.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantages: Quick/faster decision-making, so can respond to opportunities sooner such as taking over a competitor; Do not need to consult with employees, leading to quicker decision-making; Decisions are made by (more) experienced workers, so less chance of mistakes in the insurance business.
