Disadvantages: Demotivate employees from the 1000/950 employees, leading to higher labour turnover/because they have no input into decisions; Supervisors have less time to focus on other tasks, leading to lower productivity/as employees are closely monitored; Lack of ideas from employees. Application words: insurance business, 1000/950 employees, 50 (supervisors), take over a competitor, competitive market, 5% (market share), methods of communication.

text: Explain two sources of finance which could be used to fund business growth. Which source of finance would be the best to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. There are many sources of finance available to fund business growth.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. (Bank) loan: Can receive all the money at once; (Long time to) repay; Need to pay interest, which can increase costs. Retained profit: No repayment costs; May not be enough funds available. Sell shares/share issue: No need to repay/permanent source of capital; Will dilute ownership/lead to loss of control; Shareholders may expect dividends. Sell (unwanted) non-current assets. Justification: e.g. a bank loan is the best source because there may not be sufficient retained profit which may delay the expansion.

text: Identify two ways legal controls could affect marketing strategy.
context: Viktor is starting up a business as a photographer, a sole trader. There are legal controls which could affect his marketing strategy.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 2). Only award first two responses. Ways: Cannot make misleading/false claims in advertisements/may have to change/withdraw/restrict how or where advertise/promote; Increase costs/time (spent on marketing); May have to change what is written on packaging/make sure product description is accurate/not misleading; Could lead to restrictions about where they can sell it; Cannot sell underweight goods; Goods must be fit for purpose; Cannot charge less than minimum price set/more than maximum price set/cannot fix prices (with competitors).

text: Define 'quality control'.
context: Viktor is starting up a photography business, quality control will be important.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Checking for quality at the end of the production process. OR Checking the quality of goods through inspection. Partial (1 mark): Checking the (standard/quality of) work.

text: Outline two reasons why Viktor might use sampling when carrying out market research.
context: Viktor is starting up a business as a photographer, a sole trader, plans to use sampling when carrying out market research, will employ 5 photographers.
ms: 1 mark per reason + 1 mark application (max 2 reasons = 4 marks). Reasons: Cheaper (than researching the whole market), which is important for a start-up business; Quicker (than researching the whole market), to find out what photography customers want. Application words: start-up, photography, 5 employees, sole trader.

text: Explain two disadvantages to Viktor of operating as a sole trader.
context: Viktor is starting up a business as a photographer, a sole trader, will employ 5 photographers, plans market research and knows about ways to motivate employees.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 disadvantages = 6 marks). Disadvantages: Difficult to raise capital, which could restrict growth of the photography business; Unlimited liability of his start-up business, so his personal assets are at risk if he cannot pay debts; Has all the responsibility/make decisions on own, so may lead to wrong decisions being taken; May have to work long hours; Business does not have a separate legal identity; No continuity of business/if he dies, the business will close; No one to share risks/losses with. Application words: photography, start-up/new business, 5 employees, (carry out) market research, motivate employees, legal controls (over marketing).

text: Explain two ways a service business could motivate its employees. Which would be the best way to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Viktor knows there are many ways to motivate employees.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Ways: Bonus, employees will try to achieve targets set; Job rotation, as variety can make the work more interesting; Job enrichment, as employees feel they are being given more responsibility; Training, so employees have a higher level of skills; Increase wage (rate), increases business costs; Profit sharing, which only pays if a profit is made; Praise, no cost/free; Commission, employees will have an incentive to try to sell more products; Opportunities for promotion. Justification: e.g. job rotation is best as the flexible workforce means services can still be offered when other employees are absent, which could still help the business achieve its targets.

text: Define 'primary sector'.
context: NFF is a fishing business which catches fish and other seafood, in the primary sector, 6 fishing boats and 36 employees. Contributing to sustainable development is important. NFF has a high level of debt.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Businesses/firms whose business activity involves the extraction of raw materials. OR Extracts and uses the natural resources of the earth to produce raw materials used by other businesses. Partial (1 mark): Involves natural resources, OR generates/produces raw materials. Do not award examples.

text: Calculate the value of NFF's current liabilities. Show your working.
context: NFF's statement of financial position at 30 Sept 2022 ($000): Trade payables 60, Trade receivables 50, Overdraft 20, Bank loan 200.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): $80,000. Method: Trade payables + overdraft = 60,000 + 20,000 (1 mark). Award 1 mark where $80,000 is shown as part of the answer but not given as the final answer.

text: Outline two internal sources of finance NFF might use.
context: NFF is a fishing business, 6 boats, 36 employees, has a high level of debt. Jennifer wants to know about internal sources of finance.
ms: 1 mark per source + 1 mark application (max 2 sources = 4 marks). Sources: (Retained) profit from the fishing business; Sale of (existing) non-current/fixed assets as has 6 boats; Owner's savings/sell own assets to help reduce the high level of debt; Sale of current assets/inventories/reduce inventory levels; Ask customers to pay more quickly. Application words: fish/seafood/fishing, 6 boats, $50,000 (trade receivables), $60,000 (trade payables), $200,000 (bank loan)/high level of debt.

text: Explain two possible problems for NFF of having a high level of debt.
context: NFF is a fishing business, 6 boats, 36 employees, contributing to sustainable development is important, has a high level of debt.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 problems = 6 marks). Problems: Difficult to arrange (additional) finance, may be difficult to expand so may not contribute to sustainable development; Amount/high level of interest, especially as already have $200,000 in bank loans, increasing expenses/cash outflows; May struggle/cannot meet repayments, leading to liquidity problems; Increase financial risk when buying boats, so bank may not be willing to lend extra funds. Application words: fish/seafood, 6 fishing boats, 36 employees, $200,000 (bank loan), $20,000 (overdraft), $50,000 (trade receivables), $60,000 (trade payables), sustainable development.

text: Explain two ways a business in the primary sector might contribute to sustainable development. Which do you think is the best way? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. NFF operates in the primary sector.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Ways: Reduce/limit the number of raw materials extracted/harvested, so more left for future use but could reduce potential sales; Buy energy efficient machinery/electric vehicles, but high initial cost the business might not be able to afford; Use renewable energy, as this conserves finite (limited) resources; Recycle, which helps reduce number of materials needed/less waste; Reuse materials; Replant trees/restore land to nature after use. Justification: e.g. electric vehicles are better because harvesting less could be difficult for sectors such as farming who need to provide sufficient food to meet people's basic needs, whereas changing to electric vehicles can still mean fewer finite resources are gathered but helps the current population survive.

text: Define 'limited company'.
context: GBR manufactures shoes, produces 18,000 pairs weekly, a limited company, main objective is to increase profit, 450 employees, does not export.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): A business which has a separate legal identity/status to its owners. Partial (1 mark): A business that can sell shares, OR benefit from limited liability. Features of a limited company - max 1 mark.

text: Outline two reasons why having objectives might be important for a business.
context: GBR's main objective is to increase profit, which can conflict with other stakeholder groups.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two responses. Reasons: A clear target/aim/purpose to work towards/guides the business in the right direction; Help provide focus for decision making; Helps motivate employees; Allows measurement of success/can judge performance/track progress.

text: Outline two opportunities of globalisation for GBR.
context: GBR manufactures shoes, produces 18,000 pairs weekly, limited company, 450 employees, does not export, directors interested in opportunities of globalisation.
ms: 1 mark per opportunity + 1 mark application (max 2 opportunities = 4 marks). Opportunities: Increase potential sales/access to more markets, which could help achieve its profit objective; Increase brand awareness, as does not currently export; Spread risk when making its shoes; Access to cheaper labour, as currently has 450 employees; Access to cheaper materials, to make 18,000 pairs (per week). Application words: shoes, 18,000 pairs per week, 450 employees, limited company, does not export, objective is profit.

text: Explain how one objective for each of the following stakeholder groups might conflict with GBR's objective to increase profit: Employees AND Suppliers.
context: GBR's main objective is to increase profit. This can conflict with those of other stakeholder groups including GBR's 450 employees.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per stakeholder (max 6 marks). Employees: May want higher/high pay for its 450 employees, which could lead to higher costs; May want job security, especially with globalisation, but GBR might want to make some redundant; Safe working conditions; Job satisfaction/motivation/training/promotion. Suppliers: Might want to charge higher prices for materials for the shoes whereas GBR might want to use its power to reduce prices (to increase profit margin); Increased/regular number of orders but GBR might want to reduce orders; Receive prompt payment for goods supplied but this could increase cash outflows/lead to liquidity problems; To be treated fairly. Application words: shoes, 18,000 pairs per week, 450 employees, limited company, does not export, globalisation.

text: Do you think the size of the market is the most important factor for a business to consider when deciding on a method of production? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Size of the market: If high level of demand needs to be able to produce a lot, otherwise risk losing sales. Other factors: Capital available/cost, as business might not be able to afford machinery needed for some methods; Type/variety/nature of product, as if the product is unique then do not need to produce on large scale; Availability of suitable employees; Factory space/storage space available. Justification: e.g. type of product is more important because if the product is unique then do not need to produce on large scale — the business has limited choice about the method it can use, and if it cannot produce a product that meets customer needs, the size of market doesn't really matter.

text: Identify two reasons why people work.
context: MDL is a hotel with 160 rooms, 600 employees, plans to recruit 20 new employees. The HR Manager knows there are many reasons why people work.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two responses. Reasons: To earn money/pay for basic needs; Job satisfaction/feeling you have done a good job; Safety/security or examples such as knowing job is safe; Social or examples such as feel part of a group; Esteem/recognition/status; Opportunity to reach your potential/challenge yourself/learn new skills/gain experience; Help others/society.

text: Define 'trade union'.
context: MDL is a hotel with 160 rooms, 600 employees. Trade union membership will be encouraged for new employees.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Group of workers who join together to ensure their interests are protected. OR Organisation that represents the workers and fights for improvements to pay and conditions. Partial (1 mark): Group of people who act together to protect their rights.

text: Identify the four stages of the business cycle.
context: The HR Manager said difficulty finding people to work at the hotel could be because of the stage of the business cycle.
ms: 1 mark per stage (max 4). Only award first four responses. Stages: Recession; Slump; Growth; Boom. Can award alternatives to 'slump' — downturn or depression.

text: Explain one benefit and one limitation for MDL of using induction training.
context: MDL is a hotel with 160 rooms, 600 employees, plans to recruit 20 new employees. All new employees will be offered induction training.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per benefit AND limitation (max 6 marks). Benefits: Helps new employees understand/familiarise with the work/workplace/job role, so can help maintain standards in the hotel; May be a legal requirement, so must offer to avoid any fines and possible action by the trade union; Less likely to make mistakes, which can help protect the business reputation. Limitations: Employees are not working but are still being paid, which increases costs of the 20 employees; Delays when employees start their job, so may not be able to operate at full capacity of 160 rooms; Increased costs. Application words: hotel, 160 rooms, 20 employees, business cycle, trade union (membership is encouraged).

text: Explain two stages of the recruitment and selection process that businesses use. Which stage do you think is more important? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. MDL plans to recruit 20 new employees.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Stages: Job analysis — helps work out whether need to recruit someone/tasks and duties can be given to someone else; Job description — provides a clear idea of what job involves, so can help avoid applications from people who cannot do the job; Person/job specification — identifies qualifications/skills/experience needed; Advertising the vacancy — raises awareness of the job, increasing potential applicants; Shortlisting/screening — allows business to reduce number of candidates who will be interviewed; Interview — find out more about candidate's abilities/skills, but time consuming. Justification: e.g. the job description is more important because without knowing what you want the person to do, the business is unlikely to know if it has found a suitable candidate, meaning the money spent on advertising may not be cost effective. Focus should be on the business, not employees.

text: Define 'niche market'.
context: Caleb wants to be an entrepreneur, starting up a business selling handmade furniture including tables and chairs, sold to a niche market.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): A small, usually specialised, segment of a much larger market. Partial (1 mark): Small part/segment of a (large) market, OR part of the market with specific needs/characteristics.

text: Identify two impacts of legal controls on marketing strategy.
context: Caleb knows there are many legal controls that can impact his marketing strategy.
ms: 1 mark per impact (max 2). Only award first two responses. Impacts: Cannot make misleading/false claims in advertisements/adverts may have to be changed or withdrawn/influence where/when/who it can be advertised; Increase costs/time spent on marketing; May have to change what is written on packaging/ensure product description is accurate; Cannot sell underweight goods; Cannot charge less than minimum price set/more than maximum price set/cannot fix prices (with competitors).

text: Outline two reasons why having a good brand image might be important for Caleb's business.
context: Caleb wants to be an entrepreneur, selling handmade furniture (tables, chairs) to a niche market. Having a good brand image will be important.
ms: 1 mark per reason + 1 mark application (max 2 reasons = 4 marks). Reasons: Increase sales/customers of his handmade product; To differentiate the product (from competitors) when using ecommerce; Helps promote/aids recognition of his furniture; Create/maintain customer loyalty/customers will keep buying its products rather than competitors, which could be important for this start-up business; Can charge higher price, helpful as it's a niche market. Application words: furniture or examples such as tables/chairs, handmade, ecommerce, legal controls over marketing, location decision, new/start-up business, niche market.

text: Explain two threats to Caleb's business of using e-commerce to sell his products.
context: Caleb is considering selling his handmade furniture using e-commerce, a niche market, good brand image important.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 threats = 6 marks). Threats: More competition/difficult to stand out from competition, especially as it's a new business, leading to less revenue; No passing trade, so could mean fewer sales, which could influence Caleb's location decision; Not everyone has access to the internet, which reduces its target market for this niche market product; Cost to design/maintain website, increasing cash outflows; Lack of personal service/no face-to-face contact, which might make it difficult to develop brand loyalty, damaging its reputation; Need to pay for pop-ups to advertise on popular sites/feature at top of search engine listings; Risk of hackers/fraud. Application words: (handmade) furniture or examples such as tables/chairs, legal controls over marketing, location decision, new business/start-up, niche market, brand loyalty (is important), entrepreneur.

text: Explain two factors a service business should consider when deciding on a suitable location. Which factor do you think is more important? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Caleb has to decide on a suitable location for the business.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Factors: Availability of suitable premises/cost of site, as high rent will increase (fixed) costs which the business might not be able to afford; Access to customers/demand/sales, to increase revenue; Government influence/grants/legal controls, which may influence or restrict where/how the business can operate; Competitors, where there are many competitors it could mean high footfall; Access to employees, as might need trained workers to offer good level of service/may not be suitable workers nearby. Justification: e.g. access to customers is likely more important as a business has limited influence over the cost of rent whereas it can influence its sales — if it locates where there are many customers, the business has a better chance to gain enough revenue to pay its rent even if this is higher than in quieter locations.

text: Define 'market share'.
context: EQR owns 150 cafes, sells a range of drinks including coffee. Being ethical is important. Objective to increase its 6% market share. Plans to grow by selling franchises for $85,000.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Percentage of total market sales held by one brand/business. OR The revenue of a business expressed as percentage of total market revenue. OR Percentage of total sales that a firm achieves in a market. Partial (1 mark): Share of all sales made, OR percentage of customers/sales a business has.

text: Define 'statement of financial position'.
context: The Managing Director has been analysing EQR's statement of financial position.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Shows the value of a business' assets and liabilities at a particular point in time. OR An accounting statement that records assets, liabilities, and owners' equity/capital of a business at a particular date. Partial (1 mark): Shows assets and liabilities (of a business), OR what a business owns and owes.

text: Outline two ways EQR could increase added value.
context: EQR owns 150 cafes, sells coffee/drinks, being ethical is important, 6% market share, considering ways to increase added value.
ms: 1 mark per way + 1 mark application (max 2 ways = 4 marks). Ways: Increase prices at its cafes; Reduce material/variable costs of coffee; Branding/change packaging, which can also help when selling its franchises; Excellent/better service; Additional product features/improve design; Convenience. Application words: cafes, 150 (locations), coffee/drinks or examples e.g. beans, franchise, ethical, 6% (market share), $85,000.

text: Explain two advantages to EQR of selling franchises as a way to grow its business.
context: EQR owns 150 cafes, being ethical is important, 6% market share, Managing Director plans to grow by selling franchises for $85,000.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 advantages = 6 marks). Advantages: Franchise fee must be paid/licence has to be bought for a cafe, providing funds for investment; Can expand at a faster rate, which can help increase its market share above 6%; Receives royalties/share of (franchisee) profit as well as the $85,000; Not/franchisees responsible for day-to-day management, so have time to focus on other issues such as increasing added value; Increase brand awareness of it being ethical, increasing sales. Application words: cafes, 150 (locations), coffee/drinks or examples e.g. beans, ethical, 6% (market share), $85,000.

text: Do you think a business being ethical will always lead to lower profits? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Being ethical is important to EQR.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: Enhance reputation/brand image, helps attract customers; Customers may pay higher prices, increasing revenue/which could help cover the costs; Can help motivate employees, increasing productivity/reduces absenteeism/lowers labour turnover; Can increase costs, leading to higher prices which may lead to fewer customers/sales; May not be sufficient materials/difficult to find ethical suppliers, reducing output; Ethical suppliers may have higher prices/unethical suppliers may be cheaper. Justification: e.g. being ethical can benefit a business as in the long term this may increase revenue, which could result in higher profit overall, since some customers may be prepared to pay extra for ethical products which can help offset the increased costs.

text: Define 'revenue'.
context: Kemala makes high-quality beauty products, demand for her best-selling hand cream is price inelastic. Revenue $480,000, Gross profit $192,000, Profit for the year $72,000.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Money coming in from selling a product over a given period of time. OR Amount of money a business earns from the sale of its products. OR Income of the business from the sale of goods or services. OR Price × quantity sold. Partial (1 mark): Income of the business.

text: Calculate Kemala's profit margin. Show your working.
context: Kemala's income statement 2021 ($000): Revenue 480, Gross profit 192, Profit for the year 72.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): 15%. Method: Profit ÷ revenue × 100 = 72/480 × 100 (1 mark). If correct answer given with no working shown, award 2 marks. For both marks answer must include %.

text: Outline two reasons why cash is important for Kemala's business.
context: Kemala makes high-quality beauty products, said: 'When I started my business, I did not understand why cash is important.'
ms: 1 mark per reason + 1 mark application (max 2 reasons = 4 marks). Reasons: Pay wages/employees who make the beauty products; Pay suppliers/trade payables to maintain high-quality; Pay expenses/heating/rent/advertising such as in specialist magazines; Repay (short term) debts; For use in an emergency. Application words: beauty products/hand cream, high-quality, $480,000, $192,000, $72,000, specialist/beauty magazine, started her business.

text: Explain two possible reasons why demand for Kemala's best-selling product is price inelastic.
context: Kemala makes high-quality beauty products, demand for her best-selling hand cream is price inelastic, advertises in specialist beauty magazines.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 reasons = 6 marks). Reasons: Unique/no (close) substitutes, as its high-quality, so an increase in price is likely to result in a lower percentage change in demand; Considered a necessity/need, so customers likely to remain brand loyal (even if the price increases) for the hand cream; Low proportion of income spent on product, so customers would still buy (if the price increased), increasing revenue above $480,000. Application words: beauty products/hand cream/skincare, high-quality, $480,000, $72,000.

text: Do you think advertising in specialist magazines is the best way for a business to promote high-quality products? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Kemala advertises her products in specialist beauty magazines.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Specialist magazines: Attract specific customers/target market, increasing sales; Able to use colour/pictures, which can help attract attention; Can keep for future reference; Magazines are often only published once a week/month; Not everyone reads/buys specialist magazines. Other methods: Social media — large potential market/cover wide area/seen by many people; Newspapers — not everyone reads them, so can restrict target market/lead to fewer sales; Leaflets — but people may throw them away/seen as litter. Justification: e.g. social media is a better option as customers can still be targeted but it allows the business to cover many people, building a bigger customer base to maximise potential revenue.

text: Identify two reasons why effective internal communication is important for a business.
context: DBG is a construction company (hospitals, roads, schools), 2000 employees, managers use a democratic leadership style, know effective internal communication is important.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two responses. Reasons: Fewer mistakes/less waste (of resources); Improve efficiency/better productivity/increase output; Improve co-ordination (between departments); Enable faster/better decision-making; Better collaboration between workers/manager; Improve motivation/job satisfaction.

text: Define 'organisational structure'.
context: DBG plans to change its organisational structure, leading to some employees being made redundant.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Refers to the levels of management and division of responsibility within an organisation. OR The formal, internal framework of a business that shows how it is managed and organised. Partial (1 mark): Shows who reports to who.

text: State four factors a business should consider when deciding which employees to make redundant.
context: DBG plans to change its organisational structure, leading to some employees being made redundant.
ms: 1 mark per factor (max 4). Only award first four responses. Factors: Importance of role being performed/whether job still needed; Performance/experience/skills/flexibility/qualities/qualifications; Length of time worked for business/redundancy costs; Attitude/behaviour/attendance/disciplinary record; Wages/salary paid; Which departments need to lose/retain workers; Whether anyone offers/volunteers to leave job.

text: Explain two advantages to DBG of its managers using a democratic leadership style.
context: DBG is a construction company with 2000 employees, managers use a democratic leadership style.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 advantages = 6 marks). Advantages: Employees could be motivated, leading to increase in output/productivity when constructing; Helps keep employee loyalty/lower labour turnover, leading to lower recruitment costs for a business of 2000 employees; Workers may have more experience/understanding of problems, leading to better decisions; More ideas/better communication. Application words: construction/hospitals, roads, or schools, 2000 (employees), organisational structure, redundant.

text: Do you think all businesses benefit from an increase in government spending? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. The Managing Director has to decide how changes in government spending might affect business activity.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: Increase in demand/sales, leading to higher revenue; Can create jobs, so able to maintain/increase output, but may be difficult for some businesses to recruit skilled workers; May have to pay higher taxes (to pay for spending), which increases costs, could delay investment; Obtain grants/subsidies, generating additional funds; Can encourage business start-ups, increasing competition. Justification: e.g. all businesses can benefit — construction businesses are likely to benefit the most from higher revenue when the government builds roads, but other businesses still benefit from better transport links which help all businesses send or receive goods on time.

text: Define 'globalisation'.
context: TYA is a limited company which manufactures 300,000 cars a year, 600 employees, high fixed costs. Globalisation is changing how businesses operate.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Increase in worldwide trade and movement of people and capital between countries. OR Increasing trend for businesses to trade across international boundaries and for people to live/travel to countries that are not their own. OR The process by which countries are connected with each other because of the trade of goods and services. Partial (1 mark): (Increase in) trade of goods and services.

text: Identify two examples of fixed costs.
context: TYA manufactures 300,000 cars a year, has high fixed costs.
ms: 1 mark per example (max 2). Only award first two responses. Examples: Rent/rates; Electricity/gas/heating and lighting/water; Insurance; Loan repayments/interest payments; Storage costs; Marketing costs; Salaries.

text: Outline, with reference to TYA, the difference between a limited company and an unincorporated business.
context: TYA is a limited company which manufactures 300,000 cars a year, 600 employees, high fixed costs, Managing Director wants to improve efficiency.
ms: 1 mark relevant point + 1 mark outlining the difference + 1 mark application (max 2, total max 4). Points: A limited company has separate legal identity, so assets such as the factory and the 600 cars are owned by the business rather than the individual, whereas the owners and the business are the same for an unincorporated business; An unincorporated business has unlimited liability, whereas the risk for shareholders/owners of a limited company is limited to the amount invested in the car business, so they may be less concerned about the high fixed costs; A limited company can sell shares whereas an unincorporated business can find it difficult to raise a large amount of finance; A limited company has continuity. Application words: factory, 600 (employees), 300,000, cars, high fixed costs, improve efficiency, relocate, globalisation.

text: Explain two methods TYA could use to increase efficiency.
context: TYA is a limited company which manufactures 300,000 cars a year, 600 employees, high fixed costs, wants to improve efficiency in the factory.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 methods = 6 marks). Methods: Increase in capital intensity/automation/introduce new technology, increasing output/faster production of cars; Training its 600 employees, so they can work faster/make fewer mistakes/better quality; Introduce just-in-time inventory control, to reduce amount of space needed in the factory; Kaizen, helps reduce waste (of resources), may help lower high fixed costs; Improve layout of machines, so saves time moving between areas; Improve motivation or examples e.g. bonuses; Cell production; Improve quality/quality assurance. Application words: factory, 600 (employees), 300,000 (units), cars, high fixed costs.

text: Do you think legal controls are the most important factor for a manufacturing business to consider when deciding which country to locate its operations in? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Many manufacturing businesses are considering whether to relocate their operations to other countries.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Legal controls: May restrict/not able to locate in certain places, so no output; Business may have to change its production methods, which would increase costs; May restrict amount of goods they can export/import, reducing potential sales. Other factors: Access to suppliers/cheaper sources of materials, would increase transport costs decreasing profit margin; Access to/cost of labour, could lower variable costs; Access to/cost of land, may need a large space, increasing fixed costs; Access to transport networks/power, as poor transport links could delay deliveries/production; Availability of government grants/subsidies. Justification: e.g. legal controls are likely to be most important as the law will stop the factory being built, whereas there are ways to overcome problems caused by access to employees which may increase costs but will still ensure production can take place.

text: Define 'on-the-job training'.
context: SSG manufactures mobile (cell) phones using batch production, quality control is important, 130 employees who all receive on-the-job training. Product X is in the maturity stage.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Training at the place of work, watching or following an experienced employee. OR Training at the place of work — usually the person does the actual job while an experienced employee observes and guides him or her. Partial (1 mark): Training while you are working. Do not award answers which clearly relate to induction. Accept: watching a more experienced worker doing the job.

text: Calculate total variable cost per month. Show your working.
context: SSG's cost and output data for product X: Rent and other expenses per month $300,000, Variable cost per unit $80, Output per month 12,000.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): $960,000. Method: Variable cost per unit × output = $80 × 12,000 (1 mark). Award only 1 mark if $960,000 is written as part of the answer but not given as the final answer. $ sign not required.

text: Identify four factors a business should consider when deciding which method of production to use.
context: SSG manufactures mobile phones using batch production, quality control is important.
ms: 1 mark per factor (max 4). Only award first four responses. Factors: Amount of capital available/costs (of machinery/production); Demand/size of the market/how much they are likely to sell/output needed; Nature/type/variety of goods produced; Amount of suitable space/storage; Access to (suitable/skilled) labour/amount of labour needed. Award 'size of business' with benefit of doubt.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to SSG of using quality control.
context: SSG manufactures mobile phones using batch production, quality control is important, 130 employees, variable cost $80 per unit.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantage: Tries/may eliminate errors before customers receive the product, improving the reputation of its phones; All workers do not need to be trained for quality control, reducing costs of its 130 employees; Production is not slowed. Disadvantage: Inspectors/someone needs to be employed to check the product, increasing labour costs; Faulty products must be scrapped, therefore variable cost is higher than $80 per unit; Does not identify where/why the fault has occurred, so vulnerable to repeating the errors; There is less reason for employees to help ensure quality, leading to more faults in products. Application words: (mobile/cell) phones, 130 employees, on-the-job training, $80, 12,000, $300,000, maturity/extension strategy, batch production.

text: Do you think adding new features to a product is the best extension strategy for a manufacturing business to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Product X is in the maturity stage of the product life cycle so SSG is considering possible extension strategies.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Adding new features: Product appears more appealing, attracting new/more customers, increasing revenue; High cost of development/market research, which the business may not be able to afford; Customers may dislike changes, reducing sales; Adds value to product, therefore can charge a higher price. Other strategies: Finding new markets — widening customer base; Adapt/change the packaging — improving appeal but existing customers may not recognise the product; Increase advertising/marketing/promotion — remind customers the product still exists; Sell through additional outlets. Justification: e.g. finding new markets could increase sales revenue without the risk that customers may not like new features, so it's safer and cheaper.

text: Define 'opportunity cost'.
context: DNG provides electricity to 16 million customers, a limited company, planning to stop using coal, the Managing Director knows there will be an opportunity cost to this change.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): The next best alternative foregone/given up. OR The benefit that could have been gained from an alternative use of the same resource. OR A benefit, profit, or value that a firm gives up in order to achieve something else. Partial (1 mark): What you must give up/forgo.

text: Identify two limitations of using the number of employees to measure the size of a business.
context: DNG is a limited company, 6500 employees, provides electricity to 16 million customers.
ms: 1 mark per limitation (max 2). Only award first two responses. Limitations: Does not account for capital intensive business/depends on method of production used; Could have many part-time employees; May give a different indicator of size to other measures used.

text: Outline how having limited liability might benefit DNG's shareholders.
context: DNG provides electricity to 16 million customers, a limited company which means DNG's shareholders benefit from limited liability.
ms: Up to 2 marks relevant points + up to 2 marks application (total max 4). Points: Shareholders' risk is limited to the amount invested in this electricity business; Protects personal assets in case the business decision to contribute to sustainable development does not work; Encourages (potential/existing) shareholders to invest. Answers must refer to the owners/shareholders and not the business itself. Application words: electricity, (stop using) coal, 16 million (customers), 6500 (employees), pressure groups, opportunity cost.

text: Explain two ways a pressure group might influence DNG's decisions.
context: DNG provides electricity to 16 million customers, planning to stop using coal. Pressure groups had an influence on this decision.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 ways = 6 marks). Ways: Create (negative) publicity/publish information/write to newspaper about the impact of using coal, damaging its reputation; Organise customer boycotts of its 16 million customers, leading to fewer sales/less revenue; Demonstrations/protests about electricity production, which could reduce investment in the business; Petition/send letters to government against this limited company; Lobbying; Take legal action. Application words: electricity, coal, 16 million (customers), 6500 (employees), opportunity cost, limited company/shareholders.

text: Explain two methods of internal communication a large business could use to share important information with its employees. Justify which method should be used.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. The Managing Director is considering the best way to communicate important information to DNG's 6500 employees.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Methods: Meeting/briefing/video conference — workers receive the message at the same time but workers will not be working so output may fall; Email — message can be sent to multiple people at the same time but people may not be able to access the internet; Phones — allows for immediate feedback; Text/SMS — contains only very limited information; Posters/noticeboards; Announcements; Internal newspapers; Social media; Letter. Do not award types of communication such as written, verbal, electronic on their own. Justification: e.g. email is better as it may not be possible to get all employees in a large business together at the same time, whereas with an email all employees receive information they can refer back to later.

text: Define 'non-current assets'.
context: CPK operates 5 sports clubs, uses job enrichment, 60 employees. Non-current assets $2m (2020), $2m (2021).
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Resources owned by a business which will be used for a period longer than one year. OR Items owned by a business for more than one year. Partial (1 mark): Items owned by the business, OR items in the business for more than one year. Do not award examples.

text: State two elements of the marketing mix.
context: Having the right marketing mix is important to CPK's success.
ms: 1 mark per element (max 2). Only award first two responses. Two from: Price, product, place, and promotion.

text: Outline two ways CPK might be affected by an increase in taxation.
context: CPK operates 5 sports clubs offering gym and yoga classes, 60 employees. Current ratio: 1.6 (2020) → 1.3 (2021). Profit margin: 12% (2020) → 10% (2021).
ms: 1 mark per way + 1 mark application (max 2 ways = 4 marks). Ways: Less profit to help improve the sports clubs; Decreased demand at the 5 locations; May have to increase prices, affecting its marketing mix; Can increase expenses/cost of buying materials. Application words: sports club or examples such as activities/gym/yoga class, 5 (locations), 60 (employees), marketing mix, 10%/12%.

text: Explain one possible effect on CPK of the change in each of the following ratios as shown in Table 3.1: Current ratio AND Profit margin.
context: CPK's financial statements: Current ratio 1.6 (2020) → 1.3 (2021), Profit margin 12% (2020) → 10% (2021), Non-current assets $2m (both years). 5 sports clubs, 60 employees.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per ratio (max 6 marks). Current ratio: Decreased/fallen/worsened. Analysis: May need to reduce creditors/trade payables to avoid cashflow problems in the sports clubs; May need to improve cash by selling more products or unwanted non-current assets; May have problems paying its short-term liabilities/less liquidity; May make it harder to obtain finance; Suppliers may be less willing to provide goods on credit. Profit margin: Decreased/fallen/worsened. Analysis: May need to increase prices to improve profit margin in the 5 clubs; Need to look for ways to increase added value; May look for ways to lower variable costs/expenses. Application words: 2%/12% or 10%, 0.3/1.6/1.3, sports club or examples such as gym/yoga class, 5 (clubs).

text: Do you think job enrichment is a better way for a business to motivate its employees than profit sharing? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. CPK uses job enrichment to keep its 60 employees well-motivated.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Job enrichment: Business able to make most/full use of employee's skills, which can help increase labour flexibility; Training may be needed, which can increase expenses; Workers gain more job satisfaction/feel recognised/valued; Not all workers are able/want to do more complex work, leading to mistakes/waste; Not easy to add extra tasks to some jobs; Time consuming to redesign tasks; May create conflict between employees. Profit sharing: Money is a major motivator for many employees; Can help build team spirit/sense of belonging/common goal; Not everyone is motivated by money; If business makes low/no profit, there is little/nothing to share, which could decrease motivation. Justification: e.g. job enrichment is better as making the job more interesting is more likely to motivate employees every day, whereas profit-sharing is at the end of the year and therefore likely to have less impact on daily effort.

text: Define 'recession'.
context: Following the end of a recession in country X, Beena wants to start up a hairdressing business.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): When there is a period of falling gross domestic product/GDP. OR A sustained (over a period of time) reduction in GDP/national income/output. Partial (1 mark): Fall in output/fall in GDP. Do not award features of a period of recession.

text: Identify two ways of segmenting a market.
context: Beena knows there are many ways to segment a market for her hairdressing business.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 2). Only award first two responses. Ways: Age; Gender; Socio-economic group/social status/class; Geographical/region/location; Lifestyle; Ethnic group; Family characteristics; Education; Occupation; Use of product.

text: Outline two reasons why having enough working capital might be important for Beena's business.
context: Beena wants to start up a hairdressing business, one option being purchasing a franchise. She has $800 in savings and knows having enough working capital will be important.
ms: 1 mark per reason + 1 mark application (max 2 reasons = 4 marks). Reasons: To pay for (day-to-day) expenses/short-term debts of her hairdressing business; Evidence to support loan applications if she decides to take the franchise; Use in an emergency/pay for unexpected expenses in case she needs more than $800; To ensure the business has a good credit reputation, especially as her business is a start-up; Ensures the business can take advantage of discount on bulk purchases. Application words: hairdressing or related words such as haircut or shampoo, start-up/new business, recession, franchise, $800, market research, (market) segment.

text: Explain two possible advantages to Beena of buying a franchise.
context: Beena wants to start up a hairdressing business following the end of a recession, one option being purchase of a franchise from an established hairdressing business. She has $800 in savings.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 advantages = 6 marks). Advantages: Established brand/well-known brand, therefore no need to spend on advertising; Reduces risk of failure, especially after a recession; Training/advice offered by franchisor, which saves costs important for a start-up business; Attracts customers, helping to ensure/increase revenue for her hairdressing business; Easier to obtain finance/bank more willing to lend, which may be necessary with savings of $800; Franchisor pays for advertising; Stock control and accounting systems often provided by franchisor, can help make business more efficient and improve her working capital; All supplies obtained from a central source/the franchisor, which can help ensure quality; Fewer decisions to be made (than an independent business). Application words: hairdressing or related words such as haircut or shampoo, start-up/new business, recession, $800, market research, (market) segment, working capital.

text: Do you think it is always better for a start-up business to use primary market research, rather than secondary market research, when making decisions? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Beena plans to use market research to help her decision-making.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Primary market research: Relevant/up to date data gathered, so should help you find out what you want to know; High cost/time to collect information, which a new business might not be able to afford; Only available to own business; May find it difficult to find people that represent target market/population. Secondary market research: May not be relevant/outdated, which can lead to wrong decisions; Readily available; Cheap; Can collect wide range of information. Justification: e.g. secondary research may be better for a start-up business given limited finance available, but the information must be from a reliable source. Do not accept mirror arguments.

text: Define 'pressure group'.
context: MTD manufactures specialist cleaning products including soap, uses batch production and just-in-time inventory control. Took 18 months to develop its latest environmentally friendly cleaning product.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Groups of people who act together to try to force businesses or governments to adopt certain policies. OR Organisation of like-minded people who put pressure on businesses and the government to change their policies. OR People who have a common interest who take action to change/influence business (or government) decisions. Partial (1 mark): Group formed by people with a common interest. Do not award examples.

text: Identify two features of batch production.
context: MTD manufactures cleaning products including soap. Batch production is used.
ms: 1 mark per feature (max 2). Only award first two responses. Features: Goods produced in sets/groups; Machines need to be reset between batches (frequently); Lower unit costs than job production; Large amount of work-in-progress; Flexibility/variety; Machine breakdowns do not seriously affect production.

text: Outline two factors MTD should consider when deciding on the packaging for its new product.
context: MTD manufactures cleaning products including soap, took 18 months to develop its new environmentally friendly product, must decide packaging and promotion. Pressure groups are important. MTD wants to contribute to sustainable development.
ms: 1 mark per factor + 1 mark application (max 2 factors = 4 marks). Factors: Protection/security for product, so no leakage of soap; Carries/what information it needs to include about product such as it took 18 months to develop; Who selling to/attract target market/customers, which can help decide the method of promotion; Promotes brand image such as that it is environmentally friendly; Type/quality of materials to use, to avoid action from pressure groups; Ease of transport; Ease of storage/display; Whether/how easy it is to use/open. Application words: soap/cleaning products or related words, environmentally friendly, sustainable development, 18 months to develop, pressure groups, (has to decide) method of promotion.

text: Explain two possible advantages to MTD of using just-in-time inventory control.
context: MTD manufactures cleaning products including soap, uses just-in-time inventory control, batch production, took 18 months to develop new environmentally friendly product.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 advantages = 6 marks). Advantages: Less inventory held, so less chance of wastage, important when trying to contribute to sustainable development; Lower insurance costs, which will help reduce expenses for this cleaning product; Less warehouse space, lower storage costs; Improve working capital, as less money tied up in inventory, can be used for promotion of the new product; Improve cash flow, as finished product can be produced/sold to order so money comes back to the business more quickly. Application words: soap/cleaning products, environmentally friendly, develop new products, batch production, packaging.

text: Do you think using social media is the best way for a business to promote a new product? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. MTD's Marketing Manager has to decide on the method of promotion for its new environmentally friendly cleaning product.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Social media: Cover wide area/seen by many people, leading to additional revenue; Low cost method of advertising, so fewer cash outflows; Easy/quick to update, so can spend time on other tasks; Can target specific groups; No internet access/not everyone uses social media/message 'lost' among many messages; Lack of control over comments; Comments can be altered/hacked/bad reviews, could lead to a bad reputation/publicity; Takes time to continually post/monitor messages. Other methods: Newspaper — can be referred back to later; Specialist magazines. Justification: e.g. it may depend on the type of product — a new product may benefit from social media as it may not have much awareness yet, so a wider area of coverage is likely to be of greater importance.

text: Define 'revenue'.
context: TJM is a private limited company, a food retailer with 450 shops. In 2021 TJM's revenue increased by $500 million.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Money coming in from selling a product (over a given period of time). OR Amount of money a business earns from the sale of its products. Partial (1 mark): Income of the business.

text: Calculate working capital. Show your working.
context: TJM's financial statements 2021 ($m): Non-current assets 400, Current assets 300, Current liabilities 240, Profit for the year 200.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): $60 million or 60m. Method: Current assets − current liabilities = $300m − $240m (1 mark). If correct answer given with no workings shown, award 2 marks. $ sign not required but units (m) must be included to gain full marks.

text: Outline two advantages of TJM being a private limited company.
context: TJM is a private limited company, food retailer with 450 shops. Directors are planning to expand by opening 20 new shops.
ms: 1 mark per advantage + 1 mark application (max 2 advantages = 4 marks). Advantages: Limited liability (for owners) of the 450 shops; Control over who can buy shares for this retailer; Can sell shares (to raise capital) for the 20 shops/expansion; Separate legal identity/incorporated; Continuity. Application words: 450 (shops), 20 new or 470 shops, food/retailer, $500 million (revenue), 400 employees, $200 million (profit).

text: Explain two possible reasons why profit might be important to TJM.
context: TJM is a private limited company, food retailer with 450 shops. In 2021 revenue increased by $500 million. Directors planning to expand by opening 20 new shops, recruiting 400 new employees.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 reasons = 6 marks). Reasons: Provide an (internal) source of funds for the private limited company, so business has full control over how it is spent/no interest to pay; Reward for risk-taking, as owners invested their money in hope of making a return on investment; Represents return on shareholder investment in this private limited company, as otherwise they could invest elsewhere; Measure of success, as made a profit of $200m; Attract investors/finance; Needed for long-term survival; Can use to pay for unexpected events. Application words: 450 shops, 20 new or 470 shops/plans to expand, food/retailer, $200m (profit), 400 (new jobs), private limited company.

text: Do you think an interview is the best way for a large business to select new employees? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. TJM will have to carry out a recruitment and selection process for 400 new employees.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Interview: Able to use in-depth questions/obtain detailed answers, allowing understanding of qualities/personality; Able to read/see body language/facial expressions; Time consuming to set up/carry out (multiple interviews), so HR manager has less time to focus on other activities. Other options: Skills test — shows/proves the person can carry out required tasks, but may not be feasible for some activities; Group situation/role play — allows opportunity to show interpersonal skills, but actions of others may distort process; Assessment centre/days. Justification: e.g. a group activity is better as there may be limited value in appointing someone good in a 1-to-1 situation if they cannot work as part of a team, and in a large business they are likely to work closely with many other people.

text: Identify two reasons why businesses need objectives.
context: Gareth is planning to start a car washing business using government support. He said: 'I will need to set business objectives.'
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two responses. Reasons: Provides targets/goals to work towards; Way to measure success/judge/assess performance; Helps decision-making/allocate resources.

text: Identify two possible reasons why an owner might want their business to remain small.
context: Gareth plans to keep his car washing business small.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two responses. Reasons: Access/availability/lack of capital (to expand); Personal preference/owners' choice; Size of the market; Type of industry/need to maintain close employee/customer relationships.

text: Outline two ways higher taxes might affect Gareth's business.
context: Gareth is planning to start a car washing business, plans to keep it small. He is worried about the possible effects of higher taxes. Average price $6.34, 77% of people own cars.
ms: 1 mark per way + 1 mark application (max 2 ways = 4 marks). Ways: Lower demand/sales for car washing; Increased costs/lower profit, which may be a problem for a business only started one year ago; May have to increase prices, so his price may be above the average of $6.34; May delay any (future) expansion plans. Application words: car wash, small business, $6.34, 23% or 77%, one year ago, government support, business objectives.

text: Explain how the data shown in Figure 3.1 and Figure 3.2 could be useful to Gareth.
context: Gareth is analysing market research data. Figure 3.1 shows 77% of people own cars. Figure 3.2 shows average price people pay for car washing is $6.34.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per figure (max 6 marks). Figure 3.1: Shows large proportion of people owning cars at 77%, which can help him calculate the potential size of the market/demand; Shows potential demand/whether there are sufficient customers for car washing, which could mean higher revenue. Figure 3.2: Shows average price people pay for this service at $6.34, which can help him set prices; Help set (suitable) prices at $6.34, allowing him to increase market share/remain competitive; Know how much people might be willing to pay. Application words: small business, $6.34, 23% or 77%, (car) wash/washing (cars).

text: Do you think offering financial help, such as grants, is the best way for a government to support business start-ups? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Gareth is starting his business using government support.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Financial support/grants: Needs funds to buy assets, without which it cannot operate; Start-up business is likely to have access to fewer sources of finance. Other options: Information/support/advice/mentors — a new entrepreneur may lack experience, so helps make better decisions/fewer mistakes; Interest free/low cost loans — reduces cash outflows; Lower taxes — lower costs; Free/low cost training schemes; Low rent areas. Justification: e.g. financial help is better due to the limited sources of finance available and banks may be less willing to take the risk of lending money to a start-up business, and without this there is no business.

text: Define 'external cost'.
context: BCZ is a multinational company operating in 12 countries, manufactures cement, a building material used by construction companies. Making cement creates external costs.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Costs paid for by the rest of society, other than the business, as a result of business activity. OR The negative impact of a business decision on society. OR Costs/disadvantages that fall on third parties that are not directly involved in the production process. Partial (1 mark): Costs society/third party has to pay. Do not award examples or 'harms environment' as too vague.

text: State two responsibilities of a director.
context: BCZ is a multinational company that manufactures cement.
ms: 1 mark per responsibility (max 2). Only award first two responses. Responsibilities: Provide strategic direction/guidance; Setting targets; Legal responsibility (to represent business); Direct and control resources; Prepare corporate plan; Take decisions that can affect the whole department/company; Protect the interests of shareholders (and other stakeholders).

text: Identify four potential benefits to a country's economy of a multinational company locating there.
context: BCZ is a multinational company operating in 12 countries, manufactures cement, quality assurance is important.
ms: 1 mark per benefit (max 4). Only award first four responses. Benefits: Jobs created; Increased/new investment/infrastructure; Increased/more exports; Fewer imports; Taxes paid to government; Increased customer choice/quality; Improves/increased competition/lower prices; Improves country's reputation.

text: Explain one possible effect on BCZ and one possible effect on its employees of the new legal controls that will reduce the maximum number of working hours.
context: BCZ manufactures cement in country X. The government of country X plans to introduce new legal controls reducing maximum working hours from 45 to 35 hours per week.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per effect (max 6 marks). Effect on BCZ: Lower output in the factory, so fewer sales/less revenue; May need to recruit more workers to make cement, leading to an increase in recruitment/training costs; May encourage BCZ to become more capital intensive, which will reduce the number of workers; Lower labour costs (if do not need extra workers). Effect on BCZ's employees: Lower pay, as only able to work 35 hours, so lower standard of living; Better health/work life balance; May have to look for a second/another job. Application words: cement, factory, 35 or 45 or 10 hours, 12 countries, external costs.

text: Do you think it is better for a large manufacturer to use quality assurance rather than quality control? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Making cement so quality assurance is important for BCZ.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Quality assurance: Tries to eliminate errors at all stages/errors spotted earlier in process, so less money/time spent on rework; Can motivate employees, leading to higher output/fewer mistakes; All workers need training, which increases training costs; Time to train all workers may reduce output (in short term); Not all workers are interested/able to spot problems. Quality control: Need to recruit inspectors to check/test products, increasing recruitment/labour costs; Production does not stop (for checks), ensures some output is available; Does not check all products (customers may still receive poor-quality products), damaging reputation; May lead to wasted resources, increasing variable costs; Does not encourage all workers to be responsible for quality. Justification: e.g. quality assurance is the better method as although training employees will increase costs, especially for a large manufacturer, the lower levels of wastage should offset the additional cost of training.

text: Define 'current liabilities'.
context: AHG is an established business selling garden products including plants and flowers, uses competitive pricing, 4 managers and 30 other employees. All managers use delegation.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): (Short-term) debts owed by a business, to be repaid in less than one year. OR Debts of a business which it expects to pay before the date of the (next) statement of financial position. Partial (1 mark): Money owed by a business.

text: Identify two examples of non-current assets.
context: AHG is analysing its statement of financial position: Non-current assets $800,000, Current assets $660,000, Current liabilities $600,000.
ms: 1 mark per example (max 2). Only award first two responses. Examples: Land/buildings/factory/property/warehouse; Machinery/technology/equipment; Fixtures/fittings; Vehicles or examples such as cars/trucks; Investments/shares in another business.

text: Outline two possible reasons why liquidity is important to AHG.
context: AHG is an established business selling garden products (plants, flowers), 4 managers, 30 employees, interested in liquidity, current ratio 1.1.
ms: 1 mark per reason + 1 mark application (max 2 reasons = 4 marks). Reasons: To make sure the business has access to enough cash/money to pay day-to-day expenses/(short term) liabilities/avoid interest charges/keep its suppliers, as shown by the current ratio of 1.1; To help arrange/apply for finance for this established business; Ensure business survival/allow it to continue trading to sell flowers; To provide for (unforeseen) emergencies. Application words: plants/flowers/gardening products or other examples such as seeds, 660,000 to 600,000, established (business)/operating for a long time, 4 managers, 30 or 34 employees, competitive pricing.

text: Explain two advantages to AHG of its managers using delegation.
context: AHG is an established business, 4 managers, 30 employees, all managers use delegation, uses competitive pricing.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 advantages = 6 marks). Advantages: Managers cannot do all tasks on own/reduce managers' workload/managers have time to focus on (important/complex) tasks such as improving liquidity, so better/quicker decision making; Can motivate employees as there is less control from its 4 managers, increasing productivity; Quality of managers' work is often improved/managers are less likely to make mistakes, leading to a better business reputation of its garden products; Builds trust between managers and employees/better working relations, improving loyalty of its 30 employees; Way to develop skills of employees/increase flexibility of workforce, leading to new ideas. Analysis must refer to impact on business and not employees. Application words: plants/flowers/garden products, 4 (managers), 30 employees, established business/operating for a long time, liquidity/current ratio of 1.1, statement of financial position.

text: Do you think competitive pricing is the best method for an established business to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. AHG is an established business using competitive pricing.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Competitive pricing: Price will not discourage customers from buying, so maintain customer loyalty; Prevents business losing market share, which could result in less revenue; Customer may be prepared to pay more (if it is a popular brand); Need another way to attract customers, which could increase costs; May not cover the costs, so may find it difficult to break even; Takes time/money to find out competitor's prices. Other methods: Cost-plus pricing — know costs will be covered, easy to calculate, but does not consider what competitors do; Promotional pricing — help attract sales, helps renew interest if sales are falling. Justification: e.g. it depends on what they sell — while cannot ignore what other businesses charge, if the business has a good reputation which an established business might have, it may be able to use other pricing methods that allow it to charge more.

text: Define 'off-the-job training'.
context: RWB manufactures buses, 1200 employees, all receive off-the-job training. Last year RWB made a $1.7 million loss.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Training that takes place away from the workplace usually by a specialist trainer(s). OR Training that takes place away from the workplace, for example at college, university or a specialist training provider's premises. Partial (1 mark): Training away from the workplace. Do not award examples on their own.

text: Identify two reasons (other than financial) why people work.
context: RWB manufactures buses using 1200 employees, uses financial rewards to motivate its employees.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two responses. Reasons: Job satisfaction/feeling you have done a good job/enjoyment; Social or examples such as feel part of a group/meeting people/making friends at work; Esteem/recognition/status/feel important; Opportunity to reach your potential/challenge yourself/improve skills/gain experience; Help others.

text: Outline two methods of financial rewards RWB might use to motivate its employees.
context: RWB manufactures buses, 1200 employees, uses financial rewards to motivate its employees. Last year RWB made a $1.7 million loss.
ms: 1 mark per method + 1 mark application (max 2 methods = 4 marks). Methods: High(er) wages/wage rates/time-based rates for workers in the factory; Piece rate paid to its 1200 employees; High(er) salary for making buses; Bonuses, but this may be difficult as business has made a loss; Profit sharing/share ownership schemes; Performance related pay. Application words: buses, 1200 (employees), factory, ($1.7 million) loss.

text: Explain two ways RWB might be affected by new legal controls over business activities which affect the environment.
context: RWB manufactures buses, 1200 employees, made a $1.7 million loss. The Managing Director mentioned new legal controls over business activities which affect the environment.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 ways = 6 marks). Ways: Change its production methods/equipment e.g. need to buy new machines, leading to higher interest/finance costs which may increase its loss; May need to redesign products, may be able to charge a higher price/allow the business to reduce variable costs; Require more training/retraining for its 1200 employees, which could delay production; May have to buy (pollution) permits/pay fines/higher taxes/recycle/change how it disposes of waste, increasing cash outflows; May have to change materials/components used/switch suppliers, increase variable costs; Stop/limit/slow production of its buses; Lower emissions/use renewable energy in the factory, helping lower energy costs (in the long run); May need to change location, increase cost of rent. Application words: buses, 1200 (employees), factory, ($1.7 million) loss, off-the-job training.

text: Do you think a reduction in the level of unemployment always benefits businesses? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. The Managing Director mentioned changes in the level of unemployment as an external influence.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: Increase in sales, could lead to higher revenue; Difficult to recruit workers, which may lead to an increase in recruitment costs/difficult to increase output/meet orders; Higher wages may need to be paid, increasing labour costs; Available workers may lack necessary skills, leading to lower productivity/higher training costs/lower quality. Justification: e.g. it may depend on whether the business needs employees or not, as without sufficient workers they may not be able to produce enough to benefit from higher potential sales.

text: Identify one benefit and one cost to a business of developing new products.
context: CHW manufactures electrical products including cameras, developing new products.
ms: 1 mark per benefit/cost (max 1 each). Benefits: Provides diversification/spreads risk; Increase revenue/sales; Enter new markets/attracts new customers; Allow the business to expand into existing markets/increase market share; Maintain customer loyalty. Costs: Costs of carrying out (market) research; Producing trial products; (Cost of) raw materials/labour/equipment; Marketing/advertising costs. Only award the first response given for each.

text: Calculate the break-even level of output for 2021. Show your working.
context: CHW's data for one type of camera (2021): Selling price per unit $120, Variable cost per unit $40, Fixed costs $200,000, Margin of safety 500 units.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): 2500. Method: Fixed costs ÷ (selling price − variable cost) = 200,000/(120-40) (1 mark). If correct answer given with no working shown, award 2 marks. Award only 1 mark if 2500 written as part of the answer but not given as final answer. Max 1 where $ sign included as it is not a financial value.

text: Outline two ways CHW could increase its margin of safety.
context: CHW manufactures electrical products including cameras. Selling price $120, variable cost $40, fixed costs $200,000, margin of safety 500 units.
ms: 1 mark per way + 1 mark application (max 2 ways = 4 marks). Ways: Lower fixed costs from $200,000 for the year; Lower variable costs/variable cost per unit from $40; Increase price of cameras. Application words: factory, cameras/electrical products, 500 (margin of safety), 2500 (break-even output), flow production, 200,000 (fixed costs), $120 (selling price), $40 (variable cost per unit).

text: Explain two ways in which the stage of the product life cycle might affect CHW's marketing decisions about promotion.
context: CHW manufactures electrical products including cameras, developing new products, wants to introduce flow production into the factory.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per stage/way (max 6 marks). Must name the stage and why/how much promotion to access knowledge marks. Introduction: High level/amount of promotional activity, to help raise awareness/inform/attract/persuade new customers about its cameras; Attract/inform/persuade customers to increase sales/revenue; Establish brand image to make business competitive. Growth: High level/amount of promotion, to try to encourage brand loyalty so it can sell 2500 to break even. Maturity: Likely to be less promotion, as product is well known/business wants to use funds for other purposes such as developing new products; To remind customers about its products, so maintain sales/market share; Spending might increase if use an extension strategy. Decline: Limited promotion/spending, to reduce marketing costs; May only inform customers of price reductions, so no longer selling at $120, to encourage some sales. Application words: cameras/electrical products, 500/margin of safety, develop new products, 2500 (break-even output), $120 (selling price), $200,000 (fixed costs), $40 (variable cost per unit), factory. Do not award answers which identify methods of promotion.

text: Do you think flow production is the best method of production for a manufacturing business to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. CHW would like to introduce flow production into its factory.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Flow production: High output, so able to meet demand (on time); Benefit from economies of scale, leading to lower unit costs; More capital intensive, leading to lower labour costs; Lower (employee) motivation, leading to lower productivity; Can produce 24 hours a day; If one machine breaks down whole production line stops, lose output/fewer sales; Requires a large capital investment. Batch production: more flexible/produce a variety of products. Job production: unique products so able to charge a higher price. Justification: e.g. flow production is only worthwhile if there is a large market for a standardised product, which can cover the high initial costs, especially given lower unit costs from economies of scale.

text: Define 'entrepreneur'.
context: Tom wants to leave his job to become an entrepreneur, planning a window cleaning business with his sister.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): A person who takes the risk for a new business venture. OR An individual who takes the financial risk of starting and managing a new business. Partial (1 mark): Person who starts up a business. For both marks must have idea of a person starting a new business, and that they take a risk to do this [+1].

text: Define 'opportunity cost'.
context: Tom knows that every decision he makes will have an opportunity cost.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): The next best alternative given up by choosing another item. OR The benefit that could have been gained from an alternative use of the same resource.
