OR A benefit, profit or value that a firm has to give up in order to achieve something else. Partial (1 mark): What you have to give up/forgo. Do not award examples.

text: Identify four reasons why a new business might be at greater risk of failure than an established business.
context: Tom has been told that new businesses are at a greater risk of failure than established businesses.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 4). Only award first four responses. Reasons: Lack of/cannot get finance/cash flow problems/lack of liquidity; Level of competition/lack of customer loyalty/customers/demand/sales; Poor planning/no business plan/lack of objectives; Lack of (managerial/business) experience/skills/knowledge; Inadequate/no market research; No reputation/low brand awareness/no brand image.

text: Explain two suitable sources of start-up capital Tom's business might use.
context: Tom and his sister plan to start a window cleaning business. Tom has calculated the business will need $700 as start-up capital.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 sources = 6 marks). Sources: Own savings from his time working in his other job, as no need to repay/no interest to pay; Borrow from friends/family such as his sister, as may give long time to repay; (Bank) loan for this window cleaning business, as could provide all the money at once; Overdraft, can arrange quickly/only pay interest when used; Government grant, as may be willing to support entrepreneurs, no interest/no need to repay; Crowdfunding, to raise the $700, so no interest to repay; Micro-finance, as does not need security to obtain. Application words: window cleaning, $700, wants to leave his job/other job, sister, partnership, opportunity cost, entrepreneur. Do not award retained profit/profit or sell shares.

text: Do you think a partnership is the best form of business organisation for a new business? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Tom has to decide whether a partnership is a suitable form of business organisation for the new business.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Partnership: Share workload/responsibility, which could allow time for each partner to focus on different business activities; More ideas/skills, which could help make the business more competitive; Can share any potential loss/risks; Unlimited liability, personal possessions at risk if unable to pay business debts; Risk of disagreements/slow decision making, so less responsive to changes in customer demand; Must share any profits made. Other options: Sole trader — simple to set up, little paperwork, requires limited start-up capital, make all decisions, keep all profit, but limited access to finance. Private limited company — limited liability but more paperwork/legal requirements. Justification: e.g. a partnership is a better choice than starting up as a sole trader — while there is still unlimited liability, sharing some risk and working together with extra skills can help reduce potential problems, increasing chances of success.

text: Define 'competitive pricing'.
context: Pamela is a successful entrepreneur, owns a gift shop selling celebration cards, toys and candy, started 30 years ago, now has 5 employees. Uses competitive pricing.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): When a product is priced in line or just below competitors' prices (to try to capture more of the market). OR Setting a price similar to that of competitors' products already established in the market. Partial (1 mark): Have similar prices to other businesses, OR bases their prices on competitors' pricing.

text: Define 'marketing budget'.
context: Most of Pamela's marketing budget is spent on sales promotion.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): A financial plan for the marketing of a product or product range (for a specified period of time). OR The amount of money made available by a business for its marketing activities during a particular period of time. Partial (1 mark): Money to be spent on marketing.

text: Outline two possible threats to Pamela's business of using e-commerce.
context: Pamela's gift shop (cards, toys, candy) started 30 years ago, 5 employees, does not use e-commerce, uses competitive pricing, sales promotion.
ms: 1 mark per threat + 1 mark application (max 2 threats = 4 marks). Threats: Increased competition, which makes it harder to calculate a competitive price; Unfamiliarity/customers are less likely to buy from a business they don't know, leading to fewer sales of toys; No face-to-face contact which could make it difficult to establish a relationship, so difficult to gain customer loyalty; Website design must be clear/attractive/easy to use, or customers will not visit; Limited/no access to the internet; Increasing costs as a specialist may need to be employed/website design/maintenance; May need a larger space to store products increasing costs; Packaging/delivery of each item will increase costs per product; Larger number of returns could lead to higher business costs; All customers can see negative reviews. Application words: gift shop, (celebration) cards/toys/candy, entrepreneur/the owner, 30 years ago, 5 employees, customer loyalty, competitive pricing, marketing budget, sales promotion.

text: Explain two methods Pamela's business can use to maintain customer loyalty.
context: Pamela's gift shop (cards, toys, candy) started 30 years ago, 5 employees, knows maintaining customer loyalty is important.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 methods = 6 marks). Methods: Communicate with customers e.g. newsletters, social media, so that they remember your business when they next need candy/toys/cards; Offer rewards to existing customers/introduce a loyalty scheme using money from the marketing budget, so consumers have an incentive to return; Train staff/offer good quality service from all 5 employees; Extra services or examples such as delivery/credit facilities; Ask for feedback/carry out market research, so items sold match customer needs; Resolve complaints quickly, so customers don't go elsewhere; Introduce new products/high quality products, satisfying customer needs; Brand loyalty. Application words: gift shop, (celebration) cards/toys/candy, 5 employees, entrepreneur, 30 years ago, competitive pricing, marketing budget, sales promotion.

text: Do you think being a risk-taker is a more important characteristic of a successful entrepreneur than being creative? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Pamela is a successful entrepreneur.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Risk-taker: A successful entrepreneur must take risks otherwise there is no business; Entrepreneurs take the risk of investing their own money, this may bring high rewards, however they may fail and lose their personal possessions; Taking risks is a way to learn if an idea is good or not. Creative: New ideas, leading to increased sales/revenue; Creativity adds value, so higher prices can be charged; Creativity alone does not guarantee success if customers do not purchase. Justification: e.g. being creative may be more important because making a business different to its competitors can lead to increased sales, and in a competitive market this helps the business stand out, whereas an entrepreneur can take risks but if customers will not buy, they will not be successful.

text: Define 'public limited company'.
context: CTF is a public limited company, manufactures beds using batch production. Break-even output 14,000, current level of output 18,000, maximum factory output 25,000.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Businesses owned by shareholders, but they can sell shares to the public and their shares are tradeable on the stock exchange. OR A company that sells its shares to the general public through a stock exchange. Partial (1 mark): A business that can sell shares.

text: Calculate the margin of safety for CTF's children's beds. Show your working.
context: CTF's output data (children's beds per month): Break-even output 14,000, Current level of output 18,000, Maximum factory output 25,000.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): 4000. Method: Current output − break-even output = 18,000 − 14,000 (1 mark). If correct answer given with no working shown, award 2 marks. Award only 1 mark if 4000 written as part of the answer but not given as final answer.

text: Outline two ways an increase in inflation might affect CTF.
context: CTF is a public limited company manufacturing beds using batch production. The Operations Director wants to know how an increase in inflation might affect CTF.
ms: 1 mark per way + 1 mark application (max 2 ways = 4 marks). Ways: Employees might ask for pay rise, reducing its margin of safety; Increase in raw material costs for manufacturing (beds); Prices may have to increase; Fewer sales/customers cannot afford to buy the beds. Application words: public limited company (PLC), (children's) beds, factory/manufacturer, margin of safety/4000, batch production, environmental pressures, 14,000 (break-even output), 18,000 (current output), 25,000 (capacity).

text: Explain two possible advantages to CTF of using batch production.
context: CTF is a public limited company manufacturing beds using batch production, break-even output 14,000, current output 18,000, capacity 25,000.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 advantages = 6 marks). Advantages: Flexible, easy to change the type of beds, to adapt to customer demands; Economies of scale/materials can be bought in bulk, which can help reduce average costs, improving the margin of safety; Production may not be affected to any great extent if machinery breaks down, so some output made, helping reach its break-even output of 14,000; Variety of products, which could lead to increased sales; Variety of tasks can motivate workers, leading to less absenteeism/lower labour turnover at the factory; Spread risk (as can make more than one type of product). Advantages should focus on the business not employees. Application words: public limited company (PLC), (children's) beds, factory/manufacturer, margin of safety/4000, environmental pressures, 14,000 (break-even output), 18,000 (current output), 25,000 (capacity).

text: Do you think manufacturing businesses should always respond to environmental pressures? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. CTF's Operations Director knows there are many environmental pressures that a manufacturing business could respond to.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: Reduces the risk of a customer boycott; Enhance brand image/reputation, leading to more potential customers/revenue; Help recruit/retain employees; Help attract investors, so raise more capital; Reduces risk of legal action/fines, avoiding bad publicity; May need to buy new equipment, which increases costs, leading to higher prices; Reduce productivity, which could lower profit margin; May need to find new suppliers of raw materials, leading to higher unit costs. Justification: e.g. responding to environmental pressures can improve reputation leading to increased revenue, and the additional revenue could offset the costs, so if the business can find the resources they need at a competitive price, they should.

text: Define 'shareholders' equity'.
context: VCG manufactures high-quality briefcases and travel bags, 50 skilled production workers, planning to expand by building a second factory. Financial statements 2021: Revenue $2,000,000, Current assets $300,000, Current liabilities $250,000, Shareholders' equity $800,000.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): (Total sum of) money invested into the business by the owners of the company. OR Share capital plus reserves. OR Total assets minus total liabilities. Partial (1 mark): Money raised from selling shares.

text: Identify two financial statements a public limited company is legally required to publish each year.
context: VCG manufactures high-quality briefcases and travel bags, both internal and external stakeholder groups interested in this information.
ms: 1 mark per financial statement (max 2). Only award first two responses. Two from: Income statement (Profit and loss); Statement of financial position (Balance sheet); Cash-flow statement/statement of cash flows; Statement of changes in equity. Do not award cash-flow forecast.

text: State whether each of the following are classified as a current asset or a current liability: Overdraft; Trade receivables; Trade payables; Cash in bank.
context: VCG's financial statements show current assets and current liabilities.
ms: 1 mark per correct answer (max 4). Overdraft: current liability. Trade receivables: current asset. Trade payables: current liability. Cash in bank: current asset.

text: Explain one way each of the following stakeholder groups might use VCG's accounts: Shareholders AND Suppliers.
context: VCG manufactures high-quality briefcases and travel bags, 50 skilled workers, planning second factory. Revenue $2m, Current assets $300,000, Current liabilities $250,000, Shareholders' equity $800,000. Current ratio 1.2.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per stakeholder (max 6 marks). Shareholders: Help assess business performance/profits, to see whether they will receive a dividend/return on investment from this bag manufacturer; Help decide whether to continue to invest, as the business is looking to open a second factory, which could mean less dividends paid; Assess liquidity, they do not want to invest in a business with serious cash/liquidity problems; Compare performance over time, and how much the $800,000 in equity increases; Compare performance between different businesses. Suppliers: Can see the total value/level of debt, current liabilities $250,000, to help decide whether to offer (more) credit; Assess whether the business has sufficient cash, within current assets of $300,000, for the business to repay them when debts become due; Assess profitability/level of sales, successful business may need more materials, especially as make high-quality products. Application words: bags or examples such as briefcase/travel bag, (second) factory, $2m (revenue), $800,000 (equity), $300,000 (current assets), $250,000 (current liabilities), 1.2 (current ratio), high-quality, 50/skilled workers.

text: Do you think access to labour is the most important factor for a manufacturing business to consider when deciding where to locate a new factory? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. VCG is planning to expand by building a second factory, different locations being considered.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Access to labour: Skilled labour may be difficult to find/recruit, which could increase recruitment/labour costs, but can use machinery to reduce the need for labour; Labour intensive production requires access to labour, without labour they cannot operate; Can depend on type of workers required, unskilled workers may be easy to find. Other factors: Good transport links, to ensure products arrive/sent when needed; Proximity to market, to ensure sales/revenue can be made; Type of product, a fragile/heavy product may need to be closer to customers; Access to raw materials/components, so production is not delayed; Availability/cost of suitable land, which could restrict size of factory/limit output/increase fixed costs; Government influence or examples e.g. government grants, can help reduce costs. Justification: e.g. labour is most important if the business is labour intensive because without labour the new factory cannot produce output, but other factors would be of greater importance in a new capital-intensive factory.

text: Identify two objectives for a business organisation in the public sector.
context: MBH is a business organisation in the public sector, controls 5 hospitals, 5600 employees including 440 doctors.
ms: 1 mark per objective (max 2). Only award first two responses. Objectives: Financial or examples e.g. meet targets set by government, improve efficiency/reduce costs; Make product/service affordable to all; Provide a service to everyone; Protect or create jobs in certain areas (social objectives).

text: Define 'chain of command'.
context: MBH has a tall organisational structure and a long chain of command.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): The structure in an organisation which allows instructions to be passed down from senior management to lower levels of management. OR The route through which authority is passed down through an organisation. Partial (1 mark): Shows who gives orders.

text: Outline two ways MBH can use ideas from Herzberg's theory to motivate its employees.
context: MBH controls 5 hospitals, 5600 employees including 440 doctors. The HR Director uses ideas from Herzberg's theory to improve employee motivation.
ms: 1 mark per way + 1 mark application (max 2 ways = 4 marks). Ways: Could give employees more responsibility in the hospital; Offer more interesting work as many are skilled employees; Offer more praise for good work; Give chances for promotion as there is a tall organisational structure. Application words: 440/doctors, (5) hospitals or related words, 5600 employees, public sector, communication barriers, phone/email, long chain of command, tall organisational structure, skilled employees. Do not award examples of hygiene factors on their own e.g. pay, working conditions.

text: Explain how MBH might reduce or remove each of the following communication barriers: Messages lost AND Use of jargon.
context: MBH is worried about communication barriers within the organisation, has a tall organisational structure and long chain of command. Most internal communication is by email and phone calls.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per barrier (max 6 marks). Messages lost: Ask for feedback, to ensure the message is received by all 5 hospitals; Make sure the medium of communication is suitable/works; Delayering/flattening the structure because it is a long chain of command. Use of jargon: Use simple language on the phone/email, so easy for everyone/receiver to understand; Make sure language is appropriate to the receiver, to make sure there is no misunderstanding; Providing opportunities for the receiver to ask questions. Application words: 440/doctors, (5) hospitals or related words, 5600 employees, public sector, phone/email, long chain of command, tall organisational structure, externally recruited.

text: Do you think an organisation should always use external recruitment when recruiting skilled employees? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. External recruitment is used when recruiting skilled employees at MBH.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. External recruitment: Bring in new skills/ideas, which could help improve productivity/effectiveness/efficiency; Can bring in valuable knowledge and experience of competition, gaining a competitive edge; Wider choice of applicants, increases possibility of finding best person for job; No knowledge of how business works/current operations, so might need induction training; Avoids risk of upsetting employees when someone internal is promoted; Higher recruitment costs; More time spent/takes longer to fill vacancy; Required if no suitable candidates in the business. Internal recruitment: Can help motivate other employees, which could lead to fewer people leaving/reduce absenteeism; Internal promotion can create another vacancy that then needs to be filled. Justification: e.g. it depends on the skills within the business — if there are no suitable workers, external recruitment would be the only choice.

text: Identify two reasons for globalisation.
context: CXN manufactures glass bottles using flow production, 130 employees, benefited from globalisation, products exported to 39 countries.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two responses. Reasons: Free trade agreements/economic trading blocs/reduction in trade barriers; Improved/cheaper transport/travel links; Improved communication networks/technology; Emerging markets are quickly expanding/rapid economic growth in developing countries; Change in government economic policy/allowing foreign company to set up operations in own country; Increased labour migration.

text: Define 'depreciation of an exchange rate'.
context: The Managing Director of CXN knows that depreciation of an exchange rate can affect business activity.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): A currency's value falls against another currency. OR The value of the currency goes down with respect to another (currency). OR When the value of a currency falls — it buys less of another currency than before. Partial (1 mark): Currency is weaker/falling, OR can buy less with currency.

text: Outline one possible objective for each of the following stakeholder groups of CXN: Government AND Employees.
context: CXN manufactures glass bottles using flow production, 130 employees, exports to 39 countries, has a number of stakeholder groups. Thinks all manufacturing businesses should contribute to sustainable development.
ms: 1 mark per objective + 1 mark application (max 2 stakeholders = 4 marks). Government: Increase tax (revenue)/paid correct amount of tax from the manufacture of bottles; Provide/increase number of jobs/minimum unemployment benefits to pay; Expect business to stay within the law. Employees: Increase pay/wages/receive fair wage/regular payments for its 130 employees; Better/safe working conditions when using flow production; Access to training/development because the business is trying to contribute to sustainable development; Job security; Have contract of employment; Work provides motivation/opportunities for promotion. Application words: glass/bottles, 130 (employees), (export to) 39 countries, flow production, sustainable development, globalisation.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to CXN of using flow production.
context: CXN manufactures glass bottles using flow production, 130 employees, exports to 39 countries, benefited from globalisation.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantages: High output/fast production/increase efficiency of bottles, so able to meet orders (on time); Benefit from economies of scale, leading to lower average/unit costs; Can produce 24 hours a day/continuous production, so able to produce large output; Allows for capital intensive methods/fewer employees, so only need 130 employees, reducing labour cost. Disadvantages: Inflexible (if demand changes), especially as export to 39 countries, which could lead to high level of wastage; Lower motivation (as work may be boring), so employees are less efficient/lower output/high labour turnover; If one machine breaks down whole production line stops, lose output/fewer sales; High set up/machinery costs, leading to large cash outflows. Application words: glass/bottles, 130 (employees), 39 countries, sustainable development, globalisation. Do not award points such as faster/cheaper on their own as too vague.

text: Do you think using renewable energy is the best way for a manufacturing business to contribute to sustainable development? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. CXN's Managing Director thinks all manufacturing businesses should contribute to sustainable development.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Renewable energy: No/low energy bill, which reduces expenses; Need to use fewer scarce resources/conserve natural resources/supply not limited; High set up cost, which business might not be able to afford; Amount of energy can depend on weather conditions/may not be a reliable source of power, which could lead to less output/delays in production. Other methods: Develop environmentally friendly production methods — reduce amount of waste, leading to lower average costs; Use fewer resources — can also help reduce production costs; Develop new environmentally friendly products/packaging — may help attract new customers/markets; Recycle waste; Replant trees; Reuse materials. Justification: e.g. developing new environmentally friendly products is better because the new products could also help attract new customers which helps recover the initial costs and encourages others to contribute to sustainable development.

text: Identify X and Y.
context: Nancy is starting a book shop, preparing a break-even chart. X is the line starting from origin rising steeply. Y is the difference between current level of output and break-even output on the chart.
ms: 1 mark per correct answer (max 2). X: (Total) revenue/total value of sales. Y: Margin of safety.

text: Define 'total cost'.
context: Nancy is calculating her total costs to help complete a break-even chart for her new book shop.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Fixed costs and variable costs (combined). OR All the variable and fixed costs of producing the total output. OR Fixed costs + (total) variable cost. Partial (1 mark): All costs added together.

text: Identify four factors a service business should consider when deciding on a suitable location.
context: Nancy has identified a suitable location for her book shop and prepared a business plan.
ms: 1 mark per factor (max 4). Only award first four responses. Factors: Demand/market potential/number of customers; Accessibility for customers/parking spaces/transport links; Availability of suitable/vacant site/size of premises; Rent/taxes/cost of site; Near to other businesses/shops/competitors; Availability/cost of labour; Security; Legal controls/government influence; Infrastructure or examples such as access to electricity/water; Owner's personal preference. Do not award access to raw materials as not appropriate for a service business.

text: Explain two ways having a business plan could help Nancy.
context: Nancy wants to be an entrepreneur, decided to start up a book shop, analysed market research data, identified a location, prepared a business plan, considering e-commerce.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 ways = 6 marks). Ways: Help get a bank loan/finance for her book shop, as lender can see the business is able to repay; Provide targets/sense of purpose/direction/focus for her new business, so she can see what she needs to do to achieve her aims; Help decision-making such as whether to use e-commerce, so does not waste time/money on the wrong target market/products; Act as a checklist/way to monitor progress for this entrepreneur; Help set budgets, to help calculate her margin of safety; Help organise resources/labour requirements/marketing strategy. Application words: book (shop), market research, break-even chart/margin of safety, (suitable) location, e-commerce, new/start-up business, entrepreneur.

text: Do you think the threats of e-commerce are greater than the opportunities for a new business? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Nancy is considering using e-commerce for her new book shop.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Threats: Increased/high competition, which could make it harder to calculate a competitive price/may have to set lower price; Unfamiliarity/customers are less likely to buy from a business they don't know, lowering revenue; High cost of design of website, which the business might not be able to afford; Technical problems/no power, so may lose potential sales. Opportunities: Increase potential number of customers/sales/can access customers around the world, increasing market share; (Low cost) way to promote/advertise business, which can raise awareness; Fewer employees needed, so lower labour costs; No/fewer shops. Points must focus on impact on the business, not customers. Justification: e.g. there are more opportunities because competition is an issue that any new business must manage, and the wider market means it may still be able to generate sales needed for a successful start.

text: State two stages of the business cycle.
context: D2G is a driving school, started 3 years ago, wants to know how changes in the business cycle might affect the business.
ms: 1 mark per stage (max 2). Only award first two responses. Two from: Recession; Growth; Boom; Slump.

text: Calculate D2G's gross profit margin. Show your working.
context: D2G's income statement for year ending 31 Dec 2021: Revenue $20,000, Gross profit $12,000, Profit for the year $2,000.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): 60%. Method: Gross profit ÷ revenue × 100 = 12,000/20,000 × 100 (1 mark). If correct answer given with no working shown, award 2 marks. Award only 1 mark if 60% is written as part of the answer but not given as final answer. Must have % to gain 2nd mark.

text: Outline, with reference to D2G, the difference between profit and cash.
context: D2G is a driving school started 3 years ago, plans to buy a new vehicle. Revenue $20,000, Gross profit $12,000, Profit for the year $2,000. Mattan wants to understand the difference between profit and cash.
ms: 1 mark relevant knowledge of profit/cash + 1 mark showing understanding of difference + 1 mark application (max 2, total max 4). Points: Cash is needed to pay day-to-day costs such as fuel for the car, whereas profit is necessary for the long-term survival of his driving school; Cash may be received beforehand so the profit of $2,000 will not increase until later when driving lessons have taken place; D2G may offer credit to customers for the driving which is counted in profit of $2,000 but the cash is not yet received until the lesson takes place; Profit is a source of finance; Profit is a measure of success; Profit is a reward for risk-taking; Cash is necessary to help avoid cash flow problems. Application words: driving school/teach people to drive or related words, (new) car/vehicle or related words, $2000 profit, $12000 (gross profit), $20000 (revenue), 3 years, business cycle.

text: Explain two ways D2G might respond to an increase in competition.
context: D2G is a driving school started 3 years ago, plans to buy a new vehicle. Mattan wants to know how an increase in competition might affect D2G.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 ways = 6 marks). Ways: Decrease prices, making it more affordable for customers of his driving school; Increase advertising, which can help raise awareness/attract customers to use its service (rather than competitors); Improve/maintain customer relationships, to help ensure customer loyalty and maintain its profit of $2,000; Add/develop new products/services, to set it apart/stand out from the competition; Look for new markets, which could help widen its customer base so able to increase its revenue of $20,000. Application words: driving school/teach people to drive or related words, $2000 profit, (new) car/vehicle or related words, $12000 (gross profit), $20000 (revenue), 3 years.

text: Do you think leasing is the best source of finance for a small business to use for a new vehicle? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Mattan plans to buy a new vehicle for D2G.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Leasing: Business does not have to find a large sum of cash to purchase the vehicle, which can allow the business to obtain/use the vehicle more quickly; Care and maintenance are carried out by the leasing company, which can lower expenses; Total cost is higher than purchasing the vehicle outright, which increases total cash outflow; Do not own asset, so cannot sell the vehicle if not needed anymore/need (more) cash. Other options: Bank loan — can repay over a long period, but interest payable adds to costs. Retained profit — no need to repay, immediately available, but may not have sufficient funds. Justification: e.g. leasing is best especially as a small business may struggle to convince the bank to provide finance to buy a new vehicle, so while it may work out more expensive, at least the business obtains the vehicle it needs to operate.

text: Define 'delegation'.
context: WTB is a private limited company manufacturing breakfast cereals, 600 production workers, managers use delegation, directors considering converting to public limited company.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Giving a subordinate the authority to perform particular tasks. OR When a manager gives authority to another employee to complete a task (although the manager retains the ultimate responsibility for the completion of the task). Partial (1 mark): Manager gives task to employee, OR subordinate given task to do.

text: Identify two motivational theories.
context: The HR Director is interested in using motivational theories to help improve employee motivation.
ms: 1 mark per theory (max 2). Only award first two responses. Theories: Taylor's (scientific theory); Maslow's (Hierarchy of needs); Herzberg's (two-factor theory).

text: Outline two benefits to WTB of having part-time employees.
context: WTB manufactures breakfast cereals, 600 production workers in its factory, many employees are part-time. Directors plan to expand.
ms: 1 mark per benefit + 1 mark application (max 2 benefits = 4 marks). Benefits: Reduces labour costs/when not working no need to pay, to make the (breakfast) cereal; More flexible in hours of work in the factory; Easier to ask employees just to work at busy times; Easier to extend operating hours by working evenings/weekends; Provides a wider range of skills/experiences of the workforce of 600 employees; Helps keep experienced employees, which may be important as business is planning to expand; Can attract well qualified employees who need to have flexible hours. Application words: factory, 600 (production workers/employees), (breakfast) cereal, private limited company, public limited company, delegation, motivational theories/improve motivation, planning to expand, training.

text: Explain two reasons why training might be important to WTB.
context: WTB manufactures breakfast cereals, 600 production workers, part-time employees, all employees receive training, managers use delegation.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 reasons = 6 marks). Reasons: Improve efficiency/increased output/faster production, which could help lower (average) cost in the factory; More skilled/flexible employees/workers know what to do, so able to cover absences of others who work part-time; Fewer mistakes/better quality from its 600 employees, which could lower costs of rework; Increase motivation, which can help reduce labour turnover/encourage employee loyalty/retention; Fewer customer complaints about its cereal, increasing customer loyalty; Less supervision needed, so able to make more use of delegation, managers have time to focus on other activities; Fewer accidents/ensure safe working conditions; Helps introduce a new process. Application words: factory, 600 (production workers/employees), (breakfast) cereal, private limited company, public limited company, delegation, motivational theories/improve motivation, part-time (employees), planning to expand.

text: Do you think a public limited company is a better form of business organisation for a growing business than a private limited company? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. The directors plan to expand WTB and are considering whether to convert it into a public limited company.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Public limited company: Access to very large amounts of capital, which does not need to be repaid; Shares available on the stock exchange/can sell shares to public; Cannot control who buys the shares, which increases the risk of a takeover; More legal requirements/controls to follow/must hold an annual general meeting, which increases costs/time-consuming; Selling shares to the public is expensive. Private limited company: Can only sell shares to friends/family, which could limit amount of finance able to raise; Able to control who buys the shares, which can help reduce risk of takeover. Do not award points that apply to both forms (e.g. dividends, divorce of ownership and control, limited liability, incorporated, must issue accounts). Justification: e.g. becoming a public limited company is better because as the business is growing, access to more funds is likely to be very important otherwise it could delay its plans, whereas a private limited company is restricted to a smaller group of people so may not raise sufficient funds.

text: Define 'private limited company'.
context: VDN is a private limited company. One of VDN's objectives is to be ethical, produces office products including pens and paperclips, all raw materials imported, 380 employees.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): A business owned by shareholders, but they cannot sell shares to the public. OR A business owned by shareholders, but they can only sell shares to friends or family. OR Often a small to medium-sized business owned by shareholders who have limited liability; the company cannot sell its shares to the general public. Partial (1 mark): Have limited liability, OR can sell shares.

text: Define 'average cost'.
context: The Managing Director plans to introduce new machinery to help lower average costs.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Total cost of production divided by total output. OR The cost of producing a single unit of output. Partial (1 mark): Cost per unit.

text: Outline two ways VDN could be ethical when producing its products.
context: VDN is a private limited company producing office products (pens, paperclips), all raw materials imported, 380 employees.
ms: 1 mark per way + 1 mark application (max 2 ways = 4 marks). Ways: Pay fair wages to its 380 employees; Source environmentally friendly products/buy local/recycle/reduce waste in its factory; Not use child labour/not buy from producers using child labour when importing materials; Pay suppliers a fair price for pens/paperclips; Pay suppliers on time. Application words: factory, office equipment or examples such as pens/paperclips, import all its raw materials, 380 employees, Kaizen, average cost. Do not award answers outlining legal factors such as paying minimum wage.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to VDN of introducing Kaizen.
context: VDN's Managing Director wants to introduce Kaizen into the factory, 380 employees, produces office products.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantages: Increase productivity, which helps lower average costs and could improve its profit margin; Work in progress is reduced, reducing inventory costs; Can reduce amount of space needed for production, decreasing rent costs; Improved layout/combining of jobs in the factory can release some employees to do other jobs; Help motivate employees (as involved in change), leading to less absenteeism/higher productivity of its 380 employees. Disadvantages: Only designed to produce small changes/no radical changes, so will not gain any significant increase in output of office equipment; Over time it is difficult to identify (extra) improvements, which can demotivate employees; Workers may need training, which increases costs; Not all employees may want/able to implement Kaizen; Meetings take time, which could decrease output. Application words: factory, office equipment or examples such as pens/paperclips, 380 employees, reduce average costs, ethical (objective).

text: Do you think off-the-job training is the best method for a large business to use when introducing new machinery? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. VDN plans to introduce new machinery requiring training for its 380 employees.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Off-the-job: Can focus on training, so less likely to make mistakes; Access to up-to-date knowledge; May have to pay more/high cost of specialists; Business may not have the skills to train its workers. On-the-job: Still work while training so output/production does not stop; Cheaper than off-the-job; Workers might not have the skills to train others (as its new machinery); Employees learn way the business wants them to/can control what is taught, so standards easier to maintain; Slows down work of experienced worker. Justification must clearly relate to a large business — e.g. off-the-job is better because existing employees may not have any knowledge of the new equipment, so the extra cost is worth it to avoid costly mistakes.

text: Define 'unemployment'.
context: Asmaa used a government grant to set up a small car repair business 4 years ago, now has 3 full-time employees, thinks her business has benefited from a low rate of unemployment.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): When people want to work but cannot find a job. OR The proportion or percentage of the population that are capable of working but are unable to find a job. Partial (1 mark): People have no job.

text: Identify one cash inflow and one cash outflow a business might have.
context: Asmaa is reviewing her cash-flow forecast for the car repair business.
ms: 1 mark cash inflow + 1 mark cash outflow (max 1 each). Cash inflows: money from cash/credit sales, sale of fixed assets, money received from bank loan/overdraft/other sources of finance. Cash outflows: payments to employees, rent paid, interest payments, payments to suppliers, tax payments, dividend payments. Only award the first response given for each.

text: Outline one advantage and one disadvantage to Asmaa of using a government grant as a source of finance.
context: Asmaa used a government grant to set up her small car repair business 4 years ago, now has 3 full-time employees.
ms: 1 mark advantage/disadvantage + 1 mark application (max 2 each = 4 marks). Advantages: No need to repay by the car repair business; No finance cost/no interest to pay, which could help the cash-flow forecast. Disadvantages: May not provide full amount needed, when she started 4 years ago; May be restrictions about how it is used/cannot use the money how you want to; Can take time to apply/obtain. Application words: car repair, small (business), new/start-up (business)/when started 4 years ago, cash-flow forecast/cash inflow.

text: Explain how the closure of a competitor and an increase in the minimum wage rate might affect Asmaa's cash-flow forecast.
context: Asmaa's cash-flow forecast (January-March, $000s): Cash inflow 40/55/40, Cash outflow 50/35/35, Net cash flow (10)/20/5, Opening balance 50/40/60, Closing balance 40/60/65. She has 3 full-time employees and wants to keep them well-motivated.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per change (max 6 marks). Closure of competitors: Could increase customers/demand for the car repair business, increasing cash inflows; Could increase prices, which may lead to higher cash inflow than $40,000 in March. Increase in minimum wage: May increase costs to her 3 employees, which will increase cash outflow; No effect, as may already pay them a higher amount as she wants to keep them well-motivated. Application words: car repair (business), 3/full-time employees, well-motivated/motivated employees, correct use of information in the cash-flow table.

text: Explain two non-financial methods a small tertiary sector business could use to keep its employees well-motivated. Justify which method should be chosen.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Keeping her employees well-motivated is important to Asmaa.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Methods: Job rotation, as switching tasks can make work more interesting; Job enrichment, as workers feel they have been given more responsibility/more important; Delegation/empowerment, so workers feel more important/valued; Praise, helps employees meet their esteem needs; Employee of the month awards, recognition of hard work/outstanding service; Provide opportunities for promotion; Team working. Justification: e.g. praise is the better option because a small tertiary business may not have sufficient tasks to be able to rotate everyone via job rotation, whereas praise can easily be offered to everyone, helping keep everyone motivated rather than just a few.

text: Define 'economic growth'.
context: The economy of country C is experiencing economic growth. Samuel started a plumbing business based on secondary market research.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): When a country's GDP increases, more goods and services are produced than in the previous year. Partial (1 mark): An increase in a country's spending, OR increase in GDP.

text: Define 'secondary market research'.
context: Samuel started his plumbing business based on secondary market research data.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Uses information that has already been collected and is available for use by others. OR The collection of data from secondhand sources/data collected by other agencies/businesses. Partial (1 mark): Information already collected. Do not award desk research as this is an alternative name; do not award examples; do not award answers that simply define market research.

text: Outline how providing a good quality service could help Samuel's business increase added value.
context: Samuel operates a plumbing business as a sole trader, installs and repairs bathroom equipment, used all his $500 savings to buy tools, thinks quality service could help increase added value.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application (max 2, total max 4). Points: Quality service can mean customers are willing to pay a higher price for a good plumber, which increases the gap between price and cost of inputs, helping choose an appropriate pricing method; Good quality can help boost reputation/brand image, important as it's a new business, so customers may be willing to pay a higher price and allow Samuel to take advantage of economic growth. Application words: plumbing or related words such as bathrooms, used all his savings/$500, new business, sole trader, pricing method, economic growth.

text: Explain two possible disadvantages to Samuel of operating as a sole trader business.
context: Samuel operates as a sole trader plumbing business, used all his $500 savings to buy tools, had to decide on a suitable pricing method.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 disadvantages = 6 marks). Disadvantages: Unlimited liability, so could lose his house as well as the $500, as his personal assets can be used to repay business debts; Limited sources of finance for his plumbing business, which could create cash flow problems/difficult to fund expansion; Few/only has own skills, so may not be able to do all jobs on time/properly, making it difficult to offer a good quality service; Has all the responsibility/makes decisions on own; Business does not have a separate legal identity, so he would be personally liable for the debts of the business; Has to work long hours/difficult to take holidays; No one to share risks/losses with. Application words: plumbing or related words such as bathrooms, used all his savings/$500, new business, quality service, pricing method, economic growth, added value.

text: Do you think penetration pricing is a better method for a new business to use than cost-plus pricing? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Samuel had to decide on a suitable pricing method for his new plumbing business.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Penetration pricing: Setting a lower price than competitors should attract customers, leading to higher number of sales; Help build up market share quickly/enter new market quickly; Customers may get used to low prices and may not buy if prices increase; Might not be appropriate for a product being promoted as high quality. Cost-plus pricing: Easy to apply, which could allow time for new business to focus on other issues; Ensures costs are covered, so will make a profit per item; Price may be (much) higher than competitors, making the business uncompetitive/leading to fewer sales; Little/no incentive to reduce costs. Justification must clearly relate to a new business — e.g. penetration pricing is better because a new business needs to gain customers, and setting a low price allows more people to afford it, improving the chances of the new business being successful.

text: Define 'flow production'.
context: BEF is a large business based in country X, uses flow production to manufacture a wide range of products including toothpaste and shampoo. All products currently sold in country X.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Where large quantities of a product are produced in a continuous process. OR The production of very large quantities of (identical) goods using a continuously moving process. Partial (1 mark): Large quantities of a (standardised) product, OR large-scale production/large volumes/continuous production.

text: Calculate output per worker per week in 2020. Show your working.
context: BEF's production data for one product: Average number of production workers 2019: 240, 2020: 250. Total output per week 2019: 300,000, 2020: 310,000.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): 1240. Method: Total output ÷ number of employees = 310,000/250 (1 mark). If correct answer given with no working shown, award 2 marks.

text: State four factors a business should consider when selecting an appropriate method of internal communication.
context: BEF knows that having effective methods of internal communication are important.
ms: 1 mark per factor (max 4). Only award first four responses. Factors: Who the message is to be sent to; Where/location of the sender/receiver; How many people does the message need to be sent to; Mediums available; Amount of information to be sent; How important/urgent is the message/when the message needs to be sent/received; How sensitive/confidential is the information; Whether feedback is required; Whether a written record is required. Do not award methods of internal communication.

text: Explain one reason why import tariffs and language might be important to BEF when deciding whether to export to country Y.
context: BEF manufactures toothpaste and shampoo using flow production, currently sold only in country X, considering exporting to country Y.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per factor (max 6 marks). Import tariffs: Higher import prices/products become more expensive, leading to lower demand/so less competitive when selling its toothpaste/shampoo; Business may decide to maintain prices/not pass on price increase to customers, reducing profit margin. Language: May need to translate/change wording on the packaging (so customers understand) on some of its 310,000 units, which increases costs; Communication problems with retailer/agent in other country, leading to wrong orders/decisions being taken especially as have a wide range; Potentially fewer sales as customers may not understand what is written on the packaging, leading to less revenue. Application words: toothpaste/shampoo, wide range of products, 310,000 units, flow production, correct use of data from the table, large business.

text: Do you think it is better for a large business to produce a wide range of products than a small range of products? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. BEF is a large business manufacturing a wide range of products including toothpaste and shampoo.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: Attracts new customers/increase sales/wider customer base, increasing revenue; Enhances brand image/reputation, leading to customer loyalty; Spread risk, as do not have to rely on only one/few products to generate sales; May need high levels of inventory, which can increase variable costs; May need more storage space, which can increase fixed costs; May have many competitors, so difficult to manage/respond to actions of other competitors, may lose customers to rivals rather than gain; May have limited/not enough production capacity, so may have difficulty meeting demand for all products; High cost of research and development, which increases cash outflows. Justification must clearly relate to a large business — e.g. a wide range can help spread risk, but may mean it has many competitors, so it may only be successful if the business is able to manage a wide range of products effectively.

text: Define 'secondary sector'.
context: SWB is in the secondary sector, produces 150,000 wooden bookcases each week using batch production, sells all output to one customer. Quality control is important. 240 employees, 100 part-time.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Firms that process and manufacture goods from natural resources. OR Manufacture goods using the raw materials provided by the primary sector. OR Uses manufacturing to transform the raw materials generated in the primary sector into a product. Partial (1 mark): Makes products. Do not award examples.

text: Identify two factors a business should consider when deciding whether to introduce just-in-time inventory control.
context: The Operations Manager is considering introducing just-in-time inventory control to reduce the amount of waste.
ms: 1 mark per factor (max 2). Only award first two responses. Factors: Reliability of suppliers/time/speed of delivery/availability of inventory at suppliers/distance from suppliers; Whether there is steady production/predictable demand; Efficient system of ordering materials/good communication systems; Whether discounts are available for bulk purchases; Cost/availability of storage space.

text: Outline one advantage and one disadvantage to SWB of using quality control.
context: SWB produces 150,000 wooden bookcases each week using batch production, 240 employees, 100 part-time, sells all output to one customer. Quality control is important.
ms: 1 mark advantage/disadvantage + 1 mark application (max 2 each = 4 marks). Advantages: Tries to eliminate faults before customer receives products/reduces likelihood that customers get faulty products, as only has one customer; Not all workers need to be trained (as inspectors employed to check quality), important as has 240 employees. Disadvantages: Cost/need to recruit inspectors/employees to check the bookcases; Does not find out how/where fault occurred in each batch; High cost if products must be scrapped/reworked/service repeated, which clashes with its objective to reduce waste. Application words: 150,000/bookcases or related words such as wood, batch production, 240 employees/100 or part-time employees/140 full time, factory, one customer, just-in-time inventory control, objective is to reduce waste.

text: Explain two possible communication barriers that might exist at SWB.
context: SWB has 240 employees, 100 part-time. SWB's managers use noticeboards around the factory and meetings with employees every month to help reduce communication barriers.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 barriers = 6 marks). Barriers: Technical language/jargon/different language spoken, so workers do not understand, so make wrong number of bookcases; Lack of feedback/no opportunity for feedback, so do not know/cannot check if message received/understood correctly, not able to help reduce waste; Noise, so employees may not hear/mishear orders in the factory; Employees may not be at work, as 100 work part-time, so not able to obtain the information; Too much information/detail, so not possible to absorb/take it all in; Employees may not see/read message on the noticeboard; Not listening/not paying attention in the meeting; Wrong communication method/medium used; Receiver may not trust the sender. Application words: 150,000/bookcases or related words such as wood, batch production, 240 employees/100 or part-time employees/140 full-time, factory, reducing waste, meetings (every month), noticeboards, just-in-time inventory control.

text: Do you think it is a good idea for a business to have only one customer? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. SWB sells all its output to one customer.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: Only one source of revenue/sales, so if the customer does not buy, the business could fail/experience cash flow issues; Can focus/specialise on the needs of that customer, increasing customer loyalty; Can help planning/know what to order, reduces amount of wastage; No need to advertise, leading to lower marketing costs; Can give customer too much power to influence prices; Less administration (compared to several customers). Justification: e.g. having a single customer can make it easier to focus on the needs of that customer, but spreading risk with more than one customer is safer — having a single customer is too high a risk as the business is totally dependent on one other business.

text: Define 'variable costs'.
context: Tom started ALB 5 years ago making trainers (sneakers) out of sustainable materials such as wool. Fixed costs 15%, Variable costs 30%, Manufacturers' profit 5%, Retailers' costs 50%.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Costs that change with the level of output produced/sales made. OR Costs which vary directly with the number of items sold or produced. OR Costs that change in direct proportion to output. Partial (1 mark): Costs that change. Do not accept examples.

text: Identify two limitations of break-even analysis.
context: Tom calculated some costs which he could use in his break-even analysis for ALB.
ms: 1 mark per limitation (max 2). Only award first two responses. Limitations: Assumes all costs can remain constant/be represented with straight lines; Not easy to separate some costs into fixed or variable; Assumes all output is sold/does not allow for inventory being held; Assumes selling price will remain same for all products sold; Assumes only one type of product is sold.

text: Outline two possible advantages to ALB of using retailers to distribute its products.
context: ALB makes trainers (sneakers) from sustainable materials such as wool, uses retailers to distribute its products.
ms: 1 mark per advantage + 1 mark application (max 2 advantages = 4 marks). Advantages: Access to many customers/able to attract people passing by/high footfall/wide distribution is possible, which can help increase revenue for its trainers; Lower storage costs/does not need large storage space/cost of holding inventories paid (in part) by retailer, so has more space/funds for its wool; Can act as promotion/retailer will pay for advertising, which could help raise awareness about protecting the environment; Can sell in large quantities to retailers. Application words: trainers/sneakers, wool/sustainable materials or related words, protecting the environment, 50% (retailers costs).

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to ALB of trying to protect the environment.
context: ALB makes trainers from sustainable materials such as wool. One of ALB's objectives is to protect the environment. Fixed costs 15%, Variable costs 30%, Manufacturers' profit 5%, Retailers' costs 50%.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantages: Better brand image/reputation leading to higher sales of its trainers/sneakers; Can help attract customers, which may be important as does use retailers, could lead to increase in revenue/market share; May be able to set higher price; Less likely for pressure group action/no consumer boycott/support from pressure groups, maintain sales. Disadvantages: Higher/increase in costs, leading to lower profit margin/higher prices; High variable costs, as suppliers who protect environment may charge higher prices; Can be difficult to find materials such as wool, leading to lower output; Higher fixed costs, as may need to buy specialist equipment which produces less emissions. Application words: trainers/sneakers or related words, wool/sustainable materials or related words, 5% profit margin, retailers (for distribution), 30% (variable costs), 15% (fixed costs).

text: Do you think a successful entrepreneur has to be a good manager? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Tom thinks a successful entrepreneur has to be a good manager.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Entrepreneur: Must be creative/innovate/provide new/unique ideas to help gain sales/attract customers; Need to be willing to take risks, to benefit from the reward/profit generated; Perseverance/determination, as will need to keep going when faced with problems; Can hire someone to manage the business (if you don't possess these skills), but this will cost money. Manager: Need to be able to organise operations, so able to get supplies/deliver on time to get repeat orders; Must be able to plan, so production runs efficiently; Ability to control employees, so they are all on task; Help motivate employees, to maintain efficiency/reduce absenteeism/retain employees; Activities must be coordinated, so time is not wasted; An ineffective manager can make wrong decisions, which will cost money/damage reputation. Justification: e.g. a successful entrepreneur does not have to be a good manager because they can always recruit someone if they cannot do this role, and without taking the initial risk there is no business to manage.

text: Identify two ways a government can support new business start-ups.
context: Aurelie is a sole trader who started her small hotel 1 year ago using government support.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 2). Only award first two responses. Ways: Offer grants; Loans for small businesses; Low tax rates/tax relief/tax breaks; Offer advice/support/information/mentors; Provide (free/low-cost) training; Low cost/rent-free premises; Organise business fairs.

text: Calculate X and Y.
context: Aurelie's income statement for 2020 ($): Revenue 5,600, Cost of sales 1,800, Gross profit X, Expenses 2,400, Profit Y.
ms: 1 mark per correct calculation. X = $3,800 or 3800. Y = $1,400 or 1400. No $ sign required.

text: State four financial ratios a business can use.
context: Aurelie wants to analyse her financial statements using ratio analysis.
ms: 1 mark per financial ratio (max 4). Only award first four answers. Ratios: Profit margin; Gross profit margin; Return on capital employed/ROCE; Current (ratio); Acid test (ratio).

text: Explain two ways that the introduction of a new tourist tax might affect Aurelie's business.
context: Aurelie's small hotel started 1 year ago. Revenue $5,600, Expenses $2,400. She is worried about how the Government's plan to introduce a new tourist tax of $1 per tourist per night might affect her business.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 ways = 6 marks). Ways: Increase price at her hotel, leading to lower demand; Lower demand/sales, leading to less revenue than $5,600; Increase administration costs for this sole trader, reduce her profit margin; May have to lower prices. Application words: (small) hotel or related words such as room, $1/(price) per night, sole trader, $5,600 (revenue), $2,400 (expenses).

text: Do you think offering good customer service is the best way for a small business to build customer relationships? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Aurelie knew it would be important to build good customer relationships.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Offer good customer service: Makes customers feel valued/builds trust, so improves customer loyalty, which can help maintain/increase revenue; Can help build reputation/brand image; May need to train/recruit employees, which increases costs. Other options: Loyalty (reward) scheme, which can encourage customers to keep returning, but takes time/cost to set up/monitor; Market research; Maintain good communications; Respond to complaints/offer refunds quickly. Justification: e.g. good customer service can make customers feel valued, but may mean training costs; still the best way as it can attract additional customers, increasing revenue which offsets the training cost.

text: Identify two features of a public limited company.
context: GCF is a public limited company providing computer services (designing websites, creating apps) to businesses. HR Director uses ideas based on Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs, 250 employees.
ms: 1 mark per feature (max 2). Only award first two responses. Features: Limited liability; Can sell shares to the general public/shares quoted on stock exchange; Must publish its accounts/more regulations; Separate legal identity/business survives death of owners; Minimum of two owners; Must hold an Annual General Meeting (AGM).

text: Identify the level of Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs each of the following methods belongs to: 'Employee of the month' award AND Organises team building courses.
context: GCF's HR Director uses ideas based on Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs to motivate its 250 employees.
ms: 1 mark per correct answer. 'Employee of the month award': Level 4 OR esteem. Organises team building courses: Level 3 OR social/belonging. Do not award self-esteem as alternative to esteem.

text: Outline two advantages to GCF of having well-motivated employees.
context: GCF provides computer services (designing websites, creating apps), 250 employees, plans to expand by taking over one of its competitors, costing $50m.
ms: 1 mark per advantage + 1 mark application (max 2 advantages = 4 marks). Advantages: High/higher productivity/efficiency/output/work quicker when working for its business customers; Less likely to leave/low labour turnover of its 250 employees; Less absenteeism, so easier to offer computer services; Willing to accept change/new methods of working, which could be important when looking to take over a competitor; Good/better (quality) service/fewer mistakes. Application words: computer services or examples such as designing apps/websites, 250 (employees), business customers, takeover (a competitor)/plans to expand.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to GCF of issuing new shares as a source of finance.
context: GCF plans to expand by taking over one of its competitors, costing $50m, considering issuing new shares to finance the takeover.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantages: Access to large amounts of capital, so able to fund expansion as need to raise $50m; No interest/finance costs to pay, so fixed costs do not increase, can invest in computer services/designing websites; Permanent source of capital, so no need to repay; Avoid increasing debt. Disadvantages: Cost/time to arrange, so not able to focus on other issues such as keeping its employees well-motivated; Increased risk of takeover/original owners may lose control, which could change the direction/objectives of the business; Shares might not be bought/no guarantee can raise planned amount. Application words: computer services or examples such as designing apps/websites, $50m, takeover (a competitor)/plans to expand, well-motivated employees, public limited company.

text: Do you think the number of employees is the best way to measure the size of a tertiary sector business? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. GCF is a public limited company providing computer services.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Employees: Some businesses make use of a lot of technology/equipment, so it does not need as many workers; Some businesses may have a lot of part-time workers, which can be difficult to compare businesses; Simple/easy to calculate. Other measures: Value of sales/revenue/output, as high value can suggest many customers, resulting in higher revenue; Capital employed, but some types of business may have a high level of non-current assets/technology/shops whereas others do not; Number of outlets/branches, but could be (in area of) low demand; Market share; Number of customers/services. Do not award profit as a measure of size. Justification: e.g. value of sales is the better measure, as all businesses will have sales revenue, whereas the number of employees can depend on the type of tertiary sector business.

text: Define 'on-the-job training'.
context: SSG manufactures mobile (cell) phones using batch production, quality control is important, 130 employees who all receive on-the-job training. Product X is in the maturity stage.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Training at the place of work, watching or following an experienced employee. OR Training at the place of work — usually the person does the actual job while an experienced employee observes and guides them. Partial (1 mark): Training while you are working. Do not award answers relating to induction. Accept: watching a more experienced worker doing the job.

text: Calculate total variable cost per month. Show your working.
context: SSG's cost and output data for product X: Rent and other expenses per month $300,000, Variable cost per unit $80, Output per month 12,000.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): $960,000. Method: Variable cost per unit × output = $80 × 12,000 (1 mark). Award only 1 mark if $960,000 is written as part of the answer but not given as final answer. $ sign not required.

text: Identify four factors a business should consider when deciding which method of production to use.
context: SSG manufactures mobile phones using batch production, quality control is important.
ms: 1 mark per factor (max 4). Only award first four responses. Factors: Amount of capital available/costs (of machinery/production); Demand/size of the market/how much they are likely to sell/output needed; Nature/type/variety of goods produced; Amount of suitable space/storage; Access to (suitable/skilled) labour/amount of labour needed. Award 'size of business' with benefit of doubt.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to SSG of using quality control.
context: SSG manufactures mobile phones using batch production, quality control is important, 130 employees, variable cost $80 per unit.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantage: Tries/may eliminate errors before customers receive the product, improving the reputation of its phones; All workers do not need to be trained for quality control, reducing costs of its 130 employees; Production is not slowed. Disadvantage: Inspectors/someone needs to be employed to check the product, increasing labour costs; Faulty products must be scrapped, therefore variable cost is higher than $80 per unit; Does not identify where/why the fault has occurred, so vulnerable to repeating the errors; Less reason for employees to help ensure quality, leading to more faults in products. Application words: (mobile/cell) phones, 130 employees, on-the-job training, $80, 12,000, $300,000, maturity/extension strategy, batch production.

text: Do you think adding new features to a product is the best extension strategy for a manufacturing business to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Product X is in the maturity stage of the product life cycle so SSG is considering possible extension strategies.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Adding new features: Product appears more appealing, attracting new/more customers, increasing revenue; High cost of development/market research, which the business may not be able to afford; Customers may dislike changes, reducing sales; Adds value to product, therefore can charge a higher price. Other strategies: Finding new markets — widening customer base; Adapt/change the packaging — improving appeal but existing customers may not recognise the product; Increase advertising/marketing/promotion — remind customers the product still exists; Sell through additional outlets. Justification: e.g. finding new markets could increase sales revenue without the risk that customers may not like new features, so it's safer and cheaper.

text: Define 'opportunity cost'.
context: DNG provides electricity to 16 million customers, a limited company, planning to stop using coal, the Managing Director knows there will be an opportunity cost to this change.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): The next best alternative foregone/given up. OR The benefit that could have been gained from an alternative use of the same resource. OR A benefit, profit, or value that a firm gives up in order to achieve something else. Partial (1 mark): What you must give up/forgo.

text: Identify two limitations of using the number of employees to measure the size of a business.
context: DNG is a limited company, 6500 employees, provides electricity to 16 million customers.
ms: 1 mark per limitation (max 2). Only award first two responses. Limitations: Does not account for capital intensive business/depends on method of production used; Could have many part-time employees; May give a different indicator of size to other measures used.

text: Outline how having limited liability might benefit DNG's shareholders.
context: DNG provides electricity to 16 million customers, a limited company which means DNG's shareholders benefit from limited liability.
ms: Up to 2 marks relevant points + up to 2 marks application (total max 4). Points: Shareholders' risk is limited to the amount invested in this electricity business; Protects personal assets in case the business decision to contribute to sustainable development does not work; Encourages (potential/existing) shareholders to invest. Answers must refer to owners/shareholders not the business. Application words: electricity, (stop using) coal, 16 million (customers), 6500 (employees), pressure groups, opportunity cost.

text: Explain two ways a pressure group might influence DNG's decisions.
context: DNG provides electricity to 16 million customers, planning to stop using coal. Pressure groups had an influence on this decision.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 ways = 6 marks). Ways: Create (negative) publicity/publish information/write to newspaper about the impact of using coal, damaging its reputation; Organise customer boycotts of its 16 million customers, leading to fewer sales/less revenue; Demonstrations/protests about electricity production, which could reduce investment in the business; Petition/send letters to government against this limited company; Lobbying; Take legal action. Application words: electricity, coal, 16 million (customers), 6500 (employees), opportunity cost, limited company/shareholders.

text: Explain two methods of internal communication a large business could use to share important information with its employees. Justify which method should be used.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. The Managing Director is considering the best way to communicate important information to DNG's 6500 employees.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Methods: Meeting/briefing/video conference — workers receive message at same time but output may fall; Email — message sent to multiple people at same time but some may not access internet; Phones — allows for immediate feedback; Text/SMS — limited information; Posters/noticeboards; Announcements; Internal newspapers; Social media; Letter. Do not award types of communication such as written, verbal, electronic on their own. Justification: e.g. email is better as it may not be possible to get all employees in a large business together at the same time, whereas email lets all employees receive information they can refer back to later.

text: Define 'non-current assets'.
context: CPK operates 5 sports clubs, uses job enrichment, 60 employees. Non-current assets $2m (2020), $2m (2021).
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Resources owned by a business which will be used for a period longer than one year. OR Items owned by a business for more than one year. Partial (1 mark): Items owned by the business, OR items in the business for more than one year. Do not award examples.

text: State two elements of the marketing mix.
context: Having the right marketing mix is important to CPK's success.
ms: 1 mark per element (max 2). Only award first two responses. Two from: Price, product, place, and promotion.

text: Outline two ways CPK might be affected by an increase in taxation.
context: CPK operates 5 sports clubs offering gym and yoga classes, 60 employees. Current ratio: 1.6 (2020) → 1.3 (2021). Profit margin: 12% (2020) → 10% (2021).
ms: 1 mark per way + 1 mark application (max 2 ways = 4 marks). Ways: Less profit to help improve the sports clubs; Decreased demand at the 5 locations; May have to increase prices, affecting its marketing mix; Can increase expenses/cost of buying materials. Application words: sports club or examples such as activities/gym/yoga class, 5 (locations), 60 (employees), marketing mix, 10%/12%.

text: Explain one possible effect on CPK of the change in the current ratio AND the profit margin shown in Table 3.1.
context: CPK's financial statements: Current ratio 1.6 (2020) → 1.3 (2021), Profit margin 12% (2020) → 10% (2021), Non-current assets $2m (both years). 5 sports clubs, 60 employees.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per ratio (max 6 marks). Current ratio: Decreased/fallen/worsened.
