Analysis: May need to reduce creditors/trade payables to avoid cashflow problems in the sports clubs; May need to improve cash by selling more products or unwanted non-current assets; May have problems paying its short-term liabilities/less liquidity; May make it harder to obtain finance; Suppliers may be less willing to provide goods on credit. Profit margin: Decreased/fallen/worsened. Analysis: May need to increase prices to improve profit margin in the 5 clubs; Need to look for ways to increase added value; May look for ways to lower variable costs/expenses. Application words: 2%/12% or 10%, 0.3/1.6/1.3, sports club or examples such as gym/yoga class, 5 (clubs).

text: Do you think job enrichment is a better way for a business to motivate its employees than profit sharing? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. CPK uses job enrichment to keep its 60 employees well-motivated.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Job enrichment: Business able to make most/full use of employee's skills, which can help increase labour flexibility; Training may be needed, which can increase expenses; Workers gain more job satisfaction/feel recognised/valued; Not all workers are able/want to do more complex work, leading to mistakes/waste; Not easy to add extra tasks to some jobs; Time consuming to redesign tasks; May create conflict between employees. Profit sharing: Money is a major motivator for many employees; Can help build team spirit/sense of belonging/common goal; Not everyone is motivated by money; If business makes low/no profit, there is little/nothing to share, which could decrease motivation. Justification: e.g. job enrichment is better as making the job more interesting is more likely to motivate employees every day, whereas profit-sharing is at the end of the year and therefore likely to have less impact on daily effort.

text: Define 'recession'.
context: Following the end of a recession in country X, Beena wants to start up a hairdressing business.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): When there is a period of falling gross domestic product/GDP. OR A sustained (over a period of time) reduction in GDP/national income/output. Partial (1 mark): Fall in output/fall in GDP. Do not award features of a period of recession.

text: Identify two ways of segmenting a market.
context: Beena knows there are many ways to segment a market for her hairdressing business.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 2). Only award first two responses. Ways: Age; Gender; Socio-economic group/social status/class; Geographical/region/location; Lifestyle; Ethnic group; Family characteristics; Education; Occupation; Use of product.

text: Outline two reasons why having enough working capital might be important for Beena's business.
context: Beena wants to start up a hairdressing business, one option being purchasing a franchise. She has $800 in savings and knows having enough working capital will be important.
ms: 1 mark per reason + 1 mark application (max 2 reasons = 4 marks). Reasons: To pay for (day-to-day) expenses/short-term debts of her hairdressing business; Evidence to support loan applications if she decides to take the franchise; Use in an emergency/pay for unexpected expenses in case she needs more than $800; To ensure the business has a good credit reputation, especially as her business is a start-up; Ensures the business can take advantage of discount on bulk purchases. Application words: hairdressing or related words such as haircut or shampoo, start-up/new business, recession, franchise, $800, market research, (market) segment.

text: Explain two possible advantages to Beena of buying a franchise.
context: Beena wants to start up a hairdressing business following the end of a recession, one option being purchase of a franchise from an established hairdressing business. She has $800 in savings.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 advantages = 6 marks). Advantages: Established brand/well-known brand, therefore no need to spend on advertising; Reduces risk of failure, especially after a recession; Training/advice offered by franchisor, which saves costs important for a start-up business; Attracts customers, helping to ensure/increase revenue for her hairdressing business; Easier to obtain finance/bank more willing to lend, which may be necessary with savings of $800; Franchisor pays for advertising; Stock control and accounting systems often provided by franchisor, can help make business more efficient and improve her working capital; All supplies obtained from a central source/the franchisor, which can help ensure quality; Fewer decisions to be made (than an independent business). Application words: hairdressing or related words such as haircut or shampoo, start-up/new business, recession, $800, market research, (market) segment, working capital.

text: Do you think it is always better for a start-up business to use primary market research, rather than secondary market research, when making decisions? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Beena plans to use market research to help her decision-making.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Primary market research: Relevant/up to date data gathered, so should help you find out what you want to know; High cost/time to collect information, which a new business might not be able to afford; Only available to own business; May find it difficult to find people that represent target market/population. Secondary market research: May not be relevant/outdated, which can lead to wrong decisions; Readily available; Cheap; Can collect wide range of information. Justification: e.g. secondary research may be better for a start-up business given limited finance available, but the information must be from a reliable source. Do not accept mirror arguments.

text: Define 'partnership'.
context: WYP is a business partnership. Greg and his 3 friends started the business 7 years ago, make eyeglasses (spectacles) only sold through its website, price $95, $200 cheaper than main competitor.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Two [or more] people who agree to jointly own a business together. OR An unincorporated business that has more than one owner. Partial (1 mark): 2 or more people create/start a business. For 2 marks need idea of two or more people and ownership. Do not accept features e.g. unlimited liability.

text: Define 'customer loyalty'.
context: Greg said it would take time to develop customer loyalty for his eyeglasses business.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Likelihood of previous customers returning to buy goods or services from a business. OR Customers keep buying from a particular shop, business or buy one particular product, rather than use other shops or buy products made by other businesses. Partial (1 mark): Keeps customers, OR choose your business rather than competitors (even if cheaper). Do not award 'brand loyal' on its own.

text: Outline two possible reasons why WYP could not get trade credit.
context: WYP is a business partnership started 7 years ago, makes eyeglasses only sold through its website, price $95, $200 cheaper than main competitor. Difficult to get trade credit at the start.
ms: 1 mark per reason + 1 mark application (max 2 reasons = 4 marks). Reasons: No previous experience of selling eye glasses; Seen as higher risk/lenders don't trust them/lender unsure whether able to repay, especially as product is $200 cheaper (than main competitor); Could offer no security when started 7 years ago; Unproven product/idea of selling only through a website; No business plan. Application words: (eye) glasses/spectacles, $95 or $200, started 7 years ago, website, 3 friends, customer loyalty, partnership.

text: Explain two possible problems for WYP of selling products at low prices.
context: WYP sells eyeglasses at $95, $200 cheaper than its main competitor, only sold through its website, a business partnership.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 problems = 6 marks). Problems: Seen as cheap/seen as low quality, as $200 less, could lead to fewer sales; Cash flow problems, as does not generate as much revenue per unit when selling eye glasses; Low profit margin, so harder/need to sell more to break even; Can be difficult/less scope to use promotional pricing to encourage sales. Application words: (eye) glasses/spectacles, $95 or $200, started 7 years ago, website, 3 friends, customer loyalty, trade credit, partnership.

text: Do you think promotion is more important than product for a new business? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Greg thinks choosing the right method of promotion is important to the success of any new product.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Promotion: Helps raise awareness/inform people, leading to more sales, increasing revenue; Can help attract/persuade potential customers; Can help create/build brand image, increasing customer loyalty; Way to communicate with customers; Help compete with competitor's products. Product: This is what people buy/without a product there is nothing to promote/if dislike the product customers will not buy it; A poor/bad quality product will not last long in the market, wasting time/money spent developing it; A good product will not necessarily sell itself. Justification: e.g. it depends on the product — if unique, this is probably more important especially for a new business as there are no alternatives, giving a better chance of establishing itself in the market. To access evaluation, must discuss both elements.

text: Define 'business plan'.
context: Nadia started her successful hairdressing business 4 years ago, said she started with no experience of business plans.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): A document containing the business aims/objectives and important details about the operations, finance and owners of a business. OR A detailed written document outlining the purpose and aim of a business which is often used to persuade lenders or investors to finance a business proposal. OR States aims and/or objectives and shows how business plans to achieve them. Partial (1 mark): A document stating the aims of the business.

text: Identify two stages in the recruitment process.
context: Nadia started with no experience of recruitment when she started her hairdressing business.
ms: 1 mark per stage (max 2). Only award first two responses. Stages: Job analysis/identify a vacancy; Job description; Person/job specification; Advertising (the vacancy); Application forms sent out/received; Shortlisting/screening; Interview/testing; Selection/job offer. Answer must be from the business viewpoint not the applicant.

text: Outline one advantage and one disadvantage to Nadia's business of selling franchises to expand.
context: Nadia now has 5 hairdressing shops and 20 employees, made a profit of $100,000 last year, planning to expand by selling franchises.
ms: 1 mark advantage/disadvantage + 1 mark application (max 2 each = 4 marks). Advantages: Receives a fee to use her brand name/franchisee has to buy a licence/pay start-up costs of her hairdressing business; Expansion is much faster, so will not take as long to open the next 5 shops; Nadia will receive a share of franchisee's profits/royalties, helping increase her $100,000 profit; Franchisees will have local knowledge, helpful as business only started 4 years ago; Management of outlet is responsibility of franchisee; All products sold must be obtained from franchisor. Disadvantages: Poor management of one franchise could damage whole business reputation, as maintaining quality is important; The franchisee keeps some/most of the profits from the outlet; Has to offer franchisees help and advice/training, which may take time as when she started she had no experience. Application words: hairdressing/shop, maintain quality (is important), $100,000 (profit), 5 (shops), 20 (employees), 4 years ago, (no experience of) business plans, inflation. Do not award answers about whether she should expand in general.

text: Explain two possible effects of an increase in the rate of inflation on Nadia's business.
context: Nadia has 5 hairdressing shops and 20 employees, made a profit of $100,000 last year, did not understand how economic issues such as inflation could affect a business.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 effects = 6 marks). Effects: Lower demand/fewer sales (as people have less money to spend) for hairdressing, reducing revenue; Workers may demand higher wages in her 5 shops, increasing labour costs; May want to delay plans to expand such as selling franchises; May need to increase prices, leading to fewer customers. Application words: hairdressing/shops, maintain quality (is important), $100,000, 5 (shops), 20 employees, 4 years ago, (no experience of) business plans, selling franchises/looking to expand.

text: Do you think making a profit is more important for a growing business than managing cash flow? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Nadia is planning to expand her business.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Profit: Main objective is to make a profit, without it owners will question point of business; A source of finance, which can allow for expansion; A measure of success; Reward for risk taking; Important for long-term survival; Can help attract investors. Cash flow: Need cash to pay day-to-day costs such as suppliers, otherwise might not have sufficient materials to continue production; Helps avoid cash flow problems; A negative cash flow means business is receiving less cash than it is spending; If negative might mean business is insolvent/forced into liquidation whether business makes a profit or not; Sales may be on credit, so even if making a profit may not receive money until later; Less likely to need overdraft, which could add to cash outflows/higher expenses. Justification must relate to a growing business — e.g. cash flow is more important as a business can continue for a while without making a profit, but will find it very difficult to survive without cash, especially when growing as it needs to purchase additional items.

text: Define 'ethical business'.
context: CTF is an ethical business, manufactures a range of toys, operates in a competitive market. Technology has changed production over the years.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): An organisation that takes decisions based on a moral code. OR The moral judgements that a business makes about their behaviour, and the way they operate and interact with their stakeholders. Partial (1 mark): Doing the right thing. Do not award answers that simply refer to protecting the environment.

text: Calculate the total variable cost for product X. Show your working.
context: Cost and revenue data for product X in 2020: Fixed costs $210,000, Variable cost per toy $25, Price per toy $40, Output 18,000.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): $450,000. Method: Variable cost per unit × number of output = 18,000 × 25 (1 mark). Award only 1 mark if $450,000 written as part of the answer but not given as final answer. $ sign not required.

text: Outline one benefit and one limitation to CTF of using break-even analysis.
context: CTF manufactures toys in a competitive market, break-even data: Fixed costs $210,000, Variable cost per toy $25, Price per toy $40, Output 18,000.
ms: 1 mark benefit/limitation + 1 mark application (max 2 each = 4 marks). Benefits: Shows expected level of profit/loss at different levels of output of toys; Shows the margin of safety of 4000; Helps planning/forecasting/decision-making such as whether to import raw materials; Can see what will happen if costs/prices change such as lower price from $40; Helps apply for finance; Easy to construct/interpret. Limitations: Assumes all output sold/sales not always the same as output, so may have sold less than 18,000; Variable costs do not always stay the same/ignores effect of purchasing economies of scale/assumes all costs can be represented by straight lines; Not easy to separate costs into fixed and variable; Hard to calculate when sell many products. Application words: toys, import raw materials, ethical, competitive market, $40 (price), 18,000 (output), $25 (variable cost per unit), $210,000 (fixed costs), 14,000 units (break-even), 4,000 (margin of safety).

text: Explain two ways that technology might have changed production at CTF.
context: CTF manufactures toys, operates in a competitive market, ethical business. Technology has changed production over the years. Following closure of its local supplier, considering importing raw materials.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 ways = 6 marks). Ways: More variety/help design new products of toys, increasing potential sales; Improve productivity/efficiency/increased speed of production/increased output, easily able to make 18,000, allowing business to meet expected demand; Less errors/wastage/better/maintain quality, improving its reputation as this is an ethical business; Fewer workers needed, reducing wage costs; Improved inventory control, as easier to keep track of raw materials so do not have to order excess inventory; Different skill set for workers; More complex work possible; Continuous production (24/7)/no breaks. Application words: toys, import raw materials, ethical, competitive market, $40 (price), 18,000 (output), $25 (variable cost per unit), $210,000 (fixed costs), 14,000 units (break-even), 4,000 (margin of safety).

text: Do you think reliability of the supplier is the most important factor for a large manufacturing business to consider when deciding whether to import materials? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Following the closure of its local supplier, CTF is considering importing raw materials for product X.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Reliability of supplier: Need to ensure materials can be delivered on time, so there is no delay/stop production, otherwise not able to meet orders on time; Supplier must be able to respond to changes in orders so business can adapt to changes in customer needs quickly, or customers may switch to competitors leading to lower revenue. Other factors: Import tariffs, would increase the price of imports; Import quotas, could limit amount of goods able to bring into country, potentially restricting output; Different (legal/quality) standards in other country; Exchange rates, as an increase/appreciation could mean imports are cheaper, which would lower costs. Justification must relate to a large manufacturing business — e.g. having a reliable supplier is most important because a large business will need high levels of inventory to meet orders and protect reputation, which may be more important than tariffs.

text: Define 'business objective'.
context: DCN is a large chemical company, 8,000 employees across 3 factories, agreed to set up a joint venture with a glass making business.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): A statement of a specific target that a business works towards. OR A statement of a specific target to be achieved (they should be SMART). Partial (1 mark): Target/goal, OR something the business works towards. Do not award examples.

text: Identify two ways that business activity might affect the environment.
context: DCN plans to develop a new type of environmentally friendly packaging with a glass making business.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 2). Only award first two responses. Ways: Pollution (or examples such as air pollution, noise pollution, water pollution); (Traffic) congestion/transport of goods; Deplete/use of natural resources; Use up green space/land use/deforestation/loss of habitat; Energy use; Emission of greenhouse gases/global warming; Waste (or examples such as IT waste, packaging waste, commercial waste). Max 1 for examples of pollution.

text: Identify four examples of communication barriers.
context: DCN's Managing Director said there will need to look at ways to overcome possible communication barriers with the joint venture partner.
ms: 1 mark per example (max 4). Only award first four responses. Examples: Problem with receiver/examples e.g. not paying attention, does not check messages; Problems with medium/examples e.g. message gets lost, distorted, technology breaks down, wrong channel used; Problems with sender/examples e.g. (different) language used, technical language, speaks too quickly, sends wrong message, message too long; No opportunity for feedback; Different time zones; Long chain of command/wide span of control; Cultural differences.

text: Explain two possible advantages to DCN of setting up a joint venture with the other business.
context: DCN is a large chemical company, 8,000 employees, agreed to set up a joint venture with a glass making business to develop new environmentally friendly packaging. Different leadership styles and business objectives noted as disadvantages.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 advantages = 6 marks). Advantages: Increase capital/share costs when making the packaging, which can help reduce borrowing; Access to new knowledge/expertise, as may learn things from their different leadership styles, could lead to greater productivity/efficiency/higher output; Access new markets, as no longer just selling chemicals, leading to higher revenue; Share risk; Share resources/share distribution networks/wider range of contact; Avoid/reduce competition, increasing market share; May be a legal requirement (in some countries)/avoid government restrictions; Increase production capacity, so able to meet potential demand. Application words: chemical, glass making, packaging, different leadership styles, 8,000 employees.

text: Do you think autocratic leadership is the most effective style for managers to use when an organisation has a large number of employees? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. DCN has 8,000 employees.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Autocratic: Quick decision-making possible, so may be able to respond to opportunities as soon as available; Demotivating workers (as have no say), leading to higher absenteeism/workers leaving/less employee loyalty/less output/lower productivity; No new ideas. Democratic: Workers have a say which can motivate employees; Can lead to more/better ideas/decisions; Takes time/time consuming/disagreements might arise; Creates time for managers to do other work; Can help maintain employee loyalty, reducing recruitment costs; Mistakes can be made if workers not skilled/lack experience, could damage reputation; Some workers might not want to be consulted, slowing decision-making. Laissez-faire: Can be highly motivating; Encourages employees to show creativity/responsibility; Task/work may not be suitable to delegate power; Does not allow for consistent approach, which can damage reputation. Justification: e.g. autocratic is the best method in this situation as when quick decisions need to be taken it may not be possible to use democratic leadership, especially with a large number of employees, and the business may miss an opportunity if it waits to hear everyone's views.

text: Define 'cost-plus pricing'.
context: Pamela is a sole trader, started her successful photography business 30 years ago, specialises in taking pictures for posters, calendars and fashion magazines, a niche market. Uses cost-plus pricing, 2 employees.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): The price is based on the cost of making a product and the addition of a fixed percentage for profit. OR The cost of manufacturing the product plus a (profit) mark-up. Partial (1 mark): Profit added to the cost. First mark for explaining what the 'plus' is (e.g. profit); second for reference to/description of mark-up.

text: Define 'marketing mix'.
context: Pamela uses cost-plus pricing as part of her marketing mix.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): All activities that go into the marketing of a product or service, often summarised as the four P's — product, promotion, place and price. OR Four marketing decisions needed for the effective marketing of a product. Partial (1 mark): (Combine) price, product, promotion and place, OR different strategies to help market/sell products. Do not award '4P's' or '7P's' alone as this does not define the term.

text: Outline two reasons why offering a high quality service might be important for Pamela's business.
context: Pamela's photography business, started 30 years ago, niche market, cost-plus pricing, 2 employees. Offering a high quality service is important.
ms: 1 mark per reason + 1 mark application (max 2 reasons = 4 marks). Reasons: Increase sales/maintain sales/attract customers of calendars/poster; Helps maintain/increase customer loyalty for this sole trader business; Maintain reputation/improve brand image built up over 30 years; Set/maintain high prices, which helps as uses cost-plus pricing; Way to add value, as operates in a niche market; To reduce complaints for the 2 employees; No need to replace faulty work; Gain competitive advantage, which can help her business remain successful. Application words: sole trader, 30 years, photography/posters/calendars/(fashion) magazines/pictures/camera, niche market, cost-plus pricing, 2 employees, successful business.

text: Explain two advantages to Pamela of operating as a sole trader.
context: Pamela's photography business, started 30 years ago, niche market, cost-plus pricing, 2 employees, high-quality service, successful business.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 advantages = 6 marks). Advantages: Keeps all the profit from photography business, so has an incentive to (continue to) work hard; Has complete control/makes all the decisions/does not need to consult with anyone such as the 2 employees, so able to take decisions more quickly; Own boss; Freedom to choose her own holidays/schedule/work time, so can choose time off when business is less busy so does not miss out on sales; Able to keep (financial) information private/do not need to produce annual accounts, so competitors cannot use information to take away her customers/market share, helping her stay successful; Has close contact with customers/able to offer a more personal service, as it's a niche market, encouraging customer loyalty. Application words: 30 years, photography/posters/calendars/(fashion) magazines/pictures/camera, niche market, cost-plus pricing, 2 employees, high-quality (service), successful business. Do not award points about start-up as business has been operating 30 years.

text: Do you think operating in a niche market will help a small business have a better chance of success than operating in a mass market? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Pamela's photography business operates in a niche market.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Niche market: Able to focus more closely on customer's needs, leading to customer loyalty/good customer relations; Less competition, less pressure to lower prices/easier to attract customers; May be able to set higher prices (for a high status, exclusive product), so able to have high/increase profit margin; Can become expert in the segment; Small size of market means will not benefit from economies of scale, leading to higher average costs; Less potential for growth/low potential demand; Over dependence on single product/less able to spread risk/vulnerable to changes in consumer spending patterns; Likely to attract competition if successful. Mass market: More (potential) customers/sales, leading to higher (potential) revenue; Increased/high level of competition, so might have high level of customer loyalty. To access evaluation, must identify points for both types of markets. Justification must relate to a small business — e.g. a small business has a better chance of success in a niche market because it can continue to charge high prices as large companies will not see the market as worthwhile because of potentially low sales.

text: Define 'opening balance'.
context: NPX is an online retail business, all orders sent directly to customers from its warehouse, 60 full-time workers. Cash-flow forecast: Opening balance $5,000/$15,000/$45,000.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Amount of cash held by a business at the start of the month/trading period. Partial (1 mark): Cash that a business has.

text: State two ways a business can increase productivity.
context: NPX wants to improve productivity by introducing new technology.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 2). Only award first two responses. Ways: Improve labour skills/(improve) training; (Increase) motivation (or examples — max 1); Automation/replace workers with machines; Use more automation; (Introduce) new technology/(use) better machinery; Improve quality of materials/improve quality control/introduce quality assurance; Improve/introduce inventory control/kaizen/JIT/lean production; Reorganise layout of factory/eliminate bottleneck.

text: Identify four sources of internal finance a business might use.
context: NPX's Operations Manager is considering using internal sources or external sources to finance new technology costing $40,000.
ms: 1 mark per source (max 4). Only award first four responses. Sources: (Retained) profit; Sale of (existing) non-current assets; Sale of inventories/reduce inventory levels/sell current assets; Owner's savings; Reduce trade receivables/ask customers to pay more quickly/reduce time given for customers to pay.

text: Explain two possible effects on NPX's cash-flow forecast of introducing the new technology.
context: NPX employs 60 full-time workers. New technology costing $40,000 will select and pack items, making 35 workers redundant. Cash-flow forecast (July-Sept, $000): closing balances $15/$45/$75.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 effects = 6 marks). Effects: Higher repayment costs/initial cost to buy machinery, which increases cash outflow as need to pay $40,000; Reduce wage costs, as need 35 fewer employees, lowering cash outflow; Increased training costs, increasing cash outflows; Possible redundancy payments, increasing cash outflow; Sell old machinery/use an external source of finance, which would generate a cash inflow. Application words: $40,000, 35/60 full-time (employees)/redundant, correct use of data e.g. $110,000 cash outflow in September, online retailer, warehouse, selecting and packing items, to improve productivity, internal/external source of finance.

text: Do you think it is better for a tertiary sector business to use full-time employees rather than part-time employees? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. NPX employs 60 full-time workers.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Full-time: Consistent service/more familiar with business, which helps build/maintain customer relationships/better reputation; Workers likely to be loyal/more committed/less likely to leave, reducing recruitment costs; Easy to communicate/update (compared to part-time employees), leading to fewer errors/misunderstandings; Need to recruit/train fewer employees, saving time or cost. Part-time: Able to extend business hours, to maximise potential sales; More flexible in hours of work, so able to cover absent workers/cover busy times; Reduces labour costs (compared to full time), as only pay employees for hours worked/when needed; Provide different/more skills/increase the experience/more ideas; Some employees may not want full-time jobs, so may miss out on possible candidates if not offered part-time option; Can attract well qualified employees who want to return to work but need flexible hours. Do not award answers about manufacturing/production. Justification must relate to a tertiary sector business — e.g. full-time employees are better especially for a tertiary sector business as quality of service is likely to be an important way customers judge the business, leading to repeat sales.

text: Define 'fixed cost'.
context: GHT is a public limited company producing steel products including gates and garage doors, flat organisational structure, short chain of command, 600 employees. Fixed costs $900,000.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Costs that do not change with the level of output/sales. OR Costs that do not vary in the short run with the number of items sold or produced. Partial (1 mark): Costs that do not change. Do not accept examples.

text: Calculate the margin of safety for product X in 2020. Show your working.
context: GHT product X data: Units sold in 2020: 30,000, Price per unit $100, Variable costs per unit $60, Fixed costs $900,000, Break-even output 22,500 units.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): 7500 (units). Method: Current output − break-even output = 30,000 − 22,500 (1 mark). Award only 1 mark if 7500 written as part of the answer but not final answer. If $ sign shown, award only 1 mark as this is not a financial value.

text: Outline two advantages to GHT of having a short chain of command.
context: GHT is a public limited company producing steel products, flat organisational structure, short chain of command, 600 employees.
ms: 1 mark per advantage + 1 mark application (max 2 advantages = 4 marks). Advantages: Communication is quicker/more accurate/quicker decision-making within the public limited company; Easier to delegate tasks/more delegation to its 600 employees; Workers feel more motivated; Lower costs as fewer managers/supervisors needed. Application words: steel/gates/garage doors, 600 employees, public limited company, flat (organisational structure), job rotation, improve employee motivation, 22,500 (break-even output), 30,000 (units sold), $100 (price per unit), $900,000 (fixed costs), $60 (variable cost per unit).

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to GHT of using job rotation to improve employee motivation.
context: GHT is a public limited company, 600 employees, Managing Director considering introducing job rotation to improve motivation.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantage: (As work more varied) fewer workers might leave from its 600 employees, leading to lower recruitment costs; Business has a more flexible/skilled workforce/multiskilling, leading to higher productivity/higher output; Easier to cover/replace others when someone is absent, so may be able to meet an order on time; Can help business identify where employees work best. Disadvantage: Increased training needed, increasing costs/expenses, so may increase its break-even output above 22,500; Workers may not be familiar with each task/less specialist in task, lowering quality/increase waste/leads to mistakes, increasing variable cost above $60; Takes time to learn different tasks/switch between jobs. Application words: steel/gates/garage doors, 600 employees, public limited company, 22,500 (break-even output), 30,000 (units sold), $100 (price per unit), $900,000 (fixed costs), $60 (variable cost per unit). Do not award 'motivate or demotivate employees' as this is stated in the question.

text: Do you think the shareholders are the most important stakeholder group to the success of a limited company? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. GHT has many stakeholder groups including 600 employees.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Shareholders/owners: Provide finance/invest money/capital in business, which can help the business expand/buy more equipment, increase output; Influence the aims of the business; Have the power to vote out the directors; They have little/no influence over day-to-day decisions. Other stakeholders: Customers — they buy the products, and if ignored will lose sales/revenue; Directors/managers — responsible for day-to-day decision-making; Employees — make the products, if demotivated quality may fall; Suppliers — provide materials/inventory; Local community — provide the workers; Government — provide legal framework; Bank — provide finance/loans. Justification must relate to a limited company — e.g. customers are probably the most important stakeholder as without them even a limited company cannot generate income, whereas shareholders have little influence over day-to-day decisions once established.

text: Define 'primary sector'.
context: Raul owns a small farm growing oranges, based in country Z. Like all primary sector activities, farming creates external costs and external benefits.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Extracts and uses the natural resources of the earth to produce raw materials used by other businesses. OR The sector that generates raw materials which the secondary sector then uses to make a product. OR Firms whose business activity involves the extraction of raw materials. Partial (1 mark): Involves natural resources, OR generate/produce raw materials. Do not award examples.

text: Identify two government economic objectives.
context: The Government of country E plans to introduce either import tariffs or quotas, which might help achieve one of its economic objectives.
ms: 1 mark per objective (max 2). Only award first two responses. Objectives: Low(er) unemployment/full employment/high(er) level of employment; Economic growth/increase in GDP/improve standards of living; Low inflation/price stability; Improve balance of payments.

text: Outline one external benefit and one external cost that Raul's business activity might create.
context: Raul owns a small farm growing oranges in country Z, sells all 600 tonnes direct to a drinks manufacturer in country E.
ms: 1 mark benefit/cost + 1 mark application (max 2 each = 4 marks). External benefit: Jobs created on the farm; Pay taxes on the oranges; Other businesses move into area; Trees release oxygen/planting trees improve air quality/absorb carbon dioxide. External cost: Loss of space/land use to produce 600 tonnes; Pollution/congestion caused by exporting; Deplete natural resources/use up water. Application words: (small) farm/farming, oranges/fruit, primary sector, 600 tonnes, export business/manufacturer in another country, (sell direct to) drinks manufacturer. Do not award manufacturer alone or country Z or E as application.

text: Explain two advantages to Raul's business of selling direct to a manufacturer.
context: Raul sells all 600 tonnes of oranges direct to a drinks manufacturer in country E, a small farm in country Z.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 advantages = 6 marks). Advantages: No need for intermediaries/middlemen, increasing profit margin for the farm; More predictable demand, which makes planning easier; Better understand customer needs such as which type of oranges, which can help maintain customer loyalty/sales; Can sell in large quantity/does not need to deliver to many businesses as sells all to drinks manufacturer, reducing distribution/transport cost; Less paperwork/saves time as have to deal with fewer/one customer, reducing administration costs; Less/no need for marketing as does not need to find retailers, reducing cash outflows. Application words: (small) farm, oranges, primary sector, 600 tonnes, export business/manufacturer in another country, (sell direct to) drinks manufacturer, quotas/tariffs. Do not award manufacturer alone or country Z or E as application.

text: Do you think the introduction of import tariffs is likely to have a greater effect than the introduction of import quotas on an exporting business? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. The Government of country E plans to introduce either import tariffs or quotas.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Tariffs: May lead to an increase in the price of goods/makes goods more expensive, which makes the products less competitive, leading to fewer sales/less revenue; Business may decide to maintain prices/not pass on price increase to customers, reducing profit margin. Quotas: Will limit the amount of goods that can be brought into a country, which will reduce the supply, reducing potential sales/revenue; May have to find new market for remaining products/store leftover inventory, increasing storage costs/total cost. To access evaluation, must identify relevant points for both tariffs and quotas. Justification must relate to an exporting business — e.g. tariffs likely have less effect as at least you can still export the amount you want and customers may still pay extra, whereas quotas could reduce or restrict the possibility of any sales.

text: Define 'public sector'.
context: BKH is a large public limited company, 2000 employees across 18 locations, sells insurance products (house and car insurance). Shareholders want to increase profit. Private sector has different objectives to public sector organisations.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Government or state-owned businesses/organisations. OR Part of the economy controlled by state/government. Partial (1 mark): Not owned by individuals, OR provided/run by government.

text: Define 'profit'.
context: BKH's shareholders want the business to increase profit.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Amount of money left after all costs have been subtracted from revenue. OR Surplus after total costs deducted from sales revenue. OR (Total) revenue − total cost. OR Gross profit minus expenses. Partial (1 mark): Revenue minus costs. Do not credit 'money made by business' as too vague.

text: Identify four ways to measure the size of a business.
context: BKH is a large public limited company with 2000 employees across 18 locations.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 4). Only award first four responses. Ways: Sales value/value of output/revenue; Volume of output/amount of services/amount of sales/number of customers; (Value of) capital employed/value of statement of financial position/market capitalisation; Market share; Number of employees; Number of outlets. Do not credit measures of success such as profit.

text: Explain one way each of Customers' and Employees' objectives might conflict with BKH's objective to increase profit.
context: BKH's shareholders want the business to increase profit, which can conflict with the objectives of other stakeholder groups, 2000 employees across 18 locations, planning to expand by taking over another insurance company.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per stakeholder (max 6 marks). Customers: May want low prices/value for money when buying insurance, which could reduce revenue; Desire high-quality customer service, which requires more than 2000 staff, increasing costs/expenses; May want offices in more locations than 18, which could increase costs. Employees: May want high/regular pay for its 2000 employees, which could lead to higher costs; May require job security/contract after the takeover; Job satisfaction/motivation/training/promotion. Application words: insurance (of house or car), 18 (locations), 2000 (employees), public limited company, shareholders, takeover or expand.

text: Do you think economies of scale are the most important reason for taking over another business? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. BKH is planning to expand by taking over another insurance company.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: Possible purchasing economies of scale/bulk buying, leading to lower average costs which could allow for lower prices; Reduces competition, which could increase market share/sales and therefore revenue; Economies of scale may not be possible to achieve; A business can become too large and may experience diseconomies of scale. Justification: e.g. it depends on the business' objectives — if a direct competitor, increased market share may be more important than possible economies of scale.

text: Define 'import quota'.
context: PJA make fashion clothing for 16-25 year olds, many competitors are multinational companies, all products made in a local factory because of import quotas.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Limit on the number of goods into a country. Partial (1 mark): Limit on number of imports.

text: Calculate PJA's gross profit margin. Show your working.
context: PJA's financial statements for 2020: Revenue $7,400m, Gross profit $3,330m, Profit $1,100m, Current ratio 1.5, ROCE 8%.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): 45(%). Method: Gross profit ÷ revenue × 100 = 3,330/7,400 × 100 (1 mark). 0.45 alone = 0 marks.

text: Outline one benefit and one limitation to PJA of developing new products.
context: PJA make fashion clothing for 16-25 year olds, produces new products every 3 weeks, all made in a local factory because of import quotas.
ms: 1 mark benefit/limitation + 1 mark application (max 2 each = 4 marks). Benefit: Attract new customers/sales/growth for its clothes; Need to replace products in decline/keep up with changing customer tastes of 16-25-year-olds; Retain customers/maintain market share; Spread risk/attract new markets/have other products to rely on for sales; Charge a higher price; Improve reputation; Can create a unique selling point. Limitation: No guarantee customers will like the new product as fashion changes; Competitors might introduce rival products/reduce prices as most competitors are multinational companies; High cost; Production issues, e.g. sufficient capacity within factory; Having access to suitable materials as trying to avoid import quotas. Application words: correct use of data from table 2.1, clothes, fashion, 16-25-year-olds/young customers, local, factory, multinational companies, 3 weeks/21 days.

text: Explain two ways PJA's managers can use ratio analysis.
context: PJA's Managing Director is reviewing financial statements using ratio analysis: Revenue $7,400m, Gross profit $3,330m, Profit $1,100m, Current ratio 1.5, ROCE 8%.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 ways = 6 marks). Ways: Able to see trends over time for its clothing, to see where/whether performance has improved; See trends between competitors such as whether revenue is higher than $7,400m, to assess competitiveness; Able to measure financial performance/profitability/success, as if last year ROCE was lower than 8% profitability has improved; Help make investment/expansion decisions such as developing new products; Check/manage liquidity OR working capital, as if last year current ratio was higher than 1.5 then liquidity has got worse. Application words: correct use of data from table 2.1, clothes, fashion, 16-25-year-olds/young customers, local or factory, multinational companies, develop new products.

text: Do you think multinational companies always benefit the countries they operate in? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Many of PJA's competitors are multinational companies.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: Creates jobs/provides income, improving living standards; Technical knowhow increased, could help improve production methods/efficiency/output; Orders for local suppliers, increasing local incomes/GDP; Improve international reputation of country; Increased investment/infrastructure development; Companies pay taxes, which increases government income; Competition for local businesses, leading to lower demand/lower prices which could lead to closure of local businesses; Profits are often repatriated, limiting the country's growth; Offer higher wages, reducing supply of workers for local business; Use up limited resources, so less available for other local businesses; Jobs created may be unskilled. Justification: e.g. companies pay taxes increasing government income, but reduced sales for local businesses may lead to lower revenue — a multinational always benefits a country to some extent because of the money invested, but overall impact depends on the effect on local businesses.

text: Define 'job rotation'.
context: Alex started APB as a sole trader business 4 years ago, provides printing services for local businesses (leaflets, brochures), 6 employees, uses job rotation to help keep employees motivated.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Employees swapping around and doing each specific task for only a limited time. OR Process of switching an employee between jobs over a period of time. OR Increasing variety in the workplace by allowing workers to switch from one task to another. Partial (1 mark): Workers do a variety of tasks.

text: State two factors that a service sector business should consider when deciding where to locate.
context: Alex thinks having a good location is important to any business.
ms: 1 mark per factor (max 2). Only award first two responses. Factors: Customers/level of demand; Cost of rent/taxes; Availability of land/space/parking; Government assistance; Cost/availability of labour; Legal controls; Competitors/near to other business; Transport/accessibility/technology/infrastructure or examples such as electricity, water, gas; Personal preference of owners; Climate. Do not award access to raw materials as not appropriate for a service sector business.

text: Outline one advantage and one disadvantage to APB of using on-the-job training.
context: APB provides printing services, 6 employees who all receive on-the-job training, a sole trader business, plans to buy an additional printing machine costing $1,800.
ms: 1 mark advantage/disadvantage + 1 mark application (max 2 each = 4 marks). Advantage: Some output produced while training, so able to still print some brochures; Costs less than off-the-job, and cost might be important as he is a sole trader; Specific to business/control what is taught using the printing machines. Disadvantage: Trainer may not produce as much output/potential disruption when teaching the 6 employees; Trainer may not have the necessary skills/may not know up-to-date methods for the new machine; Trainer may pass on bad habits/may be a poor-quality trainer; Employees make more mistakes when learning which increases waste. Application words: sole trader, printing services/leaflets/brochures, printing/new machine, 6 employees.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of Alex having a democratic leadership style.
context: Alex has a democratic leadership style and uses job rotation, 6 employees, plans to buy an additional printing machine costing $1,800 to meet increased demand.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantage: Improves motivation/sense of belonging of his 6 employees, leading to increased output/productivity; Help keep worker loyalty, less time/money spent on recruiting; Creates time for managers to do other work, leading to fewer mistakes; Better decisions could be made using employees' experience and skills such as deciding which is the best machine to buy; Positive work environment/better relations; More ideas/advice provided/better communication/encourages feedback. Disadvantage: Some employees may not want/be able to cope with being consulted, slowing decision-making about what to print; Unpopular decisions less likely to be made; Mistakes can be made if workers not skilled/lack experience, damaging reputation of this sole trader business; Time-consuming/disagreements may arise. Application words: sole trader, printing services/leaflets/brochures, 6 (employees), employees are motivated, increased demand, printing/new machine.

text: Do you think the amount of money needed is the most important factor for a sole trader to consider when deciding on an appropriate source of finance? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Alex has to decide on an appropriate source of finance for the new printing machine.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: The business might not have sufficient funds, so would need to borrow; A sole trader is likely to have access to fewer sources of finance; Cost of finance/interest, would change expenses, altering profit margin; Unlimited liability for sole traders, means personal assets are at risk if unable to pay debts; Amount of debt, if a business already has high borrowing banks may not lend more; Purpose (why money is needed), if buying a non-current asset then a long-term source would be used, allowing sufficient time to repay. Justification must relate to a sole trader — e.g. unlimited liability is probably the most important factor for a sole trader because this reduces the finance options available, and they are seen as higher risk so any finance is likely to be more expensive.

text: Define 'economic growth'.
context: Economic growth in country X has created many opportunities for new businesses such as TGH, which manufacture personalised mobile (cell) phone cases using job production.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): When a country's GDP increases/more goods and services are produced than in the previous year. Partial (1 mark): Increases in a country's spending/income/output, OR increase in GDP. For 2 marks answer must relate to a country not individual business.

text: Define 'quality assurance'.
context: Quality assurance is important to all 8 employees at TGH.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Checking for quality standards throughout production process/at every stage. Partial (1 mark): Checking work done. Do not credit answers such as check at end/check final product as this defines quality control.

text: Outline two reasons why building customer relationships might be important to TGH.
context: TGH manufactures personalised mobile phone cases using job production, quality assurance important, 8 employees, operates in a niche market, uses e-commerce, considering ways to build customer relationships.
ms: 1 mark per reason + 1 mark application (max 2 reasons = 4 marks). Reasons: Increase sales of phone cases; Customer loyalty/retention when using e-commerce; Help build reputation/brand image/act as free advertising for this new business; Opportunity for feedback/help identify customer needs as operates in a niche market; Provide a competitive advantage as other businesses may also set up because of economic growth. Application words: personalised, (mobile/phone) cases, new business/start-up, economic growth, niche market, e-commerce, 8 employees. Do not award phones alone as application (only makes covers).

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to TGH of using job production.
context: TGH manufactures personalised mobile phone cases using job production, 8 employees, quality assurance important, e-commerce, niche market.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantages: Unique/meet exact customer needs for its phone cases, can help brand loyalty; Workers likely to make fewer mistakes, helping ensure quality assurance, less need for rework; More varied work leads to higher motivation, helping retention/lower absenteeism in this new business; Can charge a higher price in a niche market; High quality products, which are personalised; Flexible. Disadvantages: Skilled labour can cost more for the 8 employees, increasing labour costs; No economies of scale (likely), leading to higher average cost; Production can take a long time, causing lower output/efficiency/productivity; Costs are higher as labour intensive; Mistakes can be expensive to correct. Application words: personalised, (mobile/phone) cases, e-commerce, new business, niche market, 8 employees, quality assurance.

text: Do you think cost-plus is the best pricing method for a new business to use when selling products to a niche market? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. TGH operates in a niche market, a new business.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Cost-plus: Know cost can be covered, and can make a profit per item; Simple and easy to calculate, so saves time when setting prices; Prices may be higher than competitors, leading to fewer sales; Little incentive to control costs. Other pricing methods: Penetration pricing — setting a lower price than competitors should attract customers; Competitive pricing — but limited or no control over the price, so may not be able to recover its costs; Price skimming — customers may expect/be willing to pay more in a niche market; Promotional pricing. Justification: e.g. cost-plus pricing is the best pricing method as covering costs is important for a new business, and although the price may be slightly higher this is less important in a niche market where there are likely to be fewer alternatives.

text: Define 'limited liability'.
context: RJJ manufactures women's shoes, sells to a niche market using e-commerce, a public limited company, shareholders benefit from limited liability. Profit decreased by $50,000 last year.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): The liability of shareholders/owners in a company is limited to only the amount they invested. OR The shareholders only risk losing the amount they have invested in the company (and not any of their personal wealth). Partial (1 mark): Shareholder only loses what they have put in, OR owners won't lose their personal assets if the business fails. Do not award 'separate legal identity' as this does not explain the term.

text: Define 'niche market'.
context: RJJ manufactures women's shoes and sells them to a niche market using e-commerce.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): A small, usually specialised, segment of a much larger market. OR Involves selling goods to small clearly identifiable segments of a market. Partial (1 mark): Selling to a small part/small segment of a (large) market, OR part of the market with specific needs/characteristics.

text: Outline two opportunities for consumers of using e-commerce when purchasing RJJ's products.
context: RJJ manufactures women's shoes, sells to a niche market using e-commerce.
ms: 1 mark per opportunity + 1 mark application (max 2 opportunities = 4 marks). Opportunities: Convenience/no need to leave the house/products can be delivered/can order anytime/save travel costs when buying shoes; Better information/easy to compare prices and products between websites/access to reviews, important as it's a niche market; Wider choice/consumers can easily access products from businesses in other countries; Lower prices/avoids having to pay extra to allow for retailers' profit margin. Application words: women, shoes, niche market.

text: Explain two factors RJJ's Finance Director should consider when deciding on a source of finance for the expansion.
context: RJJ is a public limited company, profit decreased by $50,000 last year, planning to expand, could take over a competitor.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 factors = 6 marks). Factors: Amount of money required, as operate in a niche market they may not have enough retained profits, so have to borrow/look for external sources; Length of time/how long to repay/how long the finance is needed for, as a long-term project such as the takeover would need a long-term source; Level of existing borrowing, particularly as profit fallen by $50,000, so if have a high level of debt lenders may not be willing to lend more; Type of business, because they are a public limited company may be seen as lower risk so offer lower interest rates; Credit history/financial status/amount of assets/liquidity, as lenders want to know if you have the ability to repay; Security/collateral; Interest/cost of finance; How quickly the business needs the money. Application words: shoes, niche market, public limited company/limited liability, takeover (a competitor), profit decreased/$50,000. Do not award purpose as this is stated in the question.

text: Do you think a takeover of a competitor is the best way for a large business to grow? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. RJJ could take over a competitor as part of its expansion plans.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: Possible economies of scale, leading to lower average costs; Reduced/less competition/increase market share, so able to increase prices/revenue; Access to new skills/expertise; (Bad reputation as) may need to make some workers redundant/negative impact on employee motivation/job insecurity, lowering productivity; High cost, which the business might not be able to afford; Possible clash of management styles/different objectives; Diseconomies of scale e.g. communication problems, leading to higher average costs. Other ways: Expand product range, which can help better control/manage speed of change; Merger; Joint venture. Justification must relate to a large business — e.g. internal growth may be safer especially when the business is large as controlling the rate of growth could allow managers time to plan and increase the chances of success.

text: Define 'market segmentation'.
context: ABA provides short-distance flights between 60 countries, a multinational company based in country X, uses market segmentation when deciding on its pricing method.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Dividing the whole market into segments by consumer characteristics and then targeting different products to each segment. OR An identifiable subgroup of a whole market in which consumers have similar characteristics or preferences. Partial (1 mark): Dividing the (whole) market into smaller groups, OR part of the market in which consumers have similar characteristics/preferences/interests.

text: Identify two pricing methods.
context: ABA uses market segmentation when deciding on its pricing method.
ms: 1 mark per pricing method (max 2). Only award first two responses. Methods: (Market/price) skimming; Penetration (pricing); Cost-plus (pricing); Competitive (pricing); Promotional (pricing). Candidates must identify, not simply describe, the pricing method.

text: Outline two factors which could affect the accuracy of ABA's market research.
context: ABA's marketing department is carrying out market research to gain feedback on customer experiences, provides short-distance flights between 60 countries.
ms: 1 mark per factor + 1 mark application (max 2 factors = 4 marks). Factors: Sample selected/type of sample/sample not representative of the population/how carefully sample drawn up of consumers buying (short-distance) flights; Wrong sample size/sample too small; Type of market research/wrong method chosen/who carried out the research to collect feedback about customer experiences; People may not answer truthfully/may not (fully) answer questions, leading to the business choosing the wrong pricing method; Wording of questions/wrong questions asked/poorly written, so don't gather views about sustainable development; Way/how questions are asked by the interviewer, as may be used in 60 countries; Where carry out market research; Age of the information/data out of date; Bias; Time available. Application words: flights or associated words such as airline/planes, 60 countries, customer experiences, pricing method, market segmentation, sustainable development, multinational company.

text: Explain two benefits to ABA of being a multinational company.
context: ABA is a multinational company providing short-distance flights between 60 countries, based in country X, considering ways to contribute to sustainable development.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 benefits = 6 marks). Benefits: Spreading risk, as not reliant on one market for all its sales/fall in sales in one country offset by increase in another, as operate in 60 countries; Increase sales/access new markets/new customers for its flights, increasing revenue; Improve brand image/reputation, to help increase/maintain customer loyalty; Access government support/grants; Avoid barriers to trade, which could reduce costs, may be able to change its pricing method; Reduced tax liability/take advantage of favourable tax rates. Application words: flights or associated words such as airline/planes, 60 countries, market segmentation, customer experiences, market research, pricing method, sustainable development. Do not award answers about advantages of being large in general e.g. economies of scale.

text: Do you think using renewable energy is the best way for a tertiary sector business to contribute to sustainable development? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. ABA is considering ways in which it can contribute to sustainable development.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Renewable energy: High cost (of installing environmentally friendly equipment), which the business may not be able to afford; May not provide sufficient power/not a reliable power source, leading to lost sales/revenue; Retailer may not use a high amount of energy. Other options: Recycle, but not all materials can be recycled; Change to environmentally friendly packaging/stop using (single-use) plastic; Reduce amount they purchase/use, so fewer resources needed; Only buy from suppliers who provide environmentally friendly products; Reduce waste, which may help increase efficiency and lower average cost; Avoid unnecessary travel by promoting a work from home policy. Do not credit answers which clearly refer to a manufacturing business. Justification must relate to a tertiary sector business — e.g. renewable energy is best especially as a tertiary sector business is unlikely to have much influence over the products themselves, and the money and resources saved by using renewable energy can reduce long-term costs.

text: Calculate the values of X and Y.
context: SMR's cash-flow forecast ($): April: Total inflows 1000, Total outflows 1400, Net cash flow (400), Opening 100, Closing (300). May: Total inflows 900, Total outflows 1400, Net cash flow (500), Opening X, Closing (800). June: Total inflows 900, Total outflows 1300, Net cash flow Y, Opening (800), Closing (1200).
ms: 1 mark per correct calculation. X: (300). Y: (400). Answers must be shown as negative values to be credited.

text: Define 'batch production'.
context: SMR produces snack food using batch production, sold to people watching sporting events in city Y.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): The production of goods whereby each batch of products passes through one stage of production at the same time before moving on to the next stage. OR A production method where similar items are produced together — a whole batch moves through the different stages of production together. OR Is where a quantity of one product is made, then a quantity of another item will be produced. Partial (1 mark): Similar items made together (in a group). Do not credit answers which simply reorder the words e.g. 'production done in batches'.

text: Identify four methods a business could use to ensure the quality of its products.
context: SMR has received complaints from customers about the quality of its snacks.
ms: 1 mark per method (max 4). Only award first four responses. Methods: Quality control/hire inspectors; Quality assurance; (Additional) training for employees/use skilled workers; Total quality management/Kaizen/quality circles; Improve or use high quality raw materials; Introduce automation/new technology/machinery; (Apply for a) quality mark/ISO scheme/quality standard.

text: Explain two ways SMR could overcome its cash-flow problems.
context: SMR produces snack food using batch production, pays bonuses to motivate its 3 part-time employees, has forecast cash-flow problems: closing balance $(300)/$(800)/$(1200) April-June.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 ways = 6 marks). Ways: Negotiate longer credit terms with suppliers/delay payment of bills for ingredients for snacks, to keep cash in the business for longer; Overdraft, would allow the business to have a negative cash balance for a while for this snack/food business; Asking customers to pay earlier/offering discounts to encourage quicker payments/insisting on cash sales, to get over $900 in May, allowing cash inflow sooner; Bank loan, as this would increase cash inflow; Reduce level of stock bought; Increase number of customers, could increase cash inflows; Delay/cancel purchases of capital equipment/sell surplus non-current assets; Find cheaper suppliers. Application words: batch production, snack/food business, sports events, 3/part-time (employees), correct use of data from table 3.1 such as closing balance $(1200) in June.

text: Do you think paying bonuses is the best way to motivate employees in a small business? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. SMR pays bonuses to motivate its 3 part-time employees.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Bonuses: Workers can feel recognised/special if they receive a bonus; Taylor's theory suggests money is the main motivator, could lead to an increase in productivity; Business only has to pay out if the target is reached; Maslow's theory suggests money is needed to meet basic needs; Not all employees are motivated by bonuses/money is not the only motivator; May only have a short-term boost to motivation, so any increase may be temporary; Increases costs, which a small business may not be able to afford; If some employees receive a bonus and others don't this may lead to conflict; Employees may be demotivated by unrealistic targets. Other methods: Praise, involves no additional cost; Job rotation, but may have to pay for training/not all employees able or willing to switch; Opportunities for promotion; Profit-sharing; Increase wage rates; Fringe benefits (only once). Justification must relate to a small business — e.g. bonuses could lead to conflict if only some employees receive one, whereas praise can be just as effective at no extra cost to a small business that may be short of finance.

text: Identify two ways of measuring the size of a business.
context: SCT is a small business that manufactures handmade tables, 50 trained employees.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 2). Only award first two responses. Ways: (Value of) capital employed; Market share; Value of output/value of sales/revenue; Number of employees; Value of business; Number of customers/volumes of output/number of services.

text: Identify two methods of training employees.
context: SCT has 50 trained employees.
ms: 1 mark per method (max 2). Only award first two responses. Two from: Induction; On-the-job; Off-the-job.

text: Outline two effects of a high rate of labour turnover to SCT.
context: SCT is a small business manufacturing handmade tables, 50 trained employees, Operations Manager uses an autocratic leadership style, some employees are demotivated with a high rate of labour turnover, planning to relocate to a new factory.
ms: 1 mark per effect + 1 mark application (max 2 effects = 4 marks). Effects: (Higher) cost of recruiting new/replacing workers, as have 50 employees; (Higher) cost of training new employees, as all workers need to be trained; Disruption to production/lower productivity/lower output/more mistakes/lower quality when making tables; Can damage business reputation/more difficult to recruit new employees, especially as manager has an autocratic leadership style; Takes managers time away from other important work, which might be a problem as it's a small business; Time taken to recruit new/replace workers for the factory; Time taken to train new employees. Application words: 50 employees, trained (employees), (handmade) tables or associated words such as wood, factory, autocratic leadership style, relocate, small (business).

text: Explain two factors SCT should consider when deciding on the location of a new factory in the same country.
context: SCT is a small business manufacturing handmade tables, 50 trained employees, planning to relocate to a new factory in the same country.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 factors = 6 marks). Factors: Cost of land, to see if they can afford it as they are a small business; Availability/cost of (suitable) labour, as they will need trained employees otherwise quality may drop; Government influence or examples such as grant/legal controls, which may influence or restrict where/how the business is allowed to operate when making tables; Access to suppliers/raw materials, as if far away could increase transport costs; Transport/communication links; Access to power/water; Possible external economies of scale; Enough space/scale of production. Application words: 50 employees, trained (employees), tables, high labour turnover, small (business).

text: Do you think autocratic leadership is the best style for a small business to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. SCT's Operations Manager uses an autocratic leadership style when making decisions.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Autocratic: Decisions can be made quickly, so able to respond to opportunities quicker/work can happen more quickly; No employee involvement/employees cannot give opinions/one-way communication, which can demotivate them, leading to absenteeism/higher labour turnover; Employees are closely supervised, so leaders/managers have less time for other tasks, could lead to more mistakes. Democratic: Can lead to more/better ideas, increasing productivity; Allows for better relationships between workers and managers; Involving employees in decisions/likely to delegate can help improve motivation; Takes time to ask people especially when many employees; Unpopular decisions cannot be made using this method; Some employees may not want/cope with extra responsibility. Laissez-faire: Highly motivating as given most responsibility; Task/work may not be suitable to delegate power. Justification must relate to a small business — e.g. autocratic can be good for quick decisions, but as a small business is less likely to have specialist managers for each department, they need to embrace the ideas of all employees, even if this takes longer.

text: Define 'entrepreneur'.
context: Mercy and Ayo are entrepreneurs, plan to open a shop selling homemade ice cream. Mercy wants the business to be ethical, only buying high quality organic milk from local farms. Ayo used sampling for primary market research.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): A person who organises, operates and takes the risk for a new business venture. OR An individual who takes the financial risk of starting and managing a new business. Partial (1 mark): A person who starts/sets up a business. Do not award answers such as managing a business or identifies skills of an entrepreneur on its own — need idea of starting a business AND taking (financial) risks.

text: State two reasons why sampling is used when carrying out market research.
context: Ayo used sampling to help him carry out some primary market research, results from 300 people in the sample about ice cream pricing.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two responses. Reasons: To bring the population to a manageable number/reduce number of people asked; To reduce cost (of having to ask large numbers of people); To save time (to carry out market research); To help reduce errors caused by having a large number in the population.

text: Outline two ways in which being ethical could help Mercy and Ayo's business.
context: Mercy wants the business to be ethical, only buying high quality organic milk from local farms, plans to open a shop selling homemade ice cream.
ms: 1 mark per way + 1 mark application (max 2 ways = 4 marks). Ways: Higher revenue/increase demand/enter new market for ice cream; Improved brand image/reputation for the shop; Build/encourage customer loyalty for this new business; Help create good supplier relations so able to obtain high-quality milk; Investors more likely to invest; Improve employee motivation/help recruit employees; May be possible to set a premium price/increase price; Less opposition from pressure groups. Application words: ice cream, shop/store, organic/milk/farm, entrepreneur, new business/start-up. Do not award 'better quality', 'legal' or 'rights'.

text: Explain two ways in which market research results can help Mercy and Ayo's business.
context: Ayo used sampling for primary market research: results from 300 people show what price they're willing to pay for a pot of ice cream ($0.50-$1.50: 90%; $1.51-$2.50: 55%; $2.51-$3.50: 20%; Over $3.50: 5%).
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 ways = 6 marks). Ways: Identify consumer needs/demand/target market as it's a new business to ensure sales/revenue; Helps set price/decide what price to set to help ensure they can break-even/cover costs; Help decide how to promote/promotion strategy for its products; Help decide the best location/place/distribution channel so know whether/where to locate the shop; Help identify (strength of) the competition; Help decide what/amount to produce/buy right amount of raw materials to keep variable costs low/reduce wastage; Reduces risks/products launched with more confidence for these entrepreneurs; Discover current and future market size/trends for ice cream. Application words: ice cream, shop/store, organic milk/farm, entrepreneur, new business/start-up, 300 (people).

text: Do you think a new business has a better chance of success if it locates where there is no competition? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Ayo thinks a new business has a better chance of success if it is located where there is no competition.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application.
