Points: Able to gain more customers/sales/no risk of brand loyalty to another business, so increase in (potential) revenue/market share; May indicate a gap in the market; Lower costs of promotion, reduce expenses/can help maintain/improve profit margin; May indicate low demand/few or no customers available/small target market, so difficult to break-even; Could depend on product or service offered, as if new product there may not be many competitors; Able to set higher prices (as no one to compete against), leading to higher revenue. Do not award vague answers such as 'easier to compete' or 'lower/high risk', or answers which outline solutions. Justification: e.g. it might mean there are few or no customers available so small target market — if there is no demand, there is no point setting up there unless the product is unique, because they will not gain enough sales to break even let alone be successful.

text: Define 'job production'.
context: Lola and Raul are in a business partnership, make hand-printed products including t-shirts, bags and posters using job production, most customers are tourists.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Where a single product is made at a time. OR Makes one product from start to finish (before starting the next one). OR Produce a (personalised) product individually. Partial (1 mark): Single product made, OR produce a personalised product.

text: Identify two reasons why a business might want to expand.
context: Raul wants to increase output for the hand-printed products business.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two responses. Reasons: Increase sales/sales revenue; Increase profit; Return to shareholders; Spread risk; Increase reputation/brand image/prestige; Increase customer base/target new markets; Increase market share; Economies of scale.

text: Outline two ways Lola and Raul's business could use a website.
context: Lola and Raul make hand-printed products (t-shirts, bags, posters), most customers are tourists, Raul wants to develop a website.
ms: 1 mark per way + 1 mark application (max 2 ways = 4 marks). Ways: Take orders/sell its products as well as the shop; Advertise/promote/raise awareness/give out information about its products to people other than tourists; Obtain feedback/reviews about its t-shirts; Advertise job vacancies. Application words: hand-printed or examples such as T-shirts/bags/posters, tourists, (small) shop/store.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to Lola and Raul of being in a business partnership.
context: Lola and Raul are in a business partnership making hand-printed products, tourists are most customers, Lola prints at back of small shop, Raul does sales and finance.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantage: More ideas about what type of hand printed items to offer, can help increase revenue/sales; Access to more capital (than sole trader) to pay for setting up a website, improving chance of expanding; More skills/expertise/can specialise, Raul does the finance and sales, allowing time for Lola to focus on her job; Share loss/risk, so do not have to carry all the financial burden; Share workload. Disadvantage: Disagreements such as how to increase output, which could lead to lower productivity; Unlimited liability/each responsible for debts of other, so their personal belongings are at risk as well as the shop; Have to share profits; Slower decision-making. Application words: hand-printed (items) or examples such as T-shirts/bags/posters, tourists, shop/store, website, introduce machinery.

text: Do you think introducing machinery is a better way for a small business to increase output than recruiting more employees? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Raul wants to increase output — one way is to introduce machinery into the process.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Introducing machinery: Likely to be more consistent/better quality/fewer mistakes, reducing amount of rework/wastage; Machines do not need to rest, so can work for longer periods of time/24-7; Higher productivity/more efficient, lower average cost; High cost/expensive to invest in equipment, which would increase cash outflows a small business might not afford; May not have space to introduce machinery; May require more skilled workers, increasing labour costs; Higher maintenance costs, increasing expenses; Can become outdated quite quickly. Recruit more employees: Cost/time to recruit; Training may be required, increase costs. Justification: e.g. it may still be better for a small business to recruit more employees, especially if the increase in output is only temporary as the initial cost of machinery is likely high — safer to wait before taking a major financial decision to see whether higher demand can be sustained.

text: Define 'non-current assets'.
context: CLN is a public limited company selling electrical products such as televisions and computers, made a loss of $250m last year, plans to close 30 of its 120 shops.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Resources owned by a business which will be used for a period longer than one year. OR Items owned by a business that last for more than 12 months. Partial (1 mark): Items owned by a business. Do not award examples.

text: Calculate the acid test ratio. Show your working.
context: CLN's statement of financial position as at 30 Sept 2020 ($m): Non-current assets 48, Current assets 60 (of which inventories 40), Current liabilities 30.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): 0.67 or 0.66. Method: (Current assets − inventory) ÷ current liabilities = (60-40)/30 (1 mark). If correct answer given with no working shown, award 2 marks.

text: State four factors that can affect the source of finance a business might use.
context: The Managing Director said CLN needs more finance after making a loss of $250m last year.
ms: 1 mark per factor (max 4). Only award first four responses. Factors: Amount needed; Existing borrowing/gearing; Length of time/how long to repay; Purpose/what it is needed for; Level of security/assets available to use as guarantee; Interest rates; Legal form/type of business/size of business; Loss of ownership/control.

text: Explain two ways in which local communities might be affected by CLN's decision to close some of its shops.
context: CLN is a public limited company selling electrical products (televisions, computers), plans to close 30 of its 120 shops, made a loss of $250m last year, blames increased competition from e-commerce.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 ways = 6 marks). Ways (can be positive or negative): Job losses/higher unemployment, so lower standard of living/have less money to spend at other businesses as well as those selling electrical goods; Environmental benefits or examples such as less traffic, so less pollution (leading to health issues) outside the 120 shops; Reduction in local facilities, which could lead to higher prices having to be paid; Reduction in house prices/damage image of the local area. Application words: 30 or 120 (shops), electrical products or examples such as televisions/computers, $250m (loss).

text: Do you think the number of sales from each shop is the best way for a retail business to decide which shops to close? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. The number of sales from each shop will be used to decide which of CLN's shops to close.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: Higher sales could mean higher revenue, which can help contribute to break-even; Lower sales could suggest shop is not a popular location, so customers less likely to complain if it closes; What products are sold, as a shop selling high value items would not need to sell as many as one selling low value items. Other factors: Costs/expenses, as a business could still be profitable as long as costs are lower than revenue; Number of competitors; Size of target market/number of customers; Profit; Number of employees; Value of sales/revenue; Proximity to its other shops. Justification: e.g. as no method will give perfect answers, number of sales is probably best especially as it is simple to use, so at least people will understand the reasons for using it.

text: State two ways quality production can be achieved.
context: Kane started LFP 8 years ago, makes high quality furniture, imports 40% of its materials including wood.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 2). Only award first two responses. Ways: Quality control; Quality assurance; Total Quality Management/quality circles; Further training/recruit skilled workers; Improve quality of raw materials; Use new/better technology/CAM/CAD. Do not award lean production, or vague answers such as use machinery/improve motivation/check quality.

text: Identify two benefits to a business of having a clear organisational structure.
context: Kane thinks having a clear organisational structure benefits a business.
ms: 1 mark per benefit (max 2). Only award first two responses. Benefits: Shows how everybody is linked together in the organisation; Each individual can see their own position in the organisation/makes accountability easier; Shows the links and relationship between different departments; Can show where possible problems of control/communication might be/helps clear communication; Allows for effective delegation.

text: Outline two factors Kane should consider when preparing the job advertisement.
context: Kane started LFP 8 years ago, makes high quality furniture, needs to recruit 5 additional production workers as demand is increasing, preparing a job advertisement.
ms: 1 mark per factor + 1 mark application (max 2 factors = 4 marks). Factors: What information to include such as skills needed to make furniture; Where advert should be placed/which method of job advertisement to use for 5 production workers; Cost/which method can they afford to use; Comply with legal controls i.e. no age/gender discrimination. Application words: furniture/wood, 5 (production workers), well-motivated employees.

text: Explain how each of the following external influences might affect LFP: Lower employment rates AND Introduction of import quotas.
context: LFP makes high quality furniture, imports 40% of its materials including wood, needs to recruit 5 additional production workers, Kane knows there are many external influences on business activity.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per influence (max 6 marks). Lower employment levels: Wider pool of potential employees for the 5 workers, possibly at lower wage rates/better able to find quality candidates; Lower incomes, lower demand/lower sales for its furniture. Import quotas: Limit amount of products that a business can bring into a country, so have access to less wood, may be unable to fulfil all its orders; Could force LFP to find new suppliers as 40% imported, which could increase costs of sales/selling price. Application words: furniture, wood, 5 (production workers), 40%.

text: Do you think increasing wages is a better way for a business to motivate employees than introducing profit sharing? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Kane is considering either increasing wages or introducing profit sharing for well-motivated employees.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Increase wages: Taylor's theory suggests higher wages increases motivation/Herzberg's theory states pay is a hygiene factor and not a motivator; Higher wages add to business costs, which may not be covered by additional output; Only a short-term boost to motivation/likely to be paid the higher amount whether they work harder or not, so any increase is only temporary; Will provide a regular/steady income to maintain standard of living. Profit sharing: Creates team spirit/common goal/sense of belonging, which could lead to higher overall profit/increase output; Only receive/pay out if profits made; Sharing profits might reduce retained profit, which could mean less capital for expansion; Other factors can affect profit which employees cannot control, so no guarantee of receiving much. Justification: e.g. profit sharing is better as higher wages must automatically be paid whether the business makes a profit or not, which could reduce potential profit further, so it's better to use profit sharing as the business only pays out when a profit has been made.

text: Identify two features of an economic boom.
context: Kolo owns a successful hairdressing salon in the city centre, 4 part-time employees, made a profit in each of the last 3 years, wants to expand by opening another salon to take advantage of the economic boom.
ms: 1 mark per feature (max 2). Only award first two responses. Features: Rapid/fast increase in GDP/highest GDP; Increase in prices/high prices/inflation; High levels of demand; (Very) low unemployment/shortage of skilled workers; Increase in wages/high income/standard of living at highest; Increase in/high business profits/profit at its highest; Increase in/rising business costs; Significant/high levels of business investment; High capacity utilisation/increase in business output; Increase in number of business start-ups. Do not award 'high GDP' as this is associated with economic growth.

text: Identify two stages of the recruitment process.
context: Kolo plans to recruit a manager for the second salon using external recruitment.
ms: 1 mark per stage (max 2). Only award first two responses. Stages: Job analysis/identify a vacancy; Job description; Person/job specification; Advertising (the vacancy); Application forms sent out/received; Shortlisting/screening; Interview/testing; Selection/job offer. Answer must be from the business viewpoint not the applicant.

text: Outline two possible advantages to Kolo of recruiting a manager.
context: Kolo owns a hairdressing salon, 4 part-time employees, wants to expand by opening another salon, plans to recruit a manager for the second salon.
ms: 1 mark per advantage + 1 mark application (max 2 advantages = 4 marks). Advantages: Reduce Kolo's workload/can delegate tasks/share responsibility as would need to manage two businesses; Can provide new ideas/experience/skills about hairstyles; Can motivate/inspire others such as the 4 employees. Application words: hairdressing or examples such as hairstyles/shampoo, (2) salons/second/new business, 4 (employees), city (centre), make a profit in each of the last 3 years, economic boom.

text: Explain two reasons why choosing the right location for the new salon is important for Kolo.
context: Kolo has identified 2 possible candidates: Candidate 1 (5 years experience, advanced hairdressing certificate, never managed a salon) and Candidate 2 (20 years experience, basic hairdressing certificate, uses autocratic leadership style). Wants to open a second salon.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 reasons = 6 marks). Reasons: Help attract customers/number of potential customers/close to customers/level of income/target market who want their haircut, increasing revenue/allowing it to break-even; Proximity to competition/may be loyal to another business, so may have to lower prices; Have good access/easy to find/space for parking, leading to more sales; Rent, as likely to be expensive in the city centre, will increase his fixed/total costs; Distance to other salon, as if far away will increase transport cost; Help attract employees/close to employees, as it's economic boom might be difficult to find (suitably) skilled people; Provide safe/low crime environment/security, otherwise customers may not wish to visit; Location has to match its brand image; Meet legal controls/government influence. Application words: hairdressing or examples such as hairstyles/shampoo, city (centre), 4 (employees), 2 businesses/second business, make a profit in each of the last 3 years, economic boom. Do not award 'salon' as application as stated in question.

text: Do you think experience is the most important factor for a business to consider when recruiting a new manager? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Kolo has identified two possible candidates for the manager position.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Experience: Experienced person may expect higher wages, increasing labour costs; Experienced person likely to make fewer mistakes, so business may be able to provide better service/more efficient, increasing brand loyalty; Business knows they have shown ability to do the job, lower cost/time of training; May not be willing to listen to ideas of owner/other employees, which could demotivate other employees. Other factors: Personality/leadership style, as a manager must be able to lead/work with subordinates; Qualifications/skills, show technical ability; Requirements of the job, because if new role, might not be anyone with necessary experience anyway. Justification: e.g. experience is likely the most important factor as it clearly shows the person has shown ability to do the job, whereas qualifications only indicate they have the knowledge to do so, so may add value to the business more quickly.

text: Define 'pressure group'.
context: DSY is a private limited company producing washing machines and cleaning equipment, plans to spend $2bn developing electric cars. A leading pressure group has identified environmental problems of non-electric cars.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Group formed by people with a common interest who take action to change/influence business decisions or government policies. OR Organisations of like-minded people who put pressure on businesses and the government to change their policies to reach a predetermined objective. Partial (1 mark): Group formed by people with a common interest. For 2 marks must have idea of a group with a common interest and influence on business or government.

text: Define 'brand image'.
context: DSY has important decisions about the new car's brand image still to be made.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Identity/logo/unique name of a product that distinguishes it from other brands. OR The general impression/perception/reputation of a product held by consumers. Partial (1 mark): Identity given to a product, OR something that distinguishes a product from its competitors, OR how the product is seen/perceived by others.

text: Outline two advantages to DSY of being a private limited company.
context: DSY is a private limited company, produces washing machines and cleaning equipment, plans to spend $2bn on electric cars, competitive/growing electric car market.
ms: 1 mark per advantage + 1 mark application (max 2 advantages = 4 marks). Advantages: Access to more capital (than unlimited company)/can raise capital by selling shares to start making cars; Control over who buys shares/less risk of takeover (than public limited company), which may be important given the lot of competition; Continuity of existence; Separate legal identity; (Its shareholders benefit from) limited liability/incorporated. Application words: (electric) cars, lot of competition, $2bn, market is growing rapidly, different market, washing machines/cleaning equipment.

text: Explain two factors DSY should consider when deciding on a suitable method of production for the new product.
context: DSY plans to spend $2bn on electric cars, competitive/growing electric car market, decisions about method of production and brand image still to be made.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 factors = 6 marks). Factors: Access to/amount of capital available/cost of machinery, as may not afford to set up flow production when already planning to spend $2bn; Level of demand/size of market/volume needed, as there is a lot of competition, may not be able to sell/need to produce a large number; Nature/type of product, as cars are more likely to be mass produced to be cost-efficient/if luxury then job production might be suitable; Access to/amount of suitable space (inside the factory); Access to (suitable/skilled) employees; Possible environmental damage/impact/pollution, which leads to protests by pressure groups which could damage its reputation/potential sales; How efficient is the method of production/amount of waste. Application words: (electric) cars, washing machines/cleaning equipment, lot of competition, $2bn, market is growing rapidly, pressure groups.

text: Do you think entering a growing market where there is a lot of competition is the best way for a business to expand? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. DSY wants to expand into the electric car market which is growing rapidly with a lot of competition.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: Shows high potential demand/many potential customers, could lead to increase in revenue; Have to do something different to make product 'stand out'/customers may be brand loyal to other businesses, leading to higher/lower sales/revenue; Allow business to spread risk; Difficult to charge high prices/may have to set lower prices (than competitors), lowering profit margin/so difficult to break-even; (Additional) costs of promotion/market research, leading to higher expenses; Makes the business be more efficient, to reduce average costs. Other options: Develop new products; Expand in existing market; Find new market with low/no competition, provides chance for monopoly; Take over a competitor, gain their market share. Justification: e.g. it will depend on how good its product is — if customers are interested despite competition, worth the risk to gain market share justifying expansion costs.

text: Define 'micro-finance'.
context: Veronique is bored with her work in a large factory, would like to leave and start up a flower shop, has asked about micro-finance.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Provides financial services/small loans to poor people not served by traditional banks. Partial (1 mark): Not given by big banks, OR helps people who can't afford a (bank) loan, OR small loans to poor people.

text: Calculate the new net cash flow in month 3 and the new closing balance in month 3.
context: Cash flow forecast for Veronique's flower shop ($): Month 3: Cash out $1,200, Opening balance $(1,200). Veronique now thinks cash inflow in month 3 will be $1,500 (originally forecast at $2,000).
ms: 1 mark per correct calculation. New net cash flow in month 3: 300. New closing balance in month 3: (900) or −900. New closing balance must be shown as a negative value to be credited. OFR rule applies for new closing balance.

text: State four reasons why a business might have cash flow problems.
context: Veronique has prepared a cash flow forecast for her new flower shop.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 4). Only award first four responses. Reasons: Lack of demand/economic downturn/seasonal demand; Poor cash flow management/not prepared a cash flow forecast; Unable to get a bank loan/overdraft; High level of trade receivables/allowing customers (too much) credit; Not able to purchase materials on credit/pay suppliers too soon; Increase in/higher fixed costs or examples such as rent costs too high; Increase in/higher variable costs; High level of inventory/holding too much stock; Overtrading/expanding too quickly; Unexpected changes e.g. machine breakdown/loss of key employees/loss of key customer (allow only once); Inaccurate financial information.

text: Explain one method of primary market research and one method of secondary market research Veronique could have used.
context: Veronique wants to start up a flower shop, carried out market research and found demand for flowers is likely high during festivals.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per method (max 6 marks). Primary market research: Questionnaire — provides up-to-date information/specific to her business about trends for festivals; Interviews — obtain in depth details/opinions about different type of flowers; Online survey — more likely to get responses/reach more people; Focus group — provides detailed information about consumer tastes/allows follow-up questions; Observation — avoids interviewer bias; Test marketing — cost of any problem limited to smaller number of products. Secondary market research: Government statistics — being official provides more accurate data to help improve her cash flow forecast; Online sources/internet research — low cost/readily available, helpful for a new business; Market research agency reports; Trade associations/data from similar businesses. Application words: flower (shop), festivals, start-up/new business.

text: Do you think being creative is the most important characteristic of being a successful entrepreneur? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Veronique thinks she has the right characteristics to be a successful entrepreneur.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Creative: New/unique ideas to help gain sales/attract customers/maintain customer loyalty; Can open up new opportunities; Customers may not like the products. Other characteristics: Risk taker — as needs to be able to make decisions that might fail, otherwise will not know whether an idea is good or not; Perseverance/determination — will need to keep going when faced with problems; Effective communicator — need to convince suppliers/finance providers/customers; Good decision-maker/management skills; Hard-working; Optimistic; Self-confident; Independent. Justification: e.g. a creative but risk averse entrepreneur may miss the opportunity to be first to market, losing the chance to gain a competitive advantage — so creativity is important but not the most important characteristic. An answer that only discusses other characteristics without addressing being creative cannot access evaluation marks.

text: Define 'break-even'.
context: Gino owns a fast-food restaurant selling fried chicken and potato fries, employs 5 full-time chefs and 12 part-time workers, took 3 years to break-even.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): When total costs is the same as total revenue. OR Total revenue (TR) = Total cost (TC). OR The level of output at which Total revenue = Total Cost. Partial (1 mark): No profit or loss, OR revenue covers costs, OR point where start making profit.

text: Define 'Return on Capital Employed'.
context: Gino aims to achieve a Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) of 10%.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Profit as a percentage of capital employed. OR Correct formula: (Profit/Capital employed) × 100. OR Profit made on each dollar/pound invested in the business. Partial (1 mark): Money made on investment/capital, OR shows how effectively a business uses its capital. Do not award answers which simply reorder the words.

text: Outline two problems inflation might cause Gino's business.
context: Gino owns a fast-food restaurant selling fried chicken and potato fries, employs 5 full-time chefs and 12 part-time workers, inflation may be a problem for his business.
ms: 1 mark per problem + 1 mark application (max 2 problems = 4 marks). Problems: Fewer customers/lower demand/lower sales/less revenue at the restaurant; Supplier prices may increase for its chicken/fries; Employees might demand higher wages from its 17 employees; May have to increase its prices; Businesses unlikely to want to/will not expand. Application words: fast-food or examples such as fried chicken, potato fries, food, restaurant, 17 or 5 (full-time) or 12 (part-time) or chefs, menu.

text: Explain two ways Gino could increase the number of customers.
context: Gino owns a fast-food restaurant selling fried chicken and potato fries, is always looking for ways to increase the number of customers.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 ways = 6 marks). Ways: Advertise or examples such as promote on social media, to inform/raise awareness/attract about his restaurant; Promotional pricing/discounts/lower prices, to compensate for effect of inflation, more affordable; Loyalty schemes, encourage customers to return again and again; Introduce new products other than chicken/fries, target different/new market segments; Offer better customer service/better quality, improve brand image/reputation; Open additional outlet/increase size of existing place/extend opening hours/offer home delivery, able to cater for more people at same time; Free samples; Sponsorship; Competition. Application words: fast-food or examples such as fried chicken, potato fries, restaurant, 17 or 5 (full-time) or 12 (part-time) or chefs, menu.

text: Do you think having regular meetings is a better way for a business to communicate with part-time employees than using text messages? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Gino has regular meetings with his part-time employees to keep them informed about menu changes.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Meetings: Allow two-way communication/immediate feedback/allows ideas to be discussed, so can explain if instructions not understood (straightaway); Information can be given out quickly/more detailed; Message can be reinforced by body language of attendees; May take time/be difficult to arrange, as part-time employees do not work all the time; Will take people away from work, leading to lower output/lower efficiency/missed sales. Text messages: No guarantee read/may not have a phone, leading to mistakes/wasting resources; Have a hard copy/record which can be referred to later; Can send at any time, allowing people to read when convenient. Justification: e.g. meetings can be difficult to arrange but are the best option for part-time employees as slow decision making could result in missed opportunities, resulting in fewer sales, which can more than offset the cost of the time spent arranging the meeting.

text: Define 'trade union'.
context: SRB is a bank providing loans to business customers, plans to make 100 managers' jobs redundant from its 80 branches, part of a plan to save $1m in costs over 2 years, working with the trade union.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Group of workers who join together to ensure their interests are protected. OR Organisation that represents the workers and fights for improvements to pay and conditions. OR An organisation that exists to provide workplace support for its members. Partial (1 mark): Group of workers who join together, OR group of people who act together to protect their rights. Do not award pressure group.

text: Define 'level of hierarchy'.
context: SRB plans to remove one level of hierarchy as part of making 100 managers redundant.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Managers/supervisors/other employees who are given a similar level of responsibility in an organisation. OR A level of authority in a business structure. Partial (1 mark): People all at the same rank. To gain 2 marks answer should show workers are on a similar level and within one organisation.

text: Outline two advantages of SRB using delegation.
context: SRB is a bank with 80 branches, will make more use of delegation, plans to make 100 managers' jobs redundant.
ms: 1 mark per advantage + 1 mark application (max 2 advantages = 4 marks). Advantages: Workload spread more evenly/reduced workload for managers in its 80 branches; Management can focus on more important matters such as responding to increased competition; Motivates employees/gives sense of responsibility, so fewer problems with trade unions; Improved efficiency/better quality of work; Career opportunities, as able to do similar work to the 100 managers; Management can measure success of staff more easily; Can assist with training. Application words: business customers, 100 managers, 80 branches, removing one level of hierarchy, saving $1m in costs, increased competition, bank (services) or related words such as loans, develop new products and services, trade union.

text: Explain two factors SRB should consider when deciding which managers to make redundant.
context: SRB plans to make 100 managers' jobs redundant from its 80 branches, part of a plan to save $1m in costs over 2 years.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 factors = 6 marks). Factors: Importance of the role being performed, to maintain contact with business customers, to ensure good customer service; Performance/experience/skills/flexibility, such as not able to use delegation, so not able to do the job required; Length of time worked/redundancy costs, may be cheaper to choose people who have not been there long; Attitude/attendance/disciplinary record, will want to lose poor/bad workers from the 80 branches; Wages/salary, as removing higher paid employees would help reduce costs long term, helping reach the $1m cost reduction; Which departments need to lose/retain workers; Number of customers at the branch; The number of subordinates under each manager; Those who volunteer. Application words: business customers, 100 managers, 80 branches, removing one level of the hierarchy, saving $1m in costs, increased competition, bank (services)/give loans, delegation.

text: Do you think that more advertising is a better way for a business to respond to increased competition than introducing new products and services? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. SRB has to respond to increased competition from online banks, could either advertise more or develop new products and services.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Advertising: To raise awareness of products, increasing revenue, but products might not be what customers want limiting effectiveness; No guarantee target customers may see it, so sales may not rise; More advertising will increase costs; Widen target market/appeal to more potential customers. Introducing new products: Widen target market/appeal to more potential customers; May not appeal to customers; High cost of development, adding to expenses; Allows access to new markets, helps spread risk and increases potential sales. Justification: e.g. it depends on reason for increased competition — if customers dislike your products then advertising may not be effective; developing products may be more expensive but the business could have little choice if it wants to remain competitive.

text: Define 'flow production'.
context: YMG is a private limited company, the largest manufacturer of soft drinks in country V, produces 1 billion litres a year using flow production, plans to increase to 3 billion litres over 5 years.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Where large quantities of a product are produced in a continuous process. OR Mass production using a production line. Partial (1 mark): Makes lots of the same thing, OR large quantities of a standardised product, OR large-scale/continuous production.

text: Identify two methods (other than technology) a business can use to improve efficiency.
context: YMG plans to invest $60m in new technology to improve efficiency.
ms: 1 mark per method (max 2). Only award first two responses. Methods: Reorganise layout/reduce waste/Kaizen/JIT/lean production; Training/improve employee skills/employ more skilled workers; Improve motivation/communication; Specialisation. Do not accept employ more workers as this will not improve efficiency.

text: Outline two sources of finance YMG could use for the new technology.
context: YMG is a private limited company, largest manufacturer of soft drinks, plans to invest $60m in new technology, wants to expand into new markets in other countries.
ms: 1 mark per source + 1 mark application (max 2 sources = 4 marks, long-term sources required). Sources: Sell shares/owners capital, as a private limited company; Bank loan, as need $60m; (Retained) profits, as likely to have funds as the largest manufacturer; Leasing, as moving into new markets overseas may not be successful; Hire purchase; Owners savings; Sell unwanted assets; Crowdfunding. Application words: private limited company/sell shares to family and friends, flow production, $60m, new markets, the largest manufacturer, 3 billion litres, soft drinks.

text: Explain how each of the following problems might affect YMG when entering new markets in other countries: Lack of local knowledge AND Import quotas.
context: YMG plans to sell products in new markets in other countries, knows import quotas and lack of local knowledge can cause problems but there are ways to overcome them.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per problem (max 6 marks). Lack of local knowledge: May not be aware of competitors' actions, leading to fewer sales/lower revenue of soft drinks; May not understand customer buying habits, so must spend more money developing new products rather than investing $60m in new technology; Customers may not like the soft drinks. Import quotas: This limits the number of items that can be brought into the country, so fewer litres needed, which could lead to higher prices. Application words: private limited company, flow production, $60m, the largest manufacturer, 3 billion litres, new technology, soft drinks, expanding production. Do not accept answers which clearly refer to tariffs.

text: Do you think a joint venture is the best way for a business to enter a new market in another country? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. YMG wants to start selling its soft drinks in new markets in other countries.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Joint venture: Allows the business to gain important local information about customers, better able to meet customer requirements, ensuring sales; Wider range of contacts/better access to resources, may be able to obtain cheaper resources, reducing production costs; Less competition, as working with local business, helping to increase market share; Can provide access to other specialist staff and technology; Clash of management styles, lead to conflict/problems with decision making; Must share profits. Other options: Franchising — reduces problem of local knowledge but may negatively affect reputation; Licensing — losing control over production; Expand themselves — allows retaining all profits. Justification: e.g. a joint venture is the best way as it helps reduce the risks of setting up in a new country, since expanding on their own would require raising more capital which may be too expensive.

text: Define 'sole trader'.
context: Elton is a sole trader, sells specialist clothing and equipment for sports (baseball, hockey), a niche market, started 5 years ago, remained small.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Ownership of business in the hands of one individual/person. OR Unincorporated business owned by one person. Partial (1 mark): Run/operated by one person. Do not accept features such as unlimited liability.

text: Calculate X and Y.
context: Elton's revenue and cost data for 2018 and 2019 ($): 2018 — Revenue 24,000, Cost of sales 7,200, Gross profit 16,800, Expenses 8,400, Profit X. 2019 — Revenue 25,000, Cost of sales Y, Gross profit 18,000, Expenses 10,000, Profit 8,000.
ms: 1 mark per correct calculation. X = 8,400. Y = 7,000. $ sign not required.

text: State four factors that can influence the amount of inventory a business might hold.
context: A wide range of inventory is important to Elton's specialist sports clothing and equipment business.
ms: 1 mark per factor (max 4). Only award first four responses. Factors: Demand from customers/amount of sales; Perishability of the items; Storage space available; Cost of storage; Delivery charges; Seasons/celebrations/festivals; Amount of money available (to buy inventory); Lead time/reliability of supplier; Method of production (mass may require high inventory); Stock control system — JIT/lean production.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to Elton of operating in a niche market.
context: Elton sells specialist clothing and equipment for sports (baseball, hockey), a niche market, started 5 years ago, remained small, profit margin for 2018 was 35%.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantages: Less competition, so easier to attract/retain customers to his shop; Clear focus/easier to target customers interested in certain sports, reducing costs of advertising; Builds up specialist skills and knowledge; Can often charge a higher price, helps improve profit margin; Customers are prepared to pay for expertise; Customers tend to be more loyal, so may remain in business for another 5 years. Disadvantages: Lack of economies of scale, leading to higher unit costs, so not able to lower cost of sales of $7000; Risk of over dependence on a single product or market; Likely to attract competition if successful; Vulnerable to market changes. Application words: sole trader, 5 years, clothing and equipment for sports, shop, remained small, wide range of inventory needed, profit margin was 35%, use of figures from Table 3.1. Candidates may gain credit for changes to profit margin only once in either advantage OR disadvantage.

text: Do you think Elton should be pleased with the financial performance of his business? Justify your answer using appropriate ratios.
context: Elton's financial data: 2018 — Revenue $24,000, Cost of sales $7,200, Gross profit $16,800, Expenses $8,400, Profit $8,400 (calculated). 2019 — Revenue $25,000, Cost of sales $7,000 (calculated), Gross profit $18,000, Expenses $10,000, Profit $8,000.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision using ratio analysis. Relevant calculations: Profit margin 2018 = 35%, 2019 = 32% (fallen by 3%). Gross profit margin 2018 = 70%, 2019 = 72% (risen by 2%). Points: Gross profit margin has improved from 70% to 72%, showing better control of variable costs; Profit margin has decreased, showing less control of expenses; Revenue improved by $1000; Gross profit increased by $1200; Profit decreased by $400. Justification: he should be pleased as sales and gross profit are rising, but he must be concerned about expenses. OFR applies if candidates incorrectly calculated profit in question 3(b). For evaluation, justification must follow from relevant analysis and must include ratio analysis.

text: Define 'business cycle'.
context: KTF makes building materials including cement and bricks, sales of $25bn last year, started 60 years ago, wants to know how the business cycle might affect activity.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Fluctuations in economic activity that an economy experiences over time. OR Changes in level of economic growth/GDP/economic activity over time. OR A period during which a country or economy goes from growth to recession and back again. Partial (1 mark): Shows changes in GDP, OR fluctuations in economic activity. Do not award alternative names such as trade cycle.

text: Identify two reasons why a business might change its objectives.
context: KTF's objectives have often changed since it was started 60 years ago.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two responses. Reasons: Achieved current objective(s); Changing economic conditions; Changes in legal controls/rules; Changes in the market e.g. competitors join/leave market/changes in demand; New owners; Growth of business; Change in capital available to the business.

text: Outline one advantage and one disadvantage to KTF of taking over the other business.
context: KTF makes building materials (cement, bricks), sales of $25bn last year, going to take over one of its main competitors, combined sales will be $40bn.
ms: 1 mark advantage/disadvantage + 1 mark application (max 2 each = 4 marks). Advantages: Reduces competition/increased market share, as this is one of its main competitors; Possible economies of scale, reducing the unit costs of bricks; Possible cost savings, which could be one of its objectives; Buying an existing brand can be cheaper than internal growth; Access to new skills or expertise. Disadvantages: Clash of culture and leadership styles/objectives for a business started 60 years ago; Possible legal action (as gain too much market power), so could face risk of new legal controls to protect environment; Possible diseconomies of scale or examples e.g. control/communication problems; Over reliant on one market, especially when enter different stages of business cycle; Pressure groups could oppose; Cost of redundancies; Expensive to buy the firm. Application words: building materials/cement and bricks, $25bn, started 60 years ago, main competitors, combined sales of $40bn/raise of $15bn, business cycle, interest rates, legal controls, protecting the environment, stakeholder groups.

text: Explain how two external stakeholder groups might be affected by the takeover.
context: KTF makes building materials, going to take over one of its main competitors, combined sales of $40bn, the Managing Director said many stakeholder groups will be affected.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per stakeholder (max 6 marks). Stakeholders: Banks — may have increased demand for loans to pay for taking over its main competitor; Government — may receive more tax revenue if KTF can increase its $40bn sales; [Local] community — may be concerned about possible job losses; Suppliers — could lead to fewer/increased orders for building materials; Pressure groups; Consumers — as may lead to less choice; Competitors — concerned about possible price drops due to economies of scale gained. Do not award internal stakeholders such as owners (shareholders) or employees. Application words: building materials/cement and bricks, manufacturing, $25bn, started 60 years ago, main competitors, combined sales of $40bn, business cycle, interest rates, legal controls, protecting the environment.

text: Do you think businesses will be more affected by new legal controls to protect the environment than an increase in interest rates? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. There are many external factors that affect business activity including interest rates and legal controls to protect the environment.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. New legal controls to protect environment: May have to buy pollution permits/pay fines, increasing costs which could increase prices; Introduce new techniques/change how they make things, so need to spend more to train employees; Might have to buy new machinery; May be forced to change location; May have to change raw materials. Increase in interest rates: Bank loans more expensive for business/increased cost of borrowing, less likely to invest in capital; Consumers less likely to borrow to buy expensive items, leading to lower sales; Demand for higher wages, as workers might face lower disposable income. Justification: e.g. legal controls will have more effect because a business cannot avoid them, whereas interest rates may have no effect if the business does not have to borrow money. Answers which only discuss one option cannot be awarded both evaluation marks.

text: Define 'induction training'.
context: RGP owns luxury hotels, planning a new hotel with 200 rooms in the city centre, will need 300 employees, everyone gets 6 weeks of induction training.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Introduction given to a new employee explaining the business's activities and processes and allowing them to meet other employees. Partial (1 mark): New employees learn about the business when they start.

text: Identify two ways a business could advertise a new job vacancy.
context: RGP needs to recruit 300 employees for its new luxury hotel from the local community.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 2). Two from: Job Centre; Specialist/trade magazines; Recruitment agency; Jobs website/own website; Word of mouth; Local paper/television/radio; Notice inside/outside the business.

text: Outline two reasons why effective communication between RGP's employees and customers is important.
context: RGP owns luxury hotels, plans a new hotel with 200 rooms and 300 employees, effective communication between employees and customers is important to success.
ms: 1 mark per reason + 1 mark application (max 2 reasons = 4 marks). Reasons: To make sure customer needs are understood by all 300 employees; To make sure employees carry out customer's requests correctly in the hotel; To prevent mistakes or errors which could damage its reputation for luxury; To tell customers about fire practice to keep everybody safe in the 200 rooms.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to RGP of choosing a location in the city centre.
context: RGP plans to open a new hotel with 200 rooms in the city centre, will need 300 employees, luxury hotel brand.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantage: Many people passing/close to customers to the hotel, which could increase possible demand/revenue; Prestige/image, as known for its luxury, this supports its image to attract its target market; Good infrastructure, e.g. water, electricity, internet/transport links, so customers can get there without difficulty. Disadvantage: Cost/availability of suitable land, as need large space for 200 rooms, likely more expensive; Availability of suitable employees, as need to find them from local community, increasing time/cost; Likely to be lots of competition, so might not gain as many customers; Government regulations, could stop opening in some locations.

text: Do you think selecting employees with the right personality is more important than their experience for a tertiary sector business? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. The Human Resources Director thinks selecting new employees with the right personality is more important than their experience.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Personality: More likely to make mistakes, which could damage reputation; Higher cost of training, increasing expenses; May be more willing to learn, quickly adapt to business requirements; Skills can be taught but not easy to change someone's personality. Experience: May expect higher wages, increasing labour costs; Likely to make fewer mistakes or provide better service, reducing waste; Reduces possible number of candidates, could take more time to recruit; Know they have ability/skills to do the job. Justification: e.g. personality is more important because you need people who are willing to learn/able to interact naturally with customers especially in a tertiary sector business where good customer service is important, and skills can be taught more easily than personality can be changed.

text: Define 'margin of safety'.
context: RVC uses batch production to manufacture a large range of products including soap and shampoo. Last year sales were 80,000 units a week for one brand of soap.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Difference between current level of output and break-even output. Partial (1 mark): Extras made over what you need to cover costs.

text: Identify two stages of the product life cycle.
context: Many of RVC's products are at different stages of the product life cycle.
ms: 1 mark per stage (max 2). Two from: Development; Introduction; Growth; Maturity; Decline.

text: Using Table 2.1, calculate the weekly profit. Show your working.
context: RVC soap data: Selling price $2.50, Fixed costs per week $20,000, Average variable costs $0.90, Number of sales per week 40,000.
ms: Award 4 marks for correct calculation: $44,000. Method e.g. Revenue: 40,000 × $2.50 = $100,000 (1); Total cost = Variable cost (40,000 × 0.9 = $36,000) (1) + $20,000 = $56,000 (1); Revenue − Total cost = $44,000. If correct answer given with no working shown, award 4 marks. OFR can apply.

text: Explain one benefit and one limitation to RVC of using batch production.
context: RVC uses batch production to manufacture soap and shampoo, sales of 40,000 units per week, considering new packaging or targeting new markets as extension strategy.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per benefit AND limitation (max 6 marks). Benefit: Flexible, easier to change between different soaps, better meet customer demands; Some economies of scale, as make 80,000 units each week, help reduce average costs; Less impact if machinery breaks down, so some output made; Spread risk as can make more than one type of product; Variety of products, could lead to more sales; Some variety in work can motivate workers, leading to less absenteeism. Limitation: Time lost switching/resetting machines between batches, could lead to lost output; Added cost of moving or storing semi-finished goods; Inventory may be sitting around between stages, increasing costs, so may not have sufficient money to introduce its extension strategy; One fault could affect entire batch, increasing waste.

text: Do you think targeting new markets is a better extension strategy than new packaging for a manufacturing business? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. The Marketing Director has to decide on a suitable extension strategy between new packaging or targeting new markets.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Target new markets: Widen customer base, can lead to additional revenue; Cost of market research/promotion will add to expenses; Different tastes; Lack of distribution network; Existing competition in other markets. New packaging: No guarantee packaging will appeal to customers, so sales revenue may continue to fall; Extra time and cost of development; Can help create new interest. Justification: e.g. targeting new markets may be better as the business would not risk losing existing customers by changing the packaging, which could result in less revenue to pay for the cost of any extension strategy introduced.

text: Define 'opportunity cost'.
context: PCS is a multinational company in the private sector, makes 500 brands of soft drinks sold in plastic bottles, plans to start recycling. The Operations Manager said everything has an opportunity cost.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): The benefit that could have been gained from an alternative use of the same resource. OR Next best alternative forgone/given up (by choosing another item). Partial (1 mark): What you give up when you decide to do something else.

text: State two features of a private sector business.
context: PCS is a multinational company in the private sector.
ms: 1 mark per feature (max 2). Features: Not government owned/owned by individuals; Profit motive; Finance arranged by owners.

text: Identify four aims of promotion.
context: PCS has a large marketing budget for promotion.
ms: 1 mark per aim (max 4). Aims: Increase sales/persuade/attract customers; Increase market share/compete with competitors' products; Inform/raise awareness/introduce new products; Create brand image/improve image; Ensure customer loyalty.

text: Explain two advantages to PCS of being a multinational company.
context: PCS is a multinational company, makes 500 brands of soft drinks sold in plastic bottles, many countries introduced legal controls to reduce litter, plans to start recycling plastic bottles.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 advantages = 6 marks). Advantages: Access to new markets/increase sales, as people might want their 500 brands, increasing revenue; Spread risk when selling soft drinks, so fall in demand in one market balanced by rising sales elsewhere; Better access to raw materials such as plastic for bottles, so able to maintain output; Benefit from economies of scale e.g. purchasing, financial, lowering average costs; Reduce transport costs/help distribution (as produce goods nearer market); Avoid barriers to trade; Reduce tax liability/take advantage of favourable laws.

text: Do you think all manufacturing businesses should use recycled materials? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. PCS plans to start recycling plastic bottles as many countries have introduced legal controls to reduce litter.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: Recycling can reduce amount of pollution, so reduces costs of waste; Uses energy and resources to recycle, increasing business costs; Can improve business reputation, but recycled materials can be expensive; Can depend on what they are making; Can help improve brand image, which can make them more competitive. Justification: e.g. no, because it can depend on what they are making — for some manufacturing businesses there may not be appropriate recycled materials available/suitable to use, so this is not an option.

text: Define 'Return on Capital Employed'.
context: LXA is a private limited company in country Z making children's clothing, financial data shows ROCE decreased from 8% to 6%.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Amount of profit made for each dollar invested. OR (Capital) Profit/capital employed × 100. Partial (1 mark): Profit from capital invested.

text: Define 'working capital'.
context: LXA's financial data shows working capital decreased from $200,000 to $180,000.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): How much liquid assets a business has to pay its day to day costs. OR Current assets − current liabilities. Partial (1 mark): Money for everyday expenses/funds used to buy inventory.

text: Outline two possible problems for LXA if the business grows.
context: LXA is a private limited company making children's clothing, sells in competitive markets in several countries, directors considering different ways to grow, wants to start producing adult clothing.
ms: 1 mark per problem + 1 mark application (max 2 problems = 4 marks). Problems: Poor communication, as already operates in several countries; Lack of finance, especially as considering selling clothing for adults; Slower decision making in this private limited company; Larger business more difficult to control; Lower levels of employee motivation as workers remote from managers.

text: Explain one way each of the following stakeholder groups might use LXA's financial information: Suppliers AND Shareholders.
context: LXA's financial data: Working capital $180,000 (2019) vs $200,000 (2018), Acid test ratio 0.5 vs 0.7, ROCE 6% vs 8%, Gross profit margin 20% vs 25%. The Finance Director has prepared this information before meeting with stakeholders.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per stakeholder (max 6 marks). Suppliers: Liquidity position, to know whether the business is likely to be able to repay them for clothing; Assess risk of default, as acid test ratio fallen to 0.5, shows fewer liquid assets; See level of debts. Shareholder: Help make decisions on keeping, buying or selling shares, as may not be happy ROCE reduced by 2%; Check performance e.g. profit, as operate in competitive markets, if business is successful it may increase value of shares; Assess (possible) level of dividend, to know whether will receive a return on their investment.

text: Do you think a business should use the same marketing mix to sell its products to different age groups? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. The Marketing Director wants LXA to start producing clothing for adults.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: Same marketing mix is cheaper, reducing marketing costs, helps keep prices low; Depending on your customers you may want to advertise in different locations using different media, to attract different target audiences. Justification: e.g. no, because it is unlikely that the price, promotion, place and product will be exactly the same, so they would have to change something otherwise they would risk losing/missing out on sales, which is the whole point of targeting different market segments.

text: Define 'specialisation'.
context: DWT makes solar panels in country Y, a low-cost country experiencing rapid economic growth, uses specialisation, 120 employees, imports some raw materials, Government plans 50% import tariffs.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Way in which work is divided so each worker concentrates on a specific task so becomes expert at it. OR When people and businesses concentrate on what they are best at. Partial (1 mark): Workers do only one job.

text: Identify two reasons why a government might introduce import controls.
context: The Government of country Y plans to introduce import tariffs of 50%.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two responses. Reasons: Protect jobs from cheap labour in other countries; To improve trade deficit; Protect newly started/infant industries; To earn more revenue from tariffs; Protect local businesses from low priced competition; Protect important national or strategic industries.

text: Outline two ways DWT could try to ensure quality production.
context: DWT makes solar panels using specialisation, all 120 employees know ensuring quality production is important.
ms: 1 mark per way + 1 mark application (max 2 ways = 4 marks). Ways: Quality control, check products before they are exported; Quality assurance when making solar panels; Training/recruit skilled employees to make full use of specialisation; Use better quality materials, could afford as it's a low-cost country; Use new technology/CAM/CAD.

text: Explain one objective of each of the following stakeholder groups of DWT: Customers AND Pressure groups.
context: DWT makes solar panels in country Y, experiencing rapid economic growth, Managing Director said this decision (import tariffs) will affect all stakeholders.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per stakeholder (max 6 marks). Customers: Would want high quality products to achieve value for money, which is why quality production is important; May want affordable prices. Pressure groups: Encourage the use of sustainable methods such as solar panels to protect the environment; Reduce/limit amount of pollution/environmental damage.

text: Do you think that all businesses will benefit from operating in a country which is experiencing rapid economic growth? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. DWT operates in country Y, a low-cost country experiencing rapid economic growth.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: Economic growth increases consumer incomes, which increases demand for most goods; Rapid economic growth can lead to higher rate of inflation, which raises firms' costs/reduces profit margin; Patterns of consumer demand might change, reducing revenue for some businesses; Could lead to shortage of skilled workers, so have to offer higher pay to attract/retain employees, increasing costs. Justification: e.g. unlikely all businesses will benefit as it depends what they sell — if selling basic goods, customers may switch to more expensive items as incomes increase, leading to fewer sales for some and higher sales for others.

text: Define 'trade union'.
context: MLC makes motorcycles, 200 employees, plans to close its factory and relocate production to another country, only 50 existing employees will be offered jobs, the trade union has been informed.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Group of workers who join together to ensure their interests/rights are protected. OR Organisation which represents the workers and fights for improvements to pay and conditions. Partial (1 mark): A group who fight for workers' rights.

text: Calculate the average cost of one motorcycle. Show your working.
context: MLC's cost and output data for current factory (2019): Total output 3,000 units, Total cost $1,200,000, Number of employees 200.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): 400. Method: Total cost ÷ Total output = 1,200,000/3,000 (1 mark).

text: State four features of an income statement.
context: This planned relocation will have an impact on MLC's income statement.
ms: 1 mark per feature (max 4). Features: Revenue; Cost of sales; Gross Profit; Profit (for the year); Retained Profit; Expenses.

text: Explain two possible problems for MLC of relocating its operations to another country.
context: MLC makes motorcycles, plans to close its factory and relocate production to another country, only 50 of 200 existing employees will be offered jobs at the new location.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 problems = 6 marks). Problems: Access to suitable employees/not easy to find employees, as at new site will need 150 new employees, increasing recruitment/training costs; Access to/cost of suitable land, as will need a big space to make motorcycles; Different legal controls/standards in the new factory, which may mean have to change how/where operate; Could be further away from market/suppliers/need to find new suppliers, which increases transport costs; Communication problems, as may need to learn a new language, so takes longer to complete on-the-job training.

text: Do you think on-the-job training is a better method of training for a manufacturing business to use than off-the-job training? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. All new employees at MLC will be given either on-the-job or off-the-job training after relocation.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Off-the-job training: Not necessarily tailored to individual business; Have to pay more/high cost for specialists, increasing costs; Skills might not be available in the business, so benefit from new techniques/ideas; Allows for mistakes to be made when learning, so less likely to waste resources/lower risk of damaging reputation. On-the-job training: Can reinforce errors/bad habits of trainer, reducing sales/damaging reputation; Fewer new ideas/skills will be taught; Control what is taught/employees learn exact way business wants things done; Employees can carry on working, some output still produced; Cheaper (than off-the-job). Justification: e.g. no, as it depends what the training is for — if using new techniques/machines, the business may not have a suitable person to train others, so on-the-job is not an option, meaning it would have no choice but to use off-the-job training.

text: Define 'business plan'.
context: Kala always wanted to be an entrepreneur, used to work for a business which downsized its workforce 5 years ago, started up CHL, produced a business plan which helped her obtain finance.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): A document containing the business aims/objectives and important details about the operations, finance and owners of a business. OR States aim and/or objectives and shows how business aims to achieve them. Partial (1 mark): A document showing what the business intends to do.

text: Identify two reasons why a business might downsize its workforce.
context: Kala used to work for a business which downsized its workforce 5 years ago.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Reasons: Economic crisis; Factory/shop/office closure; Merger or takeover; Need to reduce costs; Changes in management/strategy; Automation or replaced by machinery; Excess workforce; Relocation.

text: Outline two reasons why Kala's business might need finance.
context: Kala designs customised sports clothes for women, sells directly to customers using e-commerce, has a loyal customer base of 25-40 year olds, worried about increased competition in this niche market.
ms: 1 mark per reason + 1 mark application (max 2 reasons = 4 marks). Reasons: Increase working capital/examples such as buy inventory or materials/pay day to day costs, so prevent cash flow problems; To expand/buy more non-current assets, so she can enter different market segments; To pay for market research and advertising of her sportswear.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to Kala of using e-commerce to sell her products.
context: Kala designs customised sports clothes for women, sells directly to customers using e-commerce, loyal customer base of 25-40 year olds, worried about increased competition in this niche market.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantages: Able to target customers who are mainly women, better able to attract attention of people most likely to buy her products; Less rent/fewer employees needed, can help reduce costs for her sportswear; Easy to update, keep customers informed about the ways the products can be customised; Widen market/more potential customers, can increase revenue. Disadvantages: Difficult to stand out from competition at a time when she is worried about increased competition, leading to lower sales; Not everyone has access to internet; No passing trade, so could mean fewer sales; Increased costs of postage/distribution, as need to arrange for delivery/vans; Need to pay for pop-ups to advertise on popular sites; Lack of personal service; Customers may want to try before buy.

text: Do you think selling to different market segments is the best way for a small business to respond to increased competition? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Kala is worried about increased competition in this niche market. One idea is to target different market segments.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Targeting a new segment: Wider market base, could increase sales revenue; Spreads risk, as not reliant on one market for sales; Need to know reaction/current level of competition, as customers may be loyal to other businesses; High cost and time involved developing new products; Cost of promotion, as need to attract customer's attention. Other issues: Could change prices e.g. lower prices could lead to lower profit margin/seen as lower quality; Size of market could be a factor as if niche market, this will limit number of possible sales. Justification: e.g. selling to other segments means spreading risk as not reliant on one market for sales — much better than charging lower prices which could reduce revenue if they cannot generate enough extra sales to cover the price reduction, especially for a small business without sufficient funds to keep lower prices.

text: Define 'profit'.
context: ALB is a large bank, 300 branches, 5000 employees, provides financial services to business customers, operates in competitive market, last year profit decreased to $3,000m.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): The amount of money that a business makes once costs have been subtracted from the revenue. OR Total revenue minus total costs. Partial (1 mark): Money left after costs paid. For both marks must have idea there is both a sales and cost element to profit.

text: State two problems of using the number of employees to measure the size of a business.
context: ALB has 5,000 employees.
ms: 1 mark per problem (max 2). Problems: Might use a lot of machines; Difficult to count part-time employees.

text: Outline two possible ways ALB can try to reduce its costs.
context: ALB is a large bank, 300 branches, 5,000 employees, profit decreased to $3,000m last year, the Managing Director is analysing ways to reduce costs.
ms: 1 mark per way + 1 mark application (max 2 ways = 4 marks). Ways: Reduce number of employees by making some of the 5,000 employees redundant; Close number of branches from 300; Reduce amount of wastage by using less paper when dealing with business customers.

text: Explain two ways ALB could improve customer loyalty.
context: ALB operates in a competitive market, aims to maintain customer loyalty, 300 branches, 5,000 employees.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 ways = 6 marks). Ways: Communicate with customers e.g. newsletters, social media, so they remember your business when they next need financial services/help from bank; Offer good quality service, so customers want to return to the 300 branches; Train staff, so all 5,000 employees are able to offer a good quality service; Ask for feedback e.g. surveys, to find out how/what they need to do to improve; Resolve complaints quickly, so customers don't change to another bank, as it is a competitive market; Offer rewards/loyalty programs such as discounts for business customers who also use them for personal banking; Offer extra services such as online/mobile phone app.

text: Do you think changes in legal controls over employment issues will always reduce business profits? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. The Government plans to improve protection of employees by changing laws on the minimum wage and health and safety.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: Health and safety changes could mean needing to provide more training, increasing costs, but leading to more motivated/more efficient employees; Can depend on how much the minimum wage increases, as may already pay above the new rate so may not affect them; Can depend on the type of business, as health and safety may be more of an issue for a manufacturing business. Justification: e.g. yes, because any changes in legal control are likely to result in the business at least having to do something even if it is only to check they are compliant, which will cost time and money.

text: Define 'crowd-funding'.
context: Kara's business makes wax candles, sells to retailers at low prices, gives retailers 60 days to pay, has to pay suppliers when raw materials delivered, used crowd-funding to set up her business.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Asking a large number of people each for a small amount of money to raise finance for a project. Partial (1 mark): Asking general public/people to give money.

text: State two economies of scale.
context: Demand is increasing but Kara is not yet able to benefit from economies of scale.
ms: 1 mark per economy of scale (max 2). Two from: Purchasing/bulk buying; Marketing; Technical; Financial; Risk bearing; Managerial.

text: Outline two reasons why a bank might want Kara to produce a business plan before agreeing to give a loan.
context: The bank would not give Kara a loan as she did not have a business plan for her candle business. Last year revenue was $50,000.
ms: 1 mark per reason + 1 mark application (max 2 reasons = 4 marks). Reasons: Supports request for finance/shows ability to repay, increasing chance of getting finance for her candle business; Shows planning/thought seriously about issues such as recognising that cash-flow is a problem; Provide (important) information about business such as demand is increasing; Shows what security/assets the business has which can be used to support any loan. Note: focus is from viewpoint of the bank, not the business.

text: Explain two factors Kara should consider when deciding whether to increase prices.
context: Kara's wax candle business sells to retailers at low prices, revenue last year was $50,000, not yet benefiting from economies of scale, all cash inflows used to buy inventory.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 factors = 6 marks). Factors: Level of competition/selling price of competitors for candles, as a higher price could mean fewer customers; Cost of production, as higher price should improve her profit margin especially as she does not benefit from economies of scale; Price elasticity of demand, as if price elastic a higher price will result in a greater fall in demand, so revenue this year may not be $50,000; Brand image/reputation, as higher price might suggest better quality.

text: Do you think delaying payments to suppliers is the best way for a small business to improve its cash-flow? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Kara said cash-flow is a problem — all cash inflows are used to buy inventory.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: Delaying payment will allow them to delay cash outflow; Suppliers may be unwilling to supply materials, and without the necessary materials would not be able to generate any cash inflows. Other options: Ask customers to pay more quickly, but could result in fewer customers leading to lower cash inflows; Arrange an overdraft/short-term loan, but could be charged interest increasing cash outflows; Sell unwanted non-current assets, freeing up cash tied up in the business; Buy cheaper materials, reducing cash outflows. Justification: e.g. as the business is small, suppliers may not be willing to offer credit as they are seen as too high a risk, so this may not be an option for a small business.

text: Define 'multinational company'.
context: BCK is a multinational company operating many gold mines, one objective is to contribute to sustainable development, 10,000 employees.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): A business with factories, production or service operations in more than one country. OR A business with production or service operation in another country outside its normal area of operation. Partial (1 mark): Works/operates in more than one country.

text: State two ways of motivating employees.
context: BCK needs well-motivated employees among its 10,000 workforce.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 2). Ways: Financial bonuses; Performance related pay; Fringe benefits (or examples but allow only once); Profit share; Provide opportunities for promotion; Job rotation; Job enrichment; Job enlargement; Training opportunities; Increase rate of pay; Employee of the month/award schemes; Praise.

text: State four factors that might affect the leadership style used by a manager.
context: With 10,000 employees it is important for BCK to have the right leadership style.
