ms: 1 mark per factor (max 4). Factors: Personality of leader/manager; Skills of leader; Skills of employees; Work to be done; Size of business; Organisational structure.

text: Explain two ways BCK could contribute to sustainable development.
context: BCK is a multinational company operating many gold mines, one of BCK's objectives is to contribute to sustainable development, 10,000 employees.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 ways = 6 marks). Ways: Reduce output of gold, so only extract amount required (to meet demand); Use renewable energy, so need to use fewer natural resources when operating its mines; Restore land to nature when finished, so land can be reused for other purposes; Increase efficiency of its 10,000 employees, so waste fewer resources; Change methods of working.

text: Do you think using communication methods based on information technology (IT) is the best way for a large business to communicate with its suppliers? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. The Managing Director thinks effective communication with suppliers is very important.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: Phone call — can obtain immediate feedback but may not be able to contact the person when needed; Emails — allow receiver to read message when convenient, but may not read it/see as junk mail, could contain lots of detailed information; Choice could depend on location of supplier e.g. local or in another country/how much information needs including. Other methods: Meetings — allow feedback, but difficult to arrange a suitable time; Letter — have a copy to refer back to, but language may not be clear if technical. Justification: e.g. yes, especially if urgent, as electronic methods are usually quicker so action/changes can be made sooner so that operations are not delayed, which could be very costly especially for a large business.

text: Define 'brand image'.
context: NWA is a large and profitable airline business, grown quickly over 10 years, new aeroplanes have helped improve its brand image, low priced flights to 50 countries.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Unique name of a product that distinguishes it from other products or brands. Partial (1 mark): Something that makes the product easy to recognise.

text: Calculate the break-even number of customers for a typical NWA flight. Show your working.
context: NWA cost and price data for a typical flight (2019): Price per customer $40, Fixed costs $2,000, Variable cost per customer $24, Maximum number of customers 200.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): 125. Method: Fixed cost ÷ (selling price − variable cost per unit) = 2000/(40-24) (1 mark).

text: Outline two possible problems for NWA of having a high level of debt.
context: NWA's Finance Director is worried that NWA has a high level of debt as its main source of finance is bank loans.
ms: 1 mark per problem + 1 mark application (max 2 problems = 4 marks). Problems: Difficult to arrange additional finance, especially as its main source of finance are bank loans; High cost of repayment/high expenses, making it difficult to keep prices at $40; Increase financial risk when buying planes; Cash flow/liquidity problems, despite business being profitable.

text: Explain how two methods of sales promotion could increase sales for NWA.
context: NWA offers low priced flights for tourists to 50 countries, sales promotion is an important part of NWA's marketing mix.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per method (max 6 marks). Methods: Sponsorship (of events or clubs), can help boost its reputation, thereby helping further improve brand image; Short-term price discounts/special offers aimed at tourists, as more people are able to afford/willing to buy as cheaper; Loyalty schemes such as frequent flying programme, to encourage customers to return many times; Competitions, as people may buy more to increase chances of winning; Gifts; After sales service.

text: Do you think that having many levels of hierarchy is the best type of organisational structure for a large business? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. NWA's organisational chart has many levels of hierarchy with narrow spans of control.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: Having levels of hierarchy (tall hierarchy) means a long chain of command, which can slow down communication as messages have to pass through many levels, could slow down decision making; Senior managers are more remote from employees, which can demotivate employees and lower efficiency/output; Managers have fewer employees to supervise, could result in fewer opportunities for delegation; Can provide more opportunities for promotion; Having a wider structure would lead to a short chain of command/each manager having to be responsible for more people, which could mean managers lose control. Justification: e.g. no as it could depend on the leadership style of the manager — if autocratic, a tall structure may be better as this allows greater control over what all employees in a large organisation do.

text: Identify two reasons why a government might support business start-ups.
context: BMT is a business partnership owned by 2 brothers, received government support when they started BMT 6 years ago, now has 30 employees.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Reasons: Reduce unemployment; Increase competition; Increase output; Benefit society; Small businesses can grow.

text: State two types of business organisation (other than partnership).
context: BMT is a business partnership owned by 2 brothers.
ms: 1 mark per type (max 2). Types: Sole trader; Private limited company; Public limited company; Franchise; Social enterprise; Charity; Public corporation.

text: Outline two disadvantages of BMT being a business partnership.
context: BMT is a business partnership owned by 2 brothers, started 6 years ago, 30 employees, makes high quality watches, tries to achieve lean production, sold 8,000 watches in 2019.
ms: 1 mark per disadvantage + 1 mark application (max 2 disadvantages = 4 marks). Disadvantages: Unlimited liability/each responsible for debts of other, so if business cannot pay its debts there is risk to the personal assets of each brother; Fewer sources of finance (than limited company), restricting plans to expand the watch business; Possible disagreements/slower decision making, such as whether to import parts; Have to share profits.

text: Explain two ways BMT could achieve lean production.
context: BMT makes high quality watches, 30 employees, tries to achieve lean production, sold 8,000 watches in 2019, makes some parts and imports the rest.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 ways = 6 marks). Ways: Just in Time, ordering parts as and when needed for the watches, reduces storage costs; Kaizen, helps eliminate mistakes and errors when making these high-quality products; Cell production/team working of its 30 employees; Kanban.

text: Do you think the exchange rate is the most important factor for a business to consider when deciding whether to import parts for a high quality product? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. BMT had to consider a number of factors, including exchange rates, when deciding whether to import parts for watches.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Exchange rates: Appreciation in own exchange rates would mean have to pay less to import materials, lowering costs, may lower prices or improve profit margin; Changing rates are difficult to plan for, may result in much higher costs than budgeted; Exchange rate depreciate, leads to higher cost of imported materials, could mean have to increase prices which could lower sales. Other factors: The quality of parts/materials, as may not be possible to obtain resources locally; Import tariffs, would increase the price; Import quotas, could limit the amount of parts that can be brought into the country. Justification: e.g. as it is for a high-quality product, exchange rate is not as important as the materials because customers may be willing to pay the higher price to get the right quality, which could cover the financial impact of any changes in the exchange rate.

text: Define 'dismissal'.
context: HSN uses batch production to make breakfast cereals, several distribution channels, 600 production workers, problems with many employees leaving. Following dismissal of the Operations Manager, needs to recruit a new manager.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Termination by the employer because the employee has broken company rules or is not performing work to the required standard. OR When the employment is ended against the will of the employee, usually for not working in accordance with the employment contract. Partial (1 mark): When employee told/made to leave their job, OR termination of employment against the wishes of the employee. For both marks, candidates must show it is the business that ends the employment and indicate why the employee has been asked to leave.

text: State two distribution channels a business might use.
context: HSN's products are sold using several distribution channels.
ms: 1 mark per channel (max 2). Two from: Wholesalers; Retailers; Direct to customers/Online/Internet/website; Use of agents.

text: Outline two possible problems to HSN of many employees leaving.
context: HSN uses batch production to make breakfast cereals, employs 600 production workers, has problems with many employees leaving.
ms: 1 mark per problem + 1 mark application (max 2 problems = 4 marks). Problems: Cost of recruiting new/replacing workers, as employ 600 employees; Cost of training new employees to use batch production; Disruption to production/lower productivity/lower output of breakfast cereals; Can damage business reputation, so difficult to recruit new manager/harder to use external recruitment; Takes managers time away from other aspects of the business such as reducing communication barriers; Time taken to recruit new/replace workers; Time taken to train new employees. Answers must focus on problems for the business, not impact on employees.

text: Explain how each of the following could cause communication barriers within HSN: Language AND Medium of communication.
context: The Human Resources Director has to recruit a new manager who must have good communication skills to help solve communication barriers HSN has with employees.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per barrier (max 6 marks). Language: Use of new/different jargon/technical terms/difficult words/vocabulary when using batch production, so employees may not understand the message; Use foreign/different language when making cereals. Medium of communication: The wrong channel may be used/workers may not be able to use the method selected, so messages may not be seen by all 600 employees; Physical breakdown of medium, so the message is never received, important as use several distribution channels; Message may be lost/distorted (if have a long chain of command), so may be misinterpreted; No feedback is received. Answers must focus on how the communication barrier is created/arises, not the impact — do not award solutions.

text: Do you think external recruitment is better than internal recruitment when recruiting a new manager for a large business? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. The Human Resources Director has to decide whether to use internal or external recruitment for the new manager.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision, must clearly relate to a large business. No marks for application. External recruitment: Wider pool/choice of candidates, improving chances of finding the most appropriate person; Bring in new ideas/experience/skills, could help increase efficiency; Avoids risk of upsetting other employees when someone internal is promoted. Internal recruitment: Quicker/cheaper than external recruitment, reducing expenses; Acts as an incentive/motivation for employees, reducing labour turnover; People know the business, can start work more quickly; Company knows the people/employee; Suitable candidates may not be available; Would create another vacancy for the business to fill. Justification: e.g. external recruitment would be better as it may result in the appointment of a manager whose cost savings will soon outweigh the cost of external recruitment, especially in a large business.

text: Define 'economies of scale'.
context: Gomez is a sole trader, provides painting and decorating services to business customers, does not benefit from any economies of scale because small.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Factors that lead to lower average costs as a business increases in size. OR Reduction in average costs as a result of increasing the scale of operations. Partial (1 mark): Benefit of increasing in size/growth/expansion. Do not award examples or answers referring to price.

text: Calculate X and Y.
context: Gomez's cash-flow forecast ($): April: Cash in 3000, Cash out 2600, Net cash flow X, Opening 200, Closing 600. May: Cash in 2800, Cash out 3000, Net cash flow (200), Opening 600, Closing 400. June: Cash in 2600, Cash out Y, Net cash flow 200, Opening 400, Closing 600.
ms: 1 mark per correct calculation. X: 400. Y: 2400. $ sign is not required.

text: Outline two factors Gomez should consider when choosing a source of finance for the new van.
context: Gomez uses an old van borrowed from his father, thinking of buying a new van, has to pay suppliers within 1 month but gives customers 3 months to pay.
ms: 1 mark per factor + 1 mark application (max 2 factors = 4 marks). Factors: Amount needed/how much it will cost, as cash available is only $600; Cost of finance/interest rate for this painting business; Amount of security/whether he has any security to offer, as has borrowed old van; Size/type of business, may be viewed as higher risk as sole trader; Time needed to repay/time to obtain finance; Current level of debt/loans/gearing; Whether to buy or lease; Amount of finance/money available in business/liquidity.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to Gomez of being a sole trader.
context: Gomez is a sole trader providing painting and decorating services, uses an old van borrowed from his father, gives customers 3 months to pay, pays suppliers within 1 month.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantage: Keeps all the profit, so if successful will make more money/will encourage him to do better from painting business; Own boss/complete control, can make decisions more quickly; Does not have to give information about his business to anyone else/secrecy in business matters; Has freedom to choose own holidays/hours of work/prices to charge such as whether to offer customers 3 months credit; Has close contact with customers, able to respond quickly to changes in demand. Disadvantage: Unlimited liability, so if business is not able to pay the suppliers within 1 month could lose his personal possessions; Limited sources of finance/difficult to raise funds to buy new assets such as the van; May have limited range of skills, as only a small business; No continuity/if ill who will take control; Has to work long hours/difficult to take holidays otherwise may lose out on potential sales/revenue; No one to share risks/losses with; Not able to benefit from economies of scale.

text: Do you think asking customers to pay more quickly is the best way for a small business to improve its cash flow? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application, must clearly relate to a small business. Gomez gives customers 3 months to pay but pays suppliers within 1 month.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: Less/no need to borrow, so no interest paid, does not increase cash outflows; Customers may be unable or unwilling to pay more quickly, so may look for alternative suppliers reducing cash inflows. Other ways: Delay payment to suppliers/change terms; Selling (unwanted) assets; Reduce amount of inventory ordered/held; Debt factoring; Overdraft/short term loan. Justification: e.g. as the business is small, it may be better to ask suppliers for more time to pay, as the business may not have many customers so does not want to risk losing them by asking them to pay more quickly.

text: Define 'globalisation'.
context: Globalisation has changed the way many businesses operate. VKW makes cell (mobile) phones, uses just-in-time inventory control, exports 40% of its products, imports most raw materials.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): The process by which countries are connected with each other because of the trade of goods and services. OR The process of countries becoming more interconnected. OR Increase in worldwide trade and movement of people between countries. Partial (1 mark): Increase in trade around the world, OR increased movement of capital around the world.

text: State two advantages to a business of using quality assurance.
context: All 800 of VKW's employees understand the importance of quality assurance.
ms: 1 mark per advantage (max 2). Advantages: Lower cost/reduce cost of wastage/fewer mistakes/less rework (of faulty products); Encourages teamwork; Fewer customer complaints/improve/maintain reputation; Better brand image/fewer customer returns; Reduce inspection costs; Allows business to know at what stage mistakes happen.

text: Outline two ways VKW might be affected by increased import controls.
context: VKW makes cell phones, exports 40% of its products, imports most of its raw materials to help reduce total costs, many governments planning to increase import controls such as quotas.
ms: 1 mark per way + 1 mark application (max 2 ways = 4 marks). Ways: Increased import costs/more expensive to import, at a time when trying to reduce total costs; Can export less products/fewer sales in other countries, as export 40% of its phones; May not be able to obtain sufficient number/range of parts so delay/halt production, difficult to use just-in-time; May have to spend time finding local suppliers, as currently most raw materials are imported; Might have to charge higher prices; Domestic sales might rise.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to VKW of using just-in-time inventory control.
context: VKW makes cell phones, uses just-in-time inventory control, exports 40% of products, 800 employees, imports most raw materials to reduce total costs, quality assurance is important.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation per advantage AND disadvantage (max 6 marks). Advantage: Less inventory held to make phones, so less chance of wastage; Lower storage costs because there is less space/smaller warehouse needed, which also helps reduce total costs; Improve working capital/cash-flow, as less money tied up as stock; Less risk of inventory becoming obsolete/damaged, which helps quality assurance. Disadvantage: Parts might not arrive in time/limited inventory held, especially as many are imported, causing production delays; No extra stock/materials available to meet unexpected orders, could lead to lower revenue/sales; Little room for mistakes in production as little/no inventory kept for rework; May not have good relationship/communication with suppliers/requires a lot of planning to make sure goods delivered on time; No economies of scale possible, leading to higher average costs.

text: Do you think that businesses should be concerned about ethical issues such as child labour? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. The Operations Director asked all suppliers to ensure they do not use child labour.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Points: Being ethical may enhance image/reputation, so more customers want to buy its products, may increase revenue; People want to support ethical businesses/help attract customers; Can help attract investors, leading to access to more finance; Help attract/retain employees, leading to higher productivity; Can charge/may have to set higher prices, so customers may switch to cheaper competitors; Being ethical can conflict with profit objective/short term profits may fall; Being ethical may mean paying higher wages which can increase costs; Pressure groups might organise a boycott. Justification: e.g. being ethical may increase costs, so the business would have no option, even though profits may fall in the short-term this could be outweighed by additional revenue in the long term.

text: Define 'market research'.
context: WFG is a private limited company in country X, owns 120 supermarkets (20 franchises), objective to expand by opening 30 more shops in 18 months, market research shows fewer people going to local markets.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Process of gathering, analysing and interpreting information about the market. OR Process of collecting, recording and analysing data about customers, competitors and market for a product. Partial (1 mark): Find out what customers want, OR find out about competition. To award both marks, response must refer to at least two stages of the research process.

text: State two objectives (other than expansion) a business might have.
context: One of WFG's objectives is to expand by opening 30 more shops in the next 18 months.
ms: 1 mark per objective (max 2). Objectives: Survival/stay in business beyond first two years/break-even/improve cash flow; Make a profit; Increase market share/increase sales/increase revenue/enter new markets/become market leader; Return to shareholders/increase return on capital employed; Be socially/ethically/environmentally responsible; Provide a service to the community; Cuts costs/improve profit margin/add value. Do not award growth as this is the same as expansion.

text: State four factors a business should consider when deciding the price of a product.
context: The Managing Director said it is important to set prices at the right level for WFG's supermarkets.
ms: 1 mark per factor (max 4). Factors: Cost of production/examples such as cost of materials/labour/transport (allow only once)/break-even/profit mark up; Level of demand or factors such as recession/income/what people are willing or able to afford/price elasticity of demand; Actions of competitors/level of competition/price charged by competitor/where or when the product is sold/whether there are any substitutes/whether it is a niche or mass market/size of market; Business objectives/profit margin/add value; Type of product/quality of product/what is being sold/brand image; Availability of economies of scale; Government or legal controls/tax; Stage in product life cycle/new product.

text: Explain two factors WFG should consider when deciding whether to introduce new technology into its business.
context: WFG owns 120 supermarkets (20 franchises), objective to expand by opening 30 more shops in 18 months, Managing Director thinking about whether to introduce new technology.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 factors = 6 marks). Factors: Cost of technology, as has 120 locations which they may not afford; Cost of training/time taken for training, as need to offer training for the 20 franchises, increasing expenses; Potential efficiency gains to lower average cost, so able to lower the prices of its food; How many workers may lose jobs/number of redundancies; Level of demand, as most people buy at local markets, may not be able to justify cost; Opportunity cost; Availability of power/electricity; Sufficient space available, as if not the rent might increase; Customer ability to operate the technology, as if cannot use could result in fewer sales/less revenue.

text: Do you think selling franchises is a better way for a retail business to expand than opening more of its own shops? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application, must clearly relate to a retail business. WFG owns 120 supermarkets, of which 20 are franchises, plans to open 30 more shops.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Selling franchises: Franchisee pays fee to franchisor to use the brand name, so franchisor does not have to raise as much capital; Can expand more quickly (than if franchisor had to finance all new outlets); Franchisees are responsible for day-to-day management, so franchisor has time to focus on more strategic objectives; Franchisee should have local knowledge, could help increase sales/revenue; Franchisor receives a percentage of revenue/profits; Franchisor shares risks with franchisee; Brand/customer awareness increases; All products sold must be obtained from the franchisor; Wrong decision or poor management by one franchisee can damage reputation for whole business; Franchisor may have to provide training and support, increasing costs. More of its own shops: Have total control over the operations; Keep all the profits; Need to raise all the capital. Justification: e.g. it might be better to sell franchises, as it will reduce the costs especially if wanting to open a large number of shops quickly, improving chances of expanding as much as the retail business wants.

text: Identify two reasons why a business might import raw materials.
context: KPX manufactures computers. The business imports 60% of its raw materials. The Operations Director is considering ways to use lean production methods in KPX's factory. The Finance Director is reviewing KPX's financial data. Financial data for 2024 ($million): Revenue $750m, Cost of sales $360m, Gross profit $390m, Profit $90m.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two responses. Accept: Not available/limited supply in own country; Lower cost; Better quality; Wider range of materials. Other appropriate responses credited.

text: Calculate KPX's expenses in 2024. Show your working.
context: KPX manufactures computers. Financial data for 2024 ($million): Revenue $750m, Cost of sales $360m, Gross profit $390m, Profit $90m.
ms: Award 2 marks for correct answer, 1 mark for correct method but incorrect answer. Correct answer: $300 million. Method: Gross profit minus profit = $390m minus $90m = $300m. For 2 marks answer must be in millions. Dollar sign not required. Max 1 for 300 on own. If correct answer given with no working, award 2 marks.

text: Outline two ways KPX's Finance Director could use the financial data in Table 1.1.
context: KPX manufactures computers. Imports 60% of raw materials. Operations Director considering lean production. Financial data 2024: Revenue $750m, Cost of sales $360m, Gross profit $390m, Profit $90m. Expenses = $300m.
ms: Award 1 mark per way (max 2), 1 mark per application (max 2). Ways: Show whether made a profit [k] which is $90m [app]; Calculate profit margin [k] for the factory [app]; Calculate gross profit margin [k] when importing raw materials [app]; Help make decisions about whether to continue/stop production [k] of computers [app]; Track performance against objectives/time [k]; Compare performance against other businesses [k]; Support a loan application [k]. App words: computers, factory, imports 60% raw materials, lean production, $750m revenue, $360m cost of sales, $390m gross profit, $90m profit, 52% gross profit margin, 12% profit margin, $300m expenses. Can award 'use ratio analysis' where no specific examples given.

text: Explain two methods of lean production KPX could use.
context: KPX manufactures computers. The business imports 60% of its raw materials. The Operations Director is considering ways to use lean production methods in KPX's factory. Financial data 2024: Revenue $750m, Cost of sales $360m, Gross profit $390m, Profit $90m.
ms: Award 1 mark per identification (max 2), 1 mark per application (max 2), 1 mark per analysis (max 2). Methods: Just-in-time (JIT) inventory control [k] when importing raw materials [app] reducing space/inventory held/lower storage costs [an]; Kaizen [k] to help eliminate mistakes/errors [an] when making computers [app]. Analysis can focus on explaining how the method works OR an advantage of using it. App words: computers, factory, imports 60% raw materials, $750m revenue, $360m cost of sales, $390m gross profit, $90m profit, $300m expenses. Some points can be [an] of different methods but only award once e.g. lower cost, fewer mistakes.

text: Explain two reasons why profit is important for a business. Which reason is likely to be the most important? Justify your answer.
context: KPX manufactures computers. The business imports 60% of its raw materials. Financial data 2024: Revenue $750m, Cost of sales $360m, Gross profit $390m, Profit $90m.
ms: General question - no application marks. Award up to 2 marks identification, up to 2 marks analysis, up to 2 marks justified decision. Reasons: Provides a source of funds [k] as no interest to pay [an]; Reward for risk-taking [k] as owners invest money hoping for return/motivate them to continue [an]; Return on shareholder/owner investment [k] otherwise could invest elsewhere [an]; Help attract investors/finance [k] helping business expand [an]; Measure of success [k] as low profit suggests not worth continuing [an]; Need for long-term survival [k]. Must discuss two reasons to access evaluation. Evaluation capped at 4/6 without justified conclusion comparing both reasons.

text: Define 'entrepreneur'.
context: Max is an entrepreneur who wants to start up a business selling books. He has decided to use ecommerce. Max has been told there is government support for start-up businesses. He will use market research to help make business decisions. Max knows it is important for a new business to build customer loyalty.
ms: Award 2 marks for full definition, 1 mark for partial. Full: An individual who takes the financial risk of starting (and managing) a new business; OR a person who takes the risk for a new business venture. Partial: A person who starts/sets up a business. First mark for idea of starting a business. Take a risk is +1 only.

text: Identify two reasons why governments support start-up businesses.
context: Max is an entrepreneur who wants to start up a business selling books. Max has been told there is government support for start-up businesses.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two responses. Accept: Create jobs/reduce unemployment; Increase competition; Increase output/improve GDP; Generate taxation/taxes; Motivate/encourage entrepreneurs; Business can grow into larger businesses in future; Reduce imports/increase exports; Provide wider variety of goods/services. Do NOT award: Examples of government support.

text: Outline two opportunities for Max's business of using ecommerce.
context: Max is an entrepreneur who wants to start up a business selling books. He has decided to use ecommerce. Max has been told there is government support for start-up businesses. He will use market research. Max knows it is important for a new business to build customer loyalty.
ms: Award 1 mark per opportunity (max 2), 1 mark per application (max 2). Opportunities: Lower rent/no shops needed [k] so may not need as much government support [app]; Widen market/more potential customers/orders 24/7 [k] for the books [app]; Website can promote the business [k] helpful for this new business [app]; Easy/quick to update [k] for this entrepreneur [app]; Can provide detailed information [k] alongside market research [app]; Fewer employees needed [k]. App words: entrepreneur, books, new/start-up business, government support, market research, build customer loyalty. Benefits must be to the business not to customers.

text: Explain two ways Max could use market research to help make business decisions.
context: Max is an entrepreneur who wants to start up a business selling books. He has decided to use ecommerce. Max has been told there is government support. He will use market research to help make business decisions. Max knows it is important to build customer loyalty.
ms: Award 1 mark per identification (max 2), 1 mark per application (max 2), 1 mark per analysis (max 2). Ways: Identify consumer needs/target market [k] as it's a new business [app] to ensure sales [an]; Identify competition [k] influencing marketing/pricing [an] for his books [app]; Identify market size/trends/demand [k] to know what products to stock [an] which may help build customer loyalty [app]; How to promote its products [k] to raise awareness [an] as plans to use ecommerce [app]; What/amount of inventory to buy [k] keeping variable costs low [an]; Set prices [k] to ensure business can breakeven/cover costs [an]. App words: entrepreneur, books, new/start-up business, government support, ecommerce, build customer loyalty. Do NOT award: Methods of market research.

text: Explain two ways a business could build customer loyalty. Which is likely to be the best way for a new business to use? Justify your answer.
context: Max is an entrepreneur who wants to start up a business selling books. He has decided to use ecommerce. Max knows it is important for a new business to build customer loyalty.
ms: General question - no application marks. Award up to 2 marks identification, up to 2 marks analysis, up to 2 marks justified decision for a new business. Ways: Offer good customer service/train employees [k] making customers feel valued/builds trust [an]; Loyalty reward scheme/special offers/discounts to regular customers [k] so they have incentive to return [an]; Build customer relationships/communicate e.g. newsletters [k] so customers remember your business [an]; Ask for feedback/carry out market research [k] so items match customer needs [an]; Respond to complaints quickly [k] so customers are less likely to go elsewhere [an]; Offer extra services e.g. after sales service/delivery/credit [k] showing that the business cares [an]. Must discuss two ways to access evaluation. Evaluation capped at 4/6 without justified conclusion.

text: Identify two ways business activity can affect the environment.
context: STB is a public limited company. It uses job production to build houses. In 2024 the business built 13,500 houses. STB has many stakeholder groups including its 5000 employees. The Managing Director knows business activity can affect the environment and there are many reasons why a business should respond to environmental pressures. She also wants to know how economic growth might affect STB.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 2). Only award first two responses. Accept: Pollution (or examples); Use up green space/deforestation/loss of habitat; Deplete natural resources/overmining; Traffic congestion. Other appropriate responses credited.

text: Identify two reasons why a business should respond to environmental pressures.
context: STB is a public limited company. It uses job production to build houses. In 2024 the business built 13,500 houses. STB has many stakeholder groups including its 5000 employees. There are many reasons why a business should respond to environmental pressures.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two responses. Accept: Enhance/protect brand image/reputation; Attract/maintain sales; Reduce risk of customer boycott; Differentiate from competitors; To avoid pressure group action; Help recruit employees; Help retain employees; Help attract investors; Reduce risk of legal action/fines/ensure meets legal standards. Other appropriate responses credited.

text: Outline two ways economic growth might affect STB.
context: STB is a public limited company. It uses job production to build houses. In 2024 the business built 13,500 houses. STB has many stakeholder groups including its 5000 employees. The Managing Director wants to know how economic growth might affect STB.
ms: Award 1 mark per way (max 2), 1 mark per application (max 2). Ways: High demand/sales [k] for houses [app]; More difficult to recruit/find suitable employees [k] for job production [app]; Higher business profits likely [k] for this public limited company [app]; Can increase output [k] above 13,500 houses [app]; Increase in business confidence [k]; STB may consider more investment [k]; Employees may ask for higher wages [k]; Increased rent costs/less choice of location [k]. App words: builds houses/construction industry, 13,500 houses, 5000 employees/builders, public limited company/PLC, job production.

text: Explain two benefits to STB of using job production.
context: STB is a public limited company. It uses job production to build houses. In 2024 the business built 13,500 houses. STB has many stakeholder groups including its 5000 employees.
ms: Award 1 mark per identification (max 2), 1 mark per application (max 2), 1 mark per analysis (max 2). Benefits: Motivate employees [k] helping lower absenteeism/increase retention [an] among its 5000 employees [app]; Could set higher price [k] for each house [app] increasing added value/profit margin [an]; Meet exact customer requirements [k] helping brand loyalty/competitive advantage [an] for this public limited company [app]; Unique/one-off product/USP [k]; High-quality goods/service [k]. App words: public limited company/PLC, builds houses/construction industry, 13,500 houses, 5000 employees/builders, economic growth. Some analysis can be awarded for different benefits but only award once.

text: Do you think employees are the most important stakeholder group for a manufacturing business? Justify your answer.
context: STB is a public limited company. It uses job production to build houses. In 2024 the business built 13,500 houses. STB has many stakeholder groups including its 5000 employees.
ms: General question - no application marks. Candidates can focus solely on employees and still access evaluation. Award up to 2 marks identification, up to 2 marks analysis, up to 2 marks justified decision. Employees: Make/produce the products [k] otherwise nothing to sell/cannot meet demand [an]; Responsible for quality [k] improving/damaging reputation [an]; Without sufficient employees cannot meet demand [k]. Other stakeholders: Shareholders/owners [k] who provide finance/capital [an]; Customers [k] who buy the products [an] generating revenue [an]; Suppliers [k] who provide materials/inventory [an]; Local community [k] who provide workers [an]; Government [k] providing the legal framework [an]; Bank [k] who provide finance/loans [an]. Justification must follow from relevant analysis. Some points can be relevant to more than one stakeholder but only award once. Evaluation capped at 4/6 without justified conclusion.

text: Define 'tertiary sector'.
context: ZPR is a business in the tertiary sector. It has 1 restaurant which has 20 employees. The Human Resources Manager is preparing a job description as ZPR needs 2 new chefs. He said: 'I need to advertise the job vacancies externally. ZPR will use a range of financial rewards as it can be difficult to recruit employees.' The manager knows there are many factors for a business to consider when deciding who to recruit.
ms: Award 2 marks for full definition, 1 mark for partial. Full: Industry/industries which provide services to consumers/customers and/or other sectors of the economy; OR businesses that supply a service to consumers and/or other businesses. Partial: Provide services. Who the services are sold to is +1 only. Do NOT award: Examples of businesses such as delivery business, accountant, shops; Names of shops/retailers.

text: Define 'job description'.
context: ZPR is a business in the tertiary sector. It has 1 restaurant which has 20 employees. The Human Resources Manager is preparing a job description as ZPR needs 2 new chefs.
ms: Award 2 marks for full definition, 1 mark for partial. Full: Outlines the responsibilities and duties to be carried out by someone to do a specific job; OR a list of the key points about a job including job title, key duties, responsibilities and accountabilities; OR a description of the tasks, roles, and responsibilities of a particular position. Partial: States what the job involves. 1 mark for what it includes/examples of elements. 1 mark for link to job/position. Max 1 if any reference to skills/qualifications.

text: Identify four financial rewards a business could use.
context: ZPR is a business in the tertiary sector. It has 1 restaurant which has 20 employees. ZPR will use a range of financial rewards as it can be difficult to recruit employees.
ms: 1 mark per financial reward (max 4). Only award first four responses. Accept: Time-rate; Piece-rate; Salary; Bonus; Commission; Profit sharing; Fringe benefits or examples e.g. discounts on business goods; Share ownership. Other appropriate responses credited.

text: Explain two ways ZPR could use to advertise its job vacancies externally.
context: ZPR is a business in the tertiary sector. It has 1 restaurant which has 20 employees. The Human Resources Manager is preparing a job description as ZPR needs 2 new chefs. He said: 'I need to advertise the job vacancies externally. ZPR will use a range of financial rewards as it can be difficult to recruit employees.'
ms: Award 1 mark per identification (max 2), 1 mark per application (max 2), 1 mark per analysis (max 2). Ways: National newspapers [k] especially as difficult to recruit employees [app] attracting people from a wider area [an]; Recruitment agencies [k] as need 2 chefs [app] and agency does all the work saving time [an]; Specialist magazines [k] such as one aimed at restaurants [app] as potential employees more likely to see it [an]; Company website [k] of this tertiary sector business [app] likely to be free [an]; Online recruitment sites [k] reaching large number of people [an]; Government run job centres [k]; Visiting universities/colleges [k]; Local newspapers [k]. App words: tertiary sector, restaurant, 20 employees, job description, 2 chefs/cooks, difficult to recruit, financial rewards. Analysis can focus on explaining the way or an advantage of using it.

text: Explain two factors a business should consider when deciding who to recruit. Which factor is likely to be the most important for a tertiary sector business? Justify your answer.
context: ZPR is a business in the tertiary sector. It has 1 restaurant which has 20 employees. The Human Resources Manager is preparing a job description as ZPR needs 2 new chefs. The manager knows there are many factors for a business to consider when deciding who to recruit.
ms: General question - no application marks. Award up to 2 marks identification, up to 2 marks analysis, up to 2 marks justified decision for a tertiary sector business. Factors: Experience/skills [k] showing the person is able to do the job [an] AND/OR may expect higher wages [an]; Education/qualifications [k] as person likely to make fewer mistakes/provide better service [an]; Personality/attitude/whether trustable [k] as may want someone willing to learn [an]; Punctuality/disciplinary record [k] as if they are late it could cause delays [an]. Must discuss two factors to access evaluation. Justification must follow from relevant analysis. Some analysis could work for more than one factor but only award once. Evaluation capped at 4/6 without justified conclusion.

text: Define 'quality assurance'.
context: BEI is a multinational company. It manufactures aeroplanes. Quality assurance is important. BEI has 5000 employees. BEI's directors have announced plans to reduce the size of its workforce (downsize). The Human Resources Director is considering which employees to make redundant. Employee A: Worked at BEI for 1 year, worked at another manufacturing business for 12 years, able to use most of the machines at BEI, often late for work, popular with other employees, left school with 2 IGCSEs.
ms: Award 2 marks for a full definition, 1 mark for partial. Full: Checking for quality/standards throughout the production process/at every stage; OR a method of improving quality by trying to prevent mistakes happening in the production process. Partial: Checking work done/checking quality multiple times; OR try to prevent mistakes. To gain both marks, answer must show (1) checking quality/product AND (2) throughout/at every stage of the production process.

text: Identify two reasons why a business might reduce the size of its workforce.
context: BEI is a multinational company. It manufactures aeroplanes. BEI has 5000 employees. BEI's directors have announced plans to reduce the size of its workforce (downsize).
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two responses. Accept: Fall/decrease in demand/sales/revenue/recession; Introduction of automation/machinery/technology/becoming capital intensive; Financial problems/need to reduce costs; Closure of factory/shop/office; Merger/takeover; Relocation/move operations to another part of country/world.

text: Outline, with reference to BEI, the difference between redundancy and dismissal.
context: BEI is a multinational company. It manufactures aeroplanes. Quality assurance is important. BEI has 5000 employees. BEI's directors have announced plans to reduce the size of its workforce (downsize). Employee A: Worked at BEI for 1 year, worked at another manufacturing business for 12 years, able to use most of the machines at BEI, often late for work, popular with other employees, left school with 2 IGCSEs.
ms: Award 1 mark for understanding of redundancy (max 1), 1 mark for understanding of dismissal (max 1), 1 mark each for relevant application to BEI (max 2). Redundancy: Job no longer needed/exists [k] as business is downsizing [app]; Worker has done nothing wrong [k] when making aeroplanes [app]; Being asked to leave because skills/experience no longer needed [k]. Dismissal: Employee is incompetent/cannot do the job [k] at the multinational company [app]; Being asked to leave because of poor behaviour/conduct [k] which may affect quality assurance [app]; Termination of employment by employer [k]. App words: multinational/MNC, aeroplanes, quality assurance, downsize, 5000 employees, often late, worked 1 year at BEI. Do NOT award: sacked/fired/laid off on own.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of BEI making employee A redundant.
context: BEI is a multinational company. It manufactures aeroplanes. BEI has 5000 employees. BEI's directors plan to downsize. Employee A: Worked at BEI for 1 year, worked at another manufacturing business for 12 years, able to use most of the machines at BEI, often late for work, popular with other employees, left school with 2 IGCSEs.
ms: Award 1 mark per identification (max 2), 1 mark per application (max 2), 1 mark per explanation/analysis (max 2). Advantages: Less compensation to pay [k] as only been there 1 year [app] lowering cash outflows [an]; Improve productivity/efficiency [k] because often late [app] so orders met on time [an]. Disadvantages: Lose experience [k] as worked at another business 12 years [app] leading to more mistakes/less output [an]; Lose skills [k] as can use most machinery [app] leading to production delays [an]; Lower motivation of other employees [k] as popular with them [app] increasing labour turnover [an]; Have to train someone else [k] increasing costs [an]. Note: increase costs on own is [an] only; labour turnover/absenteeism is [an] only.

text: Explain two possible benefits to a country of a multinational company locating there. Which benefit is likely to be the most important? Justify your answer.
context: BEI is a multinational company. It manufactures aeroplanes. BEI has 5000 employees. BEI's directors have announced plans to reduce the size of its workforce (downsize).
ms: General question - no application marks. Award up to 2 marks identification, up to 2 marks analysis, up to 2 marks justified evaluation. Benefits: Increase jobs/employment [k] increasing income [an]/reducing unemployment [an]/improving standard of living [an]; Generate taxes [k] which may improve public services [an]; More competition [k] increasing choice/quality/lower prices [an]; Increase reputation of country [k] encouraging other businesses to invest [an]; Knowledge sharing/increase skills [k] improving production methods/efficiency [an]; Improve infrastructure [k]. Must identify two valid benefits to access evaluation. Evaluation capped at 4/6 without justified conclusion comparing both benefits.

text: Define 'cash flow forecast'.
context: OTK is a small jewellery shop in the centre of Main City. The business does not currently use ecommerce. OTK buys its jewellery from local suppliers. It pays for the jewellery 30 days later. The shop manager is analysing OTK's cash flow forecast. She is concerned about a short-term cash flow problem.
ms: Award 2 marks for full definition, 1 mark for partial. Full: Estimate of future cash inflows and outflows of a business (usually on a month-by-month basis). Partial: Shows the cash inflows and outflows of a business. First mark for understanding it refers to cash/money in(flows) and out(flows). Second mark for idea that it is an estimate or future values.

text: Identify two reasons why cash is important for a business.
context: OTK is a small jewellery shop in the centre of Main City. OTK buys from local suppliers and pays 30 days later. The shop manager is concerned about a short-term cash flow problem.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two. Accept: Pay employees/wages/salary; Pay suppliers/trade payables/raw materials; Pay rent; Pay insurance; Pay utilities; Pay advertising; Pay interest on loans/repay loan; For emergencies/unexpected costs; Ensure survival. Can award pay expenses/short-term debts/day-to-day costs when no specific examples given.

text: Identify four functions of management.
context: OTK is a small jewellery shop in the centre of Main City. The shop manager is analysing OTK's cash flow forecast.
ms: 1 mark per function (max 4). Only award first four. The five functions are: Control; Coordinate; Plan; Organise; Command. Do NOT award alternative words - must be these exact terms.

text: Explain two ways OTK could overcome a short-term cash flow problem.
context: OTK is a small jewellery shop in the centre of Main City. The business does not currently use ecommerce. OTK buys its jewellery from local suppliers. It pays for the jewellery 30 days later. The shop manager is concerned about a short-term cash flow problem.
ms: Award 1 mark per identification (max 2), 1 mark per application (max 2), 1 mark per analysis (max 2). Ways: Overdraft [k] allowing business to spend more than in current account [an] for this jewellery business [app]; Ask suppliers for longer to pay [k] delaying cash outflows [an] for more than 30 days [app]; Short-term bank loan [k] for the shop [app] increasing cash inflows quickly [an]; Delay purchase of non-current assets [k] keeping more cash in business [an]; Sell non-current assets [k] generating cash inflows [an]; Ask customers to pay sooner/offer discounts [k]. App words: small business, jewellery, shop, centre of Main City, no ecommerce, 30 days later, local suppliers. Analysis must show effect on cash inflow/outflow.

text: Explain two threats to a business of using ecommerce. Which threat is likely to be the most important? Justify your answer.
context: OTK is a small jewellery shop in the centre of Main City. The business does not currently use ecommerce. OTK buys its jewellery from local suppliers. It pays for the jewellery 30 days later.
ms: General question - no application marks. Award up to 2 marks identification, up to 2 marks analysis, up to 2 marks justified evaluation. Threats: Increased competition [k] so may have to set lower prices/spend more on advertising [an]; Need to design/build website [k] increasing costs [an]; Maintenance/updating of website [k] may need to employ someone [an]; No face-to-face contact [k] difficult to gain feedback/build customer loyalty [an]; Need to deliver products [k] increasing transport/postage costs [an]/lower profit margin [an]; Technical problems [k] losing potential sales [an]; Security threats/hacking/data theft [k] damaging reputation [an]/reducing customer loyalty [an]; Risk of bad reviews [k] lowering sales [an]; High level of returns [k]. Points must focus on business not customers. Evaluation capped at 4/6 without justified conclusion comparing both threats.

text: Define 'partnership'.
context: Miguel plans to start up a gym (sports club). It will offer a range of fitness classes including yoga. The business will be a partnership with his sister. Miguel thinks the size of the business will remain small. Secondary market research will be used to help make decisions including which pricing method to use. Miguel knows it is important for a new business to select a suitable location.
ms: Award 2 marks for full definition, 1 mark for partial. Full: Two (or more) people agree to jointly own a business together; OR a business formed by two or more people. Partial: A business run/operated/managed/controlled/led by two or more people. For two marks need: owned/formed AND at least two people.

text: Identify two ways to measure the size of a business.
context: Miguel plans to start up a gym (sports club). The business will be a partnership with his sister. Miguel thinks the size of the business will remain small.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 2). Only award first two. Accept: Number of employees/size of workforce; Value of sales/revenue; Number/amount of customers/volume of output/number of sales; Value of output; Value of capital employed. Do NOT award: Profit; Capital on its own.

text: Outline two pricing methods Miguel could use.
context: Miguel plans to start up a gym (sports club). It will offer a range of fitness classes including yoga. The business will be a partnership with his sister. Miguel thinks the size of the business will remain small. Secondary market research will be used. Miguel knows it is important for a new business to select a suitable location.
ms: Award 1 mark per method (max 2), 1 mark per application (max 2). Methods: Cost-plus pricing [k] to cover costs of the gym [app]; Penetration pricing [k] as it is a new business [app]; Competitive/competition pricing [k] based on the location [app]; Price skimming [k] for some of the classes [app]; Promotional pricing [k] based on market research results [app]. App words: gym/sports club, fitness/classes/yoga, partnership/sister, remain small, new/start-up business, secondary/market research, suitable location.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to Miguel of using secondary market research.
context: Miguel plans to start up a gym (sports club). It will offer a range of fitness classes including yoga. The business will be a partnership with his sister. Miguel thinks the size of the business will remain small. Secondary market research will be used to help make decisions including which pricing method to use.
ms: Award 1 mark per identification (max 2), 1 mark per application (max 2), 1 mark per analysis (max 2). Advantages: Low cost/free [k] important for a new business [app] so has funds for other activities [an]; Readily available [k] saves time [an] such as deciding a pricing method [app]; More/wider range of information [k] about classes/yoga [app] could help increase demand/sales [an]. Disadvantages: Out-of-date information [k] for the gym [app] leading to wrong decisions [an]; Available to all businesses [k] so may not help create competitive advantage [an] for the partnership [app]; May not be relevant/specific [k] for this small business [app] so customer needs not met reducing loyalty [an]; May not be reliable [k] as not up to date [an]. App words: gym/sports club, fitness/classes/yoga, partnership/sister, remain small, method of pricing, suitable location, new/start-up business.

text: Do you think access to employees is the most important factor for a new business to consider when deciding on a suitable location? Justify your answer.
context: Miguel plans to start up a gym (sports club). It will offer a range of fitness classes including yoga. The business will be a partnership with his sister. Miguel thinks the size of the business will remain small. Secondary market research will be used. Miguel knows it is important for a new business to select a suitable location.
ms: General question - no application marks. Evaluation only if candidate discusses access to employees. Award up to 2 marks identification, up to 2 marks analysis, up to 2 marks justified decision. Access to employees: Availability/number of employees [k] if high employment hard to find staff/if many available could pay lower wages [an] lowering costs [an]; Distance from workers [k] if far may increase transport costs/if nearby easier to recruit [an]; May need skilled workers [k] to provide good service/higher output [an]; Level of wages in local area [k] if high wages increase costs [an]. Other factors: Access to customers/proximity to market [k] to increase sales/revenue [an]; Availability of premises/rent [k] high rent increases fixed costs [an]; Number of competitors [k] may lead to high/low footfall [an]; Distance to suppliers [k] increasing transport costs [an]; Raw materials [k]; Legal controls [k]; Government grants [k]; Local infrastructure [k]; Personal preference [k]. Answers must be from business viewpoint. Evaluation capped at 4/6 without justified conclusion.

text: Define 'fixed costs'.
context: DJU manufactures clothing including jeans and trousers. There are 90 employees working in its factory. DJU uses specialisation when making its products. Fixed costs: $400,000. Total costs: $595,000. Total output: 85,000 units per week. DJU's directors are considering different ways a business could grow including taking over a competitor.
ms: Award 2 marks for full definition, 1 mark for partial. Full: Costs that do not change with the level of output/sales; OR costs that do not vary in the short run with number of items sold/produced. Partial: Costs that do not change. Do NOT award: answers confusing with variable costs; examples only.

text: Calculate DJU's average cost per unit per week. Show your working.
context: DJU manufactures clothing. Fixed costs: $400,000 per week. Total costs: $595,000 per week. Total output: 85,000 units per week.
ms: Award 2 marks for correct answer, 1 mark for correct method but incorrect answer. Correct answer: $7 (or 7). Method: Total cost divided by total output = $595,000 divided by 85,000 = $7 per unit. If correct answer given with no working, award 2 marks. Dollar sign not required. Max 1 if answer refers to 7 units.

text: Outline two ways lower interest rates might affect DJU.
context: DJU manufactures clothing including jeans and trousers. There are 90 employees. DJU uses specialisation. Fixed costs: $400,000. Total costs: $595,000. Total output: 85,000 units per week. DJU's directors are considering ways to grow including taking over a competitor.
ms: Award 1 mark per way (max 2), 1 mark per application (max 2). Ways: Increased demand/sales [k] for its clothing [app]; Lower costs/cheaper to borrow [k] for the factory [app]; Encourage DJU to invest more/more likely to apply for loan [k] as considering ways to grow [app]. App words: clothing/jeans/trousers, 90 employees, factory, specialisation, grow/takeover competitor, $595,000 total costs, $400,000 fixed costs, 85,000 units, $7 average cost.

text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to DJU of using specialisation when making its products.
context: DJU manufactures clothing including jeans and trousers. There are 90 employees in its factory. DJU uses specialisation. Fixed costs: $400,000. Total costs: $595,000. Total output: 85,000 units per week. DJU's directors are considering taking over a competitor.
ms: Award 1 mark per identification (max 2), 1 mark per application (max 2), 1 mark per analysis (max 2). Advantages: Higher output [k] of clothing [app] so able to meet orders on time [an]; Quicker/cheaper to train employees [k] not increasing costs above $595,000 [app] [an]; Increased efficiency [k] increasing output/less waste [an] in the factory [app]; Employee becomes skilled/expert [k] more efficient in that task [an]; Easier to use machinery [k] speeding up production [an]; Fewer mistakes/better quality [k] fewer complaints/lower costs/better reputation [an]. Disadvantages: Workers less motivated [k] of the 90 employees [app] more likely to leave/more errors [an]; Workers cannot cover absent colleagues [k] manufacturing may stop/slow down [an]; Need to train employees [k] increasing training costs [an]; Not spread risk [k]. Note: more sales/customers is [an] only. App words: clothing/jeans/trousers, 90 employees, factory, $595,000 total costs, $400,000 fixed costs, 85,000 units, takeover competitor, $7 average cost.

text: Do you think the advantages of taking over a competitor are greater than the disadvantages? Justify your answer.
context: DJU manufactures clothing including jeans and trousers. There are 90 employees in its factory. DJU uses specialisation. DJU's directors are considering different ways a business could grow including taking over a competitor.
ms: General question - no application marks. Must refer to both advantage and disadvantage to access evaluation. Award up to 2 marks identification, up to 2 marks analysis, up to 2 marks justified decision. Advantages: Reduced competition [k] increasing sales/revenue [an]; Gain brand name/better reputation [k] increasing customer loyalty/more sales [an]; Economies of scale [k] lower average costs [an]; Access new skills/expertise/resources [k]; More capacity/output [k] possible economies of scale [an]. Disadvantages: Increased costs [k] business might not afford [an]; Clash of management styles [k] leading to wrong decisions [an]; Could demotivate employees [k] lowering efficiency [an]; Difficult to coordinate [k] could lead to mistakes [an]; Poor communication [k] demotivating employees [an]; Less choice for customers [k]. Do NOT award: answers about monopolies; forward/backward integration. Evaluation capped at 4/6 without justified conclusion comparing advantages and disadvantages.

text: Define 'trade union'.
context: WMH is a business which operates in the secondary sector. It makes furniture including tables and chairs. WMH's employees are all members of a trade union. The Managing Director knows the business is likely to remain small. She is considering introducing new technology into WMH's factory.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Group of workers who join together to ensure their interests are protected. An organisation of employees aimed at improving pay and working conditions. Partial (1 mark): Group of workers/employees who join together. People/organisation who fight for employee/worker rights. Stand for workers' rights/protect workers.

text: Define 'secondary sector'.
context: WMH is a business which operates in the secondary sector. It makes furniture including tables and chairs.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Businesses that process/manufacture goods from natural resources. Manufacture goods using the raw materials provided by the primary sector. Converts raw materials into manufactured goods. Partial (1 mark): Makes products. Manufactures goods. Refines/processes raw materials. Do not award examples of manufactured goods.

text: Identify four reasons why a business might remain small.
context: WMH is a business which operates in the secondary sector. The Managing Director knows the business is likely to remain small.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 4). Points include: Limited access to capital to expand; Limited access to suitable labour; Personal preference/owner does not want responsibility/wants to keep control; Lack of skills/knowledge/experience; Size of the market/small market/low demand; To maintain close customer relationships/provide personal service; Some large firms dominate the market/too much competition; Can be flexible/respond quickly to changes; No economies of scale/to avoid diseconomies; Operating at maximum possible output. Only award first four responses. Do not award vague statements such as less stressful.

text: Explain two possible effects of WMH introducing new technology.
context: WMH is a business which operates in the secondary sector. It makes furniture including tables and chairs. WMH's employees are all members of a trade union. The Managing Director is considering introducing new technology into WMH's factory.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application to business + 1 mark explanation (max 2 effects = 6 marks). Positive effects: Improve quality/less waste/fewer mistakes leading to better reputation for its furniture; Increases productivity/efficiency/quicker production leading to lower costs for this small business; Improved communication leading to fewer mistakes/better efficiency in the factory; Can design new products which may increase sales/access new markets; Greater job satisfaction/motivation reducing absenteeism/lowering labour turnover. Negative effects: Purchasing new equipment/expensive increasing cash outflows/debt; Need to train workers which can increase costs; Some employees may lose their jobs/made redundant. Application words: furniture/tables/chairs, trade union, factory, small business, secondary sector/manufacturing. Some points can be knowledge or analysis but do not award the same point twice.

text: Explain two factors a manufacturing business should consider when deciding on a suitable location for a factory. Which factor is likely to be the most important? Justify your answer.
context: WMH is a business which operates in the secondary sector. It makes furniture. This is a general question so there are no marks for application.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application - this is a general question. Factors: Access to skilled labour as may be difficult to find/recruit; Access to raw materials/components so production is not delayed; Availability/rent of suitable land which could restrict size of factory; Good transport links to ensure materials arrive/products sent when needed; Proximity to market to ensure sales/revenue can be made; Government grants which could help reduce costs; Legal controls which may prevent locating in certain areas; Access to utilities/power/water as needed for production. Justification must explain why one factor is MORE important than another with reasoning - e.g. land is more important because it might limit output which could reduce ability to meet demand whereas a business can train employees and extra cost might be covered by additional revenue.

text: Define 'import tariff'.
context: CPW is a private sector business which sells electrical goods including kettles and ovens in its 36 shops. CPW buys all its inventory from local suppliers to avoid import tariffs.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): A tax placed on imported goods. A tax applied to the value of imported goods. A specific form of tax imposed on imported goods. Partial (1 mark): A type of tax. First mark is for understanding this is a tax.

text: Identify one non-current asset and one current liability.
context: CPW statement of financial position 2024: Non-current assets $120m, Current assets $70m, Current liabilities $110m, Non-current liabilities $75m.
ms: 1 mark per correct answer. Non-current assets: Machinery, Equipment, Land, Buildings/shops/factories/offices, Motor vehicles/delivery vehicles. Current liabilities: Overdraft, Short-term loan, Trade payables/creditors. Only award first responses given for each.

text: Outline two ways the information in Table 2.1 might be useful to CPW.
context: CPW statement of financial position 2024 ($million): Non-current assets 120, Current assets 70, Current liabilities 110, Non-current liabilities 75. CPW is a private sector business selling electrical goods (kettles/ovens) in 36 shops. Buying 10 new delivery vehicles.
ms: 1 mark per way + 1 mark application (max 2 ways = 4 marks). Ways: Show value of liabilities/what the business owes - current liabilities $110 million; Show value of assets/what the business owns - $190 million; Support loan application/help raise finance for the 10 vehicles; Calculate working capital/current assets minus current liabilities; Show how business finances its activities; Calculate current ratio 0.63:1 or 0.64:1; Compare performance with other businesses/over time; Show value of business/capital employed $80 million; Equity/owners capital $5 million. Application words: private sector business, electrical goods/kettles/ovens, 36 shops, 10 vehicles, local suppliers, import tariffs, delivery service, $75m non-current liabilities, $120m non-current assets, $110m current liabilities, $70m current assets, 0.63:1 current ratio, $190m total assets, negative $40m working capital, $80m capital employed, $5m equity.

text: Explain two factors CPW should consider when deciding on a source of finance for the new vehicles.
context: CPW is a private sector business selling electrical goods in 36 shops. Non-current assets $120m, Current assets $70m, Current liabilities $110m, Non-current liabilities $75m. Needs to purchase 10 new delivery vehicles.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 factors = 6 marks). Factors: Amount required for the 10 vehicles because this is a large amount a bank loan may be required; Current level of borrowing/loans as bank might not lend extra when have non-current liabilities of $75 million; Time period as vehicles needed long-term so source needs to be long-term to make deliveries; Cost of finance/affordability as high interest rates could increase cash outflows adding to current liabilities of $110 million; Size/legal form of private sector business; Security/collateral needed; Level of control; How urgently funds are required. Application words: private sector business, electrical goods, 36 shops, 10 vehicles, local suppliers, import tariffs, delivery service, $75m non-current liabilities, $120m non-current assets, $110m current liabilities, $70m current assets.

text: Explain two objectives a private sector business might have. Which objective is likely to be the most important? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Objectives: Survival/stay in business to breakeven/ensure costs are covered; Make a profit when revenue exceeds total costs; Growth/expansion as this can help spread risk; Increase sales leading to higher revenue; Increase market share which could allow controlling prices; Socially/ethically/environmentally responsible; Increase returns to shareholders to encourage investment; Increase brand image/reputation; Customer satisfaction. Justification must compare two objectives and explain why one is MORE important than the other with reasoning - e.g. survival is most important because without it there is no opportunity to make profit in the long term. Analysis can focus on explaining what the objective is or advantages of that objective.

text: Identify X and Y on the break-even chart.
context: SBL is a fast food restaurant which sells 900 chicken burgers each week. It has 14 employees. A partially completed break-even chart is shown. X is the intersection point of total costs and total revenue. Y is the line that starts from zero and rises steeply (total revenue line).
ms: 1 mark each. X: Break-even (point). Y: (Total) revenue. Only award first response given for each.

text: Define 'margin of safety'.
context: SBL sells 900 chicken burgers each week and has a break-even point of 500 units.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): The difference between the current level of output/sales and break-even output/sales. The amount by which sales exceed the break-even point. Partial (1 mark): Difference between total output and break-even point. Number of units that exceed break-even output.

text: Outline two advantages of Vicki delegating tasks to her employees.
context: SBL is a fast food restaurant selling 900 chicken burgers each week with 14 employees. Owner Vicki does not currently use delegation but provides training. Break-even output is 500 units, margin of safety is 400 units.
ms: 1 mark per advantage + 1 mark application (max 2 advantages = 4 marks). Advantages: Motivate employees helping increase sales above 900 units; Develop employee skills/increase flexibility when making burgers; Builds trust between owner and employees/better working relations; The owner cannot do all tasks alone/reduces her workload/time to focus on other tasks such as completing break-even chart; Quality of owner's work often improved/less likely to make mistakes at the restaurant; She can measure performance/success of employees. Application words: fast food/restaurant, chicken burgers, 14 employees, 900 meals a week, 500/break-even, 400/margin of safety, training, economic recession.

text: Explain two possible effects of an economic recession on Vicki's business.
context: SBL is a fast food restaurant selling 900 chicken burgers each week with 14 employees. Break-even is 500 units, margin of safety 400 units. Vicki provides training and is considering delegation.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 effects = 6 marks). Effects: Lower/fewer sales leading to lower revenue from selling burgers; May need to lower costs as revenue falling for the restaurant; More workers available so may lower labour costs of the 14 employees; Workers may be made redundant/reduce workforce which could demotivate other workers; Low business confidence so less willing to invest; The business may fail/hard to survive; May have cash flow problems so cannot pay day-to-day costs; May lower prices; May delay expansion plans; Banks may not be willing to lend; May change objective to survival; Lower profit so less funds to invest. Application words: fast food/restaurant, chicken burgers, 14 employees, delegation, 900 meals a week, 500 break-even output, 400 margin of safety. Effects can be positive or negative but mirror answers only credited once.

text: Explain two methods of training a business might use. Which is likely to be the best method for a service business to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Methods: On-the-job training - being trained in the workplace/watching experienced worker/business specific training/lower cost/some work completed during training/may learn bad habits/trainer less productive. Off-the-job training - being trained away from workplace/trained by experts/new up-to-date skills/higher cost/wages paid but no work done. Induction training - helps new employees understand workplace/job role/new workers settle in quickly/delays when start work. Justification must compare two methods and explain why one is BETTER for a service business than the other with reasoning.

text: Define 'brand image'.
context: MTL is a large business which sells children's toys. Having a good brand image is important.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): The image or identity given to a product/business which distinguishes it from competitors. Characteristics that distinguish a business from others through design or logo. The general impression of a product/business held by consumers. Personality given to a product/business through marketing activities. Partial (1 mark): Identity given to a product/business. How product/business is seen by others. Characteristics that make a business unique.

text: Identify two reasons why some markets have become more competitive.
context: MTL is a large business selling children's toys. The market has become more competitive.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Points: Globalisation/growth of free trade agreements; Changes in technology e.g. ecommerce/internet/social media; Changes in legal controls/more or fewer regulations/government intervention; Transport improvements/infrastructure improvements. Only award first two responses. Do not award factors affecting demand or spending patterns such as changes in population, changes in advertising or changes in prices. Accept reduced barriers to entry once if no other specific reasons.

text: Outline one way MTL could act ethically with each of the following stakeholder groups: Employees and Customers.
context: MTL is a large business which sells children's toys. MTL wants to act ethically with all of its stakeholder groups including its 430 employees. The market has become more competitive. Having a good brand image is important.
ms: 1 mark per way + 1 mark application (max 2 stakeholder groups = 4 marks). Employees: Pay fair/good wages to its 430 employees; Ensure fair/good working conditions when making the toys; Not employ child labour; Not use zero hours contracts. Customers: Charge a fair price which can help maintain its good brand image; Not advertise misleading prices when operating in a competitive market. Application words: children's toys, 430 employees, competitive market, large business, good brand image, new markets in other countries, methods of promotion.

text: Explain two problems MTL might have when entering a new market in another country.
context: MTL is a large business selling children's toys. MTL operates ethically and has 430 employees. Good brand image is important. MTL's directors are considering entering a new market in another country.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 problems = 6 marks). Problems: Lack of market knowledge so may not be aware of competitors' pricing/promotion for toys; Language differences so may have to translate/change wording on packaging to explain how it is ethical; Cultural differences so product may not sell there which could damage brand image; Changes in exchange rates may make it difficult to set prices for this large business; Different legal controls which could restrict what/how they can sell; Import restrictions/quotas which could restrict number of products they can import; Economic differences e.g. average income; Increased transport costs as products may be transported over long distances; Level of competition; Lack of recognition of the business; High taxes; Difficulty locating suppliers; Increased risk of non-payment as methods of payment likely different. Application words: children's toys, ethical, stakeholder groups, 430 employees, good brand image, large business, methods of promotion.

text: Explain two methods of promotion a business might use for its products. Which method is likely to be the best for a large business to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application.
