ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Methods: Television - expensive/can include moving images to attract attention; Magazines - able to target specific types of customers; Discount offers/promotional pricing/coupons/loyalty cards - makes products more affordable; Social media/internet/influencers - reach large numbers of people; Leaflets - low-cost method; Posters/billboards - seen by everyone passing by; Point of sale displays/demonstrations - customer shown how it is used; Radio advertising - target specific regions; Newspapers; Gifts; Sponsorship; Competitions - encourage customer to buy to receive reward; Free samples; BOGOF; After-sales service. Justification must compare two methods and explain why one is BETTER for a large business than the other - e.g. television is best because a large business can afford the cost and is likely to reach far more people than a poster.

text: Define 'business partnership'.
context: Brendan wants to be a successful entrepreneur. He plans to start up a flower shop using government support. Brendan's brother has offered to form a business partnership with him. Brendan knows it is important for a new business to use a suitable pricing method. He has already identified ways the business can increase added value. Brendan wants to know how an economic boom might affect his business.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Two or more people who agree to jointly own a business, usually sharing responsibility for day-to-day running. An unincorporated business that has more than one owner. Partial definition (1 mark): Business run by two or more people. Must convey BOTH the idea of shared ownership AND that it involves at least two people for full marks.

text: Identify two ways a government can support business start-ups.
context: Brendan plans to start up a flower shop using government support.
ms: 1 mark per way (max 2). Only award first two responses. Acceptable answers: grants/subsidies; low-interest loans; low-cost or rent-free premises; training provision; tax relief/holiday; advice or help with research; help promoting/advertising the business; provision of mentors.

text: Outline two ways an economic boom might affect Brendan's business.
context: Brendan wants to start a flower shop as an entrepreneur, forming a business partnership with his brother, using government support. He is aware of how an economic boom might affect his business.
ms: 1 mark per point + 1 mark per application (max 2 points = 4 marks). Points: High demand/sales/revenue for flowers; Difficulty finding employees for the shop; Ability to raise prices increasing added value; Higher costs/wages may need more government support; High business confidence for this entrepreneur; Increased competition; Harder to access materials; Harder to find a location. Application words: entrepreneur, start-up/new business, flowers, shop, government support, increase added value, business partnership, pricing method.

text: Explain two ways Brendan could increase added value for his business.
context: Brendan is starting a flower shop business partnership with his brother. He wants to increase added value. Added value = selling price minus cost of inputs.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 ways = 6 marks). Ways: Set high prices - widens gap between cost and price - for the flowers; Lower input costs by buying cheaper materials for this new business; Branding/marketing/packaging to give perception of higher quality; Unique design/products making more desirable than rivals which could influence pricing method; Improve convenience so products immediately available in the shop; Improve quality/service. Analysis: explaining why price/costs are higher/lower, or how the method increases added value. Do not award same analysis point twice. Application words: start-up/new business, flowers, shop, government support, brother, business partnership, pricing method, entrepreneur.

text: Explain two pricing methods a new business might use. Which is likely to be the best method to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Candidates must name the pricing method to access knowledge marks.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Must NAME the pricing method. Methods: Cost-plus - add % onto production costs - easy to calculate; Penetration pricing - set lower price than competitors - attracts customers; Competitive pricing - price similar to/just below competitors - may not cover costs; Price skimming - recover development costs quicker - may lead to low sales; Promotional pricing; Dynamic pricing; Psychological pricing. Evaluation must discuss TWO relevant methods and make a justified recommendation explaining why one is better for a new business.

text: Identify one way each of the following changes in country X's exchange rate might affect businesses which import raw materials. (i) Depreciation (ii) Appreciation
context: NSL is a business based in country X. It manufactures food products including bread and breakfast cereals. NSL imports 15% of its raw materials. Changes in country X's exchange rate can affect businesses which import raw materials.
ms: 1 mark each. Do NOT award answers about exports. Depreciation: imports become dearer/more expensive. Appreciation: imports become cheaper.

text: Identify two reasons why consumer spending patterns might change.
context: NSL's Marketing Manager knows the business should respond to changes in consumer spending patterns.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 2). Only award first two. Acceptable: change in price of product; change in competitor prices; changes in incomes/wages/unemployment/business cycle; changes in population size/structure/life stage; change in taste/fashion/preferences; advertising/promotion; technology; taxation; interest rates; exchange rates; weather/season.

text: Outline two reasons why maintaining quality is important for NSL.
context: NSL manufactures food products including bread and breakfast cereals. It uses lean production in its factory. Maintaining quality is important. NSL imports 15% of its raw materials.
ms: 1 mark per point + 1 mark per application (max 2 points = 4 marks). Points: Develop strong brand/reputation for its food; Keep customer loyalty as spending patterns change; Charge premium prices helping offset exchange rate effects; Lower costs/less wastage at the factory; Fewer complaints/returns; Attract new customers/increase sales; Meet legal requirements such as food standards; Adds value. Application words: food/ingredients/breakfast cereal/bread, manufacture, consumer spending patterns change, factory, exchange rates, 15% imported materials, lean production.

text: Explain two benefits to NSL of using lean production.
context: NSL manufactures food products including bread and breakfast cereals. It uses lean production in its factory. Maintaining quality is important. NSL imports 15% of its raw materials.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 benefits = 6 marks). Benefits: Fewer mistakes/errors - less rework/lower costs/improved reputation - maintaining quality is important; Less inventory held of imported materials lowering storage costs/working capital; Cut out processes when making food which speeds up production/increases productivity; Increased motivation leading to lower absenteeism/reduced labour turnover at the factory; Less waste of time/materials/improved efficiency leading to quicker/increased output; Lower unit costs improving competitiveness. Some points can be knowledge OR analysis but only award once. Application words: food/ingredients/breakfast cereal/bread, manufacture, consumer spending patterns change, factory, exchange rates, 15% imported materials, maintaining quality.

text: Explain two methods of market research a business could use to help make business decisions. Which is likely to be the best method for a manufacturing business to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Candidates must identify the specific method, not just state primary/secondary.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Must identify the specific method. Methods: Government statistics - wide sample; Internet/online sources - free/low cost/immediate; Trade associations/journals - industry-specific; Market research agency reports - detailed but expensive; Questionnaire - up-to-date, specific to business; Interviews - in-depth opinions; Survey - reaches large numbers; Focus group - detailed, allows follow-up; Test marketing - limits cost of problems; Observation - low cost; Newspapers/magazines. Evaluation: must discuss at least two methods and justify recommendation for a manufacturing business specifically.

text: Define 'dismissal'.
context: LFK is a coal-mining business. It has 135 employees. After the dismissal of one of LFK's employees there is a job vacancy for a new supervisor. External recruitment will be used.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): When employment is ended against the will of the employee, usually for not working in accordance with the employment contract. Terminated by employer because employee broke company rules or failed to perform to required standard. Partial definition (1 mark): When someone/employee is told to leave a business / lose job because of bad behaviour. Do NOT award on its own: lose job / let go. Accept fired/sacked.

text: Calculate the value of X and Y from LFK's cash flow forecast (July–September 2025, $000). July: Inflow 600, Outflow 720, Net (120), Opening 40, Closing (80). August: Inflow 400, Outflow X, Net (100), Opening (80), Closing (180). September: Inflow 730, Outflow 590, Net 140, Opening (180), Closing Y.
context: LFK is a coal-mining business. The Managing Director is preparing a cash flow forecast.
ms: 1 mark each. X = 500 ($000) — Net cash flow = Inflow minus Outflow: (100) = 400 minus X, so X = 500. Y = (40) i.e. negative 40 ($000) — Closing = Opening plus Net: (180) + 140 = (40). Y must be shown as a negative number using brackets or minus sign.

text: Identify four reasons why a cash flow forecast might be useful to a business.
context: LFK is a coal-mining business. The Managing Director is preparing a cash flow forecast.
ms: 1 mark per reason (max 4). Only award first four. Acceptable: help support a loan application/attract investors; identify possible cash flow problems; help financial planning/budgeting/manage cash flow/avoid insolvency; identify how much to borrow/size of overdraft; identify if too much idle cash; help with decision-making/decide if expansion is possible.

text: Explain two advantages of LFK training its employees.
context: LFK is a coal-mining business with 135 employees who are all provided with training. External recruitment will be used to fill a supervisor vacancy.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 advantages = 6 marks). Advantages: Motivate employees - reduce absenteeism/lower labour turnover - among its 135 employees; Help retain/attract employees/lower labour turnover; Increase skills/knowledge - more workers suitable for promotion - so may not need external recruitment; Reduce mistakes/errors/better quality; Reduce accidents increasing worker safety; Increase efficiency/productivity/reduced waste - helps reduce average costs - reducing cash outflows; Increase output; Improve competitiveness of the mine; Improve customer service; Management training improves decisions. Application words: coal, mining/mine, 135 employees, dismissal, new supervisor, external recruitment, cash flow data from table. Analysis only (not knowledge): reduce costs, better reputation, increase sales.

text: Do you think the advantages of external recruitment for a business are greater than the disadvantages? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Advantages: brings new skills/ideas improving productivity/efficiency; wider choice of applicants increases chance of finding best person; valuable knowledge of competition could give competitive advantage; avoids creating internal vacancy; avoids upsetting employees when internal candidate promoted. Disadvantages: higher recruitment costs increasing cash outflows; no knowledge of how business works so may need induction training; more time to fill vacancy. Award 'avoids upsetting employees' OR 'demotivates existing employees' only once. Evaluation must discuss both advantages and disadvantages and justify why one side outweighs the other.

text: Identify two methods of external growth a business might use.
context: PKN manufactures glass. PKN has factories in 30 countries. It has 27,000 employees. The Managing Director plans to expand the business using external growth.
ms: 1 mark each (max 2). Only award first two. Preferred: Horizontal integration; Forward vertical integration; Backward vertical integration; Conglomerate/diversification; Joint venture. Also accept if no specific type given: Merger; Takeover/acquisition; Vertical integration.

text: Identify two reasons for globalisation.
context: PKN manufactures glass and has benefited from globalisation.
ms: 1 mark each (max 2). Only award first two. Acceptable: Free trade agreements/economic trading blocs/reduction in trade barriers; improved/cheaper transport/travel links; improved communication networks/technology; emerging/new markets expanding rapidly/rising incomes; governments allow foreign companies to set up in own country.

text: Outline two ways PKN could contribute to sustainable development.
context: PKN manufactures glass and contributes to sustainable development. PKN has factories in 30 countries and 27,000 employees.
ms: 1 mark per way + 1 mark application (max 2 ways = 4 marks). Ways: Use renewable energy in each of the 30 countries; use energy-efficient/environmentally friendly methods to make glass; use fewer resources/reduce output in its factories; recycle waste; develop environmentally friendly products; avoid/reduce use of toxic chemicals; use packaging made of recycled material; use recyclable/reusable packaging; avoid unnecessary travel; use local suppliers; replant trees; switch to environmentally friendly transport. Application words: glass, factory/factories, manufacturer, 30 countries, 27,000 employees, globalisation, expand/external growth, source of finance, diseconomies of scale.

text: Explain two diseconomies of scale which might affect PKN as it grows.
context: PKN manufactures glass. PKN has factories in 30 countries and 27,000 employees. Some directors are concerned about possible diseconomies of scale as the business grows.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 diseconomies = 6 marks). Diseconomies: Low morale/motivation/lack of loyalty - leading to higher labour turnover - among its 27,000 employees; Poor communication - leading to mistakes - when making glass; Weak coordination - leading to wrong decisions - at the factories; Lack of control - leading to higher average costs. Application words: glass, factory/factories, manufacturer, 30 countries, 27,000 employees, globalisation, sustainable development, source of finance. Analysis points can apply to any diseconomy but only award once (e.g. higher average/unit costs).

text: Do you think the advantages of using retained profits to fund business expansion are greater than the disadvantages? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Advantages: No need to repay so does not increase debt/liabilities; no interest to pay so no additional cash outflows; easy/quick to obtain. Disadvantages: Takes time to generate sufficient funds which could delay expansion; may not have sufficient/any funds which limits expansion size; reduces payment/reward to owners which may deter further investment. Evaluation must discuss at least one advantage and one disadvantage and make a justified recommendation explaining why one side outweighs the other.

text: Identify two motivators from Herzberg's theory of motivation.
context: Amir and Carla are business partners. They own a luxury hotel which operates in a niche market. The business has a short hierarchical structure. Amir and Carla use Herzberg's theory of motivation to keep their 5 employees well motivated. Amir and Carla are considering opening another hotel in a different city. They will need to identify a suitable source of finance if they decide to expand. Secondary market research can be used to help a business decide whether it should expand.
ms: Award 1 mark per motivator (max 2). Motivators include: Achievement; Recognition; Personal growth; Advancement; The work itself. Only award first two responses given.

text: Identify two features of a short hierarchical structure.
context: Amir and Carla are business partners. They own a luxury hotel which operates in a niche market. The business has a short hierarchical structure. Amir and Carla use Herzberg's theory of motivation to keep their 5 employees well motivated.
ms: Award 1 mark per feature (max 2). Features include: Shorter chain of command; Wider span of control; Quicker/faster communication; Top managers are less remote from employees. Only award first two responses given.

text: Outline two advantages to Amir and Carla of operating in a niche market.
context: Amir and Carla are business partners. They own a luxury hotel which operates in a niche market. The business has a short hierarchical structure. Amir and Carla use Herzberg's theory of motivation to keep their 5 employees well motivated. Amir and Carla are considering opening another hotel in a different city.
ms: Award 1 mark per advantage (max 2) + 1 mark per application (max 2). Advantages: Can charge higher prices (for its luxury service); Fewer competitors (for the hotel); Focus on meeting the needs of customers/can target customers (through its 5 employees); Can survive in markets dominated by larger firms (which may increase the chance of expanding); Builds up specialist skills/knowledge. Application words: hotel/rooms, luxury, 5 employees, expand/new hotel/growth, different city, 2 partners/partnership.

text: Explain two sources of finance Amir and Carla could use if they decide to expand.
context: Amir and Carla are business partners. They own a luxury hotel which operates in a niche market. Amir and Carla are considering opening another hotel in a different city. They will need to identify a suitable source of finance if they decide to expand.
ms: Award 1 mark per source (max 2) + 1 mark per application (max 2) + 1 mark per explanation (max 2). Sources: Retained profits (from the hotel, does not need to pay it back); Bank loans (to obtain a large amount/varying length of time to repay/quick to arrange, for the luxury service); Owner savings (from the 2 partners, may be readily accessible/no interest to pay); Crowdfunding (no interest to pay). Application: new hotel/rooms, 2 partners/partnership, luxury, niche market, different city, market research.

text: Do you think secondary market research is the most appropriate type of market research for a business to use when deciding whether it should expand? Justify your answer.
context: Amir and Carla are business partners. They own a luxury hotel which operates in a niche market. Amir and Carla are considering opening another hotel in a different city. Secondary market research can be used to help a business decide whether it should expand.
ms: Award up to 2 marks for identification of relevant points. Award up to 2 marks for relevant development. Award up to 2 marks for a justified decision. No application marks. Secondary market research: Low cost (so more funds to spend in other areas); Quick to obtain (may speed up decision-making); Data may be out of date (may not make appropriate decisions); Wide range of data; Data may not be relevant; Data available for all businesses. Primary market research: More in-depth information; Specific/only available to the business; Up to date; May not have necessary skills to collect data; Expensive; Takes time to collect. Do not accept same point twice. Justification must compare secondary vs primary research and make a clear reasoned decision.

text: Define 'sole trader'.
context: Rachel's business produces and sells chocolate bars. Quality is important. Rachel is a sole trader who received government support when she started up her business. The business operates in a competitive market. Rachel is considering ways to increase sales of her best-selling product. She is also planning to introduce a new chocolate bar. Rachel knows deciding which pricing method to use for a new product is important.
ms: Award 2 marks for full definition, 1 mark for partial. Full: A business is owned (and controlled) by one person; An (unincorporated) business owned by one person. Partial: One person starts/runs/controls/operates a business.

text: Identify two ways a government can support business start-ups.
context: Rachel's business produces and sells chocolate bars. Rachel is a sole trader who received government support when she started up her business.
ms: Award 1 mark per way (max 2). Ways include: Providing (low cost) loans/low interest rates; Providing grants; Low-cost rent; Lower tax/tax relief; Providing training; Providing advice/research/marketing data; Providing mentors. Only award first two responses given.

text: Outline two ways Rachel could increase sales of her best-selling product.
context: Rachel's business produces and sells chocolate bars. Quality is important. Rachel is a sole trader who received government support when she started up her business. The business operates in a competitive market. Rachel is considering ways to increase sales of her best-selling product.
ms: Award 1 mark per way (max 2) + 1 mark per application (max 2). Ways: Advertising/social media (quality is important); Improve existing product/better quality materials/new features (to make its chocolate); Decrease prices/promotional pricing/offer discounts (in the competitive market); Point of sale display (by the sole trader); Free samples; Competitions; Free gifts; BOGOF; New/change packaging; Enter a new market; Sell through new outlets. Application: chocolate bars/cocoa, sole trader, competitive market, quality is important.

text: Explain two reasons why quality is important to Rachel's business.
context: Rachel's business produces and sells chocolate bars. Quality is important. Rachel is a sole trader who received government support when she started up her business. The business operates in a competitive market. Rachel is considering ways to increase sales of her best-selling product. She is also planning to introduce a new chocolate bar.
ms: Award 1 mark per reason (max 2) + 1 mark per application (max 2) + 1 mark per explanation (max 2). Reasons: Can charge higher prices (which could influence pricing method) and increase profit margin; Attract new customers increasing market share (in the competitive market); Establish brand image which can increase sales (of chocolate bars); Differentiate product from competitors which could increase market share; Reduce complaints (for the sole trader) so reduce returns/cash outflows/less waste; Maintain customer loyalty which can lead to repeat sales/increase revenue. Application: chocolate bars/cocoa/ingredients, sole trader, competitive market, pricing method, new product, best-selling product.

text: Do you think price skimming is the best pricing method for a business to use when introducing a new product? Justify your answer.
context: Rachel's business produces and sells chocolate bars. Rachel is a sole trader. The business operates in a competitive market. Rachel is also planning to introduce a new chocolate bar. Rachel knows deciding which pricing method to use for a new product is important.
ms: Award up to 2 marks for identification. Award up to 2 marks for development. Award up to 2 marks for justified decision. No application marks. Points must refer to a specific pricing method. Price skimming: Gives image of high quality (may increase reputation); May be quick to recover research/development costs (break even sooner); Increase profit margin; High price may encourage competitors to enter market (decrease market share); High price may decrease demand (decrease revenue). Other pricing methods: Penetration pricing (low price may be more affordable, increases sales); Cost-plus pricing (simple to use); Competitive pricing (should not lose sales to competition on price alone). Advantages/disadvantages of other methods can be awarded as analysis. Justification must compare price skimming vs another pricing method and make a clear reasoned decision.

text: Define 'working capital'.
context: TJK manufactures candles. Contributing to sustainable development is important to TJK. The business uses batch production in its factory in country X. The target market for TJK's products is females between 20 and 50 years of age. The Managing Director is reviewing TJK's financial data. Extract from TJK's financial data for 2024 ($000): Working capital 900, Profit 400, Revenue 1000.
ms: Award 2 marks for full definition, 1 mark for partial. Full: The money available for a business to pay its day-to-day expenses/short-term debts; Current assets minus current liabilities. Partial: Funds used to pay inventory/wages/electricity.

text: Calculate TJK's profit margin. Show your working.
context: TJK manufactures candles. Contributing to sustainable development is important to TJK. The business uses batch production in its factory in country X. Extract from TJK's financial data for 2024 ($000): Working capital 900, Profit 400, Revenue 1000.
ms: Award 2 marks for correct calculation, 1 mark for correct method but wrong answer. Correct answer: 40%. Method: Profit / Revenue x 100 = (400,000 / 1,000,000) x 100 = 40%. % sign required for 2 marks. If correct answer given with no workings, award 2 marks.

text: Identify four benefits to a business of becoming a multinational company.
context: TJK manufactures candles. The business uses batch production in its factory in country X. The Managing Director is also considering the benefits to a business of becoming a multinational company.
ms: Award 1 mark per benefit (max 4). Benefits: Increased sales/access to bigger/new markets; Better reputation/image; Lower transport costs; Avoid barriers to trade; Spread risks; Easier access to raw materials; Access to cheaper labour; Take advantage of lower tax rates; Access to government funding/grants. Only award first four responses given.

text: Explain two ways TJK could contribute to sustainable development.
context: TJK manufactures candles. Contributing to sustainable development is important to TJK. The business uses batch production in its factory in country X. The target market for TJK's products is females between 20 and 50 years of age.
ms: Award 1 mark per way (max 2) + 1 mark per application (max 2) + 1 mark per explanation (max 2). Ways: Reduce waste (when making candles) leading to less pollution; Use fewer resources (in the factory) so more left for future generations; Use environmentally friendly/sustainable materials (which could reduce harmful emissions); Use renewable energy/resources (in batch production); Develop environmentally friendly products (for females); Buy resources locally (reducing carbon footprint); Recycle (reduce amount of waste); Use environmentally friendly/sustainable packaging; Reuse materials so reduce number of materials needed. Application: candles, factory, batch production, females aged 20-50, $400,000 profit, $1 million revenue. Less pollution is analysis only.

text: Do you think batch production is the best method of production for a business to use? Justify your answer.
context: TJK manufactures candles. The business uses batch production in its factory in country X. The target market for TJK's products is females between 20 and 50 years of age.
ms: Award up to 2 marks for identification. Award up to 2 marks for development. Award up to 2 marks for justified decision. No application marks. Batch production: Flexible/can easily change from one product to another (respond quickly to changing customer tastes); Variety of products can be made (widen customer base/spread risk); Variety of tasks can motivate employees; Machines must be re-set between batches (reduce output); Warehouse space needed (increases storage costs). Flow production: Quick/high output; Economies of scale; Lower unit cost (able to charge lower price); Can operate 24 hours; Fewer employees/high automation; Machine breakdown stops whole line; High initial cost of machinery; Can lower motivation. Job production: Can charge high price (increasing profit margin); Can meet exact requirements of customers; Often high quality; Labour intensive (increases labour costs). Can accept comparative points. Justification must compare batch vs another method and make a clear reasoned decision.

text: Identify two services provided by businesses in the tertiary sector.
context: SEP operates in the tertiary sector. As a social enterprise, SEP has many objectives. It collects old books from libraries and schools and sells them to customers at a low price. SEP provides training for its 10 part-time employees. SEP's manager wants to know how the introduction of a legal minimum wage might affect a business.
ms: Award 1 mark per service (max 2). Services include: Banking; Retailing; Hotels; Holidays/tourism; Restaurant; Insurance; Accountancy; Advertising; Hairdressing; Entertainment; Transporting; Legal services; Education; Healthcare/medical/hospitals. Only award first two responses. Do not award names of businesses.

text: Identify two objectives a social enterprise might have.
context: SEP operates in the tertiary sector. As a social enterprise, SEP has many objectives. It collects old books from libraries and schools and sells them to customers at a low price.
ms: Award 1 mark per objective (max 2). Objectives: To make a profit to reinvest back into the business; Social benefit/welfare or examples e.g. to benefit/improve local community/disadvantaged groups in society; To protect the environment/environmental issues. Only award first two responses given.

text: Outline two benefits to SEP of having part-time employees.
context: SEP operates in the tertiary sector. As a social enterprise, SEP has many objectives. It collects old books from libraries and schools and sells them to customers at a low price. SEP provides training for its 10 part-time employees.
ms: Award 1 mark per benefit (max 2) + 1 mark per application (max 2). Benefits: Cheaper than full-time/reduce labour costs (which may help have low prices); More flexible hours of work (when selling books); Can ask/more likely to work at busier times (for the social enterprise); Can/more likely to extend working hours (for the tertiary sector business); Provides a range of skills/experience (among the 10 employees); Helps attract well-qualified employees who need flexible hours; Can help keep experienced staff. Application: books, social enterprise, tertiary sector, 10 employees, libraries/schools.

text: Explain two reasons why training is important to SEP.
context: SEP operates in the tertiary sector. As a social enterprise, SEP has many objectives. It collects old books from libraries and schools and sells them to customers at a low price. SEP provides training for its 10 part-time employees.
ms: Award 1 mark per reason (max 2) + 1 mark per application (max 2) + 1 mark per explanation (max 2). Reasons: Increase knowledge/skills/flexibility (of the 10 employees) which can increase quality of service; Increase motivation (in the social enterprise) which can increase productivity/efficiency; Better quality/decrease errors (when dealing with the books) which can decrease waste/cost; Increase efficiency (of the tertiary sector business) which can lower average/unit cost; Fewer accidents/ensure safe working conditions to avoid legal action; Able to train others reducing training costs; Help introduce new process which could lower mistakes; To attract new/potential employees. Application: books, social enterprise, 10 employees, part-time employees, tertiary sector, libraries/schools.

text: Do you think the introduction of a legal minimum wage will always have a negative effect on a business? Justify your answer.
context: SEP operates in the tertiary sector. As a social enterprise, SEP has many objectives. SEP provides training for its 10 part-time employees. SEP's manager wants to know how the introduction of a legal minimum wage might affect a business.
ms: Award up to 2 marks for identification. Award up to 2 marks for development. Award up to 2 marks for justified decision. No application marks. Positive effects: May encourage more people to apply for jobs (easier to recruit); Business may already pay above minimum wage so limited/no effect on costs; Increase motivation (increasing productivity/reduce absenteeism/labour turnover). Negative effects: Have to pay more to employees (increase costs, may have to increase prices); May not be able to afford to pay all workers higher wage (may have to make redundancies); Other workers paid more than minimum may ask for wage increase; May have to find other ways to reduce costs (may reduce quality). Justification must weigh whether minimum wage will ALWAYS be negative and make a clear reasoned decision.

text: Identify two roles of packaging.
context: MDZ manufactures a range of chocolate bars. It has 300 employees. MDZ purchases its ingredients from suppliers in the local area. Acting in an ethical way with its stakeholder groups is important. MDZ has products at different stages of the product life cycle. The business is also developing a new product. The Marketing Director needs to make decisions about the packaging and the price of the new product. She knows it is important for a business to use a suitable method of sales promotion for a new product.
ms: Award 1 mark per role (max 2). Roles include: Carry information about product / meet legal requirements; Protect the product; Promote brand image / name / reputation; Help advertise / attract customers; Add value; Ease of transport; Easy/convenient to open/use; Ease of storage/display; Suitable for product to fit in / contain the product. Only award first two responses given.

text: Identify two stages (other than development) of the product life cycle.
context: MDZ manufactures a range of chocolate bars. It has 300 employees. MDZ purchases its ingredients from suppliers in the local area. Acting in an ethical way with its stakeholder groups is important. MDZ has products at different stages of the product life cycle. The business is also developing a new product. The Marketing Director needs to make decisions about the packaging and the price of the new product. She knows it is important for a business to use a suitable method of sales promotion for a new product.
ms: Award 1 mark per stage (max 2). Stages (other than development): Introduction; Growth; Maturity; Decline. Candidates must name and not simply describe the stage. Only award first two responses given.

text: Outline two factors MDZ's Marketing Director should consider when deciding the price of the new product.
context: MDZ manufactures a range of chocolate bars. It has 300 employees. MDZ purchases its ingredients from suppliers in the local area. Acting in an ethical way with its stakeholder groups is important. MDZ has products at different stages of the product life cycle. The business is also developing a new product. The Marketing Director needs to make decisions about the packaging and the price of the new product. She knows it is important for a business to use a suitable method of sales promotion for a new product.
ms: Award 1 mark per factor (max 2) + 1 mark per relevant application to this business (max 2). Factors include: Brand image (as MDZ wants to act ethically); Cost of production/materials/labour (as MDZ has 300 employees); Competition/price of competitors products (for chocolate); Whether product is unique/availability of substitutes; Size of market/niche market/mass market/target market/level of demand/price elasticity of demand; Business objective; Profit margin/added value; Quality; Government or legal controls/tax. Application words: chocolate bars, ingredients, ethical, 300 employees, stakeholder groups, sales promotion, packaging, suppliers from local area.

text: Explain one way MDZ could act in an ethical way with each of the following stakeholder groups: Employees AND Suppliers.
context: MDZ manufactures a range of chocolate bars. It has 300 employees. MDZ purchases its ingredients from suppliers in the local area. Acting in an ethical way with its stakeholder groups is important. MDZ has products at different stages of the product life cycle. The business is also developing a new product. The Marketing Director needs to make decisions about the packaging and the price of the new product. She knows it is important for a business to use a suitable method of sales promotion for a new product.
ms: Award 1 mark per identification (max 2) + 1 mark per application (max 2) + 1 mark per explanation/analysis (max 2). Employees: Pay fair wages to its 300 employees to maintain their standard of living; Ensure fair working conditions when making the new product so they do not leave/become demotivated; Avoid use of child labour/not produce products in sweat shops. Suppliers: Pay on time for the ingredients to help prevent cash flow problems for them; Pay fair price to protect suppliers profit margin as products purchased in the local area. Analysis should focus on effect on the stakeholder, not on the business.

text: Explain two possible methods of sales promotion a business could use for a new product. Which is likely to be the best method to use? Justify your answer.
context: MDZ manufactures a range of chocolate bars. It has 300 employees. MDZ purchases its ingredients from suppliers in the local area. Acting in an ethical way with its stakeholder groups is important. MDZ has products at different stages of the product life cycle. The business is also developing a new product. The Marketing Director needs to make decisions about the packaging and the price of the new product. She knows it is important for a business to use a suitable method of sales promotion for a new product.
ms: Award up to 2 marks for identification of relevant points. Award up to 2 marks for relevant development. Award up to 2 marks for a justified decision on best method. No application marks. Max 3 marks if only one method discussed. Methods: Free samples (encourage customers to try product, but cost of providing samples); Point of sale displays/demonstrations (raises awareness); BOGOF/special offers/discounts (makes product more affordable); Loyalty schemes (repeat business); Free gifts; Competitions (buy more for a chance to win); After sales service. Justification must compare two methods and explain why one is better than the other for a new product.

text: Identify two ways to measure the size of a business.
context: Jonathon is a sole trader. He owns a shop selling office equipment including printers. To encourage sales Jonathon allows customers 4 weeks to pay for the office equipment. Jonathon thinks his business is likely to remain small. He knows managing cash flow is important for his business and he has prepared a cash flow forecast. Extract from Jonathon's cash flow forecast July-September 2025 ($000): July: Cash inflow 60, Cash outflow 90, Net cash flow (30), Opening balance 20, Closing balance (10). August: Cash inflow 80, Cash outflow 95, Net cash flow X, Opening balance (10), Closing balance (25). September: Cash inflow Y, Cash outflow 70, Net cash flow 20, Opening balance (25), Closing balance (5).
ms: Award 1 mark per way (max 2). Ways include: (Value of) capital employed; Value of output/sales OR revenue; Number of customers/sales/volume/amount of output; (Number of) employees. Only award first two answers given.

text: Calculate X and Y from the cash flow forecast.
context: Jonathon is a sole trader. He owns a shop selling office equipment including printers. To encourage sales Jonathon allows customers 4 weeks to pay for the office equipment. Jonathon thinks his business is likely to remain small. He knows managing cash flow is important for his business and he has prepared a cash flow forecast. Extract from Jonathon's cash flow forecast July-September 2025 ($000): July: Cash inflow 60, Cash outflow 90, Net cash flow (30), Opening balance 20, Closing balance (10). August: Cash inflow 80, Cash outflow 95, Net cash flow X, Opening balance (10), Closing balance (25). September: Cash inflow Y, Cash outflow 70, Net cash flow 20, Opening balance (25), Closing balance (5).
ms: Award 1 mark each. X = (15) or -15 (must be shown as negative). Y = 90. X = 80 - 95 = -15. Y = Net cash flow + Cash outflow = 20 + 70 = 90. $ sign and 000s not required.

text: Outline two reasons (other than finance) why Jonathon's business is likely to remain small.
context: Jonathon is a sole trader. He owns a shop selling office equipment including printers. To encourage sales Jonathon allows customers 4 weeks to pay for the office equipment. Jonathon thinks his business is likely to remain small. He knows managing cash flow is important for his business and he has prepared a cash flow forecast.
ms: Award 1 mark per reason (max 2) + 1 mark per application (max 2). Reasons: Owner's objectives/not want responsibility for managing a larger business/keep control (as a sole trader); Low demand/small size of market (in the shop); Few large businesses control the market/market domination (for office equipment); Lacks knowledge/skills/experience (to expand), such as managing cash flow; Wants to maintain close relationship with customers/personal service; Remain flexible/respond quickly to changes in consumer tastes; Type of industry/market/product. Application words: sole trader, shop, office equipment/printers, cash flow is important, data from Table 2.1.

text: Explain two reasons why Jonathon's business might have a cash flow problem.
context: Jonathon is a sole trader. He owns a shop selling office equipment including printers. To encourage sales Jonathon allows customers 4 weeks to pay for the office equipment. Jonathon thinks his business is likely to remain small. He knows managing cash flow is important for his business and he has prepared a cash flow forecast.
ms: Award 1 mark per reason (max 2) + 1 mark per application (max 2) + 1 mark per explanation (max 2). Reasons: Allow customers too long to pay/high level of credit sales (customers have 4 weeks to pay) which delays cash inflows; No trade credit/paying suppliers too quickly (for the office equipment) which increases cash outflows; Poor financial planning/unexpected costs (as operates as a sole trader) which leads to additional cash outflows; Holding too much inventory; Growing too quickly/overtrading; Seasonal/lower demand. Application: sole trader, shop, office equipment/printers, remain small, data from Table 2.1, 4 weeks for customers to pay.

text: Do you think the advantages of operating as a sole trader business are greater than the disadvantages? Justify your answer.
context: Jonathon is a sole trader. He owns a shop selling office equipment including printers. To encourage sales Jonathon allows customers 4 weeks to pay for the office equipment. Jonathon thinks his business is likely to remain small. He knows managing cash flow is important for his business.
ms: Award up to 2 marks for identification of relevant points. Award up to 2 marks for relevant development. Award up to 2 marks for a justified decision. No application marks. Advantages: Keeps all profit (incentive to work hard); Makes all decisions/complete control/own boss (quicker decisions/no disagreements); Freedom to choose own holidays/when to work; Keep financial information private (competitors cannot use it); Close contact with customers/personal service (customer loyalty); Few legal regulations. Disadvantages: Unlimited liability (may lose personal assets to repay debts); Limited sources of finance (cash flow problems/difficult to fund expansion); No one to cover if owner is ill (business may lose sales); Only has own skills (less able to compete); Must work long hours/difficult to take holidays (could lead to mistakes); No one to share risks/losses; All the responsibility; No separate legal identity; No continuity. Justification must weigh advantages vs disadvantages and make a clear reasoned decision.

text: Define 'external benefits'.
context: GAE is a multinational company. It manufactures steel. GAE has 2400 employees and has factories in 4 countries. The business regularly introduces new technology. Holding inventory is important. GAE's directors are planning to build a new factory and want to know how legal controls over location might affect this decision. The Managing Director said, 'The new factory will create many external benefits.'
ms: Award 2 marks for full definition, 1 mark for partial. Full: Gains to the rest of society other than the business as a result of business activity. Partial (1 mark): Gains to the rest of society / third party. References to business activity adds the second mark.

text: Identify two ways legal controls over location might affect a business.
context: GAE is a multinational company. It manufactures steel. GAE has 2400 employees and has factories in 4 countries. The business regularly introduces new technology. Holding inventory is important. GAE's directors are planning to build a new factory and want to know how legal controls over location might affect this decision.
ms: Award 1 mark per way (max 2). Ways include: Affect where they can/cannot locate; Affect how they produce (e.g. change production methods, change/restrict raw materials used); Affect when/hours they can operate; Increased costs. Only award first two responses given.

text: Outline two advantages to GAE of introducing new technology.
context: GAE is a multinational company. It manufactures steel. GAE has 2400 employees and has factories in 4 countries. The business regularly introduces new technology. Holding inventory is important.
ms: Award 1 mark per advantage (max 2) + 1 mark per application (max 2). Advantages: Motivate employees (as have 2400 workers); Fewer employees needed (in the 4 countries); Increases productivity/efficiency/quicker production (in its factories); Improved quality/consistent quality/less waste/fewer mistakes (when making steel); Increase output (for this multinational company); Can work 24/7/no need for breaks in production; Help design/make new products; Improved communication. Application words: steel, multinational company, factory/factories, 4 countries, 2400 employees, inventory is important, external benefits. Allow lower cost once, unless two clearly specific different costs.

text: Explain two reasons why holding inventory might be important for GAE.
context: GAE is a multinational company. It manufactures steel. GAE has 2400 employees and has factories in 4 countries. The business regularly introduces new technology. Holding inventory is important.
ms: Award 1 mark per reason (max 2) + 1 mark per application (max 2) + 1 mark per explanation (max 2). Reasons: Benefit from economies of scale/bulk buying discounts (reducing average/unit cost) for this multinational company; Maintain/not delay production/backup materials in case of breakdowns (at the factories) so can meet orders on time; Protect against delays from suppliers/shortage of materials (which could delay production in the 4 countries); Meet/satisfy demand/customer orders (of steel) which can increase revenue; Meet sudden/unexpected changes in demand (helping maintain reputation); Meet seasonal changes in demand. Application: steel, multinational company, factory/factories, 4 countries, 2400 employees, new technology, external benefits, legal controls over location.

text: Explain two benefits to a business of being a multinational company. Which benefit is likely to be the most important? Justify your answer.
context: GAE is a multinational company. It manufactures steel. GAE has 2400 employees and has factories in 4 countries. The business regularly introduces new technology. Holding inventory is important.
ms: Award up to 2 marks for identification. Award up to 2 marks for development. Award up to 2 marks for justified decision on most important benefit. No application marks. Benefits: Spreading risk (fall in sales in one country offset by increase in another); Access new/wider markets/customers (increasing revenue/market share); Improve brand image/reputation (higher prices/competitive advantage); Economies of scale (lower average/unit costs); Cheaper/better quality raw materials (reducing transport costs OR allowing new products); Access to cheap labour (lower costs/higher profit margin) OR skilled labour (increase efficiency); Avoid import quotas (fewer limits on imports); Avoid import tariffs (products not more expensive); Reduced tax liability/favourable tax rates; Access government support/grants. Justification must compare two benefits and make a clear reasoned decision on which is most important.

text: Identify two objectives (other than growth) a business might have.
context: HYT is a travel business which sells holidays. One of its objectives is growth. Last year HYT completed a takeover of one of its competitors. External sources of finance were used to fund this growth. HYT now has 460 shops and 4000 employees. The Human Resources Director knows there are benefits and limitations for a business of having full-time employees. HYT's managers use ideas from Herzberg's motivational theory to keep employees motivated. Good internal communication is important for HYT.
ms: Award 1 mark per objective (max 2). Objectives: Survival/break-even; Make a profit; Increase/gain market share; Increase/maintain number of sales/customers; Increase/gain revenue/value of sales; Improve/create business image; Increase return to shareholders/return on capital employed; Be socially/ethically/environmentally responsible. Only award first two responses given. Accept 'increase sales' where no specific examples given.

text: Identify two advantages to a business of using external sources of finance.
context: HYT is a travel business which sells holidays. One of its objectives is growth. Last year HYT completed a takeover of one of its competitors. External sources of finance were used to fund this growth. HYT now has 460 shops and 4000 employees.
ms: Award 1 mark per advantage (max 2). Advantages: Able to raise funds quicker/quickly; May be able to raise full/larger amount of finance; Can use internal sources/profit for other purposes; Provider may offer advice/support. Only award first two responses given.

text: Using Herzberg's theory, state whether each of the following would be classed as a hygiene factor or as a motivator: (1) Working conditions (2) Wages (3) Opportunities for promotion (4) Relationship with supervisor.
context: HYT is a travel business which sells holidays. HYT's managers use ideas from Herzberg's motivational theory to keep employees motivated.
ms: Award 1 mark per correct answer (max 4). Answers: Working conditions = hygiene factor; Wages = hygiene factor; Opportunities for promotion = motivator; Relationship with supervisor = hygiene factor. Only award first response given for each.

text: Explain two methods of internal communication HYT might use with its employees.
context: HYT is a travel business which sells holidays. One of its objectives is growth. Last year HYT completed a takeover of one of its competitors. HYT now has 460 shops and 4000 employees. Good internal communication is important for HYT.
ms: Award 1 mark per method (max 2) + 1 mark per application (max 2) + 1 mark per explanation (max 2). Methods: Meetings/team briefings (about its growth objective, can get instant feedback/ask questions); Email (can be sent to multiple people at the same time, to its 4000 employees); Phone/mobile calls (to one of its 460 shops, allows discussion/explanation/immediate feedback); Letter (written record); Text/SMS/WhatsApp/WeChat (can be sent quickly); Posters/noticeboards/notices (placed in various locations); Video conference/Zoom/Teams/Google Meet/FaceTime; Social media; Internal newspapers/newsletter/magazine. Application: travel business, sells holidays, 460 shops/stores, 4000 employees, full-time employees, takeover, objective is growth, external sources of finance. Same analysis point only awarded once.

text: Do you think the benefits to a business of having full-time employees are greater than the limitations? Justify your answer.
context: HYT is a travel business which sells holidays. HYT now has 460 shops and 4000 employees. The Human Resources Director knows there are benefits and limitations for a business of having full-time employees.
ms: Award up to 2 marks for identification. Award up to 2 marks for development. Award up to 2 marks for justified decision. No application marks. Points must relate to the business and not the employees. Benefits: More familiar with business/consistent service/quality (helps build/maintain customer relationships/better reputation/more productive); Workers likely to be loyal/committed/less likely to leave (reducing recruitment costs); Easy to communicate/update (fewer errors); Fewer employees to train/recruit (saving time/cost). Limitations: May not be willing/want to work overtime (difficult to meet demand); Must pay whether sufficient work or not (increasing labour costs); May miss out on potential employees who cannot work full-time. Justification must weigh benefits vs limitations and make a clear reasoned decision. Expensive/high cost can be knowledge or analysis. Accept points about cost once unless clearly explained.

text: Define 'batch production'.
context: NFC manufactures shoes using batch production. Quality assurance is used to maintain quality. NFC uses market segmentation. The Marketing Director is reviewing NFC's product range and knows there are both benefits and limitations to developing new products. The promotion of products is important.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Where a quantity/group of one product is made then a quantity of another product is produced. A whole batch/group moves through the different stages of production together. Partial definition (1 mark): Similar items made together / items made in a group or set / moving together through different stages of production. Requires both the idea of a group of products AND the production process.

text: Identify two aims of promotion.
context: NFC manufactures shoes. The promotion of products is important.
ms: 1 mark each (max 2). Only award first two. Acceptable: raise awareness/inform/remind people about products or services; persuade/attract new consumers/increase sales/revenue; create/maintain brand or company image/reputation; build customer loyalty/encourage repeat purchases; introduce new products to market; differentiate from/compete with competitors.

text: Outline one advantage and one disadvantage to NFC of using quality assurance.
context: NFC manufactures shoes using batch production. Quality assurance is used to maintain quality. NFC plans to develop new products.
ms: 1 mark advantage + 1 mark application + 1 mark disadvantage + 1 mark application = 4 marks. Advantages: errors spotted earlier/during production of the shoes; can motivate employees so may offer ideas for the product range; no need to recruit quality inspectors. Disadvantages: all workers need training - time and cost - may take funds from developing new products; not all workers willing/able to spot problems during batch production; may slow down production. Application words: shoes, batch production, promotion of products, developing new products, product range, market segmentation.

text: Explain two benefits to NFC of using market segmentation.
context: NFC manufactures shoes using batch production. Quality assurance is used. NFC uses market segmentation and plans to develop new products. The promotion of products is important.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 benefits = 6 marks). Do NOT award answers about benefits of market research. Benefits: Design/produce goods to meet specific consumer needs - costs/materials not wasted on wrong products - especially as NFC plans to develop new products; Help target advertising/marketing strategies - ensures maximum reach - which is an aim of promotion; Identify gaps in the market/new opportunities for its shoes which can help spread risk; Make marketing expenditure more effective so do not waste money/resources. Application words: shoes, batch production, quality assurance, promotion of products, develop new products.

text: Do you think the benefits for a business of developing new products are greater than the limitations? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Benefits: increase demand/customer base/sales increasing revenue/market share; spread risk/diversification so sales fall in one product offset by another; competitive advantage/USP increasing customer/brand loyalty; enter new markets; improve brand recognition. Limitations: must produce trial products/more raw materials increasing costs; need to carry out market research increasing cash outflows; need to launch/promote/market new product; large capital expenditure/new machinery costs; may need to recruit/train additional employees. Evaluation: must discuss at least one benefit and one limitation with justified conclusion.

text: Define 'profit'.
context: FLD is a furniture retailer. It has 460 shops and 20,000 employees. The Finance Director is reviewing FLD's income statement: Revenue $400m, Gross profit $200m, Expenses $60m, Profit $140m. She is concerned that FLD's gross profit is decreasing.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Total income/revenue less total costs. Total revenue minus total costs. Difference between revenue and total cost. Gross profit minus expenses. Partial definition (1 mark): Revenue minus costs. Max 1 mark if candidate uses 'money' rather than revenue/income.

text: Identify two expenses a business might have.
context: FLD is a furniture retailer. The Finance Director is reviewing FLD's income statement which shows expenses of $60 million.
ms: 1 mark each (max 2). Only award first two. Acceptable: rent; rates; electricity/gas/heating/lighting/water/utilities; insurance; interest; storage; marketing/advertising; salaries; maintenance/repairs; phone/internet.

text: Outline two possible reasons why FLD's gross profit is decreasing.
context: FLD is a furniture retailer with 460 shops and 20,000 employees. Revenue is $400m, Gross profit is $200m (decreasing), Expenses are $60m, Profit is $140m.
ms: 1 mark per point + 1 mark per application (max 2 points = 4 marks). Points: low/falling sales/demand/customers at its 460 shops; change in/increase or decrease in selling price for the retailer; increase in cost of sales/variable cost/cost of inventory so gross profit is at $200 million. Application words: furniture, 460 locations/shops, large business, retailer, 20,000 employees, $400 million revenue, $200 million gross profit. Accept 'decreased revenue' where no specific examples given.

text: Explain two advantages to FLD of using internal recruitment when recruiting new managers.
context: FLD is a furniture retailer with 460 shops and 20,000 employees. Internal recruitment is used when recruiting new shop managers. Revenue $400m, Gross profit $200m, Expenses $60m, Profit $140m.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 advantages = 6 marks). Advantages: Cheaper/lower advertising costs - lower/maintain expenses - of $60 million; Already knows the business - can be productive sooner - to help sell furniture; Less/no induction training needed; Can motivate employees at 460 locations reducing labour turnover/increasing loyalty/sales; Business knows the person's ability/reliability reducing chance of selecting wrong person; Recruitment is quicker - able to focus on other tasks - such as increasing revenue above $400 million. Application words: furniture, 460 locations, large business, retailers, 20,000 employees, $60 million expenses, $400 million revenue, $200 million gross profit.

text: Do you think job rotation is the best method for a large business to use to motivate its employees? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Candidates must name the motivation method to access knowledge marks.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Must NAME the motivation method. Job rotation: more flexible/gain new skills leading to higher productivity; can cover absent workers so meet orders on time; work more interesting/less boring leading to lower absenteeism/turnover; increased training needed increasing costs; workers may not be willing/able leading to lower quality/more waste; time to switch tasks. Other methods: Job enrichment - more responsibilities/valued/trusted; Bonus - only paid if target met; Praise - no additional cost; Training - new skills; Promotion opportunities. Evaluation: must name and compare at least two methods; justify why one is better for a LARGE business specifically.

text: Define 'private sector'.
context: Hal wants to be a successful entrepreneur. He plans to leave his job to start up a bakery. The bakery will operate in the private sector.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): The part of the economy controlled by individuals/companies for profit. Business activities owned by individuals/group of individuals. Partial definition (1 mark): Not government/state controlled. Run/controlled by individuals.

text: Identify two reasons why new businesses are at a greater risk of failure.
context: Hal knows new businesses are at a greater risk of failure.
ms: 1 mark each (max 2). Only award first two. Acceptable: lack of finance/start-up capital; cash flow problems/lack of liquidity; level of competition/market already saturated; lack of customers/demand/sales/customer loyalty; poor planning/no business plan; lack of managerial/business experience/skills; inadequate market research/poor marketing; no/low reputation/brand awareness.

text: Identify four stakeholder groups a business might have.
context: Hal's bakery will have many stakeholder groups.
ms: 1 mark each (max 4). Only award first four. Acceptable: employees/workers; managers/directors; owners/shareholders; suppliers; lenders/banks; government; local community; customers.

text: Explain two characteristics Hal will need to become a successful entrepreneur.
context: Hal wants to be a successful entrepreneur. He plans to leave his job to start up a bakery in the private sector. The business will have many stakeholder groups.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 characteristics = 6 marks). Must identify a recognised entrepreneurial characteristic. Characteristics: Risk-taking - especially as plans to leave his job - owner may lose investment; Hard-working - must do everything on own/work long hours - to set up the bakery; Creative - new ideas can help gain customers - for his private sector business; Effective communicator/persuasive - with stakeholders - convince banks/suppliers/customers; Perseverance/determination/resilience/self-motivated - prepared to keep going when facing problems; Optimistic - always believes they can succeed; Self-confident - convince people/banks to invest; Independent - able to work without help; Innovative. Application words: leave his job, start-up/new business, bakery/cakes/recipes, private sector, stakeholder groups.

text: Do you think a bank loan is the best source of start-up capital for a new business? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Bank loan: quick to arrange so does not delay plans; must pay interest increasing costs/cash outflows; must repay; able to obtain large/full amount; may need collateral - not available for start-up/personal assets at risk. Other sources: Own savings - no need to repay; Borrow from friends/family - may give long repayment time; Overdraft - arrange quickly/only pay interest when used; Government grant - no interest; Crowdfunding - no guarantee of raising full amount. Evaluation: compare bank loan against at least one other source; justify conclusion for a NEW business specifically.

text: Define 'average cost'.
context: MHL manufactures tyres for large vehicles. It has factories in 6 countries. She is reviewing data: output 200,000 units/month, fixed costs $500,000/month, variable cost $25/unit.
ms: Full definition (2 marks): Total cost divided by total output. Total cost divided by number of items produced. The cost of producing a single unit of output. Partial definition (1 mark): Cost divided by output. Total cost divided by number of units.

text: Calculate total variable cost per month. Show your working. (Output: 200,000 units/month; Variable cost per unit: $25)
context: MHL manufactures tyres. Output per month: 200,000 units. Variable cost per unit: $25.
ms: Correct answer (2 marks): $5,000,000 / $5 million. Method (1 mark): Output times variable cost per unit = 200,000 times $25. Must have correct number of zeros — $500,000 scores 0. $ sign not required but 'million' or full zeros needed. If correct answer given with no working shown, award 2 marks.

text: Outline two external costs MHL might create when producing its products.
context: MHL manufactures tyres for large vehicles. It has factories in 6 countries. The business creates external costs when producing its products.
ms: 1 mark per external cost + 1 mark per application (max 2 external costs = 4 marks). External costs: loss of space/land/deforestation for the factories; pollution such as smoke/fumes/noise/chemicals in air when making tyres; depletion of natural resources to make 200,000 units; loss of wildlife in the 6 countries. Application words: tyres/rubber, factories/factory, 6 countries, globalisation, 200,000 units, $25 variable cost per unit, $500,000 fixed costs. Max 1 mark for examples of pollution (all treated as same point).

text: Explain two opportunities of globalisation for MHL.
context: MHL manufactures tyres for large vehicles. It has factories in 6 countries. The Managing Director knows globalisation provides many opportunities for MHL.
ms: 1 mark identification + 1 mark application + 1 mark explanation (max 2 opportunities = 6 marks). Opportunities: Increase potential sales/access more markets for its tyres increasing revenue/market share; cheaper/better quality raw materials from other countries for its factories improving profit margin; lower wages/cheaper labour in the 6 countries reducing labour costs; avoid/fewer quotas which could limit quantity sold; avoid/lower tariffs so products not made more expensive; access new technologies improving efficiency/new product development; access to government grants in other countries. Application words: tyres/rubber, factories/factory, 6 countries, 200,000 units, $25 variable cost, $500,000 fixed costs.

text: Explain two methods of communication a business could use to communicate with its suppliers. Which is likely to be the best method to use? Justify your answer.
context: This is a general question so there are no marks for application. Candidates must name the specific communication method.
ms: Up to 2 marks identification + up to 2 marks development + up to 2 marks justified decision. No marks for application. Must NAME the specific method (not just 'written' or 'verbal'). Methods: Email - can be saved for future reference; Phone/telephone - allows immediate feedback; Online meeting - allows everyone to discuss/ask questions; Video conference/Zoom/Teams/Google Meet/FaceTime - people do not have to travel; Text/SMS/WhatsApp/WeChat/Messenger - but limited information; Letter - but time-consuming/expensive; Websites - but no feedback/one-way. Evaluation: must discuss TWO valid methods and justify which is best for communicating with SUPPLIERS specifically.

text: Explain four reasons why a person may set up their own business.
context: Bob set up BW after being unemployed for 7 months.
caseStudy:
Bright Windows (BW)

Bob recently set up BW, a window washing business after he had been unemployed for 7 months. Many home owners are extremely busy and find it difficult to find the time to wash the windows in their houses. Increasing incomes have also led to a high demand for window washing services. The primary market research carried out by Bob before setting up his business confirmed this high demand. Bob used sampling when carrying out a questionnaire.

Bob is a sole trader. He invested $2,000 to get his business started and to provide working capital. He needed $250 to purchase ladders, buckets and cleaning products. He also needed transport to travel between customers' houses. Bob decided to lease a van at a cost of $150 per month. Bob has to pay wages to his 2 part-time employees of $300 per month each.

Bob only has a few regular customers and he needs to promote the business to attract more customers. He is considering printing leaflets, advertising in local newspapers or just relying on social media. He has to decide which method of promotion to use. He hopes his regular customers will tell their friends about BW's excellent services. If the promotion is successful he will need to ensure his employees can meet this higher demand.

Appendix 1 — Text message from one BW employee to another: Employee 1: "I like working with Bob, he is a good boss. I am happy he asks us what we think. I do not want to work for anyone else but I would like to work more hours." Employee 2: "My last employer always told me what to do. I do not like having to make decisions. Working fewer hours and being flexible with the times I work makes it easier to look after my family."

Appendix 2 — Summary of costs, price and demand for BW: Fixed cost per month $1,250; Variable cost per house cleaned $1; Price per house $11; Average number of customers per month 225.

Appendix 3 — Article in the national newspaper, Main News, 10 February 2020, "Should window washing become more environmentally friendly?": The most effective products used to wash windows contain chemicals which damage the environment. However, these products reduce the time taken to wash windows by 50%. Many window washing businesses use plastic bottles as containers for all their cleaning products — most of these bottles cannot be refilled or recycled. Washing windows can use a lot of water, which reduces the amount available for other uses. Recently a new machine has been developed for washing windows which is very efficient and recycles the water it uses — each machine costs $1,000. The Government is being encouraged by environmental pressure groups to introduce legal controls over the window washing industry.
ms:
8 marks. Award 1 mark per reason (max 4) + 1 additional mark per explanation. No application marks for this question.

Reasons: made redundant, needing to replace lost income; to be their own boss, gaining independence from an employer's instructions; to decide how to spend time, with flexible working hours; to make a profit, potentially earning more than working for someone else; identifying a gap in the market, or wanting to use personal skills/creativity/ethical principles; to gain recognition and status.

Example: "Redundancy means loss of job (1), so setting up a business replaces the income which was lost (1)."

text: Explain the benefits to BW of employing part-time employees and full-time employees. Do you think Bob should continue to employ only part-time employees? Justify your answer.
context: BW currently has 2 part-time employees paid $300/month each; Appendix 1 shows one wants more hours and one prefers flexible part-time work.
caseStudy:
Bright Windows (BW)

Bob recently set up BW, a window washing business after he had been unemployed for 7 months. The primary market research carried out by Bob before setting up his business confirmed this high demand. Bob used sampling when carrying out a questionnaire.

Bob is a sole trader. He invested $2,000 to get his business started and to provide working capital. He needed $250 to purchase ladders, buckets and cleaning products. He also needed transport to travel between customers' houses. Bob decided to lease a van at a cost of $150 per month. Bob has to pay wages to his 2 part-time employees of $300 per month each.

He hopes his regular customers will tell their friends about BW's excellent services. If the promotion is successful he will need to ensure his employees can meet this higher demand.

Appendix 1 — Text message from one BW employee to another: Employee 1: "I like working with Bob, he is a good boss. I am happy he asks us what we think. I do not want to work for anyone else but I would like to work more hours." Employee 2: "My last employer always told me what to do. I do not like having to make decisions. Working fewer hours and being flexible with the times I work makes it easier to look after my family."

Appendix 2 — Summary of costs, price and demand for BW: Fixed cost per month $1,250; Variable cost per house cleaned $1; Price per house $11; Average number of customers per month 225.

Appendix 3 — Article in the national newspaper, Main News, 10 February 2020, "Should window washing become more environmentally friendly?": The most effective products used to wash windows contain chemicals which damage the environment. However, these products reduce the time taken to wash windows by 50%. Many window washing businesses use plastic bottles as containers for all their cleaning products — most of these bottles cannot be refilled or recycled. Washing windows can use a lot of water, which reduces the amount available for other uses. Recently a new machine has been developed for washing windows which is very efficient and recycles the water it uses — each machine costs $1,000. The Government is being encouraged by environmental pressure groups to introduce legal controls over the window washing industry.
ms:
12 marks. Levels-based marking.

Part-time benefits: more flexible hours, boosting motivation; easier to increase hours at busy cleaning times, meeting demand; easier to recruit given flexibility fitting family commitments; may reduce labour costs versus full-time staff.
Full-time benefits: more likely to be trained, raising productivity/speed; lower labour turnover as staff see the job as long-term, cutting recruitment costs; more committed, raising motivation and efficiency; more suitable for future promotion if BW expands; easier to communicate with given longer daily hours.

Valid conclusions: continue part-time only — as a new business without many customers yet, part-time keeps wage costs lower and flexible; OR switch to full-time — if BW plans to expand, full-time staff could develop the skills needed to take on more responsibility and help Bob delegate.

text: Explain two reasons why Bob used sampling when carrying out a questionnaire.
context: Bob carried out primary market research using a questionnaire with sampling before starting BW.
caseStudy:
